requirement: Every requirement defined anywhere in the plan document is completed before launch is declared — no item may be deferred, partially shipped, or left as a follow-up.
sourceQuote: We must complete all work defined in this document.
acceptance: A committed launch checklist enumerates every requirement ID derived from the plan and maps each to a landed commit or shipped deliverable; the count of items in state 'deferred', 'partial', 'TODO', or 'blocked' at sign-off is exactly zero.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the launch checklist now exists and is generated — `pnpm launch:record` writes docs/engineering/launch/launch-checklist.md and launch-record.json from the 399-row baseline plus docs/engineering/launch/slices/*.md. But the acceptance's count is not zero: the generated summary reads `not-started 366 / in-progress 21 / closed 12`, `Launch-blockers not closed 133`, `Sign-off gate violations 387`, and `Sign-off: withheld`. Only four slice files were ever filed (ci-gating, launch-governance, security-and-domains, test-standards) even though ~1048 files changed across 45 commits, so most shipped work claims no requirement id at all.
notes: Nothing to audit against. This is the meta-requirement, so its absence means there is currently no artifact that could show a zero deferred/partial/TODO count at sign-off.

requirement: All anticipated or implied functionality must be demonstrated working in the production environment, not only in local dev or a preview deployment.
sourceQuote: all functionality that is anticipated or implied actually works in production
acceptance: Each primary flow (sign-in, workspace/org creation, project creation, task creation, calendar, cycles, Athena session, each connector) is exercised against the deployed production hostname — evidence is a screenshot or HTTP trace per flow whose URL bar/host is the production domain (never localhost or a *.vercel.app preview) and whose outcome is success with zero console errors.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): re-probed production directly. `curl -s https://docket-api.hypertext.studio/v1/openapi.json` → 204 paths; the local HEAD API serves 236; `/me/athena/*` is still absent from production (`has /me/athena/chat: false`). docs/engineering/launch/production-verification.md records the same verdict from `pnpm launch:verify-prod` (exit 1, 'production 32 paths behind HEAD'). No primary flow can be demonstrated on the production hostname for the entire personal-Athena surface because it is not deployed there.
notes: No per-flow production evidence exists anywhere in the repo. I could not exercise the flows myself: production is passkey-only and I am prohibited from entering credentials. But the endpoint-count delta alone is decisive — 32 endpoints of current functionality are not deployed.

requirement: When data or documentation cannot be obtained by a simple web fetch, it must be retrieved by driving a browser or another means — inaccessibility is not grounds for leaving work incomplete.
sourceQuote: If some data is not available, like because some documentation is not accessible via a simple web fetch, you MUST use a browser or some other means to obtain the data.
acceptance: Zero requirements in the launch record are closed as blocked/unimplemented with a rationale citing unavailable documentation, a paywalled/JS-only doc site, or a failed fetch; any requirement that hit such an obstacle records the browser/CLI/account session actually used to obtain the data.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): docs/engineering/launch/obstacle-log.md (247 lines) now exists and the generated record reports `State: blocked 0`, so no requirement is closed as blocked citing unavailable documentation. The clause that cannot be confirmed is coverage: only 4 of the build's lanes filed a slice, so obstacles hit by unrecorded lanes would not appear in the log and their absence proves nothing.
notes: The verification artifact this requirement is graded against — a launch record enumerating these 43 IDs with per-item disposition — does not exist anywhere in the repo. There is therefore nothing to audit for 'closed as blocked citing unavailable documentation'. Vacuous compliance is not compliance: status is not-built, not pass.

requirement: Lack of permission or access may never be recorded as a blocker, since full access to the host machine, browsers, CLIs, and accounts is granted.
sourceQuote: "I don't have permission" is not an excuse because you have complete and total access to my host computer, including any application, any browser, any CLI, any account, etc.
acceptance: A grep of the launch record / WORKLOG for blocker rationales returns zero open items whose stated cause is missing permission, missing access, missing credentials, or 'could not sign in'.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): `grep -ni 'permission|no access|could not sign in|missing credential'` over docs/engineering/launch/ returns no open blocker attributed to missing permission, and the generated record has zero entries in `blocked`. Same coverage caveat as GEN-03: 366 of 399 requirements are `not-started` and unowned, so 'zero blockers' is partly an artifact of nothing being claimed.
notes: Cannot return zero permission-blocked items from a record that does not exist. Note WORKLOG does contain historical blocker language of a different kind (e.g. the 2026-06-29 entry lists 'NOT YET DONE (blocked / deferred)' items citing a mixed working tree and an unapplied migration) — those are environment blockers, not permission blockers, and predate this launch.

requirement: Auth-related obstacles must be worked around rather than escalated — every integration that requires authentication must end up with a working authenticated path.
sourceQuote: you SHOULD always try to find a workaround for auth-related issues
acceptance: For each external system the launch touches (Google, Notion, Sunsama, Cloudflare, Vercel, Lovelace Lattice, Twilio), the launch record shows either a successful authenticated call/session captured, or an explicit list of at least three distinct workaround attempts with their failure output.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): docs/engineering/launch/external-systems.md (340 lines) now exists and is the artifact the acceptance asks for. Lovelace Lattice, which had zero repo hits at baseline, now has a full OAuth + gateway implementation exercised end to end against a local stub (apps/api/tests/lattice/lattice-flow.test.ts, 11 tests passing, local-lovelace-stub.ts). What is still missing is a captured authenticated session against the real service for Google, Notion, Sunsama, Cloudflare, Vercel, Lattice, or Twilio — every one of those is exercised against a fixture/mock adapter, not a live account.
notes: Also relevant to my own run: the `plugin:vercel:vercel` and `sunsama` MCP servers require OAuth and this session is non-interactive, so I could not drive them. That is a fact about this audit session, not a finding about the product.

requirement: The delivered system must minimize security holes introduced during the launch push.
sourceQuote: you should try to operate to minimize security holes and visually see stuff like API keys
acceptance: A secret scan (gitleaks or trufflehog) over the repo at the launch commit reports zero findings, and the auth-middleware test suite proves every production API route that returns user data rejects an unauthenticated request with 401/403.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): clause 2 now passes outright: apps/api/tests/security/route-auth.test.ts (`pnpm --filter @docket/api exec vitest run tests/security` → 2 files, 16 tests passing) derives the route list from the published OpenAPI document and asserts every documented route rejects an anonymous request except an explicit public allowlist, plus /mcp, the staff back-office, and the routes mounted outside the document. Clause 1 is met in substance but not in letter: `pnpm secret-scan` (scripts/secret-scan.ts, 2485 tracked files, 12 rules) reports `PASS — 0 findings` and a .gitleaks.toml (159 lines) is committed, but the repo-owned scanner — not gitleaks or trufflehog — is what actually runs.
notes: Runtime auth posture looks sound, but neither artifact the acceptance names (a passing secret scan, an auth-middleware coverage suite) exists. Both are net-new work.

requirement: API keys and other stored credentials must never be rendered in plaintext in the UI, logs, or API responses.
sourceQuote: minimize security holes and visually see stuff like API keys
acceptance: On every settings/integration surface that stores a credential, screenshots at 1440x900 in light and dark show the value masked (e.g. last-4 only); a network capture of the same page shows no full key in any response body, and server logs for the same session contain no key material.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/security/credential-masking.test.ts passes and asserts the substance directly: no org connector credential and no personal-Athena connection credential appears in any response body, no credential material is written to stdout/stderr while storing one, and no 2xx response schema in the published contract declares a credential-shaped property (with a negative control proving the check would catch one). Screenshot evidence is committed at docs/design/audits/screenshots/2026-08-02-credential-masking/ (9 PNGs incl. per-surface captures).
notes: Could not create a stored credential to photograph (POST /v1/me/athena/connections 409s on the live health check for a bogus URL), so 'masked, last-4 only' was never observed against a real stored value. No network capture or server-log check was performed.

requirement: Work must proceed autonomously to completion without interrupting the author for permission on actions this document already authorizes.
sourceQuote: I don't give a flying fucking shit how the fuck you do your work as long as the job gets done and you don't get in my way.
acceptance: The launch run reaches production sign-off with zero requests to the author for approval on tooling choice, auth workarounds, credentials, or production deploys. Every question actually asked is recorded in the launch record with three things: the requirement ID it blocked, the two or more product outcomes that were each defensible, and why neither could be selected from the plan text. The number of questions failing to record all three is zero.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): docs/engineering/launch/questions.md (102 lines) now exists in the required three-field form. It cannot be graded `pass` because the acceptance's first clause — 'reaches production sign-off' — is unmet: sign-off is withheld and production is stale (GEN-02).
notes: The requirement's evidence artifact (a per-question record with requirement ID + two defensible outcomes + why the plan text could not decide) has no home in the repo.

requirement: Subagents must be used for the work and must be granted the complete authorization needed to independently evaluate their own output.
sourceQuote: Be aggressive and relentless, using subagents that are given complete authorization needed to evaluate their work.
acceptance: Each work slice's record names the verification subagent that checked it and includes at least one verification artifact produced by that subagent rather than the implementer (screenshot, test output, or prod HTTP trace).
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): docs/engineering/launch/verification-log.md (196 lines) exists, verifier-produced artifacts are committed under docs/engineering/launch/evidence/{production,verification,integration}/, and the generated record reports `Claimed pass, awaiting independent verification: 0` — so every slice that did claim a pass names an independent verifier with an artifact on disk. It is `partial` because only 4 slices exist: the great majority of the build's work slices filed no record and therefore name no verification subagent at all.
notes: Not only is there no per-slice named verification agent, the verification artifacts cited by the existing audits have been deleted — so even the historical reviews cannot be independently re-checked.

requirement: No surface may ship in a knowingly degraded, unpolished, or 'good enough for now' state — the launch is held to a best-in-class product bar.
sourceQuote: We are trying to build the best fucking product ever here, after all.
acceptance: A committed surface inventory enumerates every user-facing route and overlay in the launch: every route under apps/web/src/app, the landing/marketing page, the OAuth consent page, the published-brief templates, and every dialog/drawer/panel reachable from them. Every entry in that inventory has a Craft Rubric scorecard under docs/design/audits/ whose hard gates all pass and whose lowest dimension score is at or above the ship bar. The number of inventory entries without a scorecard is zero, and the number of scorecards recording a known-degraded or 'ship anyway' state is zero.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the inventory half now exists: scripts/surface-inventory.ts generates docs/design/surface-inventory.md (101 surfaces — every page.tsx route plus every dialog/drawer/sheet) and packages/test-utils/tests/design-policies/surface-inventory.test.ts fails on drift. The scorecard half does not: the inventory itself records `41 of 101 surfaces have at least one scorecard; the remaining 60 have none`. Of the ten 2026-08-02 Craft Rubric scorecards, seven read `verdict: needs-work` (/inbox, /portfolio, /search, /settings, /sign-in, /today, calendar rounds 1-2) and only three read `ship` (calendar round 3, /oauth/authorize). Published-brief templates now exist (apps/web/src/app/(public)/briefs/[workspace]/[slug]/page.tsx) and are not yet scored. CAVEAT recorded at the gate: scripts/surface-inventory.ts, packages/test-utils/tests/design-policies/surface-inventory.test.ts and scorecard-schema.test.ts is present in the working tree but is NOT tracked by git (`git status` reports it untracked), so it does not exist for a CI checkout and cannot gate anything until it is committed.
notes: The Craft Rubric (docs/design/craft-rubric.md) and 10 genuinely rigorous scorecards exist, so the machinery is real — but there is no committed inventory, ~50+ routes and every dialog/drawer are unaudited, and I found live defects on surfaces that would be in it.

requirement: Every migration shipped must be non-destructive to the author's existing production data.
sourceQuote: as long as you always provide migrations that don't destroy my existing data
acceptance: The full migration chain runs to completion against a restored snapshot of the production database; afterward, per-table row counts for the willieechalmers@gmail.com account are greater than or equal to their pre-migration values, a spot-checked set of pre-existing entity IDs still resolve, and any destructive DDL (DROP TABLE/COLUMN, TRUNCATE, type narrowing, NOT NULL addition) in the diff is paired with a verified backfill in the same migration.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the two missing tests now exist and pass: `pnpm --filter @docket/db exec vitest run tests/migrations` → 7 files, 32 tests passing, including packages/db/tests/migrations/production-snapshot-restore.test.ts and destructive-ddl-policy.test.ts. That closes the destructive-DDL half of the acceptance mechanically. It is not `pass` because the restore runs against a synthesized snapshot built in-test, not a restored dump of the author's live production database, so no real pre/post row count for the willieechalmers@gmail.com account has ever been compared. CAVEAT recorded at the gate: packages/db/tests/migrations/production-snapshot-restore.test.ts and destructive-ddl-policy.test.ts is present in the working tree but is NOT tracked by git (`git status` reports it untracked), so it does not exist for a CI checkout and cannot gate anything until it is committed.
notes: Migrations run; the guarantee is unverified. The two mechanisms the requirement asks for — a restored-snapshot run with row-count assertions, and backfill pairing for destructive DDL — do not exist.

requirement: Post-deploy verification must be performed against the real production deployment signed in as the author's live account with his real data.
sourceQuote: I do have live production data for my [willieechalmers@gmail.com](mailto:willieechalmers@gmail.com) account on Docket
acceptance: Screenshots from the production hostname show the app signed in as willieechalmers@gmail.com with that account's real workspaces and work items rendered — not seeded or demo data — for Home, Portfolio, a project detail, and an Athena session.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): unchanged and re-checked: the only authenticated session in the tree is apps/web/.data/design-review/session.json, a local dev session for the synthetic 'launch-audit' account. Every 2026-08-02 screenshot under docs/design/audits/screenshots/ is from the local dev stack. No screenshot exists from a production hostname signed in as willieechalmers@gmail.com, and production is stale (GEN-02) so one could not be taken of the Athena surfaces even if the account were used.
notes: No production screenshots signed in as the author exist in the repo. I cannot produce them (passkey sign-in on production is a credential action I must not perform). The requirement is unmet today.

requirement: Docket must serve as the single source of truth for all of the author's organizations'/workspaces' work.
sourceQuote: serve as a single source of truth and content and context source for all of my organizations'/workspaces' work
acceptance: For every workspace configured at launch, all active work items are visible and editable in Docket, and for any record that also exists in an external tool, editing it in Docket and re-syncing leaves Docket's value in place (Docket wins on conflict) — demonstrated on at least one synced record per connected tool.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the conflict-resolution half is now correct and was the wrong way round at baseline. apps/api/src/routes/integration-reconcile.ts:126-134 now states and implements 'Docket is the source of truth on conflict… Docket's value wins regardless of which timestamp is newer, and the losing remote values are returned on the action as a TaskSyncConflict', explicitly replacing the previous last-write-wins tie-break. Write-back widened from one provider to two: packages/integrations/src/connector.ts:291 `WRITE_BACK_CAPABLE_PROVIDERS = new Set(['gtasks', 'notion'])`. Still not `pass`: the acceptance is per-workspace and per-connected-tool on live data, and no workspace in any reachable environment has a live connected integration to demonstrate it on.
notes: Two independent failures. (1) The acceptance requires 'Docket wins on conflict' demonstrated per connected tool; the reconciler implements LWW, so a newer external edit overwrites Docket. (2) 'Every workspace configured at launch' — the one non-personal workspace on this account (Las Vegans for Better Transit) has no connectors at all, so no synced record exists to demonstrate on.

requirement: Docket must work equally for non-software domains — marketing, strategic management, and media production — not just software engineering.
sourceQuote: whether it's for marketing or strategic management or media production or software engineering, etc.
acceptance: A workspace of each of the four kinds can be created and populated; screenshots of Home, Portfolio, and project/task detail for a media-production workspace contain no engineering-only vocabulary in required (non-optional) UI — no forced 'sprint', 'bug', 'PR', 'commit', 'story points', 'backlog grooming' labels.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): unchanged on the blocking clause and re-checked: packages/types/src/vocabulary.ts:11 still reads `VocabularyPreset = z.enum(['startup','nonprofit','agency'])` — three presets, none for marketing or media production, so 'a workspace of each of the four kinds' cannot be created as named. The no-engineering-vocabulary half continues to hold on inspection of apps/web/src.
notes: Good news: required UI carries no engineering-only vocabulary, and a per-org vocabulary skin system with singular/plural overrides exists. Gaps: the preset set covers startup/nonprofit/agency, not the four domains named (marketing, strategic management, media production, software engineering); the sidebar hardcodes 'Cycles' (a sprint analogue). I did NOT create four workspaces of each kind, so the screenshot clause is unverified.

requirement: Athena must not be strictly coupled to Docket — its core capabilities must function without a Docket instance behind them.
sourceQuote: strongly interconnected with Docket as a platform but is generally not strictly coupled to using Docket
acceptance: Athena's core packages reference Docket only through a named port/adapter interface; typechecking and the Athena test suite both pass with the Docket adapter replaced by a mock implementation, with no compile errors from missing Docket modules.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): a real enforcement mechanism now exists where none did: packages/test-utils/tests/workspace-policies/athena-boundary-policy.test.ts passes (4 tests) and asserts Docket schema, query helpers and server internals stay out of Athena core, that the Athena core manifest declares no Docket internal package, and — with a negative control — that it detects real boundary-crossing imports rather than prose mentioning them. It is `partial` rather than `pass` because the fourth test is a ratchet ('never lets the Docket-hosted agent loop spread its internal coupling to new modules'), i.e. the existing coupling in apps/api/src/agent/loop.ts is frozen, not removed, and the acceptance's 'typechecking and the Athena test suite both pass with the Docket adapter replaced by a mock' was not executed. CAVEAT recorded at the gate: packages/test-utils/tests/workspace-policies/athena-boundary-policy.test.ts is present in the working tree but is NOT tracked by git (`git status` reports it untracked), so it does not exist for a CI checkout and cannot gate anything until it is committed.
notes: There IS one clean port — `@docket/agent-runtime` (package.json deps: only @anthropic-ai/sdk, @docket/types, zod; `pnpm --filter @docket/agent-runtime typecheck` clean, `test` → 5 files / 41 tests passed). But that is the MODEL port (turn streaming), not a Docket port. Athena's reasoning loop, toolbox, transcript, approval policy and assignments all live inside apps/api and hard-bind Docket's DB schema, so there is no Docket adapter to replace with a mock.

requirement: Athena must be built on top of and inside Docket, but never route its own operation through Docket — no reaching into Docket internals and no Docket request path mediating Athena's agent/model calls.
sourceQuote: you must ensure that Athena is built on top of Docket and in Docket but not *through* Docket.
acceptance: No Athena module imports Docket's internal DB schema, query helpers, or server internals (enforced by a lint rule or dependency-graph check that fails CI on violation), and Athena's model/agent invocation path contains zero hops that require a Docket API request to succeed.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the 'no enforcement exists' finding is closed: the boundary policy test above is the dependency-graph check the acceptance asks for and it runs in the workspace test suite. The internal- import half is bounded rather than eliminated — the agent loop's coupling to @docket/db and to server internals is held at its current module set by the ratchet test rather than reduced to zero. CAVEAT recorded at the gate: packages/test-utils/tests/workspace-policies/athena-boundary-policy.test.ts is present in the working tree but is NOT tracked by git (`git status` reports it untracked), so it does not exist for a CI checkout and cannot gate anything until it is committed.
notes: The SECOND half of the requirement passes: apps/api/src/agent/toolbox.ts:16-18 wires the agent's tools through an in-process MCP client over `InMemoryTransport`, and the model call goes straight to the AgentTurnRuntime port — zero Docket HTTP hops in the model/agent invocation path. The failure is entirely the missing boundary + missing CI enforcement.

requirement: Athena must be demonstrably context-aware from data stored in Docket, retrieving real user entities at answer time.
sourceQuote: a chief of staff that is highly context aware and strongly enabled through the data that is stored in Docket
acceptance: In production, asking Athena 'what should I do today?' returns a response naming specific real tasks/projects/cycles belonging to the signed-in account, and the request trace shows those entities were fetched from Docket during that turn (retrieval call present in logs; entity IDs in the trace match rows in the database).
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): unchanged. .env.local has no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and APP_MODE=local, so the container resolves the mock turn runtime (packages/agent-runtime/src/model-backend.ts `resolveModelBackend` falls through to 'mock'). A live retrieval trace naming this account's real tasks cannot be produced locally, and production does not serve /me/athena/* at all (GEN-02).
notes: Cannot be established either way here: the local runtime is scripted, and no production instance was reachable from this environment. The retrieval plumbing does exist (apps/api/src/agent/toolbox.ts opens the MCP server with docket:// resources and list_work/find/get/brief tools), but 'demonstrably context-aware at answer time' needs a real model turn.

requirement: Docket must act architecturally as the hub for all productivity work — every integration passes through Docket rather than connecting external systems to each other.
sourceQuote: Docket MUST act architecturally as a hub for all productivity work.
acceptance: An architecture document names Docket as the hub and inventories every connector; for each connector, code inspection shows it reads/writes Docket's canonical entities, and there is zero code path where two external systems exchange work data without a Docket entity in between.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the connector registry remains single-sourced and every pull still lands in Docket entities; Notion was added to packages/types/src/provider-catalog.ts and to the write-back set, through the same spine. The doc clause is now met — docs/engineering/architecture.md and docs/engineering/specs/integration-sync.md describe the hub and the connector inventory. Held at `partial` because no code-inspection pass over every connector was re-run in this gate to prove the zero-external-to-external-path clause.
notes: The hub-shaped ARCHITECTURE holds — I found no code path where two external systems exchange work data directly; all five connectors read/write Docket's canonical task/project entities. What's missing is the required artifact: no architecture document names Docket as the hub for all productivity work ('Hub' in docs/engineering/architecture.md means the personal cross-org cockpit, a different concept), and no document inventories the connectors.

requirement: Embrace: Docket must be able to ingest and continuously synchronize context and work from the incumbent tools it connects to.
sourceQuote: Docket is going to follow the "embrace, extend, extinguish" playbook in its ability to provide and synchronize context.
acceptance: For each connected external tool, an initial import produces Docket entities matching the source records, and a subsequent change made in the source tool appears in Docket without a manual re-import — verified by editing one record per tool and observing the updated value in Docket.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): unchanged in kind. The capability grew (Notion two-way sync landed; packages/integrations/src/notion.ts + apps/api/src/routes/sync-notion.ts), but the acceptance requires editing a record in each source tool and observing it in Docket, and no environment reachable from this gate has a live connected integration.
notes: NOT a pass. The continuous-sync machinery is real and documented as shipped, but 'edit one record per tool and observe the updated value in Docket' cannot be performed in this environment because no source tool is connected. Requires a real connected account per provider to establish.

requirement: Extend: Docket must add capability on top of the imported data that the source tools do not provide, operating on imported records and not only Docket-native ones.
sourceQuote: Docket is going to follow the "embrace, extend, extinguish" playbook in its ability to provide and synchronize context.
acceptance: At least three Docket-only capabilities (e.g. cross-workspace portfolio view, cycles, Athena context/scheduling) are demonstrated operating on records that originated from an external import — screenshots show imported records participating in each capability with the same affordances as native records.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): unchanged: the three Docket-only capabilities exist and render, but there are still zero imported records to demonstrate them on.
notes: The capabilities are native-only today as far as anything observable here. Cannot show imported records participating with the same affordances because no import has occurred.

requirement: Extinguish: two-way sync must let Docket supersede the source tool, with Docket's state propagating outward so the incumbent can be abandoned without data loss.
sourceQuote: Docket is going to follow the "embrace, extend, extinguish" playbook in its ability to provide and synchronize context.
acceptance: An edit made in Docket to a synced record appears in the source tool within the sync interval, conflicting simultaneous edits resolve in Docket's favor, and disconnecting the source tool leaves every previously synced record fully intact and editable in Docket.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): materially improved: Docket-wins conflict resolution is now implemented rather than last-write-wins (see GEN-13), and Notion — the connector whose whole purpose is supersession — defaults write-back on. Still `partial`: 'an edit made in Docket appears in the source tool within the sync interval' and 'disconnecting leaves every synced record intact' were not exercised against a live provider account.
notes: Missing for launch: write-back for every provider other than Google Tasks; Linear gated behind an ungranted OAuth scope; conflict-resolution-in-Docket's-favor and disconnect-preserves-data were not verifiable at all.

requirement: The embrace-extend-extinguish approach is non-negotiable and must not be relitigated, downscoped, or argued against in any launch artifact.
sourceQuote: Do not question this.
acceptance: A reproducible check over an enumerated corpus (every plan doc, design doc, WORKLOG entry, ADR, PR body, and code comment produced for this launch) finds zero passages that propose replacing the embrace-extend-extinguish approach, recommend one-way-only sync, argue Docket should not be the source of truth on conflict, or defer two-way sync to post-launch. The corpus file list is committed with the check so the result is reproducible, and inserting a sentence such as 'we should make Notion sync read-only for launch' into any corpus file makes the check fail.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the reproducible check the acceptance asks for now exists and runs: `pnpm check:context-strategy` (scripts/context-strategy-check.ts) over the committed corpus file list docs/engineering/context-strategy-corpus.json → 'scanned 282 corpus files, 0 finding(s)'. tests/launch/context-strategy.test.ts covers the corpus resolution and the check's own failure modes, so inserting a passage that relitigates embrace-extend-extinguish into a corpus file makes it fail.
notes: The requirement asks for a reproducible guard over an enumerated corpus; neither the corpus nor the guard exists.

requirement: Produce candidate domain names for Docket and for Athena as an explicit deliverable.
sourceQuote: Please come up with some domains for Docket/Athena
acceptance: A committed document lists at least three candidate domains for Docket and at least three for Athena, records a checked availability result (registrar/WHOIS output) per candidate, and calls out a single recommended pick for each with rationale.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): docs/engineering/domains.md (277 lines) is the committed deliverable: a candidate table with a checked availability result per candidate backed by registrar/RDAP/WHOIS output (e.g. `docket.place` → 'Identity Digital RDAP → 404 Object not found'; `usedocket.com` → 'Registered 2023-06-13, Amazon Registrar'), covering well more than three candidates for each of Docket and Athena, with a recommended pick and rationale.
notes: Zero candidate domains proposed for either Docket or Athena; no availability checks recorded; no recommended pick.

requirement: The selected domains must actually be registered and wired to the production deployments, not merely proposed.
sourceQuote: Please come up with some domains for Docket/Athena
acceptance: `curl -I https://<selected-docket-domain>` returns 200 serving the production app with a valid TLS certificate whose SAN covers that host, and the same check passes for the API/Athena host; DNS records for both resolve from a public resolver.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): unchanged: no new domain is registered. The recommended picks in docs/engineering/domains.md are still only recommendations; production continues to serve from docket.hypertext.studio (`curl -I` → 200) and no candidate host resolves.
notes: There is no selected domain to register or wire, so nothing to check DNS/TLS against.

requirement: No user-facing Docket or Athena web URL may remain under hypertext.studio — the app, its API, and its in-app links must be isolated onto the new domain. The plan's one stated exception is the interim Athena inbound-mail host, which must be config-driven so the final domain replaces it without code changes.
sourceQuote: so that we can properly isolate the domains from hypertext.studio
acceptance: `curl -I https://docket.hypertext.studio` returns 301/308 to the new domain (or the host is retired), and a crawl of the production app's canonical link tags, sitemap, OG/meta URLs, and in-app absolute links yields zero hypertext.studio hostnames. The only permitted hypertext.studio reference anywhere in production configuration is the Athena inbound-mail host required by ACH-22, which appears solely as an environment/config value per ACH-23 and is listed in a committed cutover item naming the change required when the final domain lands.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the code half is now clean — d01ecd2f moved every product host behind the host-config contract (packages/env/src/hosts.ts), so the hardcoded hypertext.studio strings in apps/api/src/error.ts and apps/api/src/mcp/server.ts cited at baseline are gone. The requirement still fails on its own acceptance: `curl -I https://docket.hypertext.studio` returns HTTP/2 200 serving the production app, not a 301/308 to a new domain, and the host is not retired. The permitted exception is correctly config-shaped (`ATHENA_INBOUND_MAIL_HOST`, packages/env/src/slices.ts:336-353) and docs/engineering/domain-cutover.md (553 lines) is the committed cutover item.
notes: Every production hostname (web, API, admin) and the WebAuthn RP ID are still under hypertext.studio. No interim Athena inbound-mail host exists either — `grep -rin "athena.hypertext.studio|inbox.athena|inbound mail"` across docs/apps/packages/.github returns nothing.

requirement: Authentication state must be re-scoped to the new domain — cookies, OAuth redirect URIs, and WebAuthn RP ID — and the author's existing account must still be able to sign in after cutover.
sourceQuote: so that we can properly isolate the domains from hypertext.studio
acceptance: On the new domain, every cookie set by the app has Domain equal to the new apex and none is scoped to .hypertext.studio (verified in devtools Application tab); every OAuth/SSO provider lists only new-domain redirect URIs; and willieechalmers@gmail.com completes a full sign-in on the new domain, with a documented and exercised passkey re-registration path if the WebAuthn RP ID changed.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): unchanged: there is no new domain to re-scope cookies, OAuth redirect URIs or the WebAuthn RP ID to. docs/engineering/domain-cutover.md now documents the intended passkey re-registration path, but nothing has been exercised.
notes: Cookie Domain, OAuth redirect URIs and RP ID are all still bound to the old apex; the migration hasn't started.

requirement: Isolation must not break hypertext.studio itself — the studio site keeps working after the cutover.
sourceQuote: properly isolate the domains from hypertext.studio
acceptance: After cutover, https://hypertext.studio returns 200 serving the studio site, and a diff of its DNS zone shows no record required by the studio site was removed or repointed.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): re-probed this session: `curl -I https://hypertext.studio` → HTTP/2 522 (Cloudflare cannot reach the origin). The studio site does not return 200 today, independently of any cutover.
notes: No cutover has happened, so this failure is pre-existing rather than caused by isolation — but the acceptance condition (hypertext.studio returns 200) is not met right now, before any isolation work begins. That's a baseline problem worth fixing before anyone touches the zone.

requirement: Outbound transactional email and notifications must be sent from a Docket/Athena-owned mail domain — the new apex once obtained, the Athena subdomain in the interim — never from the bare hypertext.studio studio identity.
sourceQuote: properly isolate the domains from hypertext.studio
acceptance: A test notification sent from production has a From address on a Docket/Athena-owned mail domain (the new apex, or athena.hypertext.studio / inbox.athena.hypertext.studio while the final domain is pending), and its received headers show SPF, DKIM, and DMARC all passing for that domain. No production sender address is @hypertext.studio itself. The sender domain is read from configuration rather than hard-coded, and a committed cutover item names the change required when the final domain lands.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): unchanged in substance: the sender is config-driven (packages/mail/src/smtp.ts reads `env.MAIL_FROM`; packages/mail/src/transport.ts throws in production when RESEND_API_KEY/MAIL_FROM are absent) and docs/engineering/domain-cutover.md is the committed cutover item. Unverified: no production test notification was sent, so the actual From address and its SPF/DKIM/DMARC results are unobserved.
notes: Config-driven half: pass. Unverified: the live From address, and SPF/DKIM/DMARC — I did not send a production test notification (that would be sending mail on the user's behalf). No committed cutover item naming the domain change exists.

requirement: No surface in the app renders visual styling that reads as one-off/ad hoc; every audited screen's spacing, type, color, and radius traces to a named design-system primitive.
sourceQuote: Ensure that nothing in the app appears ad hoc.
acceptance: A scripted sweep of every top-level route under apps/web/src/app/(app) at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark enumerates the computed color, background-color, border-color, font-size, line-height, letter-spacing, padding, margin, gap, and border-radius of every rendered element, and flags any value not present in the Tailwind theme's token set. Flagging is mechanical, not editorial. The committed report lists each flagged element by route + selector + property + value; the report at the launch commit contains zero flagged elements, and none was resolved by adding a value to an ignore list or to the token set without a design-system change.
evidence: No scripted token-conformance sweep or committed report exists: docs/design/audits/ contains only hand-written per-surface rubric reviews (2026-06-10 through 2026-07-19), none enumerating computed color/spacing/radius/type per element per route. No script in scripts/ performs this sweep. Independently, live computed-style probes found off-token values — e.g. a dependency-graph project node computes `border: 1px solid lab(88.3672 -0.231206 -3.01799)` plus a 6-layer `box-shadow` including `rgba(0,0,0,0.1) 0px 1px 3px 0px`.
notes: The mechanical sweep the acceptance requires does not exist, and spot checks show it would produce a non-empty flag list today. Screenshots I captured: scratchpad/shots1, shots2, shots3, deps (all four viewport/theme combos for graph, projects, athena, cycles, cycle detail, stream, inbox, settings/athena).

requirement: Production web/admin source contains no hardcoded visual values (hex/rgb colors, arbitrary Tailwind values, inline style objects) for color, spacing, radius, or type.
sourceQuote: Everything must be connected to a design system somehow
acceptance: grep over apps/web/src and apps/admin/src production files (excluding tests, globals.css token definitions, and the Tailwind theme) returns zero matches for hex/rgb(a) color literals, bracketed arbitrary Tailwind values (e.g. text-[13px], p-[7px], w-[342px]), and style={{ ... }} props setting color/spacing/radius/font.
evidence: Hex literals in web production source: apps/web/src/components/stream/provider-badge.tsx:21-25 (`docket: '#7a5cff'`, `linear: '#5e6ad2'`, `github: '#1f2328'`, `google_calendar: '#9a948c'`, `gmail: '#9a948c'`) and :37 fallback `'#9a948c'`; apps/web/src/components/initiatives/initiative-icon-picker.tsx:330 `value={display.customColor ?? '#3b82f6'}`. Arbitrary Tailwind values: 137 matches in apps/web/src excluding tests — e.g. apps/web/src/app/(app)/today/page.tsx:51 `text-[3rem] leading-[1.1] tracking-[-0.01em]`, calendar-toolbar.tsx:128-129 `text-[11px]`, projects-client.tsx:311 `text-[11px]`, cycles/[cycleId]/page.tsx:300,316 `-[16rem]`, project-graph-panel.tsx:236 `h-[560px]`. Inline style props: 78 `style={{` occurrences in apps/web/src excluding tests.
notes: apps/admin/src and packages/ui/src are clean (0 hex, 0 arbitrary values, 0 inline style objects) — the violation is entirely in apps/web/src.

requirement: Design-system conformance is structurally enforced by shared layout or wrapper components rather than repeated per-screen markup.
sourceQuote: enforced by layout or wrapper components
acceptance: Every page.tsx under apps/web/src/app/(app) renders its content through a shared page/layout wrapper component; zero page.tsx files declare their own top-level padding, max-width, gap, header bar, or scroll container directly.
evidence: `grep -rln "PageContainer" apps/web/src` returns 3 files (page-layout.tsx itself, entity-detail-layout.tsx, and orgs/[orgId]/programs/[programId]/page.tsx) against 58 page.tsx files under apps/web/src/app/(app). Pages declare their own top-level layout directly: today/page.tsx `mx-auto flex h-full w-full max-w-4xl flex-col gap-10 px-6 py-10 @2xl:px-10 @2xl:py-14`; orgs/[orgId]/cycles/[cycleId]/page.tsx `mx-auto flex w-full max-w-6xl flex-col gap-6 p-4 @2xl:p-6 @4xl:p-8`; workspaces/new/page.tsx `max-w-2xl ... px-6 py-12`; exports/[exportId]/page.tsx `max-w-3xl`; triage, views, sessions/[sessionId], tasks/[taskId] all repeat the max-w-6xl padding string inline.
notes: The shared wrapper exists (apps/web/src/components/views/page-layout.tsx exports PageContainer/PageHeader/PageTitle and its own TSDoc says it was created precisely because 'every index page hand-rolled its own <main> wrapper') but adoption is 3/58, and the max-widths still diverge across 4xl/3xl/2xl/6xl.

requirement: All design tokens consumed by the UI are the standard tokens defined in the customized Tailwind configuration, with no parallel or duplicate scales.
sourceQuote: relying on standard design tokens that are provided by our customized Tailwind
acceptance: Exactly one source of truth defines the color/space/radius/type scales (the Tailwind theme plus its CSS custom properties); no second scale (legacy token file, per-component constant map, or duplicated CSS variable set) is imported by production components, and any legacy token names are removed from source rather than aliased.
evidence: A per-component constant color map — explicitly named as a disqualifier in the acceptance — exists in production: apps/web/src/components/stream/provider-badge.tsx:20-25 `const SYSTEM_COLORS = { docket: '#7a5cff', linear: '#5e6ad2', ... }`. A second CSS variable scale exists and is imported by production marketing routes: apps/web/src/app/(marketing)/marketing.css defines 43 custom properties including its own `--mk-paper/--mk-ink/--mk-accent/--mk-line/--mk-shadow-plate` ramp and then rebinds the shared names (`--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--border`, `--input`, `--ring`) plus its own `--radius: 0.25rem`, re-exported through apps/web/src/app/globals.css:14-20 as `--color-paper/--color-ink/--color-sienna/--shadow-plate`.
notes: packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css (238 custom properties, `@theme inline` at :223) is the intended single source. The `--color-* → --*` aliasing there is the sanctioned shadcn v4 pattern, not a duplicate scale; the marketing ramp and the hex constant map are.

requirement: Templated or slottable layout components exist that automatically apply layout and structure to the components placed inside them.
sourceQuote: create templated or slottable layout components that automatically apply layout and structure for lower-order components
acceptance: A documented set of slot-based layout primitives (e.g. page shell, toolbar row with leading/trailing slots, property list, list row, section) exists and is used by every app route; lower-order components rendered into those slots declare no padding, gap, or alignment of their own — the parent supplies it.
evidence: Slot primitives DO exist: apps/web/src/components/views/page-layout.tsx (PageContainer/PageHeader/PageTitle, documented as slot components), packages/ui/src/primitives/layout.tsx (Stack/Row with a closed `GAP` scale via cva), and packages/ui/src/components/shell/ (AppShell, ShellAside, TabBar, Sidebar). Missing: they are not 'used by every app route' — PageContainer appears in 3 files of 58 (app) pages; and lower-order children still declare their own spacing, e.g. settings pages each carry `className="flex flex-col gap-6"` at their own root (13 separate settings page.tsx files) rather than inheriting it from a section slot.
notes: The primitive set is real and well-documented; the structural enforcement the requirement asks for is not in place. This is the gap CRAFT-03 measures from the other direction.

requirement: Design-system standards are enforced automatically and block the build, not documented as advice.
sourceQuote: aggressively enforce standards
acceptance: A lint rule or source-policy test asserting CRAFT-02 and CRAFT-09 runs in CI; deliberately introducing a hardcoded hex color or a raw font-size utility into a production component makes `pnpm lint`/`pnpm test` exit non-zero.
evidence: I injected the exact violations the acceptance names into a production component (apps/web/src/components/stream/provider-badge.tsx: `const CRAFT_PROBE_COLOR = '#ff00ff'; const CRAFT_PROBE_CLASS = 'text-[13px] p-[7px]';`) and ran the gates. `pnpm exec eslint src/components/stream/provider-badge.tsx` exited 0 with no output. `pnpm exec vitest run tests/workspace-policies` in packages/test-utils reported `Test Files 3 passed (3) / Tests 11 passed (11)`. Both green with the violation present. File restored from backup afterward (grep for CRAFT_PROBE now returns 0).
notes: The only source-policy test in the repo is packages/test-utils/tests/workspace-policies/web-error-source-policy.test.ts, which enforces error-copy ownership (legacy-string-reader / provider-diagnostic / raw-error-message rules) — nothing about visual tokens. No lint rule covers CRAFT-02 or CRAFT-09.

requirement: Borders are minimized: no element uses a border purely to group or separate content when spacing, alignment, or a tinted surface can do the job.
sourceQuote: stuff like borders should be minimized as I don't really like them for everything
acceptance: A per-surface border inventory (before/after screenshots at 1440x900, light and dark) shows total border-rendering elements reduced against the recorded baseline, and every border that remains is listed with a justification limited to input affordance, focus indication, or a genuine semantic boundary; zero decorative/grouping borders remain.
evidence: No recorded baseline or justification inventory exists anywhere in the repo, so the 'reduced against baseline' clause is unmeasurable. Measured live baseline (scratchpad/craft/craft.json, 14 routes at 1440x900): visible bordered elements per route = /settings/connections 8, /settings/profile 10, settings/members 12, /tasks-ish 35, /today 35, /inbox 36, programs 36, my-work 37, teams 38, initiatives 39, cycles 46, projects 57, /portfolio 69. Purely-grouping borders confirmed in source: packages/ui/src/components/views/entity-table-row.tsx:14 (`border-b` on every table row), apps/web/src/components/timeline/timeline-canvas.tsx:329 (card `border`), :333 (header `border-b`), :357 (label-column `border-r`), :521 (tray `border-t`); initiatives uses 25 `border-outline-variant/50` row separators plus legacy `border-input` inputs.
notes: Screenshots reviewed: scratchpad/craft/*.png, scratchpad/tl2/timeline-1440x900-{light,dark}.png. Decorative/grouping borders are pervasive; nothing has been reduced yet.

requirement: Shadows are minimized: box-shadow is used only by true elevated-overlay surfaces.
sourceQuote: Stuff like shadows should also be minimized as they have a tendency to look really dumb.
acceptance: grep of production web/admin source shows shadow utilities/box-shadow only inside the enumerated overlay primitives (menu, dialog, popover/tooltip, drag preview, toast/snackbar); every other component renders zero box-shadow in every state.
evidence: grep for shadow utilities over apps/web/src, apps/admin/src, packages/ui/src. Legitimate overlay primitives use them (popover.tsx:78, tooltip.tsx:75, menu-styles.ts:53, dialog.tsx:175, command-palette.tsx:177). But ~17 non-overlay components also render shadows: settings/disconnect-confirm-dialog.tsx:46 (button), settings/contact-points-section.tsx:88 (input), today/next-up.tsx:97 (list row hover:shadow-sm), today/today-prompt.tsx:144 (composer shadow-sm + focus-within:shadow-md), scheduling/scheduling-item-card.tsx:166-169 (shadow-sm/md/lg), agents/trust-dial.tsx:75, initiatives/roadmap.tsx:238, task-detail/CommentActivityFeed.tsx:277 (textarea), canvas/project-node.tsx:84, command-palette/command-palette-trigger.tsx:34, agenda/agenda-entry-card.tsx:158, timeline/timeline-bar.tsx:204, timeline/cascade-proposal.tsx:62, entity-detail/updates-panel.tsx:154, onboarding/selectable-card.tsx:59-60, marketing/product-frame.tsx:35, scheduling/scheduling-region-preview.tsx:99.
notes: Runtime confirmation: 4-8 shadowed elements painted per route (scratchpad/craft/craft.json shadowCount).

requirement: No ad hoc or custom typography is used anywhere; every text node's size, weight, line-height, and tracking come from a named MD3 type-scale token.
sourceQuote: Do not use ad hoc or custom typography.
acceptance: A source-policy test over production web/admin components fails on any raw font-size/line-height/letter-spacing/font-weight declaration or arbitrary type utility outside the MD3 token classes (display/headline/title/body/label × large/medium/small); the test currently passes with zero exceptions in the allowlist.
evidence: `ls packages/test-utils/tests/workspace-policies/` → dependency-catalog.test.ts, google-oauth-bootstrap.test.ts, web-error-source-policy.test.ts. No typography policy test exists anywhere (`find . -name '*typography*'` → nothing). Counter-scan: `grep -rEo 'text-\[..\]|text-(xs|sm|...)|leading-\[..\]|tracking-\[..\]' apps/web/src apps/admin/src` → 819 occurrences.
notes: text-xs/text-sm are Tailwind defaults, not MD3 aliases — grep of packages/ui/src/styles/globals.css shows only --text-display-*/--text-headline-*/--text-title-*/--text-body-*/--text-label-* are defined as MD3 tokens.

requirement: Every existing occurrence of ad hoc typography that does not line up with MD3 tokens is found and refactored, not just prohibited going forward.
sourceQuote: Please find all uses of ad hoc typography that don't line up with MD3 tokens and aggressively refactor to ensure that everything is aligned.
acceptance: A committed inventory enumerates every pre-existing ad hoc typography occurrence with the MD3 token it was migrated to; re-running the inventory scan against HEAD returns zero remaining occurrences, and no occurrence was resolved by adding it to an ignore list.
evidence: No inventory doc (`grep -ril 'ad hoc typography|typography inventory|type-scale' docs/` → zero hits). Scan against HEAD in apps/web/src: 415 `text-xs`, 240 `text-sm`, 28 `text-base`, 19 `text-[10px]`, 16 `text-[11px]`, 16 `text-2xl`, 12 `text-lg`, 6 `text-xl`, 4 `text-3xl`, 3 `text-[9px]`, 3 `text-4xl`, 2 `tracking-[-0.015em]`, 1 each of `tracking-[-0.01em]`, `leading-[1.1]`, `text-[3rem]`, `text-[0.7rem]`, `text-[0.65rem]`, `text-[0.625rem]`.
notes: Nothing has been migrated; the audit scorecard for 2026-07-19 even cites `text-xs` approvingly as part of "the shared MD3 scale", which it is not.

requirement: Pill/chip structures render from one shared component so they are visually consistent, specifically in the new-object (task, initiative) dialogs the author called out.
sourceQuote: The way they're implemented in stuff like the new object (task, initiative) dialogs looks extremely inconsistent.
acceptance: In the new-task and new-initiative dialogs at 1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark, every pill has identical measured height, corner radius, horizontal padding, icon size, icon-to-label gap, and label type token; measured pixel heights of all pills in a given dialog are equal with 0px variance.
evidence: Measured live via Playwright getBoundingClientRect/getComputedStyle in both dialogs (script + raw data: scratchpad/audit.ts, scratchpad/out/results.json). NEW-INITIATIVE dialog — 9 pills, 3 distinct heights [28, 32, 36]px, 2 distinct paddings ['12px/12px','8px/8px'], icon sizes 24x24 or absent. NEW-TASK dialog — 7 pills, 3 distinct heights [20, 28, 36]px, paddings ['0px/0px','8px/8px'], icon sizes 16x16 vs 24x24 vs absent. Requirement demands 0px height variance; actual variance is 8px (initiative) and 16px (task). Screenshots looked at: scratchpad/out/new-initiative-dialog-1440-light.png shows three visually distinct pill families on adjacent rows (template pills 'Blank'/'Strategic initiative'/'Objective' are taller and bolder; property pills '+ Set owner'/'+ Set target'/'+ Set health' carry 24px plus-icons; value pills 'Active'/'No priority'/'Monthly updates' are shortest and icon-less). scratchpad/out/new-task-dialog-1440-light.png shows the same split ('Backlog' 16px icon vs '+ Set project' 24px icon vs bare 'No priority').
notes: This is precisely the inconsistency the author called out. Only 1440x900 light was measured; the geometry defect is resolution-independent (token-level), so the other three shot variants were not needed to establish failure.

requirement: Deep research into how MD3 specifies chip/pill structures is performed and written down as a referenceable document.
sourceQuote: Please, please, please do some deep research to figure out how MD3 would handle something like this and how to avoid pills with no icons.
acceptance: A document exists under docs/ (design or research) that cites specific m3.material.io chip spec sections (assist/filter/input/suggestion chips, sizes, states, icon rules) and maps each Docket pill usage to a named MD3 component plus its token set; every pill variant shipped in the app is traceable to a cited spec section in that document.
evidence: `grep -rn "m3.material.io" docs/` returns ZERO hits repo-wide. `grep -rn -i "assist chip|filter chip|input chip|suggestion chip" docs/` returns only product-feature prose about Initiatives acting as timeline filter chips (docs/core/mvp-plan.md:246,261,265; docs/engineering/specs/design-system.md:543; docs/engineering/specs/api-rpc-contract.md:381) — not MD3 spec citations. docs/ contains no research/ directory; docs/design/ holds only audits/, craft-rubric.md, ghost-grammar.md. design-system.md mentions chips only as component names in an inventory (lines 302, 439, 520) with no spec section references, no size/state tables, and no mapping of Docket pill usage to a named MD3 component + token set.
notes: No referenceable MD3 chip document exists, so nothing traces pill variants to a cited spec section.

requirement: Pills without icons are eliminated — a pill displaying only a bare text label must not ship.
sourceQuote: how to avoid pills with no icons
acceptance: A screenshot sweep of create dialogs, property rows, filter bars, and list rows at 1440x900 and 390x844 shows every rendered pill carrying a leading icon (or an avatar/status glyph), with any exception explicitly listed and justified against the MD3 document from CRAFT-12; the count of unjustified icon-less pills is zero.
evidence: Measured + looked at. NEW-INITIATIVE dialog has 6 icon-less pills: 'Blank', 'Strategic initiative', 'Objective', 'Active', 'No priority', 'Monthly updates' (scratchpad/out/results.json → initiativeDialog.pills, hasIcon:false; visible in scratchpad/out/new-initiative-dialog-1440-light.png). NEW-TASK dialog has 1 bare-text pill: 'No priority' ('LE' is an avatar glyph, which the acceptance permits) — scratchpad/out/new-task-dialog-1440-light.png. INITIATIVE DETAIL property row has 3 icon-less pills: 'Active', 'No priority', 'Monthly' — I cropped and zoomed the row to confirm (source apps/web/.data/design-review/launch-audit/base/orgs-orgId-initiatives-01KZ0S4B2C0FJ2SJKNHKXB08V8-1440x900-light.png, zoom /tmp/pills_zoom.png): 'Active', 'No priority' and 'Monthly' render as plain text in a rounded container while their row-mates '+ No health', '+ Set target date', '+ Set owner', '+ Add labels' carry plus-icons and 'No verdict yet' carries a dot. Count of unjustified icon-less pills is 10 across three surfaces, not zero.
notes: There is also no CRAFT-12 document against which an exception could be justified, so none of these are exempt.

requirement: Icon usage is deliberate and improves readability: icons are semantically apt for the concept they represent and rendered at consistent optical sizes.
sourceQuote: be a little more deliberate and craftful in icon usage to improve user readability when possible
acceptance: A committed icon inventory maps every concept (object type, status, priority, action) to exactly one icon at a token-defined size; screenshot review confirms no two distinct concepts share an icon, no concept renders two different icons across surfaces, and no icon appears at a size outside the token set.
evidence: No icon inventory exists: `find docs -iname '*icon*'` returned only a screenshot file. Confirmed collisions visually in /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/sidebar.png (2x crop of the live sidebar): 'Today' and 'My Work' render the IDENTICAL filled-house glyph; 'Inbox' and 'Triage' render the IDENTICAL tray glyph. Code collisions in apps/web/src/components/command-palette/use-hub-search.ts:37-56 — `agent: Sparkles` and `agent_session: Sparkles`; `cycle: Calendar` and `calendar_event: Calendar`; `update: Activity` and `activity: Activity`.
notes: Five distinct concept-pairs share an icon (two of them confirmed by looking at the rendered sidebar). The committed inventory mapping every concept to exactly one icon at a token-defined size does not exist.

requirement: Layout assumes flexible use of space rather than defaulting everything to left alignment.
sourceQuote: For use of space, please assume flexibility throughout. Stuff should not just be left aligned by default.
acceptance: At 1440x900 and 1920x1080, no header/toolbar/row on any app route has every control bunched at the leading edge with the remaining horizontal space left empty; each such row uses explicit leading and trailing alignment groups, verified by measured x-positions of first and last control against the container edges.
evidence: Measured child bounding boxes of top-band flex rows at 1440x900 and 1920x1080 (script output). Rows bunched at the leading edge with dead trailing space: /portfolio title row trailingGap 536px (rowRight 980, lastChildRight 444); /orgs/:orgId/cycles filter row trailingGap 457px (firstChildLeft 281, lastChildRight 523); /orgs/:orgId/projects toolbar trailingGap 134px; /orgs/:orgId/my-work tab row trailingGap 342px; /inbox tab row trailingGap 76px. Screenshot: .../audit-2026-08-02/craft/orgs-01KZ0R2DY0MNFG8BX4P297NQ9J-projects-1440.png shows List|Dependencies|Timeline|Add filter|Display all packed left.
notes: Page-title rows are fine (justify: space-between, trailingGap 0 on /tasks, /inbox, /my-work, /projects, /initiatives, /programs). The failure is the secondary toolbar/tab rows.

requirement: Whitespace is balanced using visual elements wherever possible rather than left as dead space.
sourceQuote: Use visuals whenever possible to properly balance whitespace.
acceptance: For each primary surface at 1440x900 and 1920x1080, an automated scan identifies every contiguous empty rectangle wider than 30% of the viewport that shares a horizontal band with rendered content. Each must be eliminated by a visual element, by redistributed leading/trailing alignment, or by a container max-width that is a named design-token value applied through a shared layout primitive — a per-surface inline or one-off max-width does not count as a resolution. The final report lists zero regions resolved by ad hoc means and zero unresolved regions.
evidence: No automated empty-region scan or report exists (no such script under scripts/, no report under docs/). Observed dead regions: /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/landing/1440x900-light/frame-003-477ms.png shows /today at 1440x900 with all content inside a 760px main and the entire lower ~35% of the panel empty below 'Next up'; /portfolio header row leaves 536px of empty trailing space (measured). No shared max-width layout primitive is applied — packages/ui/src/primitives/layout.tsx exposes only Stack/Row with gap/align/justify, no width token.
notes: The acceptance requires a scan whose final report lists zero unresolved regions and zero ad-hoc resolutions. Neither the scan nor the report exists, and unresolved regions are directly observable.

requirement: Filter and display controls are pushed toward the trailing end of their row while the primary view controls sit at the leading edge.
sourceQuote: stuff like filters and display should be pushed toward the end of the row while the main views should be on the left
acceptance: On every list/table/board view header (tasks, projects, initiatives, programs, cycles, triage, my-work, portfolio), measured positions show view switcher/tabs flush to the container's leading padding edge and Filter/Display controls flush to the trailing padding edge, at 1440x900 and at 390x844 (where the trailing group may collapse into a single trailing control, never into the leading group).
evidence: Screenshot /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/craft/orgs-01KZ0R2DY0MNFG8BX4P297NQ9J-projects-1440.png: the view switcher (List/Dependencies/Timeline) AND 'Add filter'/'Display' are all in one row flush to the LEADING edge (justify: normal, firstChildLeft 281, lastChildRight 846, container right 980 → 134px empty trailing). /orgs/:orgId/cycles is worse: 'Add filter Display' at firstChildLeft 281 with lastChildRight 523 and 457px empty to the right. /inbox tab row: 76px trailing gap, no trailing control group at all.
notes: Counter-example: /portfolio puts 'Display' on its own row with justify: flex-end (trailingGap 0) — correct trailing alignment, but split across two rows rather than one row with leading+trailing groups. The rebuilt /calendar toolbar (Today/prev/next leading; Calendars/Display/New trailing) is the one surface that does this right.

requirement: Icons associated with objects are rendered inline wherever objects appear as supplemental information or as selection options.
sourceQuote: Icons that are associated with objects should be displayed inline for stuff like supplemental information or selection options whenever possible.
acceptance: Every menu item, select/combobox option, autocomplete result, breadcrumb, chip, and inline object reference for a first-class object (task, project, initiative, program, cycle, workspace, team, person) renders that object's icon inline before its label; screenshots of each picker and property row show zero label-only object references.
evidence: Positive, from code + rendering: apps/web/src/components/task-detail/StatusPicker.tsx:78-87 renders `<StatusIcon type={state.type} />` before each menu item label; the task-detail screenshot apps/web/.data/design-review/audit-taskdetail/orgs-orgId-tasks-01KZ0S5VFWFNHTNEW95DTD2K94-1440x900-light.png shows the status chip, priority chip and the open tab all carrying inline glyphs. Negative, same screenshot: the 'Assign' and 'Set due date' property rows render a generic `+` glyph, not a person/date object icon.
notes: Could not complete the acceptance's picker sweep — my automated picker-opening probe timed out because the shared dev web server returned 500 mid-audit (a concurrent agent deleted apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/calendar-scheduling-sidebar.tsx while it was still imported; `./scripts/dev-stack.sh status` → web=500). Status/priority pickers verified icon-bearing; assignee, project, initiative, program, cycle, workspace and team pickers, plus breadcrumbs and chips, remain unverified.

requirement: Object-to-icon mapping has a single source of truth used by every consumer.
sourceQuote: Remember: single sources of truth are expected.
acceptance: Exactly one module exports the object-type/status-to-icon mapping; grep shows no production component importing an icon directly from @mui/icons-material to represent a first-class object type or status, and deleting an entry from the mapping breaks compilation in every consumer rather than silently diverging.
evidence: No single-source object-type→icon module exists. packages/ui/src/icons/index.ts:1-18 is a glyph re-export BARREL ('Re-exports the handful of @mui/icons-material icons the app shell and ListView family need, under stable, glyph-descriptive names') — it maps glyph-name→MUI import, not object-type→icon. The only semantic map is a local const: apps/web/src/components/command-palette/use-hub-search.ts:37 `export const SEARCH_KIND_ICON: Record<SearchDocumentKind, LucideIcon>`, scoped to search hits. The sidebar picks its own icons independently (packages/ui/src/components/shell/Sidebar.tsx imports ~20 glyphs directly at lines 30-49).
notes: Status IS single-sourced well (packages/ui/src/components/atoms/StatusIcon.tsx maps the five WorkflowStateTypes to one glyph set at one token size). Object type is not: deleting an entry from SEARCH_KIND_ICON would break only the command palette, and the sidebar/task-detail would silently diverge — exactly the failure mode the requirement names.

requirement: UI must not wrap or reflow as a substitute for deliberate layout organization — rows, toolbars, and control labels stay on one line, with overflow handled by an explicit strategy.
sourceQuote: In general, do not wrap things. You should be extremely careful about allowing any UI to just wrap or reflow because you're too lazy to properly organize stuff.
acceptance: At 1920x1080, 1440x900, 1280x800, 768x1024, and 390x844, no toolbar, header, list row, property row, table header row, or control label renders on more than one line box on any app route — measured as element clientHeight equal to its single-line height. Every overflow occurrence is recorded with which of three permitted strategies resolved it: truncation with tooltip, an overflow menu, or a documented breakpoint layout change. Wrapping is permitted only in prose body copy (descriptions, empty-state text, editor content). A blanket assertion that no flex container has flex-wrap other than nowrap is explicitly NOT the test, because deliberate breakpoint reflow is allowed.
evidence: Captured 96 route×viewport×theme combos (8 routes × 1920/1440/1280/1024/768/390 × light/dark) into /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/resp/. Looked at renderings: resp/orgs-orgId-projects-390x844-light.png shows a deliberate mobile strategy — toolbar labels collapse to icons and the Status/Health/Target columns drop, rows stay one line. resp/calendar-1920x1080-light.png shows the calendar toolbar on TWO rows even at 1920 (Today/</>/date-range, then Dates|People / Overview|Standard|Detail / Zoom / Open Athena / New); resp/calendar-768x1024-light.png shows it reflowed to THREE rows. Separately, the acceptance's required artifact does not exist: no file in the repo records overflow occurrences against the three permitted strategies (truncation+tooltip / overflow menu / documented breakpoint).
notes: Cannot cleanly separate deliberate breakpoint reflow from lazy wrap on the calendar toolbar without the missing strategy record — which is exactly the artifact the acceptance demands. My automated single-line probe produced too many false positives (it flags any button whose box height exceeds line-height) to serve as the measurement the acceptance describes; a real per-element single-line assertion still needs to be written.

requirement: Elements are not placed inline with each other merely because it is convenient; every inline grouping is a deliberate semantic group.
sourceQuote: Do not just put stuff inline because it's convenient.
acceptance: A source-policy test asserts that every element in production route source rendering display:flex or display:grid with more than one child is either one of the named layout primitives from CRAFT-05 or a direct child of one; it fails listing file + line for any other case. Each named primitive's props declare the group's role (leading toolbar group, trailing toolbar group, property pair, metadata cluster, action row). The test passes with zero exemptions, and adding a bare `<div className="flex ...">` wrapping two controls into any route makes it fail.
evidence: No such source-policy test exists. `ls packages/test-utils/tests/` → dependency-catalog.test.ts, doc-coverage.internals.test.ts, doc-coverage.test.ts, google-oauth-bootstrap.test.ts, web-error-source-policy.test.ts, workspace.ts — none inspects flex/grid containers. Layout primitives DO exist at packages/ui/src/primitives/layout.tsx (Stack/Row) but their props are only `gap`/`align`/`justify` — no role prop naming leading-toolbar-group / trailing-toolbar-group / property-pair / metadata-cluster / action-row. `grep -rEn '<div className="[^"]*\b(flex|grid)\b' apps/web/src/app` → 138 bare flex/grid divs in route source.
notes: Adding a bare `<div className="flex ...">` today makes nothing fail, because nothing checks.

requirement: The app is properly responsive at all screen sizes, verified by actual visual inspection rather than assumption.
sourceQuote: Please inspect visually for vibes because this app needs to be properly responsive for all screen sizes.
acceptance: Screenshots are captured for every top-level app route at 390x844, 768x1024, 1024x768, 1440x900, and 1920x1080 in both light and dark; none shows horizontal page scroll (document.scrollWidth <= clientWidth), clipped or cut-off content, overlapping elements, or content hidden behind a fixed chrome element.
evidence: Ran /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/responsive-audit.ts over 8 routes (/today /tasks /portfolio /inbox /calendar /orgs/:orgId/projects /orgs/:orgId/initiatives /orgs/:orgId/cycles) × 6 viewports × 2 themes = 96 combos. findings.json: 'H-OVERFLOW combos: 0' — document.scrollWidth never exceeded clientWidth anywhere. Visually inspected: resp/today-390x844-light.png, resp/calendar-768x1024-light.png, resp/calendar-1920x1080-light.png, resp/orgs-orgId-projects-390x844-light.png. VIOLATION FOUND: in resp/today-390x844-light.png the floating 'Athena / 3 needs you' dock sits on top of a proposal card and obscures its 'Review in se[ssion]' text — content hidden behind fixed chrome.
notes: The horizontal-scroll criterion genuinely passes across everything measured. Two gaps keep this off 'pass': (1) only 8 of ~25 top-level app routes were covered; (2) the floating Athena dock overlaps list content at 390px on at least /today and /orgs/:orgId/projects.

requirement: Scaling is never used to indicate interactivity on any element.
sourceQuote: Do not use scaling to indicate interactivity.
acceptance: grep of production web/admin source returns zero hover/active/focus scale transforms (scale-*, hover:scale-*, active:scale-*, group-hover:scale-*, transform: scale(...) in transitions, whileHover/whileTap scale props) on interactive elements; any remaining scale usage is on non-interactive decorative animation only and is enumerated.
evidence: Four scale-on-interaction sites in production web source: apps/web/src/components/today/next-up.tsx:97 (`active:scale-[0.99]` on a clickable card, with `transition-[...,transform]`); apps/web/src/components/agenda/agenda-entry-card.tsx:169 (`hover:scale-110 … active:scale-90` on a complete-toggle button); apps/web/src/components/agenda/agenda-view-switcher.tsx:58 (`transition-transform … active:scale-90` on a Button); apps/web/src/components/onboarding/selectable-card.tsx:69-70 (`scale-100` selected / `scale-90 group-hover:opacity-40` unselected on the selection indicator inside an interactive card).
notes: Full paths under /Users/williecubed/Projects/TheHypertextStudio/athena-web/.claude/worktrees/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9/. The one non-interactive case is agenda-entry-card.tsx:96 (a WAAPI keyframe pulse `scale(1)→scale(1.4)→scale(1)`), which is decorative celebration animation — that one is arguably permitted but is not currently enumerated anywhere.

requirement: Clicking a button or any interactive element never changes that element's rendered size.
sourceQuote: Clicking a button or some kind of interactive element MUST never change its size.
acceptance: An automated test measures getBoundingClientRect() for every interactive primitive (button, icon button, chip, list row, tab, menu item, input) at rest, on hover, on focus, and while pressed; width and height are identical across all four states with 0px tolerance for every element tested.
evidence: No such test exists: `grep -rln "getBoundingClientRect|boundingBox()" apps/web/e2e apps/admin` matches only fluid-scheduling/calendar/athena-personal specs (drag-geometry tests), and `grep -rn "does not change size|no size change|hover.*size" apps/web/e2e apps/web/tests packages/ui/tests` returns zero hits. Separately the requirement is actively violated: `active:scale-90` (agenda-view-switcher.tsx:58, agenda-entry-card.tsx:169) and `active:scale-[0.99]` (next-up.tsx:97) change getBoundingClientRect on press, since getBoundingClientRect reflects CSS transforms.
notes: Both halves fail — there is no measurement test, and the pressed state demonstrably changes rendered size on at least three primitives.

requirement: Input fields are standardized into one primitive with a single documented, closed set of variants — the current mix of bordered, flat, and shadowed inputs is eliminated.
sourceQuote: Standardize input fields. There are several variants: some with borders, some that are flat, some that are shadowed.
acceptance: Every text input, textarea, select, combobox, search field, and inline editor in the app renders from one input primitive whose variants are enumerated in the design-system docs; screenshots of every form and dialog at 1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark, show identical height, corner radius, horizontal/vertical padding, placeholder type token, and focus treatment for all inputs of the same variant, and no input exists outside the documented variant set.
evidence: There is one Input primitive (packages/ui/src/primitives/input.tsx) but it exposes NO variant API — `export type InputProps = React.ComponentProps<'input'>` (line 14), a single hardcoded class string (line 22), no `variant` prop, and no enumerated variant set in docs/engineering/specs/design-system.md. Fields bypass it wholesale in apps/web/src (excluding tests): 36 raw `<input` (e.g. sign-in/page.tsx:284, calendar-toolbar.tsx:160, initiatives-client.tsx:608, settings/calendar/page.tsx:214/233/299), 10 raw `<textarea` (settings/athena/page.tsx:97, today-prompt.tsx:145, athena-conversation.tsx:196, athena-workbench.tsx:249, CommentActivityFeed.tsx:263, updates-panel.tsx:146, activity-item.tsx:281), 30 raw `<select`. No textarea.tsx or select.tsx exists in packages/ui/src/primitives (directory listed: avatar, badge, button, card, context-menu, decorative-icon, dialog, dropdown-menu, focus, hover-card, index, input, layout, menu-styles, popover, separator, sheet, skeleton, tabs, tooltip).
notes: Visually corroborated: in scratchpad/shots2/settings-athena-1440x900-light.png the 'Instructions for Athena' textarea (bordered, tall, no shadow) and the 'Approval behavior' select (native chrome, different height and corner radius) sit 60px apart in the same card and do not share height, radius, or padding. docs/engineering/specs/design-system.md:433 lists Input/Textarea/Select as intended vendored primitives — two of the three were never built.

requirement: Inputs carry no unnecessary shadow in any state.
sourceQuote: I fucking hate unnecessary shadows.
acceptance: The input primitive and every field that composes it declare zero box-shadow in default, hover, focus, filled, disabled, and error states (a token-defined focus ring implemented as outline/ring is permitted and must be named as such); computed style checks on rendered inputs across a form sweep return box-shadow: none in every state.
evidence: packages/ui/src/primitives/input.tsx:22 — the primitive's own default class string contains `shadow-sm`: `'border-outline-variant ... flex h-9 w-full rounded-md border bg-transparent px-3 py-1 shadow-sm transition-colors ...'`.
