This is an unconditional default-state box-shadow, not a focus ring (the focus ring is separately composed as `focusRing` on line 23).
notes: Because the shadow is on the primitive's base layer it is present in every state (default, hover, focus, filled, disabled, error) for every field that composes Input. The 46 raw input/textarea elements that bypass the primitive have their own independent shadow decisions, so a computed-style sweep would need to cover those separately.

requirement: Elements that appear inline with one another must have identical heights.
sourceQuote: Things that appear inline with each other SHOULD NOT HAVE DIFFERENT FUCKING HEIGHTS.
acceptance: An automated check measures offsetHeight of every direct child of every inline row (toolbars, filter bars, property rows, dialog action rows, table header rows) across all app routes at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark; all siblings within a row report identical heights with 0px tolerance, and the check fails loudly listing route + row + offending element when they do not.
evidence: No automated height check exists anywhere (searched apps/, tests/, scripts/, .github/ for offsetHeight/alignment audits — only apps/web/tests/components/views/task-table.test.tsx mentions alignment, unrelated). Live measurement of the Projects toolbar row (scratchpad/ix2/ix2.json `projectsToolbar`): parent `flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2` with children heights 36px (lens-switcher group), 32px (Add filter), 32px (Display) — a 4px delta, tops 117 vs 119 vs 119. Broad probe across 14 routes found 24-53 flex rows per route whose visible siblings differ in height by >0.5px (scratchpad/craft/craft.json inlineHeightViolationCount).
notes: The toolbar case is exactly the requirement's named scenario and is a confirmed violation. The broad 24-53 figure is from my ad-hoc heuristic and contains false positives (items-start icon rows, page headers); it is a signal, not a certified count.

requirement: An aggressive, repeatable automated audit for visual misalignment exists and runs in CI.
sourceQuote: Find some way to aggressively audit for visually misaligned shit.
acceptance: A runnable script/test measures element edge and center positions across all enumerated surfaces and fails when elements that should share an alignment axis (repeated row labels, values, icons, column edges) differ by more than 0.5px; it is wired into CI, its failure output names route + element + delta, and deliberately nudging one element by 2px makes it fail.
evidence: No alignment-audit script or test exists: no file under apps/, tests/, scripts/, tooling/ measures element edge/center positions. .github/workflows/ci.yml jobs are quality (lint/typecheck/format), test (turbo run test), build, e2e (playwright), deploy-production — none runs an alignment audit.
notes: Entirely net-new work, including the CI wiring and the deliberate-2px-nudge self-test.

requirement: The app is actually visually aligned — repeated rows and property lists share common alignment axes.
sourceQuote: Please be extremely careful about alignment.
acceptance: The CRAFT-28 audit reports zero offenders across all app routes at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark, and screenshot overlays confirm that in every repeated list/property row the label left edges, value left edges, icon centers, and row vertical centers each align within 0.5px.
evidence: The CRAFT-28 audit this requirement is defined against does not exist (see CRAFT-28), so 'reports zero offenders' cannot be evaluated. My substitute probe (scratchpad/craft/craft.json alignIssues) reported 0 issues on 13 of 14 routes and 2 on /portfolio, but both /portfolio hits are a wrapping chip row (`flex min-w-0 flex-wrap gap-1.5`, 18 children, 426px left spread) — a false positive of my heuristic, not a real misalignment.
notes: Cannot be certified either way until the CRAFT-28 tool exists. I did not do the required 0.5px screenshot-overlay verification.

requirement: Padding and margins are sufficient that text and icons never touch or border the edges of their containers.
sourceQuote: Paddings and margins need to be appropriate to ensure that text and icons don't literally border the edges of shit.
acceptance: An automated measurement across all app routes at 1440x900 and 390x844 finds no text node or icon whose bounding box comes within less than the token-defined minimum inset (>= 8px, or the documented compact-density token) of its nearest container edge; the check reports zero violations and names route + element + measured gap when it fails.
evidence: No automated inset measurement exists in the repo. My ad-hoc probe at <2px tolerance (the acceptance demands >=8px) already found violations on every one of 14 routes (scratchpad/craft/craft.json insetViolationCount 3-9), including the agenda-rail hour labels ('12:00 AM', container `border-outline-variant/50 bg-surface sticky left-0 z-[50]`, measured gap -6.5px) present on all routes.
notes: At the required >=8px threshold the count would be far higher. My heuristic also produced false positives (grid cells whose nearest bordered ancestor is not the true container), so the exact count is not certified — but the required check does not exist and at least one genuine overflow was measured.

requirement: Every core data type (task, project, initiative, program, cycle, calendar event, time block) is modeled as one first-class object descriptor that drag, context-menu, and selection behavior all read from.
sourceQuote: every core data type is a first-class data structure in the app
acceptance: A single exported object-descriptor registry enumerates task, project, initiative, program, cycle, calendar event, and time block, each exactly once, and a grep across apps/web/src finds no component constructing its own drag payload, context-menu item list, or selection key outside that registry.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/tests/interactivity/object-descriptor.test.ts passes (12 tests) and apps/web/tests/interactivity/drag-and-drop.test.tsx asserts the descriptor round-trips a full object including kinds the legacy payload cannot express, while still mirroring the legacy entity payload so existing drop targets keep working. Drag, context menu and selection all read the same descriptor.
notes: A real single-payload drag registry exists and is well-documented — but it covers 6 of the 7 required kinds minus calendar event/time block, and neither context menus nor selection read from it.

requirement: A task can be dragged onto a project to associate it with that project.
sourceQuote: It should be possible to do stuff like drag tasks into a project
acceptance: In E2E, dragging a task row from /today onto a project in the sidebar, and onto a project row in /orgs/[orgId]/projects, reassigns it; after reload the task appears under that project and the API returns the new project id.
evidence: `grep -rn 'onDrop' apps/web/src --include=*.tsx` → drop targets exist only in calendar/scheduling surfaces and orgs/[orgId]/initiatives/initiatives-client.tsx:700,786 (hierarchy re-parenting). No project row or sidebar entry is a drop target. Live probe on /orgs/:orgId/projects: `sidebarProjectLinks: 0` — the sidebar renders no project links at all (confirmed visually in shots/orgs-orgId-projects-1440x900-light.png; the sidebar is Today/Tasks/Calendar/Inbox/Stream/Portfolio/Search + Workspace nav only).
notes: Launch-blocker. Both halves of the acceptance (sidebar project drop, projects-list row drop) have no implementation.

requirement: A task can be dragged into a time block on the schedule/calendar.
sourceQuote: drag tasks into a time block
acceptance: Dragging a task from a list onto a slot in the /calendar (or /today schedule) grid creates a time block bound to that task at that slot; after reload the block persists with the task title and the task shows the scheduled time.
evidence: Implemented: apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/calendar-scheduling-surface.tsx:247-270 — `onDropObjectOnGrid` creates a timebox titled after the task then links the task with role 'contained'. `pnpm exec playwright test e2e/fluid-scheduling-grid-drop.spec.ts` → `1 passed (4.1s)`. BUT that spec calls `installCalendarRoutes(page, state)` (line 24) which mocks every calendar endpoint, so it asserts request shape, not persistence. My live attempt against the real backend: after firing a real HTML5 drag sequence from the Tasks rail onto `[data-schedule-lane="date:2026-08-02"]`, `GET $API_URL/v1/me/calendar/items?start=2026-08-01…&end=2026-08-04…` returned `{"layers":[],"items":[]}` and shots/calendar-drop-live.png still reads "Nothing scheduled. Drag on the grid or choose New to plan time."
notes: Launch-blocker. Capability is genuinely built and mock-tested; the acceptance's real-backend + post-reload persistence is unproven and my one live attempt produced no persisted timebox.

requirement: A project can be associated with a calendar event, including for deadlines.
sourceQuote: associate projects with calendar events (like for deadlines)
acceptance: From a project detail page a deadline can be linked to a calendar event; the event on /calendar names the project and links back to it, and the project shows the event. Both directions survive reload.
evidence: calendar-scheduling-surface.tsx:281-300 — `onDropObjectOnItem` branches only on `object.kind === 'task'` (linkTask) vs calendar_item (relateItems); projects are not accepted. `grep -n 'project' packages/types/src/calendar.ts` → zero hits. OpenAPI (`$API_URL/v1/openapi.json`, 236 paths) has `/v1/me/calendar/items/{id}/tasks` and `/relations/{relatedItemId}` but no project relation.
notes: No project↔calendar-event association exists in either direction, and no deadline-linking affordance on project detail.

requirement: Right-clicking an object in the web app opens the app's own context menu instead of the browser's native menu.
sourceQuote: Right-clicking should have a useful custom context menu on the web.
acceptance: Right-clicking a task row, project row, initiative row, and calendar block each opens an app menu (role="menu") anchored at the pointer, with event.defaultPrevented === true so Chrome's native menu never appears.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/tests/interactivity/object-context-menu.test.tsx passes and asserts the app menu replaces the browser menu on an object and is anchored, while the browser menu is left alone inside a text field, outside any object, and when the object has no applicable actions.
notes: Chrome's native menu appears everywhere. Task rows, project rows, initiative rows and calendar blocks all fail.

requirement: Context menus are served by exactly one global handler, not per-component ad hoc menus.
sourceQuote: It should have a global handler that exposes options based on a callback that takes into account the object that was interacted with.
acceptance: Exactly one document-level 'contextmenu' listener is registered app-wide (one provider module), and a grep across apps/web/src finds no other onContextMenu handler that calls preventDefault and renders its own menu.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the same suite asserts 'installs a single document listener however many surfaces are mounted' — one global handler, not per-component menus.
notes: The Radix ContextMenu primitive exists (packages/ui/src/primitives/context-menu.tsx) and is consumed by exactly one component, apps/web/src/components/triage/triage-row.tsx:146-300 — i.e. the only menu in the product is the per-component ad hoc kind the requirement forbids.

requirement: The global context-menu handler derives its options from a callback that receives the specific object that was right-clicked.
sourceQuote: exposes options based on a callback that takes into account the object that was interacted with
acceptance: Right-clicking a task yields task-specific items and right-clicking a project yields project-specific items (different item sets), and invoking an item issues an API call carrying the id of the exact record that was right-clicked.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the same suite asserts the menu's contents come from the object: different items for a task and a project, the exact right-clicked record carried into the action, the whole selection acted on when the right-clicked row is part of one, and the single row when the click lands outside it.

requirement: Every context-menu item is actually useful — it performs an action or opens a submenu, with no inert placeholders.
sourceQuote: Right-clicking should have a useful custom context menu on the web.
acceptance: Each item in each object type's context menu is exercised once and produces an observable state change, navigation, or submenu; zero items are no-ops or permanently disabled without a stated reason.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the same suite asserts no item is inert: a disabled item states why it is unavailable rather than sitting there doing nothing, and the action registry carries a disabled reason for every such item (apps/web/tests/interactivity/action-registry.test.ts).
notes: Cannot be satisfied while 6 of 7 object types have no context menu at all.

requirement: Where no object handler applies (text inputs, textareas, rich-text editors), the browser's native context menu is preserved.
sourceQuote: based on a callback that takes into account the object that was interacted with
acceptance: Right-clicking inside a text input, textarea, and the rich-text editor leaves event.defaultPrevented === false and no app menu renders, so native spellcheck/paste remains available.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/tests/interactivity/object-context-menu.test.tsx asserts the native menu is preserved inside a text field and anywhere no object handler applies.
notes: Satisfied by absence of the feature, not by design. Will need re-verification the moment INT-05/06 are built.

requirement: Every view that renders multiple objects in a list-like format supports selecting multiple objects.
sourceQuote: every view in the app that renders multiple objects in a list-like format should have the ability to select multiple objects
acceptance: An inventory test enumerates /today, /inbox, /tasks, /portfolio, /search, orgs projects, initiatives, programs, cycles, my-work, triage, and the embedded task lists on project/initiative/cycle detail pages, and fails if any of them renders rows without working 2+ row selection.
evidence: No inventory test exists. Live probe across 9 list surfaces (/orgs/:orgId/my-work, /projects, /initiatives, /programs, /cycles, /inbox, /orgs/:orgId/triage, /portfolio, /tasks): `checkboxes: 0` and `multiselectable: 0` on every single one. packages/ui/src/components/views/EntityTable.tsx:77-80 exposes controlled `selected`/`onSelect`, but no consumer wires it — the 3 EntityTable consumers (cycles/[cycleId]/page.tsx, project-detail/milestone-tasks.tsx, views/task-table.tsx) pass zero `onSelect`.
notes: The only bulk-actions bar in the app is apps/web/src/components/canvas/bulk-actions-bar.tsx, on the node-graph surface — not a list view.

requirement: Multi-select honors the standard modifier-click conventions: Shift+Click selects a contiguous range and Cmd/Ctrl+Click toggles an individual row.
sourceQuote: using standard keyboard shortcuts and conventions
acceptance: Clicking row 1 then Shift+Clicking row 5 leaves exactly 5 rows selected; Cmd/Ctrl+Clicking row 3 then leaves exactly 4; the on-screen selection count matches after each step.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/tests/interactivity/selection-model.test.ts passes and covers the conventions exactly: shift-click selects the contiguous run, cmd-click toggles one row, ctrl-click is treated as cmd-click for Windows and Linux, shift wins when both modifiers are held, successive shift-clicks re-cut from the same anchor, ranges cut backwards as readily as forwards, and a plain click replaces the selection.

requirement: Multi-select is fully operable from the keyboard alone, including range extension, select-all, and clearing.
sourceQuote: using standard keyboard shortcuts and conventions
acceptance: With no pointer input: Arrow keys move the active row, Shift+ArrowDown extends the selection, Cmd/Ctrl+A selects every row in the view, and Escape returns the selection count to zero.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the same suite covers keyboard operation in full: arrows move the active row without selecting, shift+arrow extends, cmd/ctrl+A selects all, Escape clears (and is left to the surface when there is nothing to clear), Space toggles and Enter opens, Home/End jump and extend to the ends, and a bare 'a' is left alone so typeahead keeps working.
notes: Arrow navigation and Escape exist; range extension, select-all and selection-count feedback do not.

requirement: Multi-select is also achievable by point-and-click via per-row checkboxes.
sourceQuote: while also being able to use point-and-click means like checkboxes
acceptance: At 1440x900 and 390x844, in light and dark, each row exposes a checkbox (revealed on hover/focus and persistent once any row is selected); clicking it toggles that row and the bulk-action bar shows the updated count.
evidence: Screenshot /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/shots/orgs-orgId-projects-1440x900-light.png — 10 project rows (icon, name, Status, Health, Target columns) with no checkbox column and no hover-revealed checkbox slot. shots/triage-contextmenu.png (triage, 9 rows) shows a radio-style state glyph + `•••` overflow, no selection checkbox. Programmatic confirmation across 9 surfaces: `checkboxes: 0` everywhere. Mobile/dark shots (tasks-390x844-dark.png, today-1440x900-light.png) show empty states, no rows to bear checkboxes.
notes: Verified visually as required. No bulk-action bar appears anywhere in a list view.

requirement: Interaction patterns are grounded in consulted MD3 guidance rather than invented, with the mapping written down.
sourceQuote: When in doubt, think about how MD3 would do stuff. Aggressively consult the guidelines
acceptance: A committed document under docs/design/ maps each interaction pattern (context menu, list selection, drag-and-drop, cursor/state feedback) to the specific MD3 guideline section it implements, with links to the guideline pages.
evidence: `ls docs/design/` → audits/, craft-rubric.md, ghost-grammar.md. Neither doc maps interaction patterns to MD3 guideline sections — craft-rubric.md cites the MD3 *type scale* only; ghost-grammar.md is Athena's proposal visual language. `grep -rli 'context menu|drag-and-drop|drag and drop' docs/design/ docs/engineering/` → zero hits.

requirement: Every clickable element sets the native pointer cursor.
sourceQuote: When something is clickable, the cursor MUST reflect that using native cursor APIs.
acceptance: An automated pass over every element with a click handler, role="button", or href on the core app surfaces asserts getComputedStyle(el).cursor === 'pointer', with zero failures.
evidence: packages/ui/src/primitives/button.tsx:37 — the base class string is `'inline-flex items-center justify-center gap-2 whitespace-nowrap rounded-md text-body-medium font-medium transition-colors disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50 …'` with NO `cursor-pointer`. Live probe on /orgs/:orgId/my-work: of 32 visible elements matching a[href]/button/[role=button]/[role=link]/[role=tab], 14 report `getComputedStyle(el).cursor === 'default'` — including the workspace switcher ("LS launch-audit's space"), "Search", the account menu, two "New task" buttons, and the "Assigned to me"/"Delegated & approvals" tabs.
notes: Launch-blocker, and the root cause is one line in the shared Button primitive.

requirement: Every draggable element sets the native grab/grabbing cursor.
sourceQuote: When something is draggable, the cursor MUST reflect that.
acceptance: Task rows, project rows, and calendar blocks report computed cursor 'grab' at rest and 'grabbing' while the pointer is down and moving; zero draggables report 'default' or 'pointer' at rest.
evidence: packages/ui/src/lib/draggable.ts:38 — `export const DRAGGABLE = 'select-none active:cursor-grabbing';` with the docstring at lines 32-37 explicitly stating "The row keeps `cursor-pointer` at rest because its primary action is still *click to open* — a permanent `cursor-grab` would advertise the wrong affordance." Live: all 20 `[draggable="true"]` rows on /orgs/:orgId/projects report computed cursor `'pointer'` at rest; the initiative treegrid row (class `select-none active:cursor-grabbing …`) likewise reports `'pointer'`.
notes: Launch-blocker. This is a deliberate, documented design decision that directly contradicts the requirement — resolving it is a product decision, not a bug fix.

requirement: Elements with distinct click and drag behavior update the cursor to the currently applicable state as the interaction progresses.
sourceQuote: If something has different behavior for click vs. drag, the cursor should naturally update to follow the most applicable state
acceptance: For a task row and a calendar block: cursor is 'grab' at rest, becomes 'grabbing' after pointerdown plus movement, and returns to 'grab' after drop; no sampled frame during the drag reports 'pointer' or 'default'.
evidence: Measured lifecycle on the first draggable project row via Playwright (mouse.move → down → move 5 steps → up): `{before: 'pointer', during: 'grabbing', after: 'pointer'}`. The requirement demands grab → grabbing → grab with no sampled frame reporting 'pointer'.
notes: Launch-blocker. The 'grabbing' half works; the at-rest half is 'pointer' by design (see INT-16).

requirement: Non-interactive and disabled elements must not display interactive cursors.
sourceQuote: not violate user expectations
acceptance: Static text, headings, and layout containers report computed cursor 'default' or 'text', and disabled controls report 'not-allowed'; no such element reports 'pointer' or 'grab'.
evidence: Static side passes: scanning ~4000 h1/h2/h3/p/span/div nodes on /orgs/:orgId/projects that are not inside a[href]/button/[role]/draggable/label/summary → `badCount: 0` reporting 'pointer' or 'grab'. Disabled side is not met: packages/ui/src/primitives/button.tsx:37 uses `disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50` with no `cursor-not-allowed`, so a disabled Button can never report 'not-allowed'. (packages/ui/src/primitives/input.tsx:22 does carry `disabled:cursor-not-allowed`.) No disabled controls were present on the sampled page to measure directly.

requirement: During a drag, hovering a target that cannot accept the dragged object shows a rejecting cursor and performs no mutation on drop.
sourceQuote: When something is draggable, the cursor MUST reflect that.
acceptance: Dragging a task over an invalid target reports computed cursor 'no-drop' or 'not-allowed', and releasing there issues zero mutation requests and leaves the task unchanged after reload.
evidence: `grep -rn "no-drop|dropEffect" apps/web/src` → no 'no-drop' anywhere and no `dropEffect = 'none'`; the only dropEffect assignments are 'move' (initiatives-client.tsx:694,780), 'link' (scheduling-item-card.tsx:182, scheduling-all-day-item.tsx:110) and 'copy' (scheduling-canvas.tsx:256). Drop handlers guard with `acceptsDrop(event)` and return early (scheduling-item-card.tsx:187), so no mutation on an invalid drop holds by construction.
notes: Chrome's native default for a target that never preventDefaults on dragover IS the no-drop cursor, so this may pass incidentally — but nothing asserts it and I did not observe it live. No test covers it.

requirement: Likely next states are preloaded on user intent (hover/focus) before the user commits to the navigation.
sourceQuote: Try preloading whenever possible or whenever it's reasonably expected that a user may change states.
acceptance: Hovering or keyboard-focusing a sidebar nav item, a workspace switcher entry, and a list row each issues the target surface's data request during the hover; the network log shows no additional blocking fetch on the subsequent click.
evidence: Prefetch machinery exists: `usePrefetchApi` used in cycles-client.tsx:75,173, cycles/[cycleId]/page.tsx:39,311, projects-client.tsx, initiatives-client.tsx, project-detail/milestone-tasks.tsx, agenda-context.tsx; cycle-row.tsx:89-90 wires `onMouseEnter={onPrefetch} onFocus={onPrefetch}`. But sidebar nav has none: `grep -n 'prefetch|onMouseEnter' packages/ui/src/components/shell/SidebarNavItem.tsx Sidebar.tsx apps/web/src/components/app-shell-frame.tsx` → zero hits. Measured: hovering the sidebar "Portfolio" link for 1.2s issued 0 non-static requests; the RSC payload `/portfolio?_rsc=GOBkkwysRk6B8UGl` fired only on the subsequent click.
notes: List rows prefetch on hover; sidebar nav items and the workspace switcher do not — and those are the two the acceptance names first.

requirement: Loading states visible to the user in real time are minimized — prefetched or previously visited surfaces render without a spinner or skeleton.
sourceQuote: You need to minimize the amount of loading states the user sees in real time.
acceptance: Navigating to a surface that was prefetched or already visited renders content on the first painted frame; a mutation observer over the transition records zero spinner/skeleton elements entering the DOM.
evidence: My MutationObserver probe over the nav transition hung the page (`locator.click: Timeout 30000ms` waiting for navigation to finish) and I could not re-run it: a concurrent agent broke the app build mid-audit — `git status` shows `D apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/calendar-scheduling-sidebar.tsx` while calendar-scheduling-surface.tsx:34 still imports it, producing the Next.js overlay captured in shots/task-detail.png. Static facts gathered: no app-router `loading.tsx` files exist (`find apps/web/src/app -name loading.tsx` → none); 54 files reference Skeleton.
notes: Not graded. Re-run once the worktree build is green; I deliberately did not fix the other agent's in-flight refactor.

requirement: Every interactive element on every app surface is reachable and operable using the keyboard alone.
sourceQuote: Ensure that all parts of the UI are accessible via keyboard
acceptance: A keyboard-only E2E pass over each core app surface reaches every interactive control with Tab in visual order, activates each with Enter/Space, and never becomes trapped or drops focus to <body>; zero unreachable controls.
evidence: No keyboard-only E2E suite exists: `grep -rl "press('Tab')" apps/web/e2e apps/web/tests` returns only apps/web/e2e/athena-personal.spec.ts and apps/web/e2e/helpers/calendar-ui.ts (feature specs, not an accessibility sweep); there is no a11y spec file. My own Tab sweep over 10 core surfaces (scratchpad/audit.ts → scratchpad/out/results.json, a11y.*.keyboard) reached fewer elements than the visible focusable-candidate count on 6 of 10 surfaces: inbox 34/39, myWork 35/36, initiativeDetail 49/51, projectDetail 49/53, taskDetail 55/57, athena 41/42, settings 44/46 (today 43/43, portfolio 59/59, initiatives 38/38 were clean). Zero focus drops to <body> were observed on any surface.
notes: The required automated pass does not exist, so 'zero unreachable controls' is unproven. My sweep terminates on the first repeated focus key, so the reached-count gaps are indicative of unreachable controls but are not by themselves a precise count.

requirement: Every focusable element renders a visible focus indicator.
sourceQuote: Ensure that all parts of the UI are accessible via keyboard
acceptance: At 1440x900 and 390x844, in light and dark, screenshots of each focusable control type show a focus ring at >=3:1 contrast against adjacent colors; no control suppresses the outline without a replacement.
evidence: Keyboard-driven (real Tab presses, so :focus-visible engages) probe over 59 tab stops on the initiative detail surface — scratchpad/focus.ts, data in scratchpad/out/focus-results.json. 56/59 render a visible ring; 3 do not, all with `outline-style: none` AND `box-shadow: none` while `:focus-visible` matches true: INPUT 'Initiative name', INPUT 'Initiative summary', DIV[contenteditable] 'Description'. Screenshot looked at — scratchpad/out/int23-tabbed-title-input.png: the focused title input shows only the browser's text-selection highlight, no ring. Contrast scratchpad/out/int23-tabbed-print-button.png: the Print button shows a clear blue rounded ring. So these controls suppress the outline with no replacement, which the acceptance forbids.
notes: Important correction: my first detector truncated the computed box-shadow to 60 chars and misread Tailwind's transparent ring placeholders, which would have produced a false 'fail' on 56 controls. Re-measured with full box-shadow parsing; the shared focus ring is in fact broadly healthy and the defect is narrow (3 inline-edit controls). The >=3:1 contrast ratio of the passing ring was not measured.

requirement: Dialogs, menus, and popovers manage focus correctly: focus moves in on open, is contained, Escape closes, and focus returns to the trigger.
sourceQuote: Ensure that all parts of the UI are accessible via keyboard
acceptance: For every dialog, menu, and popover (including the create-entity modals): focus lands inside on open, Tab cycles only within it, Escape closes it, and document.activeElement afterwards is the element that opened it.
evidence: Probed both create-entity modals live (scratchpad/audit.ts dialogProbe → scratchpad/out/results.json). PASSING clauses, both dialogs: focus lands inside on open (focusIn.focusInside = true); Tab is contained (40 consecutive Tab presses, tabEscapes = 0); Escape closes (afterEscape.closed = true). FAILING clause, both dialogs: focus does NOT return to the trigger — afterEscape.isBody = true and activeAfter is the `<body>` element, not the 'New initiative' / 'New task' button that opened it.
notes: Only the two create-entity modals were exercised; the acceptance covers every dialog, menu and popover, and no test suite asserts any of this. The focus-return failure alone blocks the requirement.

requirement: The UI uses proper web semantics — native elements and roles rather than click-handling divs.
sourceQuote: follow proper web semantics
acceptance: axe-core reports zero serious or critical violations on each core app surface; buttons are <button>, navigations are <a href>, row collections are list/table semantics, and every input has a programmatic label.
evidence: Measured per-surface over 10 routes (scratchpad/out/results.json, a11y.*.semantics). STRONG: `div[role=button]` / `span[role=button]` count is 0 on all 10 surfaces — controls are native <button>/<a href>. WEAK: 'every input has a programmatic label' fails on 2 surfaces — taskDetail has `<input class="sr-only" type="file">` and settings has an unlabelled file input, both with empty computed accessible names. Landmark structure also fails (see INT-27).
notes: The axe-core clause is UNVERIFIED, not passed: axe-core is not installed in this repo (`ls node_modules/axe-core` → absent, no @axe-core scope, no axe reference in apps/web/tests or e2e). I did not substitute my hand-rolled checks for an axe run, so 'zero serious or critical violations' remains unestablished.

requirement: Icon-only controls expose an accessible name; decorative icons are hidden from assistive technology.
sourceQuote: follow proper web semantics
acceptance: Every icon-only control has a non-empty accessible name (aria-label or visually hidden text), and every decorative icon is aria-hidden with no computed name; zero unnamed interactive elements.
evidence: scratchpad/out/results.json, a11y.*.semantics. Unnamed interactive elements: taskDetail 1 (`<input class="sr-only" type="file">`), settings 1 (an unlabelled file input) — the acceptance requires zero. Decorative icons: taskDetail has looseIconCount 4 — SVGs that are visible, carry no aria-hidden, are not inside an aria-hidden subtree, and compute no accessible name (samples include the react-flow background `<svg class="react-flow__background" data-testid="rf__background">` and three brand/wordmark paths). The other 8 surfaces are clean (unnamed 0, looseIcon 0).
notes: Failure is localized to the file-upload inputs and the task-detail graph canvas, but both acceptance thresholds are 'zero'.

requirement: Each page exposes correct landmark and heading structure.
sourceQuote: follow proper web semantics
acceptance: Every app route renders exactly one <main>, a labelled <nav>, exactly one h1, and heading levels that never skip a level; asserted per route.
evidence: scratchpad/out/results.json, a11y.*.semantics, measured on all 10 routes. 'exactly one <main>' FAILS on 5 of 10: initiatives, initiativeDetail, projectDetail, athena, settings all report mainCount = 2 (today, inbox, portfolio, myWork, taskDetail are correct at 1). 'exactly one h1' FAILS on projectDetail (h1Count = 2). PASSING: every surface has 3-4 <nav> elements and navsLabelled equals navCount on all 10 (every nav is labelled); headingSkips is [] on all 10 (no level is ever skipped).
notes: Two of four clauses fail; the nav-labelling and heading-sequence clauses are genuinely met.

requirement: A user can designate a relationship between a project and an initiative from the UI.
sourceQuote: It needs to be possible for me to designate relationships between projects and initiatives
acceptance: From a project detail page the project can be attached to an initiative, and from an initiative detail page the project can be added; after reload both records display the link and the API returns it.
evidence: API direction works: `POST $API_URL/v1/orgs/$A/initiatives/$IA/projects {"projectId":"$PA"}` → HTTP 200 `{"initiativeId":"01KZ0S4B2C0FJ2SJKNHKXB08V8","projectId":"01KZ0S4MH7HXG632E2G71ZAHVA","linked":true}`; readback `GET .../initiatives/$IA` returns `childMix:{programs:0,projects:1}` and `GET .../initiatives/$IA/timeline` returns Project Alpha — persisted across requests. UI, project side: PRESENT — apps/web/src/components/project-detail/properties-panel.tsx:142-146 renders an `EntityMultiPicker` bound to initiativeIds/initiativeOptions, wired from apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:299-316. UI, initiative side: ABSENT — the initiative detail page has no add-project control; its only mutating affordances are addResource (external URL attachments, line 175), the icon picker and the delete dialog, and its linked-work section renders a static 'No projects or programs linked to this yet.' empty state (line 620). Confirmed visually: apps/web/.data/design-review/launch-audit/base/orgs-orgId-initiatives-...-1440x900-light.png shows a read-only 'Connected work' list with no add affordance. A ready-made `AssociationsPanel` exists at apps/web/src/components/initiatives/associations-panel.tsx but is dead code — grep finds no importer.
notes: The acceptance requires both directions from the UI; only project→initiative is reachable.

requirement: A user can designate relationships between initiatives that live in different workspaces.
sourceQuote: initiatives between workspaces
acceptance: An initiative in workspace A can be linked to an initiative in workspace B in a single uninterrupted flow (the picker searches across workspaces); after reload both initiatives show the relation and name the other workspace.
evidence: API works cross-workspace: with initiative IA in workspace A and IB in workspace B, `POST $API_URL/v1/orgs/$A/initiatives/hierarchy-links {"parentInitiativeId":"$IA","childInitiativeId":"$IB"}` → HTTP 200. `GET .../initiatives/$IA/aggregate` returns the child WITH its foreign workspace named: `children:[{id:01KZ0S4MGGZQ8CJN2BZM606WTF, organizationId:01KZ0S3YF4ZWHX617YNE5VAK8A, organizationName:"Las Vegans for Better Transit", ...}]`. Schema backs it: packages/db/src/schema/joins.ts:58-90 `initiativeHierarchyLink` is keyed on contextOrganizationId with parent/child free to live in different orgs. GAPS: (1) no UI creates the link — the initiative detail page has no parent/child picker (only addResource/icon/delete), so there is no 'single uninterrupted flow' and no cross-workspace picker; (2) the UI does not name the other workspace — the rendered 'Sub-initiatives' row shows only 'Transit Advocacy Initiative … Active' with no workspace label, confirmed by cropping the live capture (/tmp/connected_zoom.png from apps/web/.data/design-review/launch-audit/base/orgs-orgId-initiatives-...-1440x900-light.png), even though the API supplies organizationName.
notes: Data model and API satisfy the requirement; the UI half (creation flow + naming the other workspace) does not exist.

requirement: An initiative in one workspace can declare a dependency on a project in a different workspace.
sourceQuote: Several initiatives in my personal life are directly dependent on the success of projects in the other domains I control.
acceptance: A personal-workspace initiative can be made dependent on a project in another workspace; the dependency persists after reload and is visible on both the initiative and the project.
evidence: No initiative→project cross-workspace dependency exists in any layer. Attempted live: `POST $API_URL/v1/orgs/$A/initiatives/$IA/projects {"projectId":"$PB"}` where PB lives in workspace B → HTTP 404 `{"code":"not_found"}` (the same call with a same-workspace project returned 200). Schema forbids it by construction: packages/db/src/schema/joins.ts:26-39 `initiativeProject` carries a NOT NULL organizationId shared by both sides; the only project-dependency table (joins.ts:165-181 `projectDependency`) is documented 'scoped to one organization' and is project→project, not initiative→project. Live OpenAPI (236 paths fetched from $API_URL/v1/openapi.json) exposes no initiative-dependency endpoint.
notes: The initiativeHierarchyLink cross-org mechanism covers initiative↔initiative only; there is no analogue for initiative→project.

requirement: A cross-domain dependency surfaces the depended-upon project's success signal, not just its name.
sourceQuote: directly dependent on the success of projects in the other domains I control
acceptance: The dependent initiative's detail view renders the linked project's current status/health and completion progress; changing the project's status changes what the initiative shows on next load.
evidence: The cross-domain dependency this requirement describes cannot exist (see INT-30: cross-workspace initiative→project returns 404, no table). Separately, the nearest shipped surface carries no success signal either: on the initiative detail view the linked project renders as 'Project Alpha … Project' — name plus entity-kind label only, with no status, no health and no completion progress. Verified by cropping and zooming the live authenticated capture: apps/web/.data/design-review/launch-audit/base/orgs-orgId-initiatives-01KZ0S4B2C0FJ2SJKNHKXB08V8-1440x900-light.png → /tmp/connected_zoom.png. (The sibling 'Sub-initiatives' row does show a status, 'Active', so the omission is specific to linked projects.)
notes: Both the dependency and the signal are missing; nothing to change-and-reload.

requirement: A single universal action handler exists through which actions are dispatched.
sourceQuote: All actions in the app should have a universal handler
acceptance: One action registry module exports register/invoke, every action carries a stable id, and no UI component invokes a registered action's mutation directly instead of dispatching through the handler.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/src/lib/actions is a single universal action registry and apps/web/tests/interactivity/action-registry.test.ts (20 tests) covers it: registration stamps the domain and freezes the set, ids must be domain-prefixed, duplicates inside a domain are refused, cross-domain collisions are structurally impossible, and a second module registering the same domain is refused.
notes: Every action in the app is an ad hoc handler; there is nothing to dispatch through.

requirement: The action handler supports callback-backed context injection supplied at each call site.
sourceQuote: supports callback-backed context injection at call sites
acceptance: Call sites pass context as a callback resolved at invoke time (e.g. () => currentSelection); one action id is exercised from the command palette, a context menu, and a keyboard shortcut with three different injected contexts and a single action definition.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the same suite asserts context injection at the call site: the context is resolved at invoke time rather than list time, and the same definition is served from three different entry points.
notes: No context-injection mechanism of any kind.

requirement: Every user-invocable action in the app is registered with the universal handler — no action exists only as an ad hoc handler.
sourceQuote: perform any action in the app, just like Linear supports
acceptance: A source-policy test over web production code fails on any data-mutating user-triggered handler that is not registered in the action registry; the test passes with zero exemptions.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the registry exists and is enforced for what registers with it, but nothing proves the negative — no policy test fails when a user-invocable action ships only as an ad hoc handler, so the 'no action exists only as an ad hoc handler' clause is unproven.
notes: Every data-mutating user-triggered handler is currently ad hoc by definition.

requirement: Registered actions are invocable from a single universal command surface, Linear-style, scoped to the current context.
sourceQuote: perform any action in the app, just like Linear supports
acceptance: The command palette lists every registered action applicable to the current selection/object, and invoking each from the palette produces the same observable effect as its button, context-menu, or shortcut entry point.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/tests/interactivity/action-registration.test.tsx asserts a button and a command-palette row run the same registered action and that a late domain registration appears in an already-rendered list, and the registry filters by applicability to the current context. `partial` because the acceptance's 'every registered action is invocable from the palette' was not asserted exhaustively across all domains.
notes: Palette is a navigation/search surface today, not a universal command surface.

requirement: Each domain of the app registers its actions exactly once, with no duplicate registrations.
sourceQuote: Each domain of the app should register actions exactly once.
acceptance: Each domain (tasks, projects, initiatives, cycles, calendar, workspaces, athena) has exactly one action-registration module; a test asserts all action ids are unique and that registering a duplicate id throws in development.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the same suite asserts each domain registers exactly once — 'refuses a second module registering the same domain' and 'treats re-registering the identical set as a no-op'.
notes: Cannot register exactly once when registration does not exist.

requirement: Action registration is idempotent across remounts and navigation, so the registry never accumulates duplicates at runtime.
sourceQuote: Each domain of the app should register actions exactly once.
acceptance: After navigating across surfaces and remounting providers (including React strict-mode double invocation), the registry's action count and id set are byte-identical to the values captured at first boot.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/tests/interactivity/action-registration.test.tsx asserts registration is idempotent: the same actions after strict-mode double invocation, byte-identical after navigating away and back, and correct with two surfaces holding the same domain at once.
notes: Nothing can accumulate duplicates because nothing accumulates.

requirement: Reduce placeholder UI to only those regions whose content genuinely cannot be known before a fetch resolves.
sourceQuote: Minimize the use of placeholders.
acceptance: An inventory of every skeleton/placeholder component usage in apps/web/src is produced and each surviving usage is annotated with the unknown-until-fetch data it stands in for. Screenshots of Home, Portfolio, Projects, Tasks, Calendar, Cycles and Athena at 1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark, show zero grey placeholder blocks over statically-known regions (sidebar, tab bar, page heading, toolbar, column labels, empty-state copy).
evidence: Placeholder over a statically-known region, confirmed in code: packages/ui/src/components/shell/Sidebar.tsx:239-240 `{loading ? (<WorkspaceNavigationSkeleton />)` and :269-277 renders four `<Skeleton className="h-8 …" />` bars in place of the Workspace nav — whose labels (Initiatives, Programs, Projects, Cycles, …) are static strings, not fetched. Scale: `grep -rn 'Skeleton|animate-pulse' apps/web/src --include=*.tsx | wc -l` → 227 usages across 58 files. No annotated inventory exists.
notes: The required deliverable (an inventory of every skeleton usage annotated with the unknown-until-fetch data it stands in for) does not exist. On the surfaces I shot with the API blocked, headings/toolbars/empty-state copy were correctly free of placeholders — the sidebar workspace-nav skeleton is the concrete violation.

requirement: Never render a loading animation over content that is already known or already cached at render time.
sourceQuote: Minimize the use of loading animations whenever data is known ahead of time.
acceptance: With the network throttled to Slow 3G, first-paint screenshots of every primary surface show no spinner, shimmer or pulsing skeleton anywhere except inside a region bound to an in-flight request that has no cached data. Any animated loader visible in a screenshot must be traceable to a query with no cached/placeholder data.
evidence: packages/ui/src/components/shell/Sidebar.tsx:269-277 `WorkspaceNavigationSkeleton` renders four pulsing `<Skeleton>` bars standing in for nav rows whose labels are compile-time constants — an animated loader over content known ahead of time. Its own comment ('Reserve the workspace navigation rhythm without flashing a false empty state') confirms the skeleton is for layout rhythm, not unknown data.
notes: I also captured a Slow-3G first paint (/private/tmp/.../scratchpad/shots/slow3g-today.png) showing 18 pulsing loaders and h1=null, but I am NOT resting the verdict on it: that capture overlapped the concurrent build break (web=500), so the never-resolving JS could explain it. The code citation above is independent of dev-server state.

requirement: Render every statically-known heading/title immediately on first paint rather than gating it behind a data fetch.
sourceQuote: If you know the heading for something, just outright display it instead of blocking the entire page.
acceptance: With all API requests aborted at the network layer, a cold load of each primary surface still paints the page heading and toolbar labels. Screenshot of each surface at 1440x900 and 390x844 shows the heading text present with API traffic blocked.
evidence: Probe with every request to the API origin aborted at the network layer (Playwright route abort on `*.api.docket.localhost` and `/v1/`), cold load of each surface. Output: `[today] h1="Today"`, `[portfolio] h1="Portfolio"`, `[tasks] h1="Tasks"`, `[calendar] h1="Aug 2, 2026 – Aug 3, 2026"`, `[projects] h1="Projects"`, `[cycles] h1="Cycles"` — all with nav=true. Looked at /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/shots/blocked-today.png: 'Today' + 'Sunday, August 2' + the prompt-box toolbar all painted with the API dead.
notes: Verified at 1440x900 only. The acceptance also asks for 390x844; I did not repeat the API-blocked run at mobile width.

requirement: No screen may replace its entire viewport with a loading state when any part of the screen is already known.
sourceQuote: just outright display it instead of blocking the entire page
acceptance: With the API blocked, no primary surface renders a full-viewport loader: in every screenshot (1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark) the app shell — sidebar, tab bar, page heading, toolbar — is painted and only the data region shows a loading or error state. Zero surfaces show a centered full-page spinner.
evidence: Same API-blocked probe. In /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/shots/blocked-today.png the sidebar, tab region, heading and toolbar are fully painted and only the data region shows an application-owned error card — 'Could not load your day.' with a 'Try again' button. /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/shots/blocked-tasks.png shows heading 'Tasks' + sidebar painted with loading blocks confined to the list region. Zero surfaces rendered a centered full-page spinner across all six.
notes: Error copy is application-owned (no provider/exception text leaked), which is the right treatment. Verified at 1440x900 light only — the acceptance's 390x844 and dark variants were not re-run with the API blocked.

requirement: Reads that have been fetched once in the session must re-render from cache immediately on return navigation instead of showing a loading state again.
sourceQuote: Anything that does need to be loaded should generally be optimistic as the kinds of use cases that we have expect the user to have access to the internet.
acceptance: Navigate A -> B -> A. A screenshot captured within 100ms of the second navigation to A shows fully populated content with no spinner or skeleton frame. Repeated for at least Home, Portfolio, Projects, Tasks, Calendar and Cycles.
evidence: Client-side navigation probe (real sidebar link clicks, A→Tasks→A, screenshot + DOM sample 100ms after the return click): `[Portfolio] pulsing@100ms=0 bodyLen=1425`, `[Calendar] pulsing@100ms=0 bodyLen=746`, `[Cycles] pulsing@100ms=0 bodyLen=1376`, `[Today] pulsing@100ms=0 bodyLen=1033`. Screenshots at /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/shots/csr-return-*.png.
notes: Four of the six named surfaces return from cache with zero skeleton frames — Home(Today), Portfolio, Calendar, Cycles all pass, and Tasks was the intermediate 'B' on every trip and also rendered populated. Projects was not exercised as a return target. Worth recording: an earlier run using full page reloads instead of client-side nav showed 18 skeletons on Cycles — the cache only survives in-app navigation, which is what the requirement asks for, but it is not resilient to reload.

requirement: Mutations must apply optimistically in the UI before the server confirms, and roll back with an application-owned error message on failure.
sourceQuote: Anything that does need to be loaded should generally be optimistic as the kinds of use cases that we have expect the user to have access to the internet.
acceptance: For each mutation type (task status, assignee, dates, project/initiative field edits, drag-and-drop reparenting), a test asserts (a) the UI shows the new value before the mutation promise resolves and (b) when the request is forced to fail, the UI reverts to the prior value and surfaces a UserFacingError — never raw provider/exception text.
evidence: Infrastructure is real: apps/web/src/lib/query.ts:287-296 `optimisticPatch` writes `setQueryData` then restores `previous` on failure; :213-250 `useApiMutation` wires onMutate/onError/onSettled. 20 files use onMutate, including apps/web/src/lib/use-task-mutations.ts:124 (state), :147 (priority), :192 (patch — assignee/dates), :232 (subtask toggle). Test gap: `ls apps/web/tests/lib/` shows use-project-mutations.test.tsx but NO use-task-mutations test; no drag-and-drop reparenting rollback test exists.
notes: The acceptance demands a test per mutation type asserting both pre-resolution display and revert-with-UserFacingError. Only project mutations have that coverage. Task status/assignee/dates and DnD reparenting are implemented optimistically but untested against the rollback + application-owned-error clause.

requirement: Authentication must work end-to-end in production: sign-in, session persistence across reload, protected-route enforcement, and sign-out.
sourceQuote: Please make sure that authentication is properly implemented.
acceptance: An e2e suite run against the production domain passes: passkey sign-in succeeds; an OAuth-provider sign-in succeeds; a full page reload keeps the session; requesting a protected in-app route while signed out redirects to sign-in; sign-out clears the session and a subsequent protected-route request redirects again. Zero failures, zero skipped specs.
evidence: PASSES: `pnpm exec playwright test e2e/sign-in.spec.ts` → '1 passed (55.8s)' (passkey sign-in). Session persistence verified in a real browser: authed /today → full reload → URL still /today and app shell still rendered. FAILS (as of the pass that wrote this line; not re-verified in the OAuth pass below): a signed-out context navigating to /today and /calendar is NOT redirected — final URL stayed on the protected route and body text was 'Loading your workspace … Sign in to continue / Your session is no longer available for this action…' (modal over the app shell). Same after an explicit POST /api/auth/sign-out then GET /today. NOW ALSO PASSES (OAuth-provider clause, previously the fully-open half of this item): `pnpm --filter @docket/web exec playwright test e2e/auth/oauth-sign-in.spec.ts` → '4 passed (3.1s)', including a real end-to-end OAuth2 ceremony — a real `POST /api/auth/sign-in/oauth2` against Better Auth's real `generic-oauth` plugin (the `test-oauth` provider added in `packages/auth/src/auth-builder.ts`, gated to `APP_MODE ∈ {local,test}` and structurally absent in production, proven in `packages/auth/tests/builder/generic-oauth.test.ts`), a real cross-origin redirect to a real local authorization server (`apps/api/src/lib/oauth-stub-provider.ts`: real `/authorize` → `/token` → `/userinfo`, not a browser-side stub), a real one-time code, a real return through the real `/api/auth/oauth2/callback/test-oauth` handler (real server-to-server token exchange + userinfo call), and a real minted session confirmed via `GET /api/auth/get-session` (real user id, real session token, identity matching the stub's userinfo response). The prior spec at this path asserted the OPPOSITE — that no session existed — which is why the OAuth-provider clause was previously fully open, not merely undertested.
notes: The e2e `signOut` helper (e2e/helpers/app.ts:26-30) POSTs the API and clears cookies rather than driving the UI control; not re-checked in this pass. Everything above still ran against the local dev origin, not a production domain — the acceptance requires production, so `status` stays `partial` until a full run (including the protected-route-redirect clause) is re-verified against it with zero failures and zero skipped specs. `test-oauth` is deliberately not a real product provider and has no sign-in button of its own (see the spec's module doc comment) — it exists only to give the ceremony a real, controlled identity provider to complete against, since no environment here holds real Google/GitHub/etc. credentials. NOTE (historical): an earlier sign-out probe invalidated the shared .data/design-review/session.json; it was regenerated (new orgId 01KZ0TDENDESTZ4MT8E0VZHNAH).

requirement: An already-authenticated user must never see the authentication page flash when entering the app from the landing page.
sourceQuote: I should not be seeing a flash of the authentication page when I try to open the app from the landing.
acceptance: With an authenticated session, capture frames every 50ms through the landing -> app transition (Playwright video/trace). Zero captured frames contain the sign-in page's distinguishing element (e.g. the passkey/sign-in heading or provider buttons). Run in both light and dark, at 1440x900 and 390x844.
evidence: Frame capture through the authenticated landing→app transition in 4 configurations (1440x900 and 390x844 × light/dark), 59-73 frames each. Every frame probed for /Sign in with a passkey|Continue with Google|Welcome back|Sign in to Docket/ and for an auth pathname. Result in all four runs: 'frames with sign-in marker: []' and 'frames on an auth path: 0'. Frames written to /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/landing/<config>/.
notes: Two honest caveats: (1) the sampler achieved ~75-90ms per frame, not the 50ms the acceptance specifies, because each Playwright screenshot costs time — a sub-90ms flash could hide between frames; (2) run against the local dev origin, not the production domain.

requirement: Clicking "Open app" on the landing page must land the authenticated user directly on an in-app route with no intermediate auth screen paint.
sourceQuote: I MUST go straight from the main page, click Open app, directly into the app itself
acceptance: An e2e test on the production domain clicks the landing page's "Open app" control while authenticated and asserts the recorded navigation chain contains no document request or paint for /sign-in (or any auth route) and the final URL is an in-app route. The "Open app" control exists and is reachable on the landing page.
evidence: Clicking the landing CTA while authenticated: recorded main-frame navigation chain was ['/','/','/','/','/today'] and document requests were only ['/','/'] — no document request for /sign-in or any auth route; final URL /today. Verified in all 4 viewport/theme configs.
notes: Two deviations from the stated acceptance: (1) the control is labeled 'Open Docket', not 'Open app' — apps/web/src/components/marketing/marketing-cta.tsx:43, :73, :117, :134 (href /today); (2) verified against the local dev origin, not the production domain.

requirement: No frame of the landing-to-app transition may paint half-styled or unstyled content.
sourceQuote: not seeing a flash of half-styled content
acceptance: Frame-by-frame capture (50ms interval) of the landing -> app transition contains no frame with fallback/default-font text, missing theme background, or unstyled layout. The first painted app frame already uses IBM Plex Sans and the correct light/dark surface color. Verified in both themes at 1440x900 and 390x844.
evidence: Across every captured transition frame the computed body font was the single value '"IBM Plex Sans", "IBM Plex Sans Fallback", ui-sans-serif, …' (distinct fonts set size 1) and the background a single value, in all 4 configs. /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/landing/1440x900-light/frame-003-477ms.png — I looked at it: the app is already fully styled (sidebar, Today heading, prompt box, right rail), correct light surface, no fallback-font text.
notes: Same caveats as SCR-08: ~75-90ms sampling interval rather than 50ms, and local dev origin rather than production. Background was read from `document.body` which is transparent (rgba(0,0,0,0)) — the theme color lives on the html element, so the 'correct surface color' clause rests on the screenshot, not the probe.

requirement: The OAuth authorization page must be rebuilt against the design system — MD3 type tokens, standard layout/wrapper components, no ad hoc styling.
sourceQuote: Please do a pass on craft for the authorization page.
acceptance: /oauth/authorize passes all eight dimensions of the Docket Craft Rubric with a scorecard committed to docs/design/audits/. Every text node maps to an MD3 type token (no ad hoc font-size/weight), the page uses the shared layout/wrapper components, and there is no element-level styling outside design tokens.
evidence: Design side is good: apps/web/src/app/(auth)/oauth/authorize/page.tsx composes the shared `AuthLayout` (line 52, 384) and Avatar/Button primitives (line 62); every text node uses an MD3 type token (text-headline-small :389, text-label-medium :177, text-body-medium :180/:213/:225, text-label-large :402, text-body-small :234/:446) — no ad hoc font-size/weight. Runtime probe of the rendered page found only 3 elements with a style attribute, all injected by the Next.js dev-tools overlay. Screenshot: /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/oauth/oauth-authorize-1440x900-light.png.
notes: FAILS the scorecard clause: `ls docs/design/audits/*.md` → 10 files (2026-06-10-design-pass, 2026-07-06-athena-surfaces, 2026-07-10-project-management, 2026-07-13-calendar, 2026-07-13-initiatives, 2026-07-14-initiative-mobile-rhythm, 2026-07-14-projects-experience, 2026-07-14-settings-production, 2026-07-15-personal-athena, 2026-07-19-athena-connections-mcp-relocation) — none covers /oauth/authorize, and grep for 'oauth/authorize|consent' across them returns nothing.

requirement: The OAuth authorization page must explicitly tell the user which of their resources the third-party app is requesting and what it will do with them.
sourceQuote: third-party developers will rely on it to properly inform the user how they're using their resources
acceptance: The consent screen displays the requesting client's name and, for every requested scope, a human-readable line naming the data covered and whether access is read or write. A test enumerates every scope the OAuth server can issue and asserts each has a copy entry — no scope renders as a raw identifier (e.g. "tasks:write") or as "Unknown scope".
evidence: The set of issuable scopes is closed and fully covered: packages/auth/src/auth-builder.ts:503 `scopes: ['work:read','work:write','agents:run','connectors:link','offline_access']` (the hard ceiling), matching CONNECT_SCOPES at apps/api/src/mcp/scope.ts:54, and SCOPE_INFO at page.tsx:74-106 has a plain-language label+detail for all five. Rendered page (screenshot /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/oauth/oauth-authorize-1440x900-light.png) shows 'claude.ai wants access to your Docket account', Your account, Returns to, and five readable lines: Read your work / Create and update work / Manage agent sessions / Link external items / Stay connected.
notes: MISSING the required test: `grep -rn 'SCOPE_INFO|CONNECT_SCOPES' apps/web/tests apps/web/src packages` matches only page.tsx:74 and :199 — no test enumerates issuable scopes against the copy map. Worse, page.tsx:201 is `const label = info?.label ?? scope`, so an unrecognized scope renders as a RAW IDENTIFIER, and apps/web/tests/components/auth/oauth-authorize-page.test.tsx:165 ('renders an unrecognized scope rather than dropping it') locks that behavior in.

requirement: The OAuth authorization page must be visually presentable at every supported screen size and theme.
sourceQuote: It needs to look presentable
acceptance: Screenshots of /oauth/authorize at 1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark: no horizontal page scroll, no clipped or truncated text, no element touching the viewport edge without padding, and no element in an inline row whose height differs from its siblings.
evidence: Captured and looked at /oauth/authorize at both required sizes and themes: /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/oauth/oauth-authorize-1440x900-light.png, -1440x900-dark.png, -390x844-light.png, -390x844-dark.png. Runtime probe at 1440x900: scrollWidth 1440 == clientWidth 1440, and zero elements with a right edge past the viewport. In the 390x844 dark shot the card has consistent padding off both edges, no text clipped or truncated, and the five permission rows are identical height with the chevrons aligned.
notes: Buttons reorder correctly (Authorize above Deny stacked on mobile, Deny→Authorize left-to-right at width) with matching heights.

requirement: All user-facing copy on the OAuth authorization page must be understandable by a non-technical layperson.
sourceQuote: ESPECIALLY have understandable copy for a layperson
acceptance: Every visible string on /oauth/authorize is plain language: no raw scope identifiers and none of the terms "OAuth", "token", "client_id", "redirect_uri", "scope", "API", or "endpoint" in user-facing copy; body copy scores at or below a Grade 9 reading level. Verified from a screenshot of the rendered page, not from source strings.
evidence: Runtime scan of the rendered page's innerText at 1440x900: bannedTerms = [] for the word-boundary set OAuth/token/client_id/redirect_uri/scope/API/endpoint, and rawScopeIdentifiersVisible = false. Full rendered text was: 'Docket / C / D / claude.ai wants access to your Docket account / Your account … / Returns to claude.ai / This app will be able to / Read your work / Create and update work / Manage agent sessions / Link external items / Stay connected / Deny / Authorize / Revoke access any time in Connected apps.' Confirmed visually in /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/oauth/oauth-authorize-1440x900-light.png. Every sentence is short, concrete, and well below Grade 9.
notes: Holds for all five scopes the server can actually issue. It would break for an unrecognized scope because of the raw-identifier fallback at page.tsx:201 (see SCR-12), but no such scope is issuable today.

requirement: All behavior must be covered by unit tests, enforced by coverage thresholds that fail the build when unmet.
sourceQuote: All behavior must have clearly defined, properly organized unit and end-to-end tests.
acceptance: `pnpm turbo run test` passes with coverage thresholds enforced per the repo coverage policy (90% default, 100% for trust-spine packages) and the command exits non-zero when any package falls below its threshold — demonstrated by temporarily lowering coverage in one package and observing a red run.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the gate is wired and red, which is the honest state. `pnpm turbo run test:coverage` is its own CI job and sits in `deploy-production.needs`; thresholds live in tooling/vitest/preset.ts (90 default, 100 for the trust-spine packages). docs/engineering/coverage-ledger.md records the measured run: `Tasks: 3 successful, 16 total`, exit 1 — 13 of 16 measured packages are below their threshold (@docket/notifications at 29.55% against 90, @docket/blob-store 52.00, @docket/billing 63.06), with zero test failures. @docket/admin and @docket/runner have no test:coverage script and are outside the gate entirely.
notes: Two distinct defects: (a) four packages are below the 90% policy threshold today; (b) the command the requirement names and the command CI runs do not enforce thresholds at all. Also apps/admin and apps/runner have no test:coverage script (16 coverage tasks vs 18 test tasks), so they are entirely outside the coverage gate.

requirement: All behavior must be covered by end-to-end tests, with no skipped or disabled specs.
sourceQuote: All behavior must have clearly defined, properly organized unit and end-to-end tests.
acceptance: Every core user journey listed in the core-e2e document has at least one Playwright spec, and `pnpm --filter @docket/web test:e2e` passes with zero skipped, `.fixme`, or `.only` specs (asserted by a lint/policy check over the e2e sources).
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the 'no skipped or disabled specs' half is now enforced: packages/test-utils/tests/workspace-policies/e2e-discipline-policy.test.ts passes as part of `pnpm --filter @docket/test-utils exec vitest run tests/workspace-policies` (6 files, 27 tests). The coverage half is not met — 32 Playwright specs across 8 journey directories do not cover 'all behavior', and the e2e job's own pass was not observed on GitHub Actions in this gate. CAVEAT recorded at the gate: packages/test-utils/tests/workspace-policies/e2e-discipline-policy.test.ts is present in the working tree but is NOT tracked by git (`git status` reports it untracked), so it does not exist for a CI checkout and cannot gate anything until it is committed.
notes: Confound I must flag: the dev stack is shared with other agents, and during the run a concurrent agent deleted apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/calendar-scheduling-sidebar.tsx while calendar-scheduling-surface.tsx:34 still imports it, producing a Next.js build error mid-window — that plausibly explains the two calendar/attachment failures. An isolated re-run was attempted but was contaminated by the same break. Independent of flakiness, the 'every core journey in the core-e2e document has a spec' half cannot be satisfied because that document does not exist (see SCR-18).

requirement: Tests must live in a separate tests/ directory mirroring the source structure and never be colocated in src/.
sourceQuote: All behavior must have clearly defined, properly organized unit and end-to-end tests.
acceptance: A repo policy test enumerates every workspace and fails if any file matching *.test.* or *.spec.* exists under a package's src/ directory; the test passes with zero violations across apps/{web,api,admin,runner}, packages/*, and services/*.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): packages/test-utils/tests/workspace-policies/test-layout-policy.test.ts now enforces it and passes: no test file is colocated in any package's src/, and every package's tests live in a tests/ tree mirroring source. Verified by running the workspace-policies suite (27 tests passing). CAVEAT recorded at the gate: packages/test-utils/tests/workspace-policies/test-layout-policy.test.ts is present in the working tree but is NOT tracked by git (`git status` reports it untracked), so it does not exist for a CI checkout and cannot gate anything until it is committed.
notes: Nothing enforces this, so it can regress silently. The enumerate-every-workspace-and-fail test still needs to be written.

requirement: Documentation must identify which end-to-end tests are the "core" ones.
sourceQuote: Documentation must make it clear what the "core" end-to-end tests are.
acceptance: A committed document under docs/engineering/ lists each core end-to-end test by spec path with a one-line description of the journey it covers, and an automated check asserts (a) every listed path exists on disk and (b) every spec tagged/marked core appears in the document — the check fails if the two lists diverge.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): docs/engineering/specs/core-e2e.md is the committed document naming which end-to-end specs are the core ones, and apps/web/e2e is now organized into the journey directories it names (athena, auth, calendar, mcp, platform, scheduling, work).
notes: Neither the document nor the divergence check exists. This also blocks half of SCR-16's acceptance.

requirement: The production deploy must be gated on every test-running CI job succeeding.
sourceQuote: CI must be set up to not pass for deployment unless all tests succeed.
acceptance: In .github/workflows/ci.yml, `deploy-production.needs` includes every job that executes tests or checks (currently quality, test, build, e2e), and a guard (policy test or lint rule over the workflow file) fails when a new test-running job is added without being added to that `needs` list.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): re-verified this session: `pnpm ci:gate-policy` → 'PASS — every check job gates the production deploy, and no gating step is soft-failed', reporting `deploy-production.needs = [quality, secret-scan, test, coverage, build, e2e]` against .github/workflows/ci.yml's 6 check jobs. scripts/ci-gate-policy.ts is the guard that fails when a new test-running job is added without being added to that needs list.
notes: Adding a new test-running job to ci.yml without adding it to deploy-production.needs would go unnoticed today.

requirement: No test step may be soft-failed such that a failing test still yields a passing CI status or an executed deploy.
sourceQuote: CI must be set up to not pass for deployment unless all tests succeed.
acceptance: No test-executing step in .github/workflows/*.yml uses `continue-on-error: true`, `|| true`, or `if: always()` on a gating check. Proven empirically on a scratch branch: force one unit test to fail and, separately, one e2e spec to fail — in both cases the workflow run reports failure (not merely a skipped deploy) and deploy-production does not run.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the static and local-empirical halves hold — `pnpm ci:gate-policy` passes and asserts no gating step carries continue-on-error or `|| true`, and docs/engineering/launch/evidence/production/2026-08-02-scr20-forced-failure.txt records a forced failure. No GitHub Actions run was observed in this gate confirming the behavior on the real CI provider.
notes: The empirical half was NOT performed — proving a forced unit-test failure and a forced e2e failure both turn the workflow run red and skip deploy-production would require pushing a scratch branch to CI, which I did not do. Related but separate gap: because CI runs `turbo run test` and not `test:coverage` (see SCR-15), a coverage regression is silently non-gating even though no step is soft-failed.

requirement: No test file may sit at the root level of any module's testing directory — enforced automatically.
sourceQuote: No tests may be at the root level of the testing directory for any module.
acceptance: A policy test enumerates every testing directory in the repo (each workspace's tests/ plus apps/web/e2e) and fails if any file matching *.test.* or *.spec.* sits directly at that directory's root instead of inside a subdirectory. The test passes with zero violations repo-wide.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): packages/test-utils/tests/workspace-policies/test-layout-policy.test.ts enforces that no test file sits at the root of any module's testing directory, and it passes. This is the automatic enforcement the acceptance requires, not a one-time sweep. CAVEAT recorded at the gate: packages/test-utils/tests/workspace-policies/test-layout-policy.test.ts is present in the working tree but is NOT tracked by git (`git status` reports it untracked), so it does not exist for a CI checkout and cannot gate anything until it is committed.
notes: apps/web/e2e is the sole offender, but it is the whole violation and it is unenforced.

requirement: Relocate every Playwright spec currently sitting flat at the root of apps/web/e2e into topical subdirectories.
sourceQuote: No tests may be at the root level of the testing directory for any module.
acceptance: `ls apps/web/e2e/*.spec.ts` returns nothing — all 23 specs presently at that root (account-eol, athena-personal, composer-reset, the six fluid-scheduling-* specs, google-calendar, layered-calendar, layered-calendar-drawer, mcp-connect, mcp-connect-cold-start, mcp-session, notifications, passkey-signal, pwa-offline, recovery-codes, sign-in, verify-attachments, verify-composer, verify-today) live in subdirectories. Afterwards `pnpm --filter @docket/web test:e2e` discovers and passes a spec count greater than or equal to the pre-move count, with zero specs silently dropped from discovery.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): verified by listing: every one of the 32 Playwright specs under apps/web/e2e now sits in a topical subdirectory (athena/, auth/, calendar/, mcp/, platform/, scheduling/, work/); none is flat at the root. e2e-discipline-policy.test.ts keeps it that way. CAVEAT recorded at the gate: packages/test-utils/tests/workspace-policies/e2e-discipline-policy.test.ts (the relocation itself is committed; only its guard is not) is present in the working tree but is NOT tracked by git (`git status` reports it untracked), so it does not exist for a CI checkout and cannot gate anything until it is committed.
notes: No relocation has been started. playwright.config.ts uses testDir './e2e' with testMatch '**/*.spec.ts', so a move into subdirectories would still be discovered — the pre/post spec-count check remains to be done after the move.

requirement: Modularize code so that a change in one package does not force unrelated packages to rebuild.
sourceQuote: Code should be appropriately modularized to reduce the amount of time it takes to rebuild stuff
acceptance: `pnpm turbo run build --dry=json` after touching only apps/web/src lists no package outside web and its dependents in the tasks-to-execute set; the same check after touching packages/ui lists only ui and its dependents. The affected-set for each workspace is recorded in a committed check that fails if an unrelated package enters the set.
evidence: `pnpm turbo run build --dry=json` (with dev-stack env) shows 21 graph nodes but only 4 real build tasks (@docket/web, @docket/admin, @docket/api, @docket/runner) — `Tasks: 4 successful, 4 total`. @docket/web#build depends on api/env/eslint-config/notifications/tsconfig/types/ui; nothing depends on @docket/web, so a web-only edit can only rebuild web. Workspace packages ship raw TS (turbo.json comment: `"types": "./src/index.ts"`), so they have no build task at all. No committed affected-set check exists: `grep -rn "affected" package.json scripts/ .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns nothing, and CI just runs bare `pnpm turbo run build --cache-dir=.turbo` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:125).
notes: The graph shape is fine, but I could not run the touch-based dry-run the acceptance names — modifying source was denied by the permission system, and I'm auditing, not editing. The 'committed check that fails if an unrelated package enters the set' does not exist.

requirement: Build caching must produce full cache hits on unchanged code, locally and in CI.
sourceQuote: with caching used to improve build speed
acceptance: Running `pnpm turbo run build` twice with no source change reports FULL TURBO / 100% cached on the second run locally, and a CI run on an unchanged commit shows every build task replayed from cache rather than re-executed (visible in the workflow log).
evidence: Local half verified. First run (cold, with API_URL/WEB_URL/NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL/NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL/ADMIN_URL/SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION set): `Tasks: 4 successful, 4 total / Cached: 2 cached, 4 total / Time: 20.563s`. Second run, no source change: `Tasks: 4 successful, 4 total / Cached: 4 cached, 4 total / Time: 110ms >>> FULL TURBO` (real 0.43s). CI half not verified: `gh run list --workflow=ci.yml --limit 5` shows the three most recent main runs as `failure`, so there is no green run whose log shows every build task replayed from cache.
notes: Note the build only succeeds when API_URL, WEB_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL and ADMIN_URL are all supplied — a bare `pnpm turbo run build` fails at next.config load and again at admin's /lifecycle prerender ('NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is required to construct the auth client during SSR').

requirement: A shared remote build cache must be actually configured (not inert) so CI build minutes are reduced across runs and machines.
sourceQuote: reduce build minutes
acceptance: TURBO_TOKEN, TURBO_TEAM and TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY resolve to real values in CI (not empty, so turbo is not silently falling back to the local .turbo cache), a CI run on a commit already built elsewhere shows remote cache hits in the log, and the measured wall-clock time for a no-op build run is recorded and lower than the pre-change baseline for both the GitHub Actions build job and the Vercel web build.
