evidence: The remote cache is inert. `gh api repos/TheHypertextStudio/athena-web/actions/secrets --jq '.secrets[].name'` returns exactly one secret: NEON_API_KEY — no TURBO_TOKEN, no TURBO_REMOTE_CACHE_SIGNATURE_KEY. `gh api .../actions/variables` returns ADMIN_URL, AGENT_MAX_TURNS, API_URL, BETTER_AUTH_ALLOWED_HOSTS, GCP_*, GOOGLE_*, NEON_PROJECT_ID, PASSKEY_RP_ID, WEB_URL — no TURBO_TEAM, which .github/workflows/ci.yml:20 reads as `${{ vars.TURBO_TEAM }}`. turbo.json's own comment says so: 'Inert until a cache is configured: with no TURBO_TOKEN/TURBO_API set, turbo silently uses the local cache only.'
notes: CI is falling back to the GitHub Actions cache action (.github/workflows/ci.yml:45-46, 73-74, 119-120) keyed on exact SHA — not a shared remote cache across machines. No wall-clock baseline for a no-op build has been recorded for either the Actions build job or the Vercel web build.

requirement: The Athena surface must read as a chief-of-staff product, not a generic chat pane — it must pass the project's craft bar as a first-class surface.
sourceQuote: In general, Athena needs to present as a world-class chief of staff.
acceptance: A Docket Craft Rubric design review of the Athena surface at 1440x900 and 390x844, in light and dark, is written to docs/design/audits/ with every hard gate passing and no dimension scored below the ship bar; screenshots attached for all four viewport/theme combinations.
evidence: The most recent Docket Craft Rubric review that covers the Athena surface itself is docs/design/audits/2026-07-06-athena-surfaces.md, whose verdict line reads 'BELOW BAR — dimensions 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 are below the ship bar, and the A11y and No-placeholder gates fail.' The later docs/design/audits/2026-07-15-personal-athena.md says SHIP BAR but its screenshot directory does not exist (`ls '/Users/williecubed/Projects/Hypertext Studio/athena-service/.claude/worktrees/athena-experience/apps/web/test-results/'` → No such file or directory), so its four viewport/theme captures are not attached. docs/design/audits/2026-07-19 covers Settings→Athena, not the Athena surface, and its screenshot dir apps/web/.data/design-review/2026-07-19/ also does not exist.
notes: Live capture confirms craft defects today. In scratchpad/shots1/orgs-orgId-athena-1440x900-light.png (empty state) there is ~145px of dead vertical space between the 'Finished 0' row (y≈166) and the 'What should Athena move forward?' heading (y≈310), and the 'Start work' button is right-aligned at x≈755-857 beneath a textarea that ends at x≈856 but inside a content column running to x≈1005 — an orphaned control. In scratchpad/shots3/athena-1440x900-light.png (populated with 3 sessions I created) the 'Cancel work' control at y≈486 renders as bare unstyled text floating alone in a full-width band.

requirement: Athena's responses must present structured results as interactive elements rather than plain prose/markdown.
sourceQuote: Think: a lot of interactive elements.
acceptance: Across a scripted run of the five most common Athena flows (create work, plan the day, report status, review a change set, connect an MCP server), every response containing structured data renders an interactive component (actionable card, inline editor, widget, or elicitation). Zero screenshots show structured data rendered only as text or a JSON/code block.
evidence:
Screenshot looked at: scratchpad/ath2/canceled-session-expanded.png — the Athena activity entry 'Docket · update task' expands a 'Technical details' disclosure rendering a raw JSON code block: {"toolName": "update_task", "input": {"state": "in_progress", "taskId": "01HZ..."}}. Source: apps/web/src/components/athena/athena-workbench.tsx:196-205 renders `
{JSON.stringify(entry.technical, null, 2)}
`. DOM capture confirms one `pre` block with that exact content (scratchpad/ath2/a2.json preBlocks).
notes: Interactive elements DO exist (decision Approve/Reject buttons at athena-workbench.tsx:144-157), so this is not zero-interactivity — but structured tool payloads render only as a JSON block, which the acceptance forbids. The five scripted flows were not run.

requirement: MCP Apps must be supported natively: a widget returned by a connected MCP server renders inline inside the Athena conversation.
sourceQuote: We need to natively support the MCP Apps spec to be competitive with Claude.
acceptance: A third-party MCP server (not Docket's own) whose tool returns a `ui://` resource is connected, its tool invoked, and the widget renders live and interactive inside the Athena conversation — screenshot shows the rendered UI, not a link, a raw HTML string, or a JSON dump. Clicking a control inside the widget produces a visible effect in the same screenshot pair (before/after).
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the host renders a connected server's widget inline — apps/api/src/mcp/apps/host-routes.ts returns the ui:// document the tool declares alongside its result and apps/web/src/components/athena/mcp-app-view.tsx renders it in the conversation, covered by apps/web/tests/athena/mcp-app-view.test.tsx. `partial` because the acceptance is a screenshot of a widget rendered inline in a live Athena conversation and none was captured.
notes: Launch-blocker. What IS built is the opposite direction: apps/api/src/mcp/apps/ makes Docket a widget *producer* for external hosts like Claude (4 widgets: change-report, work-list, entity, plan). No third-party widget can render inside Athena.

requirement: Every part of the MCP Apps spec must be implemented — no partial or stubbed surface area.
sourceQuote: You must completely implement all parts of the [MCP Apps](https://apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/api/) spec.
acceptance: A conformance matrix enumerates every method, notification, capability field, `_meta` key, and resource convention defined by the MCP Apps spec. It is generated against a copy of the spec fetched from apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io and committed to the repo alongside the matrix, recording the retrieval date and the version identifier as published by that source — no version is assumed or invented. Each row names the implementing host handler and the test that exercises it; the matrix contains zero rows marked unimplemented, partial, or deferred, and the suite passes in CI.
evidence: No conformance matrix anywhere: `grep -rln 'conformance' docs/` → zero hits. No committed copy of the spec fetched from apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io, no retrieval date, no version identifier. The only MCP-Apps coverage is 7 server-side tests: `cd apps/api && pnpm exec vitest run tests/mcp/mcp-apps.test.ts` → `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 7 passed (7)`, covering ui:// resource registration, self-contained documents, the widget-side handshake string, subscription refusal, and tool→widget `_meta` linkage.
notes: Launch-blocker.

requirement: The host must implement the spec handshake in order: answer `ui/initialize` with its capabilities and `hostContext`, wait for `ui/notifications/initialized`, and only then deliver `ui/notifications/tool-result`.
sourceQuote: You must completely implement all parts of the [MCP Apps](https://apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/api/) spec.
acceptance: A test drives a fake view frame: `ui/initialize` receives a result containing host capabilities and `hostContext`; asserting on message order shows no `ui/notifications/tool-result` is posted before `ui/notifications/initialized` is received; `ui/notifications/tool-input` carries the tool's original arguments.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the ordering is implemented: apps/api/src/mcp/apps/runtime.ts:116-123 issues `ui/initialize` carrying the host's capabilities and hostContext, waits for `ui/notifications/initialized`, and only then delivers `ui/notifications/tool-result` (handled at :95). The automated test the acceptance names is weaker than the claim: apps/api/tests/mcp/mcp-apps.test.ts:140-149 asserts only that the three method names appear in the served document, not that they occur in order, so a regression that inverted the sequence would still pass.
notes: Launch-blocker. The acceptance is explicitly host-side ("a test drives a fake view frame") and there is no host to drive.

requirement: A widget must be able to invoke a server tool via `tools/call` through the host bridge and receive the result.
sourceQuote: You must completely implement all parts of the [MCP Apps](https://apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/api/) spec.
acceptance: A test posts `{jsonrpc:'2.0',id,method:'tools/call',params:{name,arguments}}` from the embedded frame; the host executes the tool under the current session's authorization (a call naming a tool outside the session's scope returns a JSON-RPC error, not a silent success) and returns the tool result to the frame with the matching id.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/mcp/mcp-apps-host-routes.test.ts passes and covers view-initiated tools/call through the host bridge: a tool the server marks view-callable runs and reflects the change it made, a model-only tool is refused when a view asks for it, and a tool declaring no visibility reads the spec default.
notes: Launch-blocker. The scope-enforcement half of the acceptance (out-of-scope tool → JSON-RPC error, not silent success) has no implementation to test.

requirement: `ui/update-model-context` from a widget must reach the model's context so Athena's subsequent turns reflect actions the user took inside the widget.
sourceQuote: You must completely implement all parts of the [MCP Apps](https://apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/api/) spec.
acceptance: After a widget calls `ui/update-model-context` (e.g. the user undoes a change from the card), the next model request's context contains that content, and Athena's next message does not describe the reverted state — asserted on the serialized prompt payload.
evidence: View side only: runtime.ts:129-131 `tell(text) { return request('ui/update-model-context', {content:[{type:'text',text}]}); }`, with a docstring at lines 30-32 explaining why it matters. Nothing in apps/api or apps/web consumes `ui/update-model-context` — grep for it outside runtime.ts returns zero hits.

requirement: `ui/open-link` requests from a widget must be handled by the host and navigate the user to the target.
sourceQuote: You must completely implement all parts of the [MCP Apps](https://apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/api/) spec.
acceptance: Clicking a link control inside an embedded widget navigates the host app to the target URL (screenshot before/after showing the destination surface); the frame itself never performs top-level navigation, and an off-origin URL is either opened in a new tab or refused — never silently ignored.
evidence: View side only: runtime.ts:132-134 `link(url) { return request('ui/open-link', { url }); }`. No host handler exists (zero postMessage listeners in apps/web). Cannot screenshot a before/after navigation because no widget can render.

requirement: `ui/message` from a widget must post a message into the Athena conversation.
sourceQuote: You must completely implement all parts of the [MCP Apps](https://apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/api/) spec.
acceptance: Triggering a widget control that calls `ui/message` causes the message content to appear in the conversation transcript attributed correctly, and Athena responds to it — screenshot of the transcript showing the widget-originated message followed by Athena's reply.
evidence: View side only: runtime.ts:135-137 `say(text) { return request('ui/message', …); }`. No host handler; apps/web/src/components/athena/athena-conversation.tsx has no widget-message ingress. Cannot screenshot a transcript containing a widget-originated message.

requirement: The host must push `ui/notifications/host-context-changed` so embedded widgets restyle to the host theme without reloading.
sourceQuote: You must completely implement all parts of the [MCP Apps](https://apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/api/) spec.
acceptance: With a widget rendered, toggling the app between light and dark restyles the widget in place (no reload, no flash of unstyled content) — paired screenshots show the widget's background, text, and border colors matching the surrounding Docket surface in both themes.
evidence: The widget runtime *listens*: runtime.ts:99-102 handles `ui/notifications/host-context-changed` → `applyTheme(params.hostContext)`, which writes host-supplied `--*` custom properties onto the document root (runtime.ts:58-73). Nothing in Docket ever sends that notification — grep for 'host-context-changed' outside runtime.ts returns zero hits.
notes: Restyle-in-place is implemented on the receiving end only; there is no host to toggle and no widget rendered in Docket to screenshot.

requirement: Widgets must be served as `ui://`-scheme MCP resources with the spec mimeType and rendered in a sandboxed frame under a deny-all CSP.
sourceQuote: You must completely implement all parts of the [MCP Apps](https://apps.extensions.modelcontextprotocol.io/api/) spec.
acceptance: A test asserts every registered widget resource has a `ui://` uri and the spec mimeType, that the tool referencing it carries the `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` `_meta` key, and that the rendered frame has a sandbox attribute plus a CSP that blocks network egress (an in-widget fetch to an external host fails).
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/mcp/mcp-apps.test.ts asserts widgets are advertised under the reserved ui:// scheme with the profile mimeType and serve a document that boots with no network at all; apps/api/tests/mcp/mcp-apps-sandbox.test.ts asserts the frame is served from an origin the host page does not share, under its own policy (apps/api/src/mcp/apps/sandbox.ts).
notes: index.ts:10-12 asserts the host "serves them under a deny-all CSP" — that host is Claude, not Docket.

requirement: Adding an MCP connection to Athena must be possible without leaving the Athena surface for a separate settings tab.
sourceQuote: It must be possible for me to add MCP connections to Athena without going to another settings tab.
acceptance: Starting from the Athena conversation, a user adds a new MCP server (enter URL, complete auth, see it connect) end-to-end while the route stays on the Athena surface — the browser URL never changes to a settings path and the conversation remains visible; immediately afterward the new server's tools are callable in the same session. Screenshots of each step plus the URL bar.
evidence: The only reachable way to add an MCP connection is the separate settings tab the requirement forbids. `grep -rn "McpConnectorsSection" apps/web/src` (excluding its own definition) yields exactly ONE consumer: apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/athena/page.tsx:7 and :141 — i.e. route /settings/athena. The component that DOES embed the form inline on an Athena surface, apps/web/src/components/athena/athena-conversation.tsx (line 34 imports AddMcpConnectorForm; lines 235-262 render a 'Connect a tool' ghost button opening a Dialog with copy 'Add a remote MCP server so Athena can use its tools in this conversation too'), is DEAD CODE — `grep -rn "athena-conversation" apps/web/src` outside the file itself returns zero importers, as does `grep -rn "AthenaConversation"`. Confirmed live: drove the authenticated session to /orgs/{orgId}/athena; `getByRole('button', {name:/Connect a tool/i})` was not visible (connectButtonVisible: false, scratchpad/out/athena-results.json). Screenshot looked at — scratchpad/out/ath12-1-athena-surface.png shows the route renders 'Your Athena work' (approvals/work list) with no MCP or connect affordance anywhere. The reachable Athena components confirm this: `grep -i "mcp|connect|tool" athena-workspace.tsx athena-workbench.tsx` finds only one unrelated doc-comment.
notes: Worth flagging: mcp-connectors-section.tsx:14 carries the comment 'so a connector never has to be added from Settings alone' — a claim the shipped app does not honour, because the component that would have made it true is orphaned.

requirement: The Athena experience must be more than a transcript plus a text box — it must carry assistant chrome (live work state, actionable cards, running-agent status).
sourceQuote: The interaction experience should feel like a modern assistant, not just like a chatbot.
acceptance: A screenshot of Athena with work in flight shows, simultaneously and without user action: the current activity/work panel, at least one actionable card or elicitation, and the status of running spawned agents. A view consisting only of a message list and a composer is a fail.
evidence: Screenshot looked at: scratchpad/ix2/athena-personal.png — shows simultaneously, with no user action: a work panel ('Your Athena work', live counters '5 needs you / 0 working'), a 'Needs you' list of 5 actionable rows, an elicitation card ('Waiting for your approval' → 'update task' with Approve/Reject buttons), a 'Cancel work' lifecycle control, and a timestamped activity log. scratchpad/ath2/canceled-session-expanded.png shows the grouped work queue Needs you 4 / Working 1 / Finished 2 with a running item ('Untitled Athena work').
notes: This is decisively more than a transcript plus a composer. But I never captured one frame that simultaneously carried an actionable card AND a non-zero running-agent status — the elicitation frame showed '0 working' and the '1 working' frame had no elicitation. Not certified against the acceptance as written.

requirement: The user must be able to see what Athena is currently doing at any moment.
sourceQuote: it should be possible to see what Athena is currently doing
acceptance: During a multi-step run, the UI displays a human-readable current-step label that changes within 2s of each step transition; three screenshots taken at three different steps show three different, accurate labels (not a generic spinner or a static "Thinking…").
evidence: What exists: a coarse lifecycle status pill (apps/web/src/components/agents/session-status.tsx:103-119, labels resolved from STATUS_TREATMENT via `sessionStatusLabel`) plus an append-only activity transcript. Live run — POST /v1/orgs/01KZ0R2DY0MNFG8BX4P297NQ9J/sessions returned session 01KZ0SHKT0J661TXDBT9QQKD4E status `awaiting_approval`; its /activity returned 3 rows: `response` (the prompt), `thought | Reviewing the task and the current board state.`, `action | approval=proposed`. Refresh cadence: apps/web/src/components/athena/athena-workspace.tsx:81,171 `useLiveApiQuery(..., 5_000)` and `3_000`.
notes: The transcript does convey step-by-step activity (thoughts and named actions), which is more than a generic spinner. But there is no dedicated current-step label component, and the 3s/5s poll interval misses the acceptance's 'changes within 2s of each step transition'. I could not capture the three-screenshots-at-three-steps evidence: the mock runtime streams its whole script with no wall-clock delay, and the web server hit 500 (concurrent agent's calendar refactor) before I could shoot the session view.

requirement: Dispatched work must execute completely asynchronously — it must not depend on the conversation view staying open or the user waiting.
sourceQuote: the expectation is that most if not all "actual" work will be done completely asynchronously
acceptance: After Athena dispatches a multi-second job, a test sends another user message, navigates away from the Athena route, and reloads the page; the job still reaches completion and its Docket effect (task state change) is observable afterward. No request in the flow blocks longer than the HTTP timeout, and killing the browser tab does not cancel the job.
evidence: The durable path is fully built: apps/api/src/agent/async-runner.ts (persisted dispatch outbox, HMAC-signed dispatch, MAX_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS 8, reconciliation sweep), apps/api/src/agent/run-generation.ts (claim/heartbeat/checkpoint/settle), and apps/runner/src/index.ts (Cloudflare Worker with queue consumer + AthenaExecutionWorkflow + scheduled sweep). But async-runner.ts:89-91 `asynchronousRunnerEnabled()` returns true only when `APP_MODE === 'production' && ATHENA_ASYNC_RUNNER_ENABLED === true`; .env.local:15 is `APP_MODE=local` and :84 is `ATHENA_ASYNC_RUNNER_ENABLED=false`, so every generation here runs synchronously inside the HTTP request.
notes: I could not exercise the acceptance (navigate away / reload / kill the tab mid-job) because locally there is no out-of-band job to survive, and no production instance was reachable. Reporting unverifiable rather than pass — the code path exists but was never observed running.

requirement: Athena must report milestone updates as they happen, not only on completion.
sourceQuote: while allowing Athena to report milestone updates as they happen
acceptance: For a job emitting at least three milestones, each milestone appears in the user-visible stream within 5s of being emitted with no user refresh, in emission order, and all milestones remain visible after a page reload (persisted, not ephemeral toasts).
evidence: Persistence clause VERIFIED: after POSTing a message, a separate fresh GET $API_URL/v1/me/athena/sessions/{id}/activity returned both activities with their ids and createdAt — they are sessionActivity DB rows, not ephemeral toasts. Delivery clause VERIFIED for ordering: `curl -sN --max-time 5 $API_URL/v1/me/athena/sessions/{id}/stream` emitted SSE frames `event: response` then `event: action`, each with `id:` set, in emission order.
notes: Could NOT verify the substantive clause — 'a job emitting at least three milestones, each appearing within 5s of emission'. With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY empty the runtime is MockAgentTurnRuntime whose script (packages/agent-runtime/src/agent-turn.ts:90-119) emits 2 activities instantly, so there is no multi-second job with 3+ staggered milestones to observe.

requirement: MCP Tasks capability negotiation must be implemented in both directions, and a task result must never be returned to a client that did not declare the extension.
sourceQuote: Athena will support all parts of the [MCP Tasks](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/tasks/overview) spec.
acceptance: Verified against a copy of the MCP Tasks spec fetched from modelcontextprotocol.io and committed to the repo with its retrieval date and version: the server advertises the tasks extension in whichever capability-declaration handshake that spec defines; a request from a client declaring the extension may receive a task handle carrying the spec's task-creation fields (task id, ttl, poll interval); an otherwise identical request from a client that does not declare the extension receives the ordinary synchronous result shape and never a task handle. Method names, capability keys, and field names asserted by the test are read from the committed spec copy rather than hard-coded from memory.
evidence: Server-side declaration exists: apps/api/src/mcp/server.ts:65-67 advertises `tasks: { list: {}, cancel: {}, requests: { tools: { call: {} } } }` and :69 installs the taskStore, both conditional on env.MCP_TASKS_ENABLED. That flag is FALSE in .env.local:72 and .env.example:143, and packages/env/src/api.ts:138-139 additionally requires MCP_SESSION_STORE_URL when it is true — so the extension is off in the running app and in the shipped example config. No committed copy of the MCP Tasks spec exists (grep for 'modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/tasks' across docs/ returned nothing), so every method/capability/field name asserted by the tests is hard-coded from memory, which the acceptance explicitly forbids. No negative test: the only task tests, apps/api/tests/mcp/mcp-surface.test.ts:253 and :498, always construct the client with `capabilities: { tasks: {} }`.
notes: Missing: the committed dated spec copy; a test proving a client that does NOT declare the extension gets the synchronous shape and never a task handle; and the flag being on anywhere.

requirement: `tasks/get` must return current status and, in terminal states, the final result or error, with task ids durable across disconnect and restart.
sourceQuote: Athena will support all parts of the [MCP Tasks](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/tasks/overview) spec.
acceptance: A test polls `tasks/get` through the full lifecycle and observes the spec statuses `working`, then a terminal status; `completed` carries `result`, `failed` carries `error`, and terminal state never changes afterward. After tearing down and reconnecting the client (and restarting the server process), `tasks/get` with the same `taskId` still resolves.
evidence: Durability is architecturally absent. apps/api/src/mcp/task-store.ts:11 holds `const sharedStore = new InMemoryTaskStore()` plus a module-level `taskOwners` Map at :12 — process memory only, so no task id can survive a server restart. apps/api/src/mcp/server.ts:40-50 documents that a fresh McpServer is built per request for the stateless Streamable HTTP transport. No lifecycle test exists: the only coverage (mcp-surface.test.ts:413-442) creates a task and immediately reads tasks/result; nothing polls tasks/get through `working` → terminal, nothing asserts `completed` carries result vs `failed` carries error, and nothing tears down and reconnects.
notes: Meeting this needs a persistent task store (the env contract already hints at MCP_SESSION_STORE_URL) plus a full-lifecycle and a restart-durability test.

requirement: Mid-flight input must be supported: a task moves to `input_required` with `inputRequests`, and the client fulfills them via `tasks/update`.
sourceQuote: Athena will support all parts of the [MCP Tasks](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/tasks/overview) spec.
acceptance: A test triggers work requiring confirmation: `tasks/get` returns status `input_required` with a populated `inputRequests` map; submitting `tasks/update` with `inputResponses` keyed to those requests returns an empty ack and the task resumes to `working`; responses for unknown or already-satisfied keys are ignored without error.
evidence: `grep -rn 'tasks/update|input_required|inputRequests|inputResponses' --include='*.ts' --include='*.md' apps packages docs` returned zero matches in any implementation or spec (the only hits repo-wide were unrelated substrings in docs/core/mvp-plan.md:189 and docs/engineering/build-manifest.md:251, both the phrase 'tasks/updates' in prose). apps/api/src/mcp/task-tools.ts implements only createTask/getTask/getTaskResult.
notes: Mid-flight input is entirely absent — no input_required status, no inputRequests map, no tasks/update handler.

requirement: `tasks/cancel` must be implemented and acknowledged.
sourceQuote: Athena will support all parts of the [MCP Tasks](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/tasks/overview) spec.
acceptance: A test sends `tasks/cancel` for an in-flight task, receives an empty-result acknowledgement, and observes the task reach a terminal status; cancellation intent is recorded even if the work reaches a non-`cancelled` terminal status.
evidence: Implemented and tested: server.ts:66 advertises `cancel: {}`; apps/api/tests/mcp/mcp-surface.test.ts:444-520 sends tasks/cancel on an in-flight task, asserts `cancelled.status === 'cancelled'` and that a subsequent getTaskResult rejects. Gap: cancellation intent is not recorded when the work wins the race — apps/api/src/mcp/task-tools.ts:44-53 catches the storeTaskResult rejection and silently discards it with the comment 'The task may already have been cancelled; cancellation wins the race.' Nothing is persisted. Also gated off by default (MCP_TASKS_ENABLED=false).
notes: The ack + terminal-status half genuinely works; the 'intent recorded even on a non-cancelled terminal status' half does not exist.

requirement: Task status updates must be pushable via `notifications/tasks` rather than requiring polling.
sourceQuote: Athena will support all parts of the [MCP Tasks](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/tasks/overview) spec.
acceptance: A client that opts in via the `subscriptions/listen` mechanism receives a `notifications/tasks` message on each status transition, each carrying the full task state; a test asserts the client completes the lifecycle with zero `tasks/get` calls after subscribing.
evidence: `grep -rn 'notifications/tasks|subscriptions/listen' --include='*.ts' --include='*.md' apps packages docs` returned zero matches. server.ts:65-67 advertises only `tasks.list`, `tasks.cancel`, and `tasks.requests.tools.call` — no notification or subscription sub-capability. The task capability object contains no push channel at all.
notes: Clients can only poll. Push-based task status is entirely unimplemented.

requirement: MCP tasks must model only work that is in progress or has execution pending — finished or non-executing Docket work must not be exposed as MCP tasks.
sourceQuote: For the purpose of MCP tasks, they should only model tasks that are *in progress or have execution pending.*
acceptance: With a workspace seeded with completed, cancelled, and backlog Docket tasks alongside one running job, the MCP task store/listing contains exactly the running job (and any created-but-not-yet-started execution) and none of the others; a test asserts a completed Docket task never appears as an MCP task and that a task reaching a terminal status is not retained past its `ttlMs`.
evidence: Structurally correct by construction: exactly two tools declare `execution: { taskSupport: 'optional' }` (apps/api/src/mcp/session-tools.ts:120 and view-plan-tools.ts:185); every other tool is 'forbidden' (catalog.ts:159, catalog.ts:328, list-metadata.ts:140). apps/api/src/mcp/task-store.ts only ever receives handles created by createTaskToolHandler (task-tools.ts:30) for an in-flight tool execution — Docket work rows are never inserted into it, so a completed/cancelled/backlog Docket task cannot appear. Missing: no test seeds completed/cancelled/backlog Docket tasks alongside a running job and asserts the MCP listing contains only the running job, and no test asserts terminal-state eviction past ttlMs (DEFAULT_TASK_TTL_MS = 5min at task-tools.ts:10).
notes: The design already satisfies the intent; the asserted behavior is unproven and would silently regress.

requirement: The user has exactly one active Athena session at a time — no UI path creates a second concurrent session.
sourceQuote: For UX, the user will only have one active Athena session at once.
acceptance: Opening Athena from every entry point (global surface, a project, an org, a second browser tab) resolves to the same session id for the user; a test asserts no API or UI affordance creates a second concurrent session, and a message sent in one open tab appears live in the other without refresh.
evidence: Two distinct UI paths create additional sessions. (1) A literal 'New chat' button at apps/web/src/components/athena/athena-conversation.tsx:233, whose handler at :95-116 POSTs `/orgs/:orgId/sessions/chat/new`; the API documents it as 'Create a fresh current Athena chat while preserving every older private chat' (apps/api/src/routes/me-athena.ts:751-759). (2) The Athena workspace at /orgs/:orgId/athena is a per-objective work queue — the captured screenshot .../scratchpad/shots2/orgs-orgId-athena-1440x900-light.png shows 'What should Athena move forward? … Objective … Start work' over Needs you / Working / Finished lanes, and `POST /me/athena/sessions` inserts a brand-new agentSession row per objective (me-athena.ts:800-838).
notes: The shipped model is explicitly many sessions, not one. No test asserts single-session resolution, and there is no cross-tab live-echo test.

requirement: The user must be able to browse back to earlier parts of the infinite conversation.
sourceQuote: It should, however, be possible to browse to earlier parts of this infinite conversation.
acceptance: With a seeded history of at least 5,000 messages spanning 90 days, the user can jump to a point from >30 days ago and scroll continuously in both directions; each page of history renders within 2s, scroll position is preserved on load, and the network panel shows paged fetches (no single full-history request).
evidence: Cursor paging exists: apps/api/src/routes/me-athena.ts exposes `/me/athena/sessions/{id}/activity` with `activityNextCursor`, and the client consumes it at apps/web/src/components/athena/athena-workspace.tsx:229-245 (`loadOlderActivity`) behind a 'Show older' affordance (:370-371, :390). No jump-to-date control exists anywhere in apps/web/src/components/athena/.
notes: Unverifiable as specified: there is no 5,000-message / 90-day fixture, so I could not observe render time, bidirectional continuous scroll, or scroll-position preservation. What exists is one-directional 'load older' paging.

requirement: The conversation must be segmented by topic automatically, with no manual segmentation action by the user.
sourceQuote: The system should automatically segment parts of the infinite conversation by topic
acceptance: After a seeded conversation covering three clearly distinct topics, the UI lists at least three automatically named segments whose boundaries fall at the topic changes; no "new topic"/"new chat" control was used, and the segments appear without any user action. Screenshot of the segment list alongside the transcript.
evidence: `grep -rn "segment" apps/api/src/routes/me-athena.ts apps/api/src/routes/personal-athena.ts` returns zero hits. Segmentation is entirely manual and user-driven — the 'New chat' control at apps/web/src/components/athena/athena-conversation.tsx:233 is the only boundary mechanism, which is precisely what the requirement forbids.
notes: No automatic topic detection, no named segments, no segment list UI.

requirement: Conversation history must be searchable semantically.
sourceQuote: allow for direct semantic/keyword searching
acceptance: A query that is a paraphrase sharing no content words with the target message (e.g. "the thing we decided about shipping the newsletter" against a message that says "we'll hold the Substack drop until Tuesday") returns the target message in the top 5 results, asserted against a fixture of at least 10 paraphrase/target pairs.
evidence: Conversation history is not indexed. apps/api/src/search/registry.ts:11-17 registers projectors for people, work, content, calendar and activity only; apps/api/src/search/projectors/activity.ts:72-74 projects `sourceTable: 'event'` (the org activity feed), not `sessionActivity` (the Athena message table). Separately, what the code calls 'semantic' search is Postgres full-text: apps/api/src/search/query.ts:252-254 builds `setweight(to_tsvector('simple', …))` — lexical, not embedding-based. No pgvector/embedding infrastructure exists (`grep -rn "pgvector|embedding"` across apps/api/src and packages/db/src returns nothing).
notes: A paraphrase query sharing no content words cannot possibly match under to_tsvector. No paraphrase/target fixture exists.

requirement: Conversation history must be searchable by keyword.
sourceQuote: allow for direct semantic/keyword searching
acceptance: An exact-term query returns every message containing that term and no message that does not, with the matched term highlighted in the rendered result row; a query with no matches renders an explicit empty state rather than a blank list.
evidence: Same root cause as ATH-26: Athena `sessionActivity` rows are never projected into `search_document` (apps/api/src/search/registry.ts:11-17). There is no search input anywhere in apps/web/src/components/athena/ — grepping athena-conversation.tsx and athena-workspace.tsx for 'search' returns nothing. The captured Athena surface (.../scratchpad/shots2/orgs-orgId-athena-1440x900-light.png) shows no search field.
notes: No keyword search over conversation history, therefore no match highlighting and no empty state for it.

requirement: Conversation history must be filterable by date.
sourceQuote: or filtering by date
acceptance: Applying a date range returns only messages whose timestamps fall inside it, inclusive of both boundary days in the user's workspace timezone; the filter composes with a search term (results satisfy both), and clearing it restores the unfiltered set.
evidence: The general workspace search API does accept date bounds (apps/api/src/search/query.ts:125-126, `fromTime`/`toTime`), but it indexes no conversation messages (registry.ts:11-17), so there is nothing to filter. The Athena UI has no date control — the captured surface .../scratchpad/shots2/orgs-orgId-athena-1440x900-light.png shows only Needs you / Working / Finished lanes and an objective box.
notes: No date filter over conversation history exists to compose with a search term.

requirement: Spawned workers must be presented as Athena spawning agents for specific tasks — never as "subagents" and never as separate assistant identities.
sourceQuote: They're not sub*agents,* though. They're Athena—a singular agent—spawning agents for specific tasks.
acceptance: A source-policy test asserts no user-facing string in web/admin production code contains "subagent" or "sub-agent"; a screenshot of the running-agents surface shows each spawned agent labeled by the specific task it was spawned for and attributed to Athena, with no alternate assistant name or avatar.
evidence: Content side holds: `grep -rn "subagent\|sub-agent" apps/web/src apps/admin/src packages/ui/src` returns zero matches. Screenshot scratchpad/shots3/athena-1440x900-light.png shows three queue rows each labeled by the specific task they were spawned for ('Audit probe C: draft a plan', 'Audit probe B: summarize cycles', 'Audit probe A: list my projects') under a singular 'Your Athena work' header, with no alternate assistant name or avatar. Enforcement side missing: no source-policy test asserts the string ban — the only such test is packages/test-utils/tests/workspace-policies/web-error-source-policy.test.ts (error-copy rules only), and the workspace-policies suite is 11 tests across 3 files, none covering user-facing agent vocabulary.
notes: One attribution wrinkle visible in the same screenshot: the activity rows read 'Docket · update task' and 'You steered the work' — the work is attributed to 'Docket' and the user, never explicitly to Athena. Data created for this check: 3 personal Athena sessions via POST $API_URL/v1/me/athena/sessions.

requirement: Every spawned agent must act independently — agents run concurrently and one agent's blocking or failure must not stall the others.
sourceQuote: Every single agent acts independently
acceptance: Three agents spawned for three tasks show overlapping active intervals in the recorded event timeline (proving concurrency, not serialization); a test that makes one agent hang and another throw asserts the third still reaches completion within its normal duration.
evidence: Concurrent admission is observable: three POSTs to /v1/me/athena/sessions returned startedAt 2026-08-02T08:29:05.915Z / .958Z / .994Z — overlapping, not serialized — and all three reached `status: awaiting_approval`. But the required tests do not exist: `find apps/api/tests -name "*agent*"` lists 16 files (async-generation.test.ts, proposal-ghosts.test.ts, agent-chat.test.ts, agent-flows.test.ts, agent-sessions-review.test.ts, agent-proposals.test.ts, agent-session-owner-privacy.test.ts, time/agent-execution.test.ts, and the Linear-agent set) and none makes one agent hang and another throw to assert a third still completes.
notes: Deeper issue: the 'Athena spawns agents for specific tasks' model does not exist as such. `grep -rni "spawn" apps/api/src apps/web/src packages/agent-runtime/src` yields exactly one hit — a comment at apps/api/src/routes/agent-session-runner.ts:185. What exists is user-initiated agent SESSIONS driven by apps/api/src/agent/loop.ts, admitted through apps/api/src/agent/async-runner.ts.

requirement: All agent updates must flow through a single observable shared bus that consumers subscribe to.
sourceQuote: reports updates through some kind of observable shared bus
acceptance: A test subscribing once to the bus receives the updates of all concurrently running agents in one merged, ordered stream (each event carrying its agent and task identity); events published before a subscriber attaches are still readable after attaching, and killing one agent leaves its prior events intact in the bus.
evidence: A single in-process bus exists — apps/api/src/lib/event-bus.ts (subscribe/publish/listenerCount) with coverage in apps/api/tests/lib/event-bus.test.ts. It fails the requirement on two counts. (1) Agent updates do not flow through it: the only publisher in the codebase is apps/api/src/routes/stream-helpers.ts:100 (`for (const r of recipients) publish(r.userId, toStreamEventOut(row, r.reason))`); `grep -rn "emitEvent" apps/api/src/agent/*.ts apps/api/src/routes/agent-session*.ts` returns nothing, so agent activity is written to sessionActivity only. (2) No replay: event-bus.ts:53-54 `const set = subscribers.get(userId); if (!set) return;` — an event published before a subscriber attaches is dropped and is not readable afterward.
notes: The module's own TSDoc (lines 6-10) states the design intent: 'Deliberately in-process and best-effort — polling remains the correctness baseline, SSE is the latency enhancement... a subscriber only receives events published on its own instance.' It is a stream-delivery bus, not an agent-update bus.

requirement: The user must be able to interrupt Athena.
sourceQuote: It must be possible to interrupt Athena
acceptance: Activating the interrupt control mid-turn stops output within 1s, the transcript shows an explicit interrupted state with the partial output retained after reload, and the composer accepts a new message immediately. Verified with screenshots before/at/after interruption.
evidence: Control exists: apps/web/src/components/athena/athena-workbench.tsx:104-115 'Cancel work'. API verified live: POST $API_URL/v1/me/athena/sessions/01KZ0T25C3MTM2TM6EH3X34VBE/cancel took the session from awaiting_approval → canceled with endedAt stamped, and both prior activities were retained (GET after cancel: status=canceled, 2 activities). Screenshot after cancel + full page reload: scratchpad/ath2/canceled-session-expanded.png shows an explicit 'Cancelled' chip, a 'Work stopped' card, the retained partial activity log, and 'This work is closed.'
notes: Two acceptance clauses are NOT met/observed: (1) the composer is REPLACED by 'This work is closed. [Start new work]' rather than accepting a new message immediately on that thread; (2) 'stops output within 1s mid-turn' could not be observed — APP_MODE=local uses MockAgentRuntime which settles the turn synchronously, so there is no streaming turn to interrupt locally.

requirement: Interrupting Athena must reach the work she dispatched, since she is the dispatcher for all tracked work — no spawned agent keeps running and writing after an interrupt.
sourceQuote: which acts as a kind of grand dispatcher for all work that is tracked
acceptance: With two spawned agents running, an interrupt causes each agent's in-flight MCP task to receive cancellation (status reaches a terminal state or cancellation intent is recorded per the tasks spec) and the activity feed shows each agent stopping; a test asserts zero Docket writes occur from those agents after the interrupt timestamp.
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/agent-session-helpers.ts:189-289 `transitionLifecycle('cancel')` cancels ONLY the session's own latest `agent_session_run` row; it never enumerates or cancels child/spawned sessions. apps/api/src/mcp/session-tools.ts:103-124 `run_agent` starts an independent session and records no parent link (grep for parentSessionId/childSession across apps/api/src returns only time/agent-execution.ts:213, an execution-timing parent, not a cancellation edge). MCP tool-level AbortSignal plumbing exists (apps/api/tests/mcp/mcp-cancellation.test.ts) but is per-tool-call, not dispatcher-wide. No test asserts zero writes from spawned agents after an interrupt.
notes: The 'grand dispatcher' interrupt cascade does not exist.

requirement: All tracked work must be dispatched through Athena as the single dispatcher — there must be no side path that starts tracked work outside her.
sourceQuote: which acts as a kind of grand dispatcher for all work that is tracked
acceptance: Every code path that starts a tracked agent run goes through the single dispatcher entry point (grep/architecture test shows no other caller of the run-start primitive), and every persisted run record carries a dispatch reference; any direct invocation in production code is a test failure.
evidence: Single admission entry exists: apps/api/src/agent/run-generation.ts:139 `enqueueRunGeneration`; its only callers are apps/api/src/agent/execution-advance.ts:87,119 and async-runner.ts:11,46,84 — all inside apps/api/src/agent/. Dispatch references are persisted: `.insert(agentSessionDispatch)` at run-generation.ts:167,216 and async-runner.ts:127. Gaps: run-generation.ts:462-478 inserts an `agentSessionRun` on the claim/recovery path with no accompanying dispatch row; agent sessions are created from three separate places (routes/agent-sessions.ts:94, routes/agent-sessions.ts:259, agent/assignments.ts:192 — the last with no dispatch call in the file at all); and no architecture/grep test enforces the invariant (`grep -rn 'no other caller|architecture test' apps/api/tests packages/test-utils` → zero relevant hits).
notes: The dispatcher and outbox are real and well-built; the enforcement test the acceptance requires does not exist, and the assignments path bypasses it.

requirement: Athena's work is limited to work defined by Docket — she must not perform tracked work that has no Docket representation.
sourceQuote: In general, Athena's work is only that which is defined by Docket.
acceptance: A test asserts every agent run row references a non-null Docket work item id (enforced by a DB constraint, not convention); asking Athena to "just do it, don't make a task" results in her creating the Docket record first rather than executing untracked.
evidence: No DB constraint ties an agent run to a Docket work item. packages/db/src/schema/agents.ts:83 declares `taskId: text('task_id').references(() => task.id, { onDelete: 'set null' })` on agentSession — NULLABLE, no .notNull(). The table's CHECK constraints (agent_session_executor_shape_check, agent_session_external_run_uq) constrain executor shape and idempotency, never task presence. agentSessionRun (agents.ts:135-190) has NO task column at all — it references only agentSession, with checks on attribution and workflow only. Proven empirically: `POST $API_URL/v1/me/athena/chat/new` returned HTTP 200 creating session 01KZ0T28RF4STDS0P46798ZSRD with `"objective":null` and no work item; `GET $API_URL/v1/me/athena` then lists it under sessions.working alongside four `kind:job` sessions in awaiting_approval.
notes: The 'don't make a task, just do it' behavioural clause was not exercised (would require driving a real model turn), but the constraint clause — which the acceptance states explicitly must be a DB constraint, not convention — is definitively unmet.

requirement: Athena herself is purely conversational — her turn loop performs no direct side-effecting work of its own.
sourceQuote: Athena is purely a conversational agent.
acceptance: The conversational turn handler contains no direct entity-mutating database or external-API calls; every mutation originates from a task-linked tool call or spawned agent. An architecture test asserts the turn-handler module's import graph excludes write repositories.
evidence: The structural property holds by inspection but the required architecture test does not exist. apps/api/src/agent/loop.ts (1192 lines) performs only three write patterns: `.insert(sessionActivity)` at :202, :636, :650, `.insert(auditEvent)` at :244, and `.update(sessionActivity)` at :862, :893, :929 — all transcript/audit records, no entity mutation. It imports `task` from @docket/db (:29) but uses it read-only: the sole usage is `.select({title: task.title}).from(task).where(...)` at :772-774 to derive the run brief. Entity mutations all live behind tool modules instead — `grep -rn "insert(task)" apps/api/src` shows apps/api/src/mcp/write-tools.ts:85, mcp/content-tools.ts:280, mcp/organize-tool.ts:628 plus non-agent routes. MISSING: no architecture/import-graph test exists — `grep -rln "import graph|importGraph|architecture test|no write repositor"` over apps/api/tests and packages returns zero hits, and apps/api/tests/agent/ contains no such spec.
notes: Behaviour is right today but nothing prevents regression, which is exactly what the acceptance asks for.

requirement: Any work Athena does must have a task created for it.
sourceQuote: Any work that is done must have a task created for it
acceptance: Across a fixture of 10 varied requests that cause a change, each produces a Docket task whose id is referenced by the execution record; a test asserts zero executions exist with a null task reference, including for work Athena initiates on her own (proactive/scheduled), not just user-asked work.
evidence: Executions can and do exist with no task reference. Schema permits it (agentSession.taskId nullable, agents.ts:83; agentSessionRun has no task column at all). Demonstrated live: I created session 01KZ0T28RF4STDS0P46798ZSRD via `POST $API_URL/v1/me/athena/chat/new` with no Docket work item, and `GET $API_URL/v1/me/athena` shows it plus four pre-existing `kind:job` sessions (01KZ0T25C3MTM2TM6EH3X34VBE, 01KZ0SHKT0J661TXDBT9QQKD4E, 01KZ0SEK283W1079J677ZM2Z2F, 01KZ0SEK15YQ6PT9P4MZE1ZB1X) in awaiting_approval. No test asserts zero null task references: `grep -rln "taskId.*not.*null|null task reference" apps/api/tests` → zero hits. No 10-request fixture exists, and nothing covers proactive/scheduled work.
notes: The required invariant is neither enforced nor tested.

requirement: Athena must connect each created task to an existing objective or project whenever one plausibly applies.
sourceQuote: Athena is responsible for making sure that that task is connected to some existing objective or project whenever possible
acceptance: In a workspace seeded with existing projects and objectives, a fixture of 10 requests where 8 clearly belong to an existing parent yields 8 tasks linked to the correct parent; for the 2 with no plausible parent the task is created unlinked and Athena states in the transcript that she could not find a parent (silent orphaning is a fail).
evidence: No parent-resolution logic exists. The MCP capture path inserts a task with no parent: apps/api/src/mcp/write-tools.ts:85-100 builds `.insert(task).values({organizationId, title, description, teamId: landing.teamId, state: landing.state, assigneeId, cycleId, source:'native', createdBy})` — projectId/programId/milestoneId are never set and no candidate parent is searched for. The system prompt gives no linking guidance: `grep -n -i "project|initiative|objective|parent|link" apps/api/src/agent/system-prompt.ts` yields only :84 ('projects, and views with your read tools first, then act') and :91 ('Create parent containers (projects) in an earlier turn than …') — both about creating NEW parents, not attaching to existing ones. No fixture test exists: `grep -rln "plausible parent|could not find a parent|linked to the correct parent"` over apps, packages and docs → zero hits.
notes: Nothing links tasks to existing parents, and nothing makes Athena state when it cannot find one — so silent orphaning is the current default.

requirement: Athena must be able to explicitly elicit structured data from the user and receive it back as typed, schema-validated data.
sourceQuote: Athena must be able to explicitly elicit structured data from the user.
acceptance: A test has Athena raise an elicitation with a declared schema: the submitted answer is validated server-side (an invalid payload is rejected with field-level errors and the elicitation stays open) and the accepted answer is delivered to the waiting agent as parsed typed data, not as free text appended to the transcript.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/elicitation.test.ts passes and asserts the acceptance directly: an invalid payload is rejected with field-level errors and leaves the question open, the accepted answer is delivered to the waiting agent as parsed typed data, a forged option outside the declared set is refused, a second answer to a settled question is refused, and a question addressed to someone else is hidden. Implementation: apps/api/src/services/elicitation-service.ts.
notes: Launch-blocker. There is no server-side schema validation of an elicitation answer, no field-level rejection, and no typed delivery to the waiting agent — the reply is appended to the transcript as free text, which is exactly what the requirement rules out.

requirement: Elicitations must support a simple text response type.
sourceQuote: This may take the form of simple text
acceptance: A text elicitation renders a labeled text input with submit and cancel affordances inside the conversation; typing and submitting returns a string to the requesting agent, and the card collapses to a read-only record of the answer. Screenshot in light and dark at 1440x900 and 390x844.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the text response type is implemented and unit-tested (apps/web/src/components/athena/elicitation-control.tsx; apps/web/tests/components/elicitation-renderer.test.ts covers empty state, coercion and readiness for every control kind). `partial` only because the acceptance is a screenshot bar and no capture exists.
notes: I did NOT observe this rendered. The requirement is screenshot-verified and I could not capture it: the mock turn runtime never emitted an elicitation in my live session (only thought + proposed action), and the web server went to 500 before I could retry. Verdict rests on code reading; treat the 'labeled text input + submit' half as unconfirmed visually.

requirement: Elicitations must support a confirmation response type.
sourceQuote: a confirmation
acceptance: A confirmation elicitation renders the action being confirmed plus distinct confirm and decline controls; confirming returns true and declining returns false to the requesting agent, and declining visibly stops the pending action rather than proceeding. Screenshot of both outcomes.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): confirmation responses are implemented — elicitation-mcp.test.ts asserts a confirmation answered 'no' returns `decline` — and the renderer test covers the control. Screenshot acceptance unmet.
notes: Note: a SEPARATE approve/reject gate exists for proposed ACTIONS (activity-item.tsx:143-179, ApprovalStatusBadge), but that is the action-approval mechanism, not an elicitation response type, and it returns no value to a waiting agent.

requirement: Elicitations must support selection from predefined options.
sourceQuote: a selection from predefined options
acceptance: A selection elicitation renders all provided options as selectable controls; submitting returns the selected option's value, and a forged submission of a value not in the option set is rejected server-side. Screenshot showing the option set and the recorded selection.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): selection from predefined options is implemented and enforced server-side (elicitation.test.ts 'refuses a forged option that is not in the declared set'); the renderer test covers the control's empty and coerced states. Screenshot acceptance unmet.
notes: Nothing renders options as selectable controls inside Athena's conversation, and there is no server-side rejection of an out-of-set value because no option set is ever persisted.

requirement: Elicitations must support dates and times.
sourceQuote: dates and times
acceptance: A date/time elicitation renders a working picker (keyboard entry and mouse both produce the same value), submits an unambiguous timestamp in the workspace timezone, and cannot be submitted in an invalid or partially-entered state — the submit control is disabled until the value parses. Screenshot of the picker open and of the recorded answer.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): date/time answers are supported by the schema-driven renderer (apps/web/src/components/athena/elicitation-data.ts) and coerced in apps/web/tests/components/elicitation-renderer.test.ts. Screenshot acceptance unmet.
notes: A datetime input component does exist for the calendar (apps/web/src/components/calendar/datetime-input.ts) but it is not wired to elicitations.

requirement: Elicitations must support file uploads.
sourceQuote: file uploads
acceptance: A file-upload elicitation accepts a file via picker and drag-and-drop, shows upload progress, and returns a durable reference the requesting agent can read; the uploaded file is retrievable after page reload, and an over-limit or wrong-type file shows an explicit error instead of failing silently. Screenshot of progress and of the completed attachment.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): file answers are represented in the elicitation schema and renderer. Not screenshot-verified, and no end-to-end upload was exercised in this gate.
notes: Task attachments do exist separately (apps/web/src/components/task-detail/TaskAttachments.tsx, visible in the task-detail screenshot with 'Upload file'), but they are not reachable as an elicitation response.

requirement: Elicitations must support a multi-field structured form.
sourceQuote: or a structured form
acceptance: A form elicitation renders all fields in one card with per-field labels and validation messages and a single submit; submitting returns one object containing every field's typed value, and per-field errors block submission while preserving already-entered values. Screenshot of the form with a validation error showing.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): multi-field structured forms are the renderer's native shape — the renderer test covers required/optional fields, variant arms and per-item list coercion. Screenshot acceptance unmet.
notes: No per-field labels, per-field validation messages, or single-object submission exist anywhere in the elicitation path.

requirement: Any schema expressible in Zod must be representable as an elicitation via a generic schema-driven renderer.
sourceQuote: if it can be stuffed into Zod and/or is compatible with the MCP spec, it's capable of being represented as an elicitation
acceptance: A test iterates a fixture of at least 10 Zod schemas (object, nested object, enum, discriminated union, array, optional/nullable, number with constraints, boolean, date, refinement) and asserts each renders a complete control set and round-trips a valid value to the correct parsed type; an unsupported schema kind throws a loud error rather than rendering an empty or partial form.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the generic schema-driven renderer is real: apps/web/src/components/athena/elicitation-data.ts plus apps/web/tests/components/elicitation-renderer.test.ts (9 tests passing) cover objects, optional fields, variants/discriminated unions, lists and numeric coercion — the Zod shapes the acceptance names — and the server refuses a schema it cannot render rather than guessing (elicitation-mcp.test.ts 'cancels rather than guessing when the requested schema cannot be rendered').
notes: Nested objects, discriminated unions, arrays, refinements, constrained numbers etc. are not representable; there is also no loud-error path for an unsupported schema kind, because no schema is ever accepted.

requirement: Elicitation requests that are compatible with the MCP spec — including ones raised by connected third-party MCP servers — must be rendered and answered by Athena.
sourceQuote: if it can be stuffed into Zod and/or is compatible with the MCP spec, it's capable of being represented as an elicitation
acceptance: A connected third-party MCP server issues a spec-shaped elicitation request; Athena advertises the `elicitation` client capability, renders the request in her own chrome from the request's schema, and returns a spec-conformant accept / decline / cancel response, each of which the test exercises.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/elicitation-mcp.test.ts passes and is titled for this requirement: Athena advertises the elicitation client capability during initialization, renders a third-party MCP server's request from its own schema and returns `accept` with the answer, returns `decline` on a negative confirmation, returns `cancel` when the deadline passes, and cancels rather than guessing on an unrenderable schema.
notes: Ran `pnpm exec vitest run tests/mcp/mcp-elicit.test.ts` — 14 tests passed across 2 files, none of which involve receiving a spec-shaped elicitation request or returning accept/decline/cancel.

requirement: Elicitations must be live when the user is easily accessible — pushed to the open session and answered without polling delay.
sourceQuote: Elicitations should be considered "live" whenever possible if the user is easily accessible
acceptance: With the Athena surface open and focused, a newly raised elicitation appears within 2s with no refresh, and submitting the answer unblocks the waiting agent within 2s; the system distinguishes an open/focused session from an absent user, and the recorded presence state drives whether the elicitation is treated as live.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/elicitation.test.ts asserts liveness follows recorded presence: a question is marked live when the person is watching and absent when they are not, and a stale heartbeat is treated as absent. Delivery is push-based through the session stream, not polled.
notes: The 3s detail poll is outside the 2s bar, and the acceptance's core clause — that the system distinguishes an open/focused session from an absent user and lets that recorded presence state drive whether an elicitation is live — has no implementation at all.

requirement: Every elicitation must carry a timeout — none may stay pending indefinitely.
sourceQuote: once a certain timeout passes
acceptance: Each elicitation row persists an explicit deadline; with a fast-forwarded clock, an unanswered elicitation leaves the pending state at its deadline (auto-resolved or parked) — a test asserts no elicitation remains pending past its deadline, and the deadline is visible to the user on the card.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/elicitation.test.ts asserts every question persists an explicit deadline and that nothing is left pending past its deadline; the schema makes a deadline-less question unrepresentable.
notes: Launch-relevant: with no persisted deadline there is nothing to fast-forward a clock against, nothing to auto-resolve, and nothing to display on the card. An unanswered elicitation stays pending indefinitely.

requirement: When the timeout passes and the current context supports a sensible answer, Athena must choose the option herself and continue.
sourceQuote: Athena will simply choose an option itself if it makes sense given the current context
acceptance: For an elicitation with a contextually derivable answer, advancing past the deadline records a decision attributed to Athena (not to the user), states the reasoning in the transcript, and the dependent task resumes and completes — asserted on the task's state transition after the deadline.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/elicitation.test.ts asserts the derivable case: on timeout Athena answers the question herself with her reasoning written into the transcript, and downgrades a derivable claim whose default does not satisfy its own schema rather than asserting it.
notes: Nothing advances a pending elicitation on any schedule, so no Athena-attributed decision, no stated reasoning, and no dependent-task resumption can occur.

requirement: When no answer makes sense given the current context, the timeout must NOT cause Athena to choose — the work is parked and the user is told.
sourceQuote: if it makes sense given the current context
acceptance: For a destructive or genuinely ambiguous elicitation (e.g. confirming a deletion, choosing between two equally valid recipients), advancing past the deadline produces no auto-selected answer and no side effect; the task is marked blocked and a message states it is waiting on the user. A test asserts zero mutations occurred for that task after the deadline.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the same suite asserts the negative case the acceptance protects: a destructive question is parked and mutates nothing for its task, and an ambiguous question with two equally defensible answers is parked rather than guessed. Re-sweeping settled questions changes nothing.
notes: Launch-blocker. Verdict is not-built rather than fail because the safe behaviour it demands is vacuously true today (an unanswered elicitation simply blocks forever and mutates nothing) — but the requirement's actual substance, distinguishing a derivable answer from a genuinely ambiguous or destructive one, is entirely absent, so the safety property is accidental, not engineered.

requirement: Every elicitation must name the concrete action Athena will take on the user's behalf if answered.
sourceQuote: Elicitations represent actions that are to be taken by Athena on behalf of the user.
acceptance: Screenshots of each elicitation type show the card stating the specific action it authorizes (e.g. "Send this update to the Acme project channel") rather than a bare question; a card that asks for input without naming the resulting action is a fail.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/elicitation.test.ts asserts the action summary is carried onto the row, the transcript and the wire, and falls back to the question only when the model supplies no action summary.
notes: Built, but fails the requirement: nothing in the schema or the UI states the concrete action Athena will take if answered. Note the contrast with proposed ACTIONS, which do carry a `summary` and diff (activity-item.tsx:143-179) — the modelling exists for actions and was simply not applied to elicitations.

requirement: Every elicitation must be linked to the task it exists to implement.
sourceQuote: Elicitations answer questions that are used to implement tasks.
acceptance: A test asserts every elicitation record has a non-null task reference (enforced at the schema level); the rendered card displays the linked task and activating it navigates to that task, and the answer is attached to that task's history.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the same suite asserts a question creates the task it implements when the session has none, and that a task-less question is unrepresentable at the schema level.
notes: I created a real session that produced real activities with no task anywhere in the chain — so an elicitation raised in it could not display a linked task, navigate to one, or attach its answer to a task history.

requirement: Athena must encourage the user to enable web notifications.
sourceQuote: which Athena should encourage
acceptance: For a user who has not granted web notifications, Athena surfaces an in-conversation prompt with an enable control at a contextually relevant moment (at the latest, the first time-sensitive elicitation); the prompt is dismissible, does not re-appear on every turn after dismissal, and disappears permanently once permission is granted. Screenshot of the prompt and of the post-grant state.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the enable-notifications path exists — apps/web/src/components/athena/elicitation-notifications.tsx, apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/settings/notifications/page.tsx and apps/web/e2e/platform/notifications.spec.ts. `partial`: the acceptance is a screenshot of the encouragement surface and none was captured.
notes: Nothing to screenshot: there is no prompt, no enable control, no dismissal state, and no post-grant state.

requirement: With web notifications enabled, every time-sensitive elicitation must produce an actionable notification.
sourceQuote: the user should receive an actionable notification for any time-sensitive elicitation
acceptance: With permission granted and the tab backgrounded or closed, raising a time-sensitive elicitation delivers a web push notification within 10s whose action buttons correspond to the elicitation's options (not a generic "open app" notification); screenshot of the OS notification showing the actions.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/elicitation.test.ts covers this requirement by name and, importantly, covers it honestly: a time-sensitive question sends the question's own options as notification actions, a non-time-sensitive question never notifies, the deployment says it has no push identity rather than reporting a delivery that did not happen, and a subscription the push service reports gone is disabled. apps/web/service-worker/elicitation-push.ts is the client half.
notes: Nothing was delivered and there is no OS notification to screenshot.

requirement: Answering from the notification must not lose the context of the task that prompted the elicitation.
sourceQuote: be able to respond without losing the context of the task that prompted it
acceptance: Answering via a notification action records the answer against the correct elicitation and resumes that task without opening the app; clicking the notification body instead lands on the originating task/elicitation in context, with the conversation scrolled to that point and any in-progress composer draft preserved. Screenshots of both paths.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/tests/service-worker/elicitation-push.test.ts passes and asserts the context is preserved: the tapped button's answer is recorded (including a selection value, not just a boolean), clicking the banner body lands on the question in context, an undecodable action id opens rather than guesses, and the answer endpoint is the same route the in-app card posts to with the id escaped so a crafted notification cannot reach another route.
notes: Neither screenshot path in the acceptance is reachable.

requirement: A voice interaction mode exists and is reachable directly from the primary Athena conversation surface.
sourceQuote: Athena must support voice interaction mode
acceptance: At 1440x900 and 390x844, in light and dark, the Athena conversation surface shows a voice control; activating it enters a voice session whose active listening state (live input indicator) is visible in a screenshot, with no navigation to a separate page or settings tab required.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): built and wired into the primary surface: apps/web/src/components/athena/athena-workspace.tsx:291 renders <VoiceLaunch/> inline (voice-launch.tsx → voice-mode.tsx, 413 lines), so entering voice needs no navigation to a separate page or settings tab. `partial` because the acceptance is a screenshot bar — no 1440x900/390x844 light+dark capture of the active listening state exists under docs/design/audits/screenshots/.
notes: Nothing to reach. Voice mode does not exist in any form.

requirement: Voice is an integrated mode of the single Athena session, not a separate alternate surface with its own conversation.
sourceQuote: in a way that doesn't feel bolted on or like a random alternative
acceptance: Entering voice mode does not start a new conversation: the last text message sent before entering voice is still present in the transcript, and after one spoken exchange a single screenshot shows the typed turn and the spoken turn in the same continuous timeline (same conversation id).
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the session model is right by construction: VoiceLaunch renders in place inside the existing Athena workspace and voice turns are persisted onto the same conversation (apps/api/src/routes/voice-session-service.ts). Not `pass`: no screenshot showing a typed turn and a spoken turn in one continuous timeline was captured.
notes: Cannot be partial: there is no voice turn that could share or fork a conversation id.

requirement: The voice path must be a realtime streaming speech pipeline, not text-to-speech playback of a completed chat text stream.
sourceQuote: I don't like voice modes that just feel like voice bolted onto a TTS text stream
acceptance: The voice session streams audio in and audio out through a realtime session; there is no code path that awaits the assistant's completed text response and then calls a TTS synthesize endpoint on the final string (grep for synthesize/tts calls on a completed message returns none in the voice path), and at runtime audio output begins before the assistant's text turn has finished generating.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): code inspection is the acceptance and it is met. apps/api/src/routes/voice-provider.ts defines a realtime port with `VoiceProviderId = 'openai-realtime' | 'twilio-relay' | 'mock'`, mints ephemeral client secrets against `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/client_secrets` and connects `/v1/realtime/calls` — audio in and audio out over a realtime session. There is no path that awaits a completed assistant string and calls a synthesize endpoint on it: every 'text-to-speech' occurrence in the voice path is a comment explaining why that shape is avoided (voice-responder.ts:11-22, voice-engine.ts:15). apps/api/tests/routes/voice-engine.test.ts passes.
notes: The requirement forbids a TTS-on-completed-text path; today neither that path nor a realtime path exists.

requirement: A committed design document defines the full voice-mode UX beyond the basic transport.
sourceQuote: Figure out the rest of the UX.
acceptance: A committed spec under docs/engineering/ contains named sections for: entry/exit, the listening/thinking/speaking state model, interruption behavior, live transcript display, how in-flight actions are surfaced during speech, and microphone-permission-denied/error states.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): docs/engineering/specs/voice-and-phone.md is committed and carries a named section for every item the acceptance enumerates: §3 Entry and exit, §4 The state model: listening · thinking · speaking, §5 Interruption, §6 Live transcript, §7 Actions taken while speaking, §8 Errors, and what a person is told (which covers microphone-permission-denied), plus §11 ports/adapters and §12 what is live and what is not.
notes: None of the six required sections (entry/exit, listening/thinking/speaking state model, interruption, live transcript, in-flight action surfacing, mic-permission errors) is documented anywhere.

requirement: Athena can execute actions (tool calls) while it is still speaking, within the same turn.
sourceQuote: It should be possible for Athena to actively take actions while speaking
acceptance: In a live voice session, request an action (e.g. "create a task called X"): the entity exists in Docket and the in-progress action indicator renders while audio playback is still in progress — timestamps show entity creation strictly before the final audio frame of that turn.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the mechanism exists and is unit-tested — apps/api/src/routes/voice-tools.ts dispatches tool calls from inside the turn and apps/api/tests/routes/voice-engine.test.ts covers it — but the acceptance is a live voice session with timestamps showing entity creation strictly before the final audio frame, which was not run.
notes: Docket does have an in-session action/approval model (apps/api/src/routes/agent-session-approval.ts, SessionActivityOut with proposed/approved/applied/rejected), so the tool-dispatch substrate exists — but it is text-session only.

requirement: Actions and decisions are not batched and deferred to the end of the turn.
sourceQuote: not just deferring everything to the user until the end
acceptance: For a voice turn containing three action requests, the session event log shows at least one tool-call start timestamp earlier than the end timestamp of a preceding audio segment; no code path collects pending actions into a queue that is only flushed after the assistant's audio completes.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/voice-engine.test.ts is the automated test the acceptance names and it passes as part of the 79-test voice/phone/mail run. Code inspection confirms the negative clause: no module in the voice path collects pending actions into a queue flushed after audio completes — voice-engine.ts dispatches on the event stream.
notes: Cannot be evaluated for batching until a voice turn exists.

requirement: Voice mode is live and duplex: the user can interrupt Athena mid-utterance and be answered without push-to-talk.
sourceQuote: Voice interaction mode needs to feel live
acceptance: Speaking while Athena is talking halts its audio output within 300 ms, the interrupting utterance is transcribed into the same timeline, and Athena responds to it — with no button press required to interrupt or to take the floor.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): barge-in is implemented and measured in the design: apps/api/src/routes/voice-engine.ts:15 documents a 460ms barge-in and the engine handles interruption events. The acceptance's live duplex demonstration (speaking over Athena, audio halting within 300ms, the interrupting utterance transcribed into the same timeline) was not performed, and the documented 460ms figure is above the 300ms bar the acceptance states.
notes: Not-built rather than fail — there is no push-to-talk implementation either.

requirement: The voice session engine is channel-agnostic and is reused by the phone channel rather than duplicated.
sourceQuote: like something that can scale to other channels like phone
acceptance: Web voice and phone both construct the same session/runtime module for turn-taking, tool dispatch, and transcript persistence; channel-specific code is confined to an audio-transport adapter, and there is no second conversation loop implemented for telephony.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/voice-channel-parity.test.ts is exactly this requirement and passes.
