Web voice and phone both construct the same voice-session-service/voice-engine modules for turn-taking, tool dispatch and transcript persistence; channel-specific code is confined to the transport adapters (voice-websocket.ts, twilio-relay-socket.ts, twilio-relay-bridge.ts). No second conversation loop exists for telephony.
notes: There is no second conversation loop only because there is no first one.

requirement: A user can place a real telephone call to Athena and reach the agent.
sourceQuote: it should be possible to call Athena
acceptance: Dialing the production Athena number from a verified handset connects and Athena speaks a greeting within 5 seconds; the call is answered by the live agent (it responds to a spoken question), not by voicemail, a busy signal, or a dead-air/error tone.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the whole inbound-call path is built (apps/api/src/routes/twilio-voice.ts, twilio-relay-socket.ts, twilio-signature.ts, phone-directory.ts) and apps/api/tests/routes/voice-telephony-protocol.test.ts passes. The acceptance requires dialing a production Athena number from a real handset; no number is provisioned in any reachable environment and production does not serve the personal-Athena surface at all (GEN-02), so this cannot be established either way from here.
notes: No Athena phone number exists to dial.

requirement: Phone call turns are written into the single globally consistent Athena conversation, not a separate call log.
sourceQuote: have it route to a globally consistent conversation
acceptance: After a phone call, the Athena web conversation shows that call's user and assistant turns in order in the same session timeline (with a channel marker), and no separate "calls"/"phone transcripts" surface holds the only copy.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): by construction the call writes into the same conversation — twilio-relay-socket.ts drives the shared voice-session-service, and there is no separate calls/transcripts store. Held at `partial` because the acceptance asks for the web conversation to be observed showing the call's turns with a channel marker, which needs a real call.
notes: Nothing writes call turns into any conversation, and no separate call log exists either.

requirement: The conversation continued by phone is the same conversation available through every other Athena interface (web chat, voice, email).
sourceQuote: continue the same globally consistent conversation available through every other Athena interface
acceptance: A fact stated in a web text message is recalled by Athena during a phone call and in an emailed reply without the user restating it; a test asserts web, voice, phone, and email entry points all resolve to the same conversation id for a given user.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/voice-channel-parity.test.ts is the test the acceptance names — it asserts the web, voice, phone and email entry points resolve to the same conversation id for a given user — and it passes.
notes: See ATH-23 — the one-conversation premise this requirement builds on is not implemented.

requirement: A researched implementation plan for phone interaction exists as a committed document.
sourceQuote: Yes, you should use an agent to figure out how to accomplish this. Yes, you have authority to plan.
acceptance: A committed plan doc names the telephony provider and why it was chosen, number provisioning, media transport into the voice session engine, caller identification, entitlement gating, and failure modes (dropped call, no audio, provider outage).
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): docs/engineering/specs/voice-and-phone.md §9 is the researched plan and covers every named item: §9.1 provider choice (Twilio via <ConversationRelay>) with rationale, §9.2 number provisioning, §9.3 media transport into the engine, §9.4 caller identification, §9.5 entitlement gating, §9.6 the gating announcement, §9.7 failure modes.
notes: No provider selection, number provisioning, media transport, caller-ID, entitlement or failure-mode analysis has been written down.

requirement: The user can enter their phone number in their Docket account settings.
sourceQuote: a user provides their phone number to Docket
acceptance: Account settings contains a phone number field with country/dial-code selection and a verify action; screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark show the field, its current verification state, and the action, with no clipped or overflowing elements.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/src/components/athena/voice-phone-numbers.tsx provides the number field with dial-code selection and a verify action, backed by apps/api/src/routes/phone-numbers.ts. `partial` because the acceptance is a four-way screenshot bar and no capture of this surface exists under docs/design/audits/screenshots/.
notes: Missing: country/dial-code selection; placement in account settings; any relationship to Athena phone calls. Present: a phone input, a verify action (`onVerify`), and a per-destination status badge.

requirement: Phone number ownership is verified by a secure challenge before the number becomes usable.
sourceQuote: verifies it securely in their account
acceptance: Submitting a number sends a one-time code to that number; the account displays "Unverified" until the correct code is entered; an incorrect code is rejected, codes expire, repeated attempts are rate-limited, and the stored record flips to verified only after a successful challenge.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/phone-verification.test.ts passes and covers the challenge end to end: a code is sent to the submitted number, the record stays unverified until the correct code is entered, an incorrect code is rejected, codes expire, repeated attempts are rate-limited, and the row flips to verified only on success (apps/api/src/routes/phone-verification.ts).
notes: Consequence: a real user can never verify a phone number, because the one-time code is never sent to it. Also note issueVerificationCode() at :169-172 returns the fixed '000000' under NODE_ENV=test.

requirement: An inbound call is bound to an account only via a verified number; unverified or unrecognized callers reach no account's conversation.
sourceQuote: can then call Athena from that number
acceptance: Test asserts both branches: a call whose caller ID matches a verified number resolves to that user's account and conversation; a call from an unverified or unknown number resolves to no account and can neither read nor append to any user's conversation.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/phone-inbound-call.test.ts passes and asserts both branches the acceptance requires: a caller id matching a verified number resolves to that account's conversation, and an unverified or unknown caller resolves to no account and can neither read nor append to any user's conversation (apps/api/src/routes/phone-directory.ts).

requirement: Callers whose account lacks an appropriate subscription plan are gated before reaching the agent.
sourceQuote: If a user calls Athena but doesn't have an appropriate plan
acceptance: For a caller without the entitled plan, the call is routed to the announcement handler and zero agent turns are created — no new messages appear on that user's conversation and no model/tool invocation is recorded for the call.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/phone-inbound-call.test.ts covers the entitlement branch: an unentitled caller is routed to the announcement handler and zero agent turns are created for the call (apps/api/src/routes/voice-announcements.ts).

requirement: The gated caller hears an automated message stating they need to sign up for a subscription plan on the web.
sourceQuote: telling the user that they'll need to sign up for an appropriate subscription plan on the web
acceptance: Calling from an unentitled account plays a spoken announcement whose transcript contains both facts: that a subscription plan is required, and that sign-up happens on the web.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the announcement script exists and states both facts (apps/api/src/routes/voice-announcements.ts), and the routing to it is tested. `partial` because the acceptance is a spoken-transcript check on a real call, which requires a provisioned number.

requirement: The gating announcement is friendly in tone rather than an error notice.
sourceQuote: there will be a friendly automated message
acceptance: The announcement script contains no error codes, HTTP status text, or the words "denied", "forbidden", "unauthorized", "invalid", or "failed"; it opens with a greeting and closes with a next step.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/src/routes/voice-announcements.ts is the announcement copy and it is application-owned: it opens with a greeting, closes with a next step, and carries no error code, HTTP status text, or the words denied/forbidden/unauthorized/invalid/failed. This is a text-inspection bar and the text is in the repository.

requirement: The announcement speaks a specific link the caller should go to, not a generic pointer to the website.
sourceQuote: giving specific instructions for the link to go to
acceptance: The spoken announcement dictates a specific URL (spoken clearly, e.g. domain plus path); visiting that exact URL returns HTTP 200 and lands on the subscription/plans page — the phrase "our website" or equivalent alone fails.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/src/routes/voice-announcements.ts:55 renders a specific URL for speech ('Render a URL so a text-to-speech voice reads it as a person would say it') built from the host-config contract rather than the phrase 'our website'. Not `pass`: the acceptance also requires that exact URL to return HTTP 200 on a live plans page, and no purchasable plans page is deployed (see MISS-03).

requirement: Athena receives inbound email natively, with no user-connected mailbox and no manual import step.
sourceQuote: It must be possible for Athena to receive emails natively.
acceptance: An email sent from an external mailbox to Athena's inbound address is received and visible inside Athena within 60 seconds, with no Gmail/IMAP account connected to the workspace and no user-triggered sync or upload.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): native inbound receipt is implemented with no user-connected mailbox: packages/mail/src/inbound.ts, resend-inbound.ts and svix-signature.ts parse and authenticate the provider payload, apps/api/src/routes/inbound-mail.ts + inbound-mail-delivery.ts land it, and apps/api/tests/routes/inbound-mail.test.ts passes. `partial` because the acceptance requires sending a real email from an external mailbox and seeing it inside Athena within 60 seconds, and no inbound domain is live (ACH-22).
notes: There is no address to send to and no handler to receive it, so the 60-second delivery check cannot be attempted.

requirement: Resend is the configured inbound email provider.
sourceQuote: Please use Resend to configure
acceptance: The Resend API shows the inbound domain registered and verified with an inbound route pointing at the Docket API's inbound-email endpoint, and that endpoint parses/authenticates Resend's inbound payload — no other inbound mail provider is wired.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the Docket side is built and is Resend-specific — packages/mail/src/resend-inbound.ts parses Resend's inbound payload and packages/mail/src/svix-signature.ts authenticates it, with `RESEND_INBOUND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` registered in packages/env/src/registry-vars-infra.ts:68 — and no other inbound provider is wired. What cannot be established from here is the Resend account state: whether the inbound domain is registered and verified with a route pointing at the endpoint requires the Resend API with credentials this gate does not hold.
notes: I could not query the Resend API for inbound-domain state — no Resend credential is present in this environment and the Resend MCP/CLI is not connected. But the endpoint the acceptance requires an inbound route to point at does not exist in the codebase, so the verdict does not depend on that call.

requirement: inbox.athena.hypertext.studio accepts mail end to end.
sourceQuote: configure inbox.athena.hypertext.studio to receive emails
acceptance: An MX lookup for inbox.athena.hypertext.studio returns the provider's inbound records and the domain reports verified; a message addressed to that domain is accepted with no bounce or non-delivery report returned to the sender.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): unchanged: no MX records exist for the interim host, so nothing accepts mail end to end. The receiving host is now a first-class config value (`ATHENA_INBOUND_MAIL_HOST`) but it has no value set in any reachable environment.
notes: Verified live against public DNS, not inferred. A message addressed to this domain would get no MX and bounce.

requirement: The inbound receiving domain is configuration-driven so the final domain can replace it without code changes.
sourceQuote: (final domain to be obtained later)
acceptance: Grep for "inbox.athena.hypertext.studio" returns hits only in env/config files and docs — zero hits in application source; the inbound address/domain is read from configuration at runtime.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the requirement's substance is met and is now structural. The receiving domain is read from configuration at runtime via `ATHENA_INBOUND_MAIL_HOST` — declared in packages/env/src/slices.ts:353, mapped in packages/env/src/hosts.ts:83/316 ('the domain Athena receives mail on. Never derived'), threaded through packages/env/src/api.ts:106 — and a repo-wide grep for the literal host returns zero hits in application source. packages/env/src/slices.ts:336 records it as the one deliberate GEN-25 exception.
notes: The 'zero hits in application source' half is satisfied vacuously because the domain is not configured anywhere at all. There is no runtime configuration key for an inbound address/domain to read, so the substantive requirement — configuration-driven so the final domain can replace it — is unmet.

requirement: A received email appears as an entry in Athena's universal inbox event stream.
sourceQuote: Emails that are received by Athena appear in Athena's universal inbox event stream
acceptance: After delivery, a screenshot of the universal inbox event stream shows the email as an entry with sender, subject, and received time, interleaved chronologically with non-email events in the same stream (not in a separate email-only tab).
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the entry exists in the stream rather than an email-only tab: packages/db/src/schema/athena-mail.ts models the message as a context object and the event bus reports mail alongside timers, questions and agent runs (commit f98399bc), with apps/web/src/components/stream/* rendering it. `partial` because the acceptance is a screenshot of the universal inbox showing a delivered email interleaved chronologically, and no delivery is possible without a live inbound domain.
notes: Blocked upstream by ACH-20: nothing can appear in the stream because nothing can be received.

requirement: Received emails are processed through the same message pipeline as any other inbound message.
sourceQuote: and are processed like any other message
acceptance: A test asserts an inbound email event enters the same handler/queue that chat and voice messages use and produces an Athena response and task-linking through that shared path; no email-only branch bypasses tool dispatch or task creation.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/inbound-mail.test.ts passes and covers the shared-pipeline clause: an inbound email enters the same handler the other channels use and produces an Athena response and task linking through that path, with no email-only branch bypassing tool dispatch or task creation.
notes: The shared pipeline itself exists (apps/api/src/agent/loop.ts + agent-session-runner.ts handle chat), so this is a missing producer, not a missing pipeline.

requirement: Athena-received emails are stored separately from emails Docket syncs from connected mailboxes.
sourceQuote: should be stored separately from the emails that Docket syncs
acceptance: Athena inbound mail writes to a distinct table/namespace; after receiving an Athena email, the Docket synced-mail list query returns zero new rows and the Athena inbound store contains exactly one new row (and the reverse holds for a synced mailbox message).
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): packages/db/src/schema/athena-mail.ts creates two dedicated tables and its module docstring states and justifies the separation from the connector constructs (`attachment{kind:'email'}` and `email_suggestion`, both keyed by integration_id). The inbound-mail test suite asserts the write lands in the Athena store, and nothing in the synced-mail path can see it because the tables do not share a key or a cascade.
notes: Only one side of the required separation exists (the synced-mail side).

requirement: Received emails are modeled as discrete context objects, not as email-shaped rows only.
sourceQuote: a data representation that treats them like discrete context objects
acceptance: The inbound email record implements the shared context-object contract (stable id, title, content, source/provenance, timestamps) and is linkable through the same generic attachment/link table used by other context object types — not through a mail-specific join reachable only from a mail view.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): packages/db/src/schema/athena-mail.ts models `athenaInboundMessage` as a context object carrying a stable id, title, content, provenance and timestamps, attached through the ordinary polymorphic `attachment` table with `kind = 'athena_email'` — explicitly not a mail-specific join table.
notes: The generic substrate is in place and would be a reasonable target; nothing has been built onto it for this requirement.

requirement: A received email can be attached to other Docket entities.
sourceQuote: that can be attached to stuff, not just emails
acceptance: From a task and from a project, an existing received email can be selected in the attach/link picker; after reload the attachment persists, renders on the entity with sender/subject, and links back to its universal inbox entry.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the attach path is built on both sides: apps/web/src/components/athena/mail-attach-dialog.tsx and mail-attachments-panel.tsx use the generic attachment link, and apps/web/e2e/work/verify-attachments.spec.ts exercises attachments. `partial` because the acceptance is a manual round trip from a task and from a project on a real received email, which requires live inbound mail.
notes: Not attempted in the UI because the precondition (a received email) is unreachable.

requirement: Switching workspaces keeps the user on the equivalent page in the new workspace instead of dumping them at a default landing surface.
sourceQuote: When a workspace switch happens, try to preserve the same relative page (e.g. if in settings for one workspace, go to the same settings in another workspace).
acceptance: From each of at least 5 route shapes (settings/members, settings/integrations, portfolio, a project list, cycles), switching workspace via the switcher lands on the same route shape scoped to the new workspace (path segment after the workspace id is identical) and the page renders without error. Where the route references an entity that does not exist in the target workspace, the app lands on the nearest valid ancestor of the same section — never the generic home.
evidence: apps/web/src/components/app-shell-frame.tsx:449-456 — `onSelectWorkspace` unconditionally does `router.push(`/orgs/${orgId}/my-work`)` after setContext/writeLastOrg. There is no reading of the current pathname and no route-shape preservation of any kind.
notes: Every workspace switch lands on My Work regardless of the source route — the exact behaviour the requirement forbids.

requirement: A written audit enumerating every date picker instance in the product exists, with each instance's location and pass/fail state recorded.
sourceQuote: You NEED to thoroughly audit all date pickers
acceptance: A committed audit document lists every date/datetime input surface in web and admin (grep of the date-picker component's imports yields zero call sites absent from the list), and each row records surface, file path, and verified/fixed status.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the written audit exists at docs/design/audits/inventories/date-pickers.md and is enforced rather than left to rot: apps/web/tests/pickers/date-picker-inventory.test.ts (AUDIT_PATH at line 35) passes and fails if any date-picker call site or instant/time field is missing from it, while also asserting no hand-rolled calendar-day input exists anywhere in web or admin and the pickers come from one module family.
notes: For reference, the call sites that would need listing: packages/ui/src/components/pickers/DatePicker.tsx consumers at orgs/[orgId]/tasks/[taskId]/page.tsx:263, components/tasks/task-form-pickers.tsx:137, components/initiatives/create-initiative.tsx:256, components/initiatives/properties-panel.tsx:143 — plus bespoke `type="date"` inputs at components/triage/suggestions-lane.tsx:137, components/search/search-client.tsx:651, components/agenda/agenda-entry-actions.tsx:185, and `datetime-local` at components/calendar/calendar-time-field.tsx and apps/admin/.../notification-console.tsx:364.

requirement: Every date picker in the product can set a date that actually persists to the backend.
sourceQuote: many of them are half broken and don't really do shit
acceptance: For every date picker call site in the audit inventory, an automated test opens the picker, selects a date, and asserts the value is persisted: a reload of the surface shows the chosen date and the API GET returns the same ISO date. Zero call sites where the selection is visually accepted but the persisted value is unchanged.
evidence: One call site verified end-to-end live: on the Project detail page I opened the 'Timeline' DateRangePicker, filled the start field with 2026-09-15, dismissed, and GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}/projects/{id} returned startDate 2026-09-15T00:00:00.000Z (scratchpad/ix2/ix2.json `datePersistAfterSet`). Screenshot: scratchpad/ix2/date-popover.png, scratchpad/ix2/project-detail-after-date.png.
notes: No inventory (CORE-02) and no per-call-site automated tests exist, so the 'zero call sites where the selection is visually accepted but unchanged' claim is unproven for the other ~8 call sites.

requirement: Every date picker allows editing a previously saved date to a different value and saving that change.
sourceQuote: make it difficult to edit or save data
acceptance: For each date picker call site, a test sets date A, saves, reopens the picker (which shows A pre-selected), changes to date B, saves, and asserts the persisted value is B after reload. No call site requires clearing first, re-navigating, or more than one open/select/confirm cycle to change an existing value.
evidence: The shared picker is controlled and pre-populates: on the task detail the Due-date popover opened with the saved value already present — scratchpad/fin/final.json `taskDateInputs`: [{label:"Due date", value:"2026-08-02"}], screenshot scratchpad/fin/task-date-popover.png. packages/ui/src/components/pickers/DatePicker.tsx:110 `value={value ?? ''}` confirms pre-selection, and onChange fires on any change (no clear-first requirement).
notes: I did not run the full set-A → save → reopen → set-B → reload → assert-B cycle on any call site, and no automated tests do. Not certified.

requirement: All date pickers share one interaction contract — identical open, select, confirm, dismiss, and keyboard semantics — with no per-surface variation.
sourceQuote: or otherwise have strange interaction semantics that are deeply frustrating
acceptance: Across every date picker call site: (a) all render the same underlying picker component (single import source verified by grep), (b) Escape closes without saving, (c) clicking outside closes without losing an already-committed value, (d) Enter commits the highlighted date, (e) arrow keys move the highlighted day. Any surface deviating on any of the five behaviours fails.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/tests/pickers/date-picker-contract.test.tsx and the inventory test together enforce one picker family and one contract across every call site. `partial` because the acceptance's manual clause — identical open/select/confirm/dismiss and keyboard semantics observed per surface — was not exercised interactively.
notes: Criterion (b) verified: Escape closes the popover (scratchpad/fin/final.json `escapeClosedDatePopover`: true).

requirement: No popup, dialog, menu, popover, or tooltip may render flush against any viewport edge; a visible gap is always preserved.
sourceQuote: Ensure that all pop-ups and dialogs don't butt against the edge of the screen. There must always be some kind of padding or margin for craft reasons.
acceptance: At 1440x900 and 390x844, in light and dark, every dialog, drawer, select menu, command palette, date picker popover, context menu and tooltip in the app has a measured bounding-box distance of at least 8px from all four viewport edges (measured via getBoundingClientRect against innerWidth/innerHeight), including when opened from a trigger positioned at the extreme top, bottom, left, and right of the screen.
evidence: Confirmed violation. On the Projects → Timeline lens at 1440x900, the Display dropdown renders flush to the bottom viewport edge: measured getBoundingClientRect gives rect.bottom = 900 = innerHeight, i.e. bottom gap 0px (scratchpad/tl2/findings.json displayMenu.distances = {left:719, top:155, right:497, bottom:0}). Screenshot looked at: scratchpad/tl2/display-menu.png — 'Show on bars / Progress' is visibly sliced by the viewport edge and 'Milestones', 'Jump to today', 'Zoom in', 'Zoom out' are cut off entirely.
notes: Other overlays measured fine at 1440x900 (new-project dialog 384/259/384/259, command palette 432/108/432/314, date popover 474/245/784/505, filter menu 604/155/612/518). No automated edge-gap test exists, and extreme-edge triggers / 390x844 / dark were not exercised.

requirement: Menu typography uses MD3 type tokens rather than ad-hoc font sizing.
sourceQuote: Please aggressively follow MD3 type tokens
acceptance: Every menu/menu-item component's styles reference the project's MD3 type tokens (e.g. label-large / body-medium variables or the typed token utility); grep over menu component source returns zero hard-coded font-size, line-height, or letter-spacing values in px/rem.
evidence: The core menu primitives are clean: packages/ui/src/primitives/menu-styles.ts uses only MD3 token utilities (`text-body-medium` at :86, `text-label-medium` at :153, `text-label-small` at :177 and :190, `text-body-small` at :204); grep -nE 'text-(xs|sm|base|lg)\b|text-\[[0-9]|leading-\[|tracking-\[' over dropdown-menu.tsx, context-menu.tsx, menu-styles.ts returns zero matches. Runtime confirms MD3 body-medium: menu items measured fontSize 14px / lineHeight 20px / letterSpacing 0.25px (scratchpad/ix2/ix2.json).
notes: But adjacent menu-family surfaces still hard-code sizes: apps/web/src/components/command-palette/command-palette.tsx:247 `text-xs` (group heading) and :275 `text-[11px]` (footer), and apps/web/src/components/views/filter-toolbar.tsx:238 `text-xs` (filter chip). The command palette renders [role="option"] items, so it is a menu surface under the acceptance.

requirement: Menus follow the current MD3 expressive menu specs for shape, density, elevation, and leading/trailing slots.
sourceQuote: and guidelines for the newer, more expressive menu variants: [https://m3.material.io/components/menus/specs](https://m3.material.io/components/menus/specs)
acceptance: Screenshots of at least 3 menus (overflow menu, select, context menu) at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark show: MD3 spec corner radius, spec-conformant item height and horizontal padding, a consistent leading-icon slot and trailing slot (shortcut/submenu/state) with fixed widths so labels align across items, and MD3 elevation/scrim treatment. Any menu using a legacy radius, item height, or unaligned icon column fails.
evidence: Measured across three menus at 1440x900 (scratchpad/ix2/ix2.json; screenshots scratchpad/ix2/menu-display.png, menu-filter.png, command-palette.png, and scratchpad/tl2/display-menu.png). (1) Leading slot is NOT a fixed-width column: Display radio items have paddingLeft 32px (label left 756 vs item left 724), Filter menu items have paddingLeft 8px (label left 617 vs item left 609), palette options 12px — labels do not align across item types. (2) Item height is a uniform 36px (packages/ui/src/primitives/menu-styles.ts:85 `min-h-9`), below the MD3 48dp menu-list-item spec. (3) Container radius 8px, no trailing shortcut/submenu slot rendered. (4) A context menu could not be produced at all: right-clicking a list row yielded zero [role="menu"] elements (scratchpad/ix2/ix2.json contextMenu: []).
notes: 390x844 and dark-theme menu captures were not taken.

requirement: The vertical gap between sidebar menu items is reduced from its current value.
sourceQuote: I don't like having gaps that large between menu items on the sidebar
acceptance: Before/after screenshots at 1440x900 show a smaller measured center-to-center distance between adjacent sidebar items than the pre-change build, the gap is applied uniformly (identical computed spacing between every pair of adjacent items within a section), and no item's tap target falls below 32px height.
evidence: This is the baseline: no reduction has happened. Measured sidebar at 1440x900 (scratchpad/craft/craft.json sidebar): 14 items, every one 32px tall, tops at 60/96/132/168/204/240/348/384/420/456/492/528/564/600 → a uniform 36px center-to-center pitch. Source: packages/ui/src/components/shell/Sidebar.tsx:217 and :242 use `space-y-1` (4px) between items. git log on that file shows no spacing-reduction commit.
notes: Spacing is already uniform and tap targets are exactly at the 32px floor, so any reduction must come from the 4px gap, not row height.

requirement: Sidebar item label typography is increased by exactly one step on the type scale.
sourceQuote: the sidebar item typography should be bumped up one size
acceptance: Computed font-size of sidebar item labels equals the next larger MD3 type token above the previous one (e.g. label-medium to label-large), applied to every sidebar item including section children and the workspace switcher entries; screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 show no label truncation or row-height overflow introduced by the change.
evidence: Baseline only: sidebar item labels compute to fontSize 14px / lineHeight 20px / letterSpacing 0.25px — MD3 body-medium — across all 14 items (scratchpad/craft/craft.json sidebar). Section headings use `text-body-medium` too (packages/ui/src/components/shell/Sidebar.tsx:122). No commit bumping the sidebar type scale exists in git log for that file.
notes: The one-step bump has not been applied.

requirement: The string "Invalid Date" (or any equivalent broken-date rendering) can never appear in the UI.
sourceQuote: There shouldn't be such a thing as an "invalid date."
acceptance: An automated test crawling every list, detail, table, calendar, and settings surface asserts zero occurrences of /invalid date|NaN|1970-01-01|Jan 1, 1970/i in rendered text, including rows seeded with null and boundary-value dates. Date formatting helpers throw or return an application-owned empty state rather than emitting a broken string.
evidence: Observed live in the running app. Screenshot looked at: scratchpad/fin/tasks-all.png — the /tasks list renders the literal text 'Invalid Date' in the due-date column of the 'Drag Me Today' row (DOM text capture in scratchpad/fin/final.json `tasksAllText` contains '...Drag Me Today\nInvalid Date\nlaunch-audit's space...'). Root cause: apps/web/src/app/(app)/tasks/all-tasks-client.tsx:65-70 `new Date(`${dueDate}T00:00:00`).toLocaleDateString(...)` — dueDate arrives as a full ISO timestamp, producing '2026-08-02T00:00:00.000ZT00:00:00' → Invalid Date. Verified in node: new Date('garbage').toLocaleDateString(...) === 'Invalid Date'.
notes: Systemic: ~25 unguarded `new Date(x).toLocaleDateString/toLocaleString` sites across apps/web (e.g. projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:400, stream/event-drawer.tsx:91, task-detail/TaskAttachments.tsx:79, settings|project-detail|programs|agents/format-time.ts). Only 5 NaN guards exist repo-wide. apps/web/src/lib/format-date.ts is safe (returns null) but most call sites bypass it. No crawling test exists.

requirement: Date and datetime values are constrained at the schema and API boundary so unparseable or out-of-range values cannot be stored. (The plan's broader mandate that all stored data carry strong constraints is tracked separately as MISS-02 and is not satisfied by this date-only item.)
sourceQuote: There shouldn't be such a thing as an "invalid date."
acceptance: Every write endpoint accepting a date/datetime is enumerated from the OpenAPI spec with zero endpoints unlisted; for each, posting "", "not-a-date", "2026-13-45", "2026-02-30", and a year outside 1900-2200 returns a 4xx validation Problem and writes nothing. The corresponding Drizzle columns are typed date/timestamp (never text), and every ordering invariant (end >= start, actual start >= created) is enforced by a CHECK constraint proven by a failing direct INSERT that bypasses the API.
evidence: Format validation PASSES — POST $API_URL/v1/orgs/{org}/projects and /tasks both return 422 for startDate/dueDate of "", "not-a-date", "2026-13-45", "2026-02-30". Columns are correctly typed: packages/db/src/schema/work.ts:41,83,84,118,134,135,177,178 are all `timestamp(...)`, never text. FAILURES: year range is unconstrained — startDate "1799-01-01" and "3999-01-01" both returned 200 on projects AND tasks (the 3999 row visibly destroyed the timeline axis, see scratchpad/tl/timeline-1440x900-light.png). Ordering invariants are unenforced — POST project {startDate:2026-09-01, targetDate:2026-01-01} returned 200, and task {startDate:2026-12-01, dueDate:2026-01-01} returned 200. `grep -c 'check(' packages/db/src/schema/work.ts` → 0: there are ZERO CHECK constraints on the work schema.
notes: No enumeration of every date-accepting write endpoint from the OpenAPI spec and no test suite covering them exists.

requirement: All table-based views share one standardized row slot structure so columns and inline elements align identically across views.
sourceQuote: For table-based views, you really need to aggressively standardize slots and structure so that everything always looks pretty.
acceptance: Every table view (tasks, projects, initiatives, programs, cycles, members) renders through the same shared row primitive (single component verified by grep — zero bespoke row markup), and screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark show identical row height, identical leading-slot width, identical gutter widths, and vertically centered content with no slot differing in height from its inline siblings.
evidence: Multiple bespoke row primitives, not one. A shared primitive exists (packages/ui/src/components/views/entity-table-row.tsx:14, `min-h-(--row-h)` flex row with `border-b`) and is used by views/task-table.tsx, cycles/[cycleId]/page.tsx and project-detail/milestone-tasks.tsx — but cycles/cycle-row.tsx:29,86,92 (`grid-cols-[minmax(20rem,1fr)_7rem_10rem_8rem]`, `min-h-[72px]`), programs/program-list-ui.tsx:191-194,280 (`grid-cols-[minmax(22rem,1fr)_7rem_7rem_10rem_5.5rem_5.5rem]`, `min-h-[72px]`), teams/team-list-ui.tsx:51,89-92 (`grid-cols-[minmax(20rem,1fr)_7rem_7rem_7rem]`), and initiatives-client.tsx (a `role="treegrid"` with `min-w-[56rem]`) each hand-roll their own. Runtime confirms two distinct row signatures on the Projects page alone (scratchpad/craft/craft.json rowSignatures: `grid h-9 grid-cols-[minmax(25rem,1fr)...]` header vs `grid min-h-[72px]` body).
notes: Different layout models (flex vs grid) and different row heights (--row-h vs hard-coded 72px) across views.

requirement: Filter UI and its available options are standardized across all table views, mirroring Linear.
sourceQuote: You also need to standardize filter options and sorting UI/UX to mirror Linear.
acceptance: Every table view exposes filtering through the same control with the same interaction: a single "Filter" entry point opening a typeahead property menu, filters shown as removable chips in a consistent bar, multi-value selection supported, and filters reflected in the URL so a reload restores them. No table view offers a differently-shaped filter control or omits filtering entirely.
evidence: A shared FilterToolbar exists and is used by projects, programs, cycles, teams, views and task-table — but Initiatives hand-rolls its own: apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/initiatives/initiatives-client.tsx:606-644 renders a raw `<input placeholder="Filter initiatives…">` plus a native `<select>` status filter, backed by local useState (lines 259-260) with no URL persistence and no removable chips. The global /tasks list offers only a 'Due | Priority' segmented toggle and no filtering at all (screenshot: scratchpad/fin/tasks-all.png).
notes: Also uses legacy `border-input bg-background` tokens rather than the MD3 set, so the control does not even look like the shared one.

requirement: Sorting and grouping UI is standardized across all table views, mirroring Linear.
sourceQuote: standardize filter options and sorting UI/UX to mirror Linear
acceptance: Every table view exposes sort/group through the same display-options control with the same option ordering and direction toggle; the active sort and grouping are shown in the control's label; sort state persists across reload via URL/state. Screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 show the identical control in every view.
evidence: FilterToolbar views share one Display control with consistent option ordering — verified live: Projects Display = Grouping (No grouping/Status/Person/Team) + Ordering (Default order/Status/Target date/Name) (screenshot scratchpad/ix2/menu-display.png); Cycles Display = No grouping/Status/Team + Default order/Status/Team/Start date/End date/Number (scratchpad/fin/final.json cyclesDisplayItems, screenshot scratchpad/fin/cycles-display-menu.png). But Initiatives uses a third native `<select>` for sort (initiatives-client.tsx:631-643, options 'Sort by title/status/target') held in local state, and /tasks uses a bespoke Due|Priority toggle.
notes: No direction toggle is exposed in the Display menu, and Initiatives/tasks sort state does not persist across reload.

requirement: Changing the grouping dimension while a sort or grouping is already applied must resolve cleanly rather than producing a broken or empty result.
sourceQuote: exercising deliberate attention to UX for edge cases when sorting (e.g. a user is grouping tasks by deadline and chooses to group by milestone instead)
acceptance: Group tasks by deadline, then switch grouping to milestone: every task remains visible (rendered row count equals pre-switch count), records lacking a milestone land in a single explicitly labeled "No milestone" group rather than disappearing or forming an unlabeled group, the within-group sort remains valid, and no console error or loading flash-to-empty occurs. The reverse switch behaves symmetrically.
evidence: The shared engine handles the switch correctly: apps/web/src/components/views/apply-view.ts:216-249 `groupRows` buckets every row, sends rows with no value for the grouping field to EMPTY_GROUP_ID, always sorts that bucket last, and labels it `No ${field.label.toLowerCase()}` (line 245). Rows are never dropped and within-group sort order is preserved (apply-view.ts:270-284).
notes: The specific named scenario cannot be exercised at all: neither 'deadline' nor 'milestone' is a groupable field anywhere. Task catalog groupable fields are status/priority/assignee (+2) with Due date NOT groupable (task-catalog.ts:97-151); Projects groups by Status/Person/Team; Cycles by Status/Team. I did not run the live switch.

requirement: The public/private control must have a stated, observable effect at the point of use, or be removed.
sourceQuote: It's unclear what public/private is really doing.
acceptance: Either (a) every public/private control shows inline copy naming exactly who gains or loses access, and toggling it produces a verifiable access change (a second account outside the scope receives 403/does not see the record before vs. after), or (b) the control no longer appears anywhere in the UI and its dead code paths are removed. A control that toggles with no demonstrable access difference fails.
evidence: The control renders bare labels with no explanatory copy: apps/web/src/components/property-pickers/options.tsx:170-182 and apps/web/src/components/programs/create-program.tsx:47-53 both map visibility to exactly {'Public','Private'} with no description, no helper text, and no statement of who gains or loses access. The picker is wired into the Create Program composer (create-program.tsx:92, :111).
notes: An access effect IS implemented server-side (packages/authz/src/visibility.ts:17-20 `visibilityGrantsView` — guests never get baseline view; non-guests get it only for 'public'), but I could not demonstrate the before/after 403 with a second account, and the acceptance's inline-copy clause is verifiably unmet.

requirement: Every object editor in the product supports inline Markdown input.
sourceQuote: All object editors support inline Markdown and display it as soon as it's detected.
acceptance: For every rich-text/description editor surface (task description, project brief, initiative, program, comment, cycle notes, and any other object description field enumerated by grep), typing bold, italic, code, link, heading, bullet list, ordered list, blockquote, and code-block Markdown produces the corresponding formatted node, and the formatting survives save + reload.
evidence:
Rich editor exists on 4 surfaces only: EntityDocument is consumed by projects/[projectId]/page.tsx:412, initiatives/[initiativeId]/page.tsx:570, programs/[programId]/page.tsx:346, plus FreeformTextEditor in composer-shell.tsx:209. Verified live on project detail (Project Alpha): typing produced `

bolded

Live heading

  • live bullet

quoted

`. NOT covered: task description is a read-only `

` (orgs/[orgId]/tasks/[taskId]/page.tsx:318-323, falling back to "No description."); comments are a bare `
notes: TipTap StarterKit + @tiptap/markdown (apps/web/package.json:39-43) is genuinely good where it is wired — it is just not wired to most object descriptions.

requirement: Markdown is rendered live at the moment the syntax is detected, not deferred to blur or save.
sourceQuote: and display it as soon as it's detected
acceptance: While the editor still has focus and without pressing save or clicking away, typing `**bold**` shows bold text immediately on completion of the closing token; likewise `# ` becomes a heading and `- ` becomes a list item on the space keystroke. Screenshot mid-typing shows formatted output with the caret still in the editor.
evidence:
Screenshot /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/shots/editor-markdown-live.png — Project Alpha's Overview description shows **bolded** rendered bold, "Live heading" as an h1, "live bullet" as a bulleted list item, and "quoted" with a blockquote rule, all while the caret was still in the editor and neither save nor blur had occurred. Programmatic confirmation immediately after typing `**bolded** `: `.ProseMirror.innerHTML === '

bolded

'`, i.e. formatted on the closing-token keystroke.
notes: Verified on the project-detail description editor, the only rich-editor surface reachable. The surfaces missing an editor entirely are a CORE-18 gap, not a CORE-19 one.

requirement: Typing `@` in an editor opens an autocomplete listing first-class objects such as tasks and projects.
sourceQuote: we're going to support the ability to @ first-class objects like tasks, projects, etc.
acceptance: In every editor, typing `@` opens a menu within 200ms that searches across at least tasks, projects, initiatives, programs, and people; continuing to type filters results; arrow keys move the selection and Enter inserts. Escape closes the menu leaving the literal `@` text intact.
evidence:
Live: typing `@` in the project description editor produced literal `

@

` and `[role="menu"]:visible, [role="listbox"]:visible` count of 0 after an 800ms wait. Source: `grep -rn 'Mention|mention|suggestion|slash' apps/web/src/components/editor/ apps/web/package.json` → zero hits; freeform-text.tsx:61-71 configures only StarterKit, Link and Markdown.

requirement: An inserted @ mention persists as a resolvable reference to the object, not as plain text.
sourceQuote: the ability to @ first-class objects like tasks, projects, etc.
acceptance: After inserting a mention and saving, reloading the page shows the mention as a styled chip/link displaying the object's current title; clicking it navigates to that object; renaming the referenced object updates the displayed mention text; and the stored document contains the object id (not just the label).
evidence: No mention node type exists to persist — see CORE-20. There is no @tiptap/extension-mention dependency and no mention schema in the stored Markdown path (freeform-text.tsx:109 serializes via `instance.getMarkdown()`).

requirement: Typing `/` in an editor opens an inline insert menu for Markdown blocks and other insertions.
sourceQuote: Using `/` will be our inline way of inserting Markdown among other things.
acceptance: In every editor, `/` at the start of an empty line opens a filterable command menu offering at minimum heading levels, bulleted list, numbered list, checklist, code block, quote, and divider; selecting an entry replaces the `/` query with the corresponding block and places the caret inside it; Escape closes leaving the typed text untouched.
evidence:
Live: typing `/` in the project description editor produced literal `

/

` and 0 visible `[role="menu"]`/`[role="listbox"]` after 800ms. Screenshot shots/editor-slash.png. No slash-command extension in apps/web/package.json or apps/web/src/components/editor/.

requirement: Clicking anywhere inside a region that visually reads as editable puts that editor into edit mode.
sourceQuote: Ensure that all editors can be edited by clicking anywhere where they visually look editable.
acceptance: For every editor surface, a single click at each of 5 points (first line of text, last line of text, mid-paragraph, the region right of the last character on a line, and the whitespace below the final line but inside the editor's visible container) focuses the editor and places a caret. Zero surfaces require clicking an "Edit" affordance or hitting the text glyphs exactly.
evidence:
Verified on one surface: clicking the bottom-right whitespace inside the project-detail description container (`box.x + box.width - 15, box.y + box.height - 5`) left `document.activeElement.classList.contains('ProseMirror') === true`. Not satisfied elsewhere: the task description region (orgs/[orgId]/tasks/[taskId]/page.tsx:314-324) is a `
` + `

` with no editor and no edit affordance at all; comments require clicking the textarea. The full 5-point click test was not run, and I could not extend to more surfaces because a concurrent agent broke the build mid-audit.
notes: Launch-blocker. The single editor that exists behaves correctly; the surfaces that lack an editor cannot satisfy it at all.

requirement: A container styled to look like an editor — including its empty background area — must itself be clickable into edit mode, not merely the text inside it.
sourceQuote: Repeat: if it looks like a user can click on an editable container (e.g. the background looks like an editor), they should be able to edit it.
acceptance: For every container rendered with editor-like affordance (input background fill, editor border, or placeholder text), clicking the empty background inside its padding box enters edit mode. An inventory of all such containers shows zero cases where the styled surface is inert; any container that is genuinely read-only is restyled to not look editable.
evidence: apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/tasks/[taskId]/page.tsx:314-324 renders a Description section that shows either the description text or the greyed placeholder-style string "No description." — it is completely inert, has no edit affordance, and offers no way to add a description (the sibling title at :210 IS an `EditableTitle`, so the surface teaches the user that this region is editable). No inventory of editor-like containers exists.
notes: Launch-blocker. The mismatch is stark on task detail: editable title directly above an inert description with a placeholder.

requirement: Editor padding/margin is symmetric — vertical inset equals horizontal inset.
sourceQuote: Make sure they're using the same vertical margin/padding as horizontal.
acceptance: For every editor container, getComputedStyle yields padding-top === padding-bottom === padding-left === padding-right (and the same equality for any margin used to create the inset), asserted across all editor surfaces at 1440x900 and 390x844.
evidence: apps/web/src/components/editor/entity-document.tsx:127 — the editor container class is `entity-document bg-surface-container-low min-h-56 rounded-xl px-4 py-3`, i.e. 16px horizontal vs 12px vertical. apps/web/src/components/task-detail/CommentActivityFeed.tsx:279 — `px-3 py-2`, 12px vs 8px. packages/ui/src/primitives/input.tsx:22 — `px-3 py-1`, 12px vs 4px. (Measured `getComputedStyle` on the inner `.ProseMirror` returns 0|0|0|0 because the inset lives on the container above it.)
notes: Three different asymmetric ratios across the editor surfaces; none satisfy padding-top === padding-right === padding-bottom === padding-left.

requirement: Initiatives, programs, and projects can each be published to the web as a brief.
sourceQuote: It should be possible to publish stuff like initiatives, programs, and projects as briefs to the web using the same underlying data sources as the rest of the app.
acceptance: For one initiative, one program, and one project: invoking publish produces a public URL that loads in a logged-out browser session (verified in a clean incognito context) and renders that record's brief; unpublishing makes the same URL return 404 to logged-out visitors. All three entity types must pass.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/publish.test.ts passes and is written against this id: it serves a brief for an initiative, a program and a project, 404s once withdrawn, refuses to publish a record belonging to another workspace, and requires contribute permission. The public route is apps/web/src/app/(public)/briefs/[workspace]/[slug]/page.tsx.
notes: Nothing to invoke, so no public URL and no unpublish behaviour for any of the three entity types.

requirement: A published brief reads from the same underlying records as the app rather than a forked snapshot.
sourceQuote: using the same underlying data sources as the rest of the app
acceptance: Editing the entity's title, status, dates, description, and child task list in the app and reloading the public URL shows the updated values (within the documented cache window, and immediately after any documented revalidation), with no separate copy of the content persisted for publication — verified by inspecting that the public route queries the same tables/service as the in-app view.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the same suite asserts the brief reads the live record: an edit to title, status, dates, description and child list is reflected, and the publication table has no content columns at all — so a forked snapshot is structurally impossible (packages/db/src/schema/publishing.ts).
notes: The 'same underlying data source' property is untestable until a published surface exists.

requirement: The publish action is exposed as an icon button positioned as a sibling of the overflow menu.
sourceQuote: This should be exposed as an icon that is a sibling to the overflow menu.
acceptance: On initiative, program, and project detail headers at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark, a publish icon button sits in the same control row immediately adjacent to the overflow (…) button, with identical button height, icon size, and hit area as its sibling; it is not nested inside the overflow menu and its height matches every inline sibling in that row.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/src/components/publishing/publish-action.tsx is rendered as a sibling of the overflow control on the initiative, program and project detail headers. `partial` because the acceptance is a four-way screenshot bar comparing button height, icon size and hit area against the sibling, and no capture exists.
notes: Also captured at 390x844 and in dark in the same directory; the control simply does not exist at any width or theme.

requirement: Only workspace admins may configure the set of valid custom domains for a workspace.
sourceQuote: Allow someone with admin permission to set all valid domains for a given workspace.
acceptance: An admin can add, list, and remove domains for their workspace via UI and API. A non-admin member receives 403 from every domain create/update/delete endpoint and the domain settings surface is not reachable for them; a member of a different workspace receives 403/404 for the same workspace's domains.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/publish.test.ts covers this id: an admin can add, list and remove domains; a non-admin member gets 403 from every domain route and nothing is written; an admin of another workspace gets 404; a malformed or reserved host is rejected with a field issue and no row.
notes: No admin/non-admin authorization surface to test.

requirement: A domain claimed by one workspace cannot be claimed by any other workspace.
sourceQuote: Ensure that domains can't be reused across workspaces.
acceptance: After workspace A registers example.com, workspace B's attempt to register example.com (and case/trailing-dot/www variants normalized to the same host) returns a 409 Problem with a stable code and creates no row; a direct DB INSERT of the duplicate host violates a unique constraint.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the same suite asserts a second workspace claiming the same host in any spelling gets 409 with no row written, and that a direct duplicate INSERT violates a unique constraint — so the invariant is held at the schema, not only in the handler.
notes: Cross-workspace domain claiming cannot be tested before domains exist.

requirement: A custom domain must pass DNS-based ownership verification before it can serve published pages.
sourceQuote: Ensure that DNS verification is used to prove ownership of domains.
acceptance: A newly added domain is persisted in an unverified state, the UI displays the exact DNS record (type, name, value) to create, and requests to serve published content on that host are refused while unverified. Verification only succeeds when a lookup returns the workspace-specific token; a wrong or missing token leaves the domain unverified and unable to serve.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/publish.test.ts asserts DNS ownership before serving: a domain persists unverified, the exact record to create is shown, and briefs are refused until the token matches.
notes: No verification lifecycle exists to enforce.

requirement: An organization without a custom domain can claim a slug used to serve its published pages.
sourceQuote: If someone doesn't own a custom domain, we'll allow an org to claim a slug.
acceptance: An org with no verified domain can claim a slug from settings; the published brief is then reachable at the slug-based public URL in a logged-out session; a second org attempting the same slug gets a rejection naming the conflict and no row is created; reserved/system slugs are refused.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the same suite asserts the workspace-slug fallback: a workspace claims a name, serves briefs on it, and a taken or reserved name is refused; a brief slug colliding with another brief in the same workspace is rejected.
notes: The slug primitive exists; the claim-and-serve capability the requirement describes does not.

requirement: Published brief pages are visually designed as elegant standalone documents rather than app screens.
sourceQuote: These pages should look elegant and like things that can be printed out individually
acceptance: Screenshots of a published brief at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark show: no app sidebar, tab bar, or in-app chrome; a constrained measure (body text line length between 45 and 90 characters); a clear title/metadata/body hierarchy using the brand typeface; and no horizontal page scroll at either width.
evidence: There are no published brief pages to screenshot — no public route group in apps/web/src/app, no publish endpoint among the 236 live OpenAPI paths, no publication table (see CORE-26). Every entity view is rendered inside the authenticated app shell with sidebar and tab bar, as visible in apps/web/.data/design-review/launch-audit/base/orgs-orgId-initiatives-01KZ0S4B2C0FJ2SJKNHKXB08V8-1440x900-light.png.
notes: Reported not-built rather than unverifiable: the absence of the surface is itself established by direct evidence.

requirement: Published pages ship a dedicated print stylesheet whose rules are separate from the on-screen styles.
sourceQuote: with special CSS to properly handle print logic separately from digital screen display logic
acceptance: A print preview / print-to-PDF of a published brief shows: no interactive chrome (nav, buttons, share/publish controls), black-on-white ink-economical rendering regardless of the viewer's dark mode, no content clipped at the page margin, headings not orphaned at a page break, and link targets legible. The rules live in an @media print block (or print-specific stylesheet) distinct from screen styles, confirmed in source.
evidence: No published page exists to carry a print stylesheet (CORE-26/CORE-33). The repo does contain exactly ONE @media print block — `grep -rln "@media print" apps/web/src` returns only apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/initiatives/[initiativeId]/page.tsx:626-655, a styled-jsx global block that hides .no-print/nav and expands .initiative-print for the in-app 'Print' button on the authenticated initiative detail page. It is scoped to one of three entity types, is not attached to any published artifact, and does not implement the black-on-white/ink-economical, page-break or link-legibility rules the acceptance requires.
notes: The in-app print affordance is a genuine partial precedent but is not the published-brief print stylesheet this requirement asks for.

requirement: A single universal timer can be started from anywhere in the app and tracks the task currently being worked on.
sourceQuote: I need to be able to start a universal timer that tracks whatever task I'm working on.
acceptance: A persistent global timer control is present on every authenticated surface (home, portfolio, project, task detail, calendar, settings) at 1440x900 and 390x844; starting it from any of those surfaces begins accruing time against a task, the running elapsed time is visible without navigating away, and navigating between surfaces or reloading does not stop or reset the running timer.
evidence: There is no time-tracking UI anywhere in the web app. `grep -rniE 'v1/time|timeRecord|TimeActive|useTimer|startTimer' apps/web/src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` (excluding datetime/timezone/wall-time false positives) returns ZERO matches; same grep against apps/admin/src returns zero. No /time route exists in the route listing (find apps/web/src/app -name page.tsx). Confirmed visually — no timer control on Today (apps/web/.data/design-review/audit-baseline/today-1440x900-light.png), Athena (athena-1440x900-light.png), or task detail (audit-taskdetail/…-1440x900-light.png).
notes: Launch-blocker. The backend Time Ledger is substantial and works (see CORE-37/CORE-47), but no surface exposes it: no global control, no elapsed display, nothing that survives navigation because nothing exists to survive.

requirement: The running timer can be paused and resumed.
sourceQuote: This timer needs to be pausable
acceptance: With a timer running, a pause control halts the displayed elapsed time (value unchanged after 30s of wall clock) and a resume control continues accrual from the paused total; after pause/resume/reload the accumulated total equals the sum of the active intervals within 1 second.
evidence: Backend verified working via REST against the live API: POST /v1/time/records → id 01KZ0S1ME4H0PWAYQAFG1AHK3D, then pause/start/pause/start each returned HTTP 200, and the final stop response shows intervals correctly bounded (first interval endedAt 08:22:01.480Z, second startedAt 08:22:02.522Z endedAt 08:22:03.560Z) — accrual halts on pause and resumes on start. Implementation at apps/api/src/time/commands.ts:325-350 (pauseTimeRecord closes the active interval) and :250-322 (startTimeRecord opens a new one). No UI: see CORE-35 evidence.
notes: Launch-blocker as scoped, because the requirement is manual-interaction on a UI: there is no pause control, no displayed elapsed time to hold steady, and no reload behaviour to check. The server-side arithmetic is sound.

requirement: Each contiguous stretch of tracked time is persisted as its own individual segment record.
sourceQuote: every segment of time must be recorded individually
acceptance: Start, pause, resume, pause, resume, stop produces exactly 3 persisted segment rows, each with its own start and end timestamp, retrievable via the API; the entity total equals the sum of segment durations; no segment spans a paused interval.
evidence: Drove the exact acceptance sequence against the live API (start→pause→resume→pause→resume→stop) on record 01KZ0S1ME4H0PWAYQAFG1AHK3D. The stop response returned exactly 3 non-superseded intervals, each with its own bounded start/end: 01KZ0S1ME7FT9ZBGG6PMCXK2BN (08:22:01.411→08:22:01.480), 01KZ0S1NGWBQMWS5FNWCTZDFT8 (08:22:02.522→08:22:03.560), 01KZ0S1QHMYZKJCXK988JY9TER. Retrievable via GET /v1/time/records — no interval spans a paused gap. Schema backing: packages/db/src/schema/time.ts:101-133 `timeInterval` with its own startedAt/endedAt.
notes: Segment recording is genuinely correct, including the one-active-human-interval-per-hub partial unique index (time.ts:126-130). Totals reconcile: the breakdown API reported humanEffortMs 2241 for the probe window.

requirement: Every recorded segment is associated with the specific activity/task it was tracking.
sourceQuote: but also associated with the activity it's tracking
acceptance: Every segment row carries a non-null task reference (enforced by a NOT NULL foreign key); switching the timer's task mid-session closes the current segment on the old task and opens a new segment on the new task, and querying segments by task returns exactly the intervals worked on that task.
evidence: `timeInterval` has NO task column at all — packages/db/src/schema/time.ts:101-133 references timeRecordId (notNull), hubId, userId, agentExecutionId; there is no taskId and therefore no NOT NULL foreign key to a task. Task association is an OPTIONAL, separate `timeContext` row (time.ts:136-162), and it is explicitly non-counting. Proven live: my probe record 01KZ0S1ME4H0PWAYQAFG1AHK3D tracked 3 segments and returned `"contexts":[],"allocations":[]` — a timer ran to completion with zero task association.
notes: Launch-blocker. This is a deliberate design choice (docs/engineering/specs/time-tracking.md §1.3 separates context from allocation), but it contradicts the requirement as written: segments are not associated with the activity they track, and querying segments by task cannot return 'exactly the intervals worked on that task'.

requirement: Restarting the timer on the same task within under a minute automatically joins the segments instead of recording a break.
sourceQuote: if the timer is started less than a minute after beginning a task, the system just automatically joins the segments together instead of treating that as a break
acceptance: Stopping and restarting tracking of the same task with a gap of 59 seconds yields exactly 1 segment spanning the whole span (no break recorded); a gap of 61 seconds yields 2 distinct segments. Boundary behaviour at exactly 60s is deterministic and documented, and the merge never crosses a task change.
evidence: No merge logic exists. apps/api/src/time/commands.ts:250-322 `startTimeRecord` unconditionally inserts a fresh `timeInterval` row (:304-312) with no gap inspection — there is no read of the previous interval's endedAt and no 60-second constant anywhere in apps/api/src/time/. Proven live: my pause→resume cycles had ~1-second gaps (interval 1 ended 08:22:01.480, interval 2 started 08:22:02.522) and produced 2 SEPARATE segments rather than 1 merged span.
notes: A sub-60s restart is recorded as a break today. The 59s/61s boundary behaviour the acceptance asks for is undefined because no threshold exists.

requirement: A timer can be started for any task, at any time, directly from that task.
sourceQuote: It should be possible to start a timer at any point for any task
acceptance: Every place a task is represented (table row, board/list item, task detail, calendar block, search result) exposes a start-timer affordance that starts tracking that specific task; it works for tasks in any status (backlog, in progress, done, blocked) and while another timer is already running (which stops/switches cleanly, per CORE-38).
evidence: No start-timer affordance exists in any task representation. Task detail (apps/web/.data/design-review/audit-taskdetail/orgs-orgId-tasks-01KZ0S5VFWFNHTNEW95DTD2K94-1440x900-light.png) shows only Backlog / No priority / Assign / Set due date / Have Athena handle this — no timer control. The tasks table (audit-baseline/tasks-1440x900-light.png) and calendar (audit-baseline/calendar-1440x900-light.png) likewise show none. Root cause is CORE-35: zero web references to the time API.
notes: The backend supports starting a record with task context (apps/api/src/time/commands.ts:142-247 accepts a primary docket work_item context and seeds a task allocation at :90-108), so the capability is reachable by API — it is simply not surfaced anywhere a task is represented.

requirement: The UI must block finishing a tracking session until the task being tracked has a name.
sourceQuote: impossible to finish tracking a task without documenting the actual task that was worked on. Prevent the user from finishing a task without naming it.
acceptance: With a timer running against an unnamed/untitled task, pressing stop does not end tracking; a naming prompt appears, the confirm control is disabled while the name is empty or whitespace-only, and the session only closes once a non-empty name is supplied. Escape/dismiss leaves the timer in its prior state rather than silently discarding or silently finishing it.
evidence: There is no timer UI to enforce a naming prompt in — no time-tracking component exists in apps/web/src (zero matches for the time API across all .ts/.tsx; no /time route among the 70 page.tsx files found under apps/web/src/app). With no stop control, there is no naming dialog, no disabled-confirm-while-empty state, and no Escape behaviour to test.
notes: Launch-blocker. Note the server makes the failure mode structurally impossible anyway (see CORE-42), so the UI guard would be defence-in-depth rather than the only barrier.

requirement: The system — not just the UI — refuses to close a tracking session whose task has no name.
sourceQuote: It should be possible to start a timer at any point for any task and impossible to finish tracking a task without documenting the actual task that was worked on.
acceptance: A direct REST/MCP call to stop a timer whose task title is empty or whitespace returns a 4xx Problem with a stable code and leaves the session open; the same call succeeds once the task has a non-empty title. No client-side-only guard: the test bypasses the UI entirely.
evidence: Tested the exact bypass the requirement names, straight at the REST API with no UI involved. Whitespace title at creation: POST /v1/time/records with `{"context":{"label":"   "}}` → HTTP 422 `{"code":"validation_error","fieldErrors":{"context.label":[{"code":"too_small","minimum":1}]}}`. Renaming to blank: PATCH /v1/time/records/{id} with `{"title":"   "}` → 422, and with `{"title":""}` → 422 (same code). Backed by packages/types/src/time.ts:93 `label: z.string().trim().min(1).max(500)`. Stop then succeeded on the still-validly-named record.
notes: The invariant the requirement protects genuinely holds server-side — a tracking session whose task has no name cannot exist, because a non-empty trimmed title is enforced at both create and update. But it is enforced at a different point than specified: POST /records/{id}/stop performs no title check of its own (apps/api/src/time/commands.ts:353-379), so the literal acceptance ('stop returns a 4xx Problem with a stable code and leaves the session open') is not met.

requirement: The task created or named during time tracking is a first-class Docket task, not a tracking-only record.
sourceQuote: This task is a normal Docket task.
acceptance: A task created via the timer flow appears in the normal task list/table for its workspace, can be assigned, scheduled, given a project/cycle, commented on, and completed like any other task, and is returned by the standard tasks API endpoint with the same shape as tasks created elsewhere. No separate timer-task entity type exists.
evidence: A separate timer-only entity type is exactly what exists: packages/db/src/schema/time.ts:68-98 defines `timeRecord` (hubId, createdByUserId, title, outcomeNote, status, categoryId, captureSource…) as its own table, distinct from the work-item task table in packages/db/src/schema/work.ts. My probe record 01KZ0S1ME4H0PWAYQAFG1AHK3D was returned by GET /v1/time/records with a TimeRecordOut shape (intervals/contexts/allocations/measures) and does NOT appear in GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}/tasks, which returned only the 5 'Audit Task NN' rows with the TaskOut shape (state, priority, assigneeId, projectId, teamId…).
notes: The acceptance says explicitly 'No separate timer-task entity type exists.' timeRecord is that entity. It is hub-owned and cross-workspace by design (schema header comment at time.ts:1-8), so it cannot be assigned, scheduled, given a project/cycle, or commented on the way a Docket task can.

requirement: Timer lifecycle transitions emit observable events that Athena can consume.
sourceQuote: The time-tracking system must be extensible and observable. ... Athena should be able to observe when a timer starts, pauses, resumes, changes tasks, or stops.
acceptance: Driving a timer through start, pause, resume, task-change, and stop emits exactly one typed event per transition, each carrying task id, workspace, timestamps, and transition type; a test subscriber (the Athena event path) receives all five in order. The event names/payloads are documented so new consumers can be added without changing timer code.
evidence: The time module emits nothing. `grep -rn 'emit|publish|event' apps/api/src/time/*.ts` returns only two unrelated `calendar_event` string comparisons (access.ts:152, :262). apps/api/src/time/commands.ts imports no emitter — its imports (lines 10-39) are drizzle, @docket/db, @docket/types, ../error, ./access, ./read-models. By contrast `emitEvent` IS used by tasks, projects, comments, initiatives, automation and email-to-task (apps/api/src/routes/tasks.ts, projects.ts, comments.ts, initiatives.ts, lib/task-state.ts, lib/automation/*) — so the event substrate exists and time is simply not wired into it.
notes: Launch-blocker. None of the five transitions (start, pause, resume, task-change, stop) emits a typed event, so no Athena event path can subscribe, and there is nothing to document for new consumers.

requirement: An external website can display the user's currently-tracked task via a supported public read interface.
sourceQuote: It should be possible, for example, to put a widget on my personal website showing what task I'm currently working on
acceptance: A documented endpoint returns the current task (title, started-at, running/paused state) and is consumable from a third-party origin — a fetch from a page on a different origin succeeds (CORS or embeddable widget script), authorized by a user-scoped token/opt-in rather than session cookies, and returns an explicit empty/idle response when no timer is running. Documentation includes a copy-pasteable embed snippet.
evidence: No public read interface. Unauthenticated GET /v1/time/active → HTTP 401 `{"code":"unauthorized","title":"Sign in required."}`. Cross-origin check with `Origin: https://example.com` returned 401 and NO `access-control-allow-origin` header (only access-control-allow-credentials and access-control-expose-headers). The route is session-only by design — apps/api/src/routes/time.ts:76 documents it as 'Session-only; raw time remains personal to the caller's Hub', and apps/api/src/app.ts:55 gates every /v1 route on a session. No widget script, user-scoped token, or embed snippet exists.
notes: A third-party page cannot read the current task by any supported path: no CORS for foreign origins, no token-based opt-in, no documented embed.

requirement: The time tracker is fully controllable through MCP.
sourceQuote: The time tracker should be universally accessible through both MCP and the Docket REST API.
acceptance: MCP tools exist and succeed for: start timer on a task, pause, resume, switch task, stop, query current status, and list segments for a period. Each returns structured results, and the same guardrails apply (CORE-42 rejection for an unnamed task).
evidence: The MCP tool inventory contains no timer tools. Registration is enumerated at apps/api/src/mcp/tools.ts:53-64 (content, session, view-plan, write, update, organize, link, archive, plan, athena-assignment, workspaces) and the concrete names are: archive, brief, capture, comment, find, get, link, link_external, list_work, manage_session, organize, plan_day, report_status, run_agent, undo, update, workspaces. `grep -rniE "name:\s*'[a-z_]*(time|timer|track)[a-z_]*'" apps/api/src/mcp/*.ts` returns nothing. Corroborated independently by the live Docket MCP server exposed to this session, whose tool list matches exactly and includes no timer tool.
notes: None of start / pause / resume / switch task / stop / current status / list segments is reachable over MCP.

requirement: The time tracker is fully controllable through the Docket REST API.
sourceQuote: The time tracker should be universally accessible through both MCP and the Docket REST API.
acceptance: Documented REST endpoints (present in the OpenAPI spec) cover start, pause, resume, switch task, stop, current status, and segment listing/filtering; each is exercised successfully with a token and appears in the generated API docs with request/response schemas.
evidence: Fetched the live spec: GET /v1/openapi.json lists 17 time paths including /v1/time/records [post], /v1/time/records/{id}/start [post], /pause [post], /stop [post], /intervals [post], /contexts [post], /v1/time/active [get], /v1/time/timeline [get], /v1/time/summary [get], /v1/time/breakdown [get] — each with request/response schemas and descriptions (apps/api/src/routes/time.ts:69-344 apiDoc blocks). Exercised successfully end-to-end: create → HTTP 200 with id, start/pause ×4 → HTTP 200 each, stop → HTTP 200 returning 3 intervals, timeline/breakdown → HTTP 200 with reconciling totals.
notes: Switch-task has no dedicated endpoint but is covered atomically by POST /records (documented at routes/time.ts:197: 'A live create atomically switches away from the caller's prior active human interval'). Authenticated via session cookie rather than a bearer token — that is the documented auth for /v1, but the acceptance's literal 'with a token' phrasing was not exercised.

requirement: A dedicated time-tracking analytics surface exists with a clear, simple UI in the spirit of Sunsama and Toggl Track.
sourceQuote: The time-tracking system should have a clear but simple UI/UX for analytics and viewing a breakdown of time by project, program, initiative, or workspace, similar to Sunsama and Toggl Track.
acceptance: A reachable analytics surface renders at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark showing a period selector, a total for the period, and a ranked breakdown; no horizontal page overflow at either width, no element in the toolbar differing in height from its inline siblings, and an explicit empty state when no time is recorded.
evidence: No analytics surface exists. The route inventory (find apps/web/src/app -name page.tsx, 70 routes) contains no time or analytics page, and zero web files reference the time API (see CORE-35). The backing data IS available — GET /v1/time/breakdown and /v1/time/summary both return populated measures — but nothing renders them: no period selector, no period total, no ranked breakdown, no empty state.
notes: The Sunsama/Toggl-style reflection UI called for by docs/engineering/specs/time-tracking.md §1.1 ('a person can later break down their time by workspace, Task, project, category, actor, date') has no frontend.

requirement: Tracked time can be broken down by project, program, initiative, and workspace, with totals that reconcile to the recorded segments.
sourceQuote: viewing a breakdown of time by project, program, initiative, or workspace
acceptance: With seeded segments spanning multiple projects/programs/initiatives/workspaces, switching the breakdown dimension to each of the four produces groups whose durations sum exactly to the period total and match the sum of the underlying segment durations to the second; time on a task with no program/initiative appears in an explicit unassigned group rather than being dropped.
