evidence: Hit GET /v1/time/breakdown live for all seven dimensions. Working: workspace, project, task, category, actor — each returned buckets with reconciling totals (e.g. workspace → `{"key":"unallocated:workspace","label":"Unallocated","measures":{"elapsedMs":4319,"humanEffortMs":2241,…}}`). Failing: `groupBy=program` → HTTP 422 `fieldErrors.groupBy [{code:'invalid_option'}]`, and `groupBy=initiative` → HTTP 422 same. Root cause: packages/types/src/time.ts:318 `TimeBreakdownDimension = z.enum(['workspace','task','project','category','actor'])`.
notes: Two of the four dimensions the requirement names (program, initiative) are simply not implemented. The parts that do work are solid: totals reconcile to the segment durations, and unattributed time lands in an explicit 'Unallocated' / 'Uncategorized' bucket rather than being dropped — exactly what the acceptance asks for.

requirement: The calendar page's persistent chrome must be reduced to a minimal, deliberate control set instead of cramming every capability into the toolbar.
sourceQuote: The calendar view looks extremely haphazard and like someone tried to stuff a thousand things into it without any clear attention to detail or craft.
acceptance: At 1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark, the persistent chrome around the calendar grid contains at most five interactive controls: date navigation (prev/today/next counts as one), range selector, New, view-settings trigger, calendar-sources trigger. Any additional control present in today's toolbar (axis/comparison/zoom/density/detail) is either removed or moved inside one of those surfaces.
evidence: Measured the live /calendar chrome after the rebuild (screenshot /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/calendar-FINAL-1440.png and calendar-RECHECK-1440-light.png). Visible interactive controls in the persistent chrome: Today, Previous dates, Next dates (one date-navigation group), Calendars, Display settings, New — 4 groups, inside the 5 allowed. Same six at 390x844.
notes: IMPORTANT: another agent rewrote the calendar in this same worktree DURING this audit (uncommitted; calendar-toolbar.tsx mtime 01:44, new files calendar-view-settings.tsx / calendar-layers-menu.tsx / calendar-range-label.ts, deleted calendar-scheduling-sidebar.tsx & calendar-week-grid.tsx). At ~00:55 this same surface had 12+ controls including an axis toggle, an Overview/Standard/Detail pill group, a zoom slider and a density readout. All CAL verdicts below describe the state at ~01:55 on 2026-08-02, git HEAD b1d285bd + dirty working tree.

requirement: The standalone zoom slider and density control must be removed from the calendar toolbar.
sourceQuote: The layout is not properly responsive and has a bunch of useless buttons and controls like zoom and density.
acceptance: No `input[type=range]` with id/name `calendar-zoom`/`calendarZoom` and no element rendering the text "Zoom", "Custom zoom", or "<X> density" exists anywhere in the calendar route's rendered DOM at any width from 320px to 1920px.
evidence: Re-ran the width sweep over /calendar at 320/390/430/744/834/1024/1280/1440/1920 after the rebuild: `document.querySelectorAll('input[type=range]').length` = 0 at every width, and a regex for /Zoom|Custom zoom|density/ over the main subtree returned false at every width. Confirmed visually in /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/calendar-FINAL-1440.png (toolbar is Today | ‹ › | August 2026 … Calendars | Display | New).
notes: At ~00:55 this failed hard — apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/calendar-toolbar.tsx then had `<input id="calendar-zoom" name="calendarZoom" type="range">` plus an `<output>` reading '<X> density' and a 'Custom zoom' select option. Those are gone.

requirement: The Overview/Standard/Detail switch must be removed.
sourceQuote: Why the fuck is there an Overview/Standard/Detail switch when zoom and density are already exposed through other controls?
acceptance: No segmented control, select, or button group offering the labels "Overview", "Standard", and "Detail" renders on the calendar route at any width or in any panel state; the ZOOM_SHORTCUTS preset row in calendar-toolbar.tsx no longer renders in the page chrome.
evidence: Width sweep 320→1920 after the rebuild: the Overview+Standard+Detail text probe returned false at every width. The ZOOM_SHORTCUTS preset row is no longer rendered in the page chrome — the Display popover instead exposes named density presets. Visually confirmed in /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/calendar-FINAL-1440.png.
notes: At ~00:55 calendar-toolbar.tsx:12-16 defined ZOOM_SHORTCUTS = Overview/Standard/Detail and rendered them as a pill group plus a mobile <select>; the pill group was visible in /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/calendar/calendar-1440x900-light.png.

requirement: All overlapping display concepts (zoom, density, detail level) must be consolidated into exactly one subtle view-settings surface.
sourceQuote: Consolidate these overlapping concepts into one subtle view-settings interface.
acceptance: Exactly one chrome affordance (a single low-emphasis icon button) opens view settings; every display preference is reachable only from inside that popover; no second control anywhere on the page changes the same underlying value. Verified at 1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark.
evidence: Re-measured at 1440x900 in both themes (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/controls/report.json). The chrome renders exactly one display affordance — the visible `main header` buttons are Today, Previous dates, Next dates, Calendars, Display settings, Open Athena for Calendar, New — and its menu holds every display preference: 'View / Dates / People / Density / Compact / Default / Spacious / Zoom / 100% / Reset to default'. `document.querySelectorAll('input[type=range]')` returns 0 across the whole route. The same single Display trigger is the only one present at 320 and 390 in both themes (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/final/*.png).
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: Zoom must be adjusted by discrete increase/decrease steps, never by a slider.
sourceQuote: you should stick to a default and have only a subtle view-settings thing that allows me to increase/decrease the zoom level in addition to support for trackpad zoom, not a whole fucking slider
acceptance: The view-settings popover exposes a decrement and an increment control (and nothing continuous); clicking increment once changes rendered pixels-per-hour by exactly one documented step. `document.querySelectorAll('input[type=range]')` inside the calendar route returns length 0.
evidence: The Display menu's only zoom controls are the two discrete steppers ['Zoom out','Zoom in']; the menu contains zero `input[type=range]`, and so does the route (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/controls/report.json, screenshot apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/controls/display-1440-light.png). One increment is a documented single step (ZOOM_STEP_IN = 1.25, applied through clampPixelsPerHour) in apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/calendar-view-settings.tsx.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: The calendar must ship with a single default density that requires no user configuration.
sourceQuote: Having support for greater density is fine, but in all honesty, you should stick to a default
acceptance: With storage cleared and no saved preference, /calendar renders at the one documented default pixels-per-hour value, and no density or zoom chooser is visible before the user opens view settings.
evidence: A freshly created account with no saved preference renders the documented default: lane height / 24 = 72 px per hour on first paint (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/controls/report.json -> zoom.before). No density or zoom control is visible in the chrome before the Display menu is opened — the visible chrome buttons are Today, Previous dates, Next dates, Calendars, Display settings, Open Athena for Calendar, New.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: Trackpad pinch-zoom must change the calendar's zoom level.
sourceQuote: in addition to support for trackpad zoom
acceptance: Dispatching a ctrl+wheel (pinch) event over the time grid changes the rendered hour height in the expected direction and calls preventDefault so the browser page does not zoom; asserted for both zoom-in and zoom-out.
evidence: Dispatching a ctrl+wheel (trackpad pinch) event over the schedule scrollport changes the rendered hour height in both directions and cancels the browser's own zoom: zoom-in 72 -> 240 px/hr, zoom-out 240 -> 63 px/hr, `event.defaultPrevented === true` on both, in light and dark (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/controls/report.json -> zoom). The listener is registered non-passively in apps/web/src/components/scheduling/scheduling-canvas.tsx.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: No combination of UX interactions may shrink the calendar grid below 10% of the viewport area.
sourceQuote: Under no circumstances—and do not create a fake-ass smoke test for this—should any combination of UX interactions result in a calendar view that takes up less than 10% of the entire fucking viewport.
acceptance: A browser test enumerates the cross-product of panel states (side panel open/closed, item drawer open/closed, layer/source panel open/closed, sync alert shown/hidden) at 1440x900, 1024x768, 834x1112 and 390x844, and asserts `gridRect.width * gridRect.height >= 0.10 * innerWidth * innerHeight` in every combination. Zero failures.
evidence: apps/web/e2e/calendar/calendar-panel-floor.spec.ts drives a real browser through the cross-product of rail docked/collapsed x {none, Calendars popover, Display menu, item drawer} x sync alert shown/hidden at 390x844, 834x1112, 1024x768 and 1440x900 — 64 measurements — and asserts gridRect area >= 0.10 * innerWidth * innerHeight in each, naming the combination. All four tests pass. Independently, a 162-width live-resize sweep puts the worst area share at 42.5% (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/sweep/report.json).
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: An expanded side panel must not bunch the calendar grid into a sliver.
sourceQuote: If a panel is extended right now, the calendar bunches up into this tiny little region.
acceptance: At 1440x900 with every side panel expanded at once, the calendar grid occupies at least 50% of the main content width; below 1024px the panel presents as an overlay/sheet instead of stealing grid width. Screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark.
evidence: At 1440x900 with the rail docked, `<main>` is 867px and the schedule grid inside it is 824px — 95% of the main content width — and 824x808 = 51.4% of the viewport (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/final/report.json). Below 1024 the rail presents as a modal sheet and costs the grid no width; the grid is 80.7% of the viewport at 390. Screenshots apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/final/{1440,390}-{light,dark}.png.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: The test guarding the 10% floor must measure real rendered geometry, not be a token smoke test.
sourceQuote: do not create a fake-ass smoke test for this
acceptance: The guarding test drives a real browser, performs the actual panel-opening interactions, and reads `getBoundingClientRect()` on the live grid element. Its sensitivity is demonstrated: temporarily forcing the side panel to full width makes the test fail, and reverting makes it pass. No assertion in it is satisfied by mere element presence.
evidence: apps/web/e2e/calendar/calendar-panel-floor.spec.ts drives a real browser, opens each panel by clicking its control, and reads getBoundingClientRect() on the live `[aria-label="Schedule"]` element; no assertion is satisfied by element presence. Sensitivity demonstrated: injecting `#shell-aside { width: 68% }` into the running page makes it fail with `1440x900 . rail docked . none . no alert: grid area is 7.38% of the viewport`; removing the injection restores the pass.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: The calendar view must never overflow horizontally at any viewport width.
sourceQuote: Please, for the love of God, ensure that the calendar view is properly responsive.
acceptance: At widths 320, 390, 430, 744, 834, 1024, 1280, 1440 and 1920, `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= clientWidth` on the calendar route, and no descendant element's right edge exceeds the viewport, in both light and dark.
evidence: `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= clientWidth` at 320, 390, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440 and 1920 in both themes, and zero elements outside the schedule scrollport extend past the viewport at any of them (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/final/report.json -> docOverflow, overflowing). The earlier 'descendant clause fails' count was measuring content inside the grid's own horizontal scrollport, which is not page overflow; that is now excluded and the remaining count is 0. A 162-width live-resize sweep (320 -> 2200, every pixel across 1010-1040 and 1420-1460) reports `overflow: 0` (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/sweep/report.json).
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: The calendar must present a usable, purpose-built layout at phone widths.
sourceQuote: I repeat: this view needs to be properly responsive.
acceptance: At 390x844 (light and dark) the calendar renders a single-day/agenda layout in which: every chrome control is visible and tappable without horizontal scrolling, no control overlaps another, no label is clipped or ellipsised to unreadability, and all tap targets measure at least 44x44 CSS px.
evidence: At 390x844 every chrome control now measures 44 x 44 CSS px — Today, Previous dates, Next dates, Calendars, Display settings, New — with the rightmost edge at 371px inside a 390px viewport, no overlap and no clipped label (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/final/report.json -> controls). The layout is a single-day lane. Screenshots apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/final/390-{light,dark}.png. The 44px step begins at a 22rem container rather than at `@sm` because `<main>` reserves a stable scrollbar gutter, so a 390px phone reports a 379px container.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: The same underlying calendar reachable through multiple connected accounts must appear only once in the calendar/source list.
sourceQuote: Surely there's some way to deduplicate shit like holiday calendars or personal calendars appearing on work accounts.
acceptance: With two connected accounts that both expose an identical calendar (matching provider calendar id or identical name+owner, e.g. "Holidays in United States"), the layer/source panel lists it exactly once, with both accounts attributed on that one row.
evidence: Implemented in apps/web/src/components/calendar/calendar-layer-panel.tsx: a calendar arriving on more than one linked account is listed exactly once, on a row attributed to all of them, and ticking that row ticks every copy (useUpdateLayerGroupVisibility). Rendered and screenshot-verified with two identical 'Holidays in United States' layers on two connections: the panel shows one checkbox, the row reads 'On 2 linked accounts', and a banner states '1 calendar arrives on more than one account. It is listed once.' with a 'Show each copy' disclosure (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/layers/calendars-1440-{light,dark}.png, apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/layers/report.json). Covered by apps/web/tests/calendar/calendar-layer-panel.test.tsx (one row + both accounts named + one tick moves both + expansion back to per-account rows).
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: Duplicate events arriving from more than one connected account must render as a single block on the grid.
sourceQuote: Surely there's some way to deduplicate shit like holiday calendars or personal calendars appearing on work accounts.
acceptance: Given a fixture where the same event (identical iCalUID, or identical title+start+end) syncs from two accounts, the week grid renders exactly one event block for it; the deduplicated sources are discoverable in its detail view.
evidence: Implemented in apps/web/src/components/calendar/calendar-event-dedup.ts (provider event id + recurrence instance, or identical case-folded title at an identical instant, and only across different layers) and applied in use-calendar-date-axis.ts before lanes are built. apps/web/e2e/calendar/calendar-duplicate-events.spec.ts drives the real grid: one block for the duplicated meeting, three blocks in total so 'fewer blocks' cannot pass for 'correct blocks', and the folded copy discoverable in the block's drawer ('Also on' section). Also visible live at 1440 in both themes, where three fixture items render as two (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/layers/report.json). Unit coverage: apps/web/tests/calendar/calendar-event-dedup.test.ts, 11 cases including a double booking inside one calendar, two occurrences of one recurring event, and native items, all of which must stay separate.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: The rebuilt calendar must be visually inspected with captured evidence, not merely asserted to be fixed.
sourceQuote: Please, please, please visually inspect this
acceptance: A design-review scorecard for the calendar exists under docs/design/audits/ containing screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 in both light and dark taken against the rebuilt view, with per-dimension scores and evidence.
evidence: docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md — a full Craft Rubric scorecard against the rebuilt view, with machine-readable front matter, per-dimension scores and per-gate evidence, citing screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 in both light and dark (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/final/*.png) plus the layer-coloured grid and duplicate-calendar panel (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/layers/*.png). Every claim in it cites a PNG that was opened or a printed measurement; the two things that could not be captured are listed as limitations rather than passed.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: Chrome must be budgeted so the grid dominates the view, producing a clear focused hierarchy.
sourceQuote: the calendar view should have an extremely clear, focused hierarchy centered on events and time blocks
acceptance: At 1440x900, persistent chrome above the grid measures no more than 96px tall and the grid fills the remaining content height; at 390x844 chrome is no more than 112px tall. Measured from screenshots plus bounding rects.
evidence: Re-measured at 1440x900: `<main>` is 867px against 573px of total chrome, and the schedule grid inside it is 824x808 = 51.4% of the viewport (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/final/report.json). The previous measurement had chrome ahead 656px to 717px.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: Events and time blocks must be the highest-emphasis elements in the calendar; no supporting chrome may compete with them visually.
sourceQuote: The focus MUST be on events and time blocks.
acceptance: In 1440x900 and 390x844 screenshots (light and dark), event/time-block surfaces are the only elements using the highest-contrast fill and the largest in-grid type; gridlines, hour gutter, all-day strip, now-line and day headers all render at lower contrast and smaller or equal type than event titles.
evidence: Event blocks now separate from the empty canvas by 1.714:1 (light) and 1.768:1 (dark) uncoloured, and 1.99-2.18:1 / 2.03-2.27:1 with a layer colour — up from the measured 1.04:1 and 1.16:1 (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/final/report.json, apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/layers/report.json). Gridlines and lane separators are outline-variant/30, the hour gutter and the weekday atom render at on-surface-variant (lower contrast), and no in-grid type exceeds an event title's 14px/500. Remaining literal gap, disclosed rather than hidden: today's 24px day badge is a filled `bg-primary` chip, which is a higher-contrast fill than an event block. It is a state marker on a date rather than competing chrome, and every calendar renders today filled, so it was kept deliberately; the acceptance's 'only elements using the highest-contrast fill' is therefore not literally met.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: The same date must not be rendered twice in two different formats.
sourceQuote: You really shouldn't need duplicate "Sat, August 15" and "2026-08-15" labels.
acceptance: For any visible day in day/week/month views, no ISO-format date string (YYYY-MM-DD) is rendered anywhere in the calendar subtree, and the humanized date for a given day appears in exactly one DOM node.
evidence: TreeWalker over the calendar subtree matching /\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}/ returned an empty array at every width 320→1920 on the rebuilt calendar. Visually, day columns now read 'Sun 2' / 'Mon 3' with no ISO line beneath (screenshot /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/calendar-FINAL-1440.png).
notes: At ~00:55 the same probe returned ['2026-07-31','2026-08-01','2026-08-02','2026-08-03','2026-08-04','2026-08-05'] rendered at 10px directly under 'Sat, Aug 1' style labels — the exact duplication the requirement names.

requirement: The current date must appear in exactly one place, not both inline and in the view header.
sourceQuote: Why the fuck does the calendar view show the date inline AND at the top of the view?
acceptance: At 1440x900 and 390x844, the string identifying the currently viewed date/range appears once. Column headers may carry weekday+day-number per column, but the header's range label is not repeated inside the grid body.
evidence: Screenshot /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/calendar-FINAL-1440.png: the range label 'August 2026' appears once, in the toolbar. The grid body carries only per-column weekday+day-number ('Sun 2', 'Mon 3'), which the acceptance explicitly permits, and the header's range string is not repeated inside the grid. Same at 390x844 (calendar-FINAL-390.png).
notes: At ~00:55 the header read 'Aug 2, 2026 – Aug 3, 2026' while each column repeated the same date twice ('Sun, Aug 2' plus '2026-08-02').

requirement: Minimum text size in the calendar must be raised so all text is legible.
sourceQuote: Please use a larger minimum text size. This shit is almost unreadable.
acceptance: At default zoom, every text-bearing node in the calendar route has computed font-size >= 12px; event titles and day headers are >= 13px; no node renders at 10px or 11px. Asserted by enumerating computed styles in a real browser at 1440x900 and 390x844.
evidence: Every text-bearing node in the calendar route now renders at 14px or 16px — the distribution is {14px: 42} at 320 and 390 and {14px: 57, 16px: 1} at 1440, in both themes, with zero nodes at 12px or below at any of the seven measured widths (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/final/report.json -> sizes). Previously 12px was 70% of all text. The hour labels (24 of them, the largest run of text on the surface) moved to 14px and the gutter widened 76 -> 88px so `12:00 AM` still fits on one line; the per-card kind label was removed rather than resized.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: Visible borders must be stripped from the calendar, with grouping expressed through surface tint and spacing instead.
sourceQuote: There are just so many fucking borders everywhere that look like visual shit.
acceptance: A computed-style enumeration over the calendar subtree finds non-transparent borders only on (a) the time grid's hour/day separators and (b) the elements CRAFT-07 permits — input affordance and focus indication — each named individually in the calendar's craft scorecard. No toolbar, panel, card, chip, event block, popover, header, or day cell renders a visible border. Verified by the computed-style count plus 1440x900 and 390x844 screenshots in light and dark.
evidence: Computed-style enumeration over `main *` at 1440x900 in both themes finds 50 bordered edges resolving to exactly four sources (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/controls/report.json -> borders): (a) toolbar Button outlines — CRAFT-07's input affordance; (b) 25 hour separators `border-outline-variant/30 ... border-t`; (c) 8 day separators `border-outline-variant/30 border-r`; (d) one event block's 4px left identity stripe, its single semantic layer marker. The header hairline the previous audit named as forbidden (`header[bg-surface-container-low border-outline-variant/40 sticky] borderBottom`) is removed — the canvas header now separates by tonal step alone. No toolbar, panel, card, chip, popover or day cell renders a border box.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: The New button must never wrap its label onto a second line.
sourceQuote: Why the fuck does the New button wrap?
acceptance: At widths 320, 390, 430, 744, 1024, 1280, 1440 and 1920, the New control's rendered height equals its single-line height (one line-box) and its scrollWidth is <= clientWidth; where space is tight it collapses to an icon-only button with an accessible name rather than wrapping.
evidence: Measured the New control's geometry across 320, 390, 430, 744, 834, 1024, 1280, 1440 and 1920. In every case scrollWidth == clientWidth (81/81 pre-rebuild; 79/79 at 1440 and 48/48 at 390 post-rebuild) and the rendered height equals a single line-box (32px at 1440, 40px at 390, computed line-height 16px). It never wraps.
notes: It does not collapse to icon-only at narrow widths — at 390 it shrinks to a 50x40 button still showing '+ New'. That is fine: the requirement only forbids wrapping, and offers icon-collapse as one acceptable way to avoid it.

requirement: Events must be draggable onto time blocks, with the association persisted.
sourceQuote: It must be possible to drag events into time blocks.
acceptance: An end-to-end test drags an event onto a time block, asserts the UI reflects the new association immediately, asserts the server persisted it, and asserts it survives a page reload.
evidence: apps/web/e2e/calendar/calendar-event-into-block.spec.ts is mock-free: it creates the block and the event through the product's own POST /v1/me/calendar/items in the signed-in browser context, drags the event onto the block with a real HTML5 drag, asserts the UI immediately (the block's drawer lists the event), re-reads GET /v1/me/calendar/items/:id/relations to prove the server persisted it, then reloads the page from scratch and asserts the association again. Passes.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). Verified against the running dev stack after the calendar tier work; see docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: Two calendar surfaces must never be visible on screen simultaneously.
sourceQuote: It shouldn't be possible to have two fucking calendars on the screen at once
acceptance: On every app route, at widths 390/1024/1440, with every panel/drawer/popover open in turn, at most one visible element rendering a calendar grid or month picker is present at a time.
evidence: Counted `section[aria-label="Schedule"]` on the rebuilt build at 390x844, 1024x768 and 1440x900 on /calendar, in the baseline state, with the Display popover open, and after toggling every reachable rail button (Tasks / Show Tasks / Collapse Tasks / Agenda): the count was 1 in every combination. Also 1 on /today, /inbox, /tasks and /portfolio at 1440x900.
notes: This was a hard FAIL 50 minutes earlier on the pre-rebuild build: /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/panels/calendar-1440-rail-0.png — which I looked at — shows two time grids side by side on /calendar (main grid 'Aug 2 – Aug 3' at x=281 w=699 and a second full grid in the right rail at x=1036 w=328), and 1024x768 rendered 2 grids even at baseline. Caveat on the pass: I did not exhaustively open every popover on every app route.

requirement: The sidebar calendar must be hidden while the full calendar view is open.
sourceQuote: the sidebar calendar should not remain visible while the full calendar view is open
acceptance: Navigating to /calendar at 1440x900 (light and dark) shows no mini/date-picker calendar in the sidebar; navigating away from /calendar restores it if it exists elsewhere.
evidence: Screenshot /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/calendar-FINAL-1440.png: the left sidebar on /calendar contains only nav items (Today, Tasks, Calendar, Inbox, Stream, Portfolio, Search, then Workspace items) — no mini/date-picker calendar. Corroborated in source: `grep -rln 'MiniCalendar|mini-calendar|DayPicker|react-day-picker|month-grid|MonthGrid' apps/web/src packages/ui/src` returns no files.
notes: Passes somewhat vacuously — there is no mini calendar anywhere in the app to hide, so the 'restores it when navigating away' clause is moot. The only date-picker surfaces are native `<input type="date">` fields (triage, search, agenda-entry-actions), whose month popups are browser chrome rather than DOM.

requirement: The calendar must be replanned, rearchitected, and rebuilt through five subagents working iteratively, with the iterations recorded.
sourceQuote: Please, for the love of God, use five subagents ITERATIVELY to replan, rearchitect, and rebuild this
acceptance: A calendar rebuild document exists under docs/engineering/ (or docs/research/) naming five distinct subagent workstreams and recording at least two iteration rounds, each with what the round changed and why.
evidence: Still not built as specified. Three iterative rounds are recorded — docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-{1,2,3}.md, each naming what the round changed and why — but no document names five distinct subagent workstreams, so the acceptance is not met.
notes: A rebuild demonstrably happened during this audit window, but it is undocumented.

requirement: The rebuilt calendar must be built from the app's shared layout and design system rather than bespoke one-off structure.
sourceQuote: rebuild this in a way that is compatible with our app and our principles
acceptance: The calendar route composes the same shared page-layout/shell components as other app screens and uses only MD3 surface/type tokens (no hard-coded hex colors, no ad-hoc font sizes or spacing literals outside the token scale) in its source files under apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar and apps/web/src/components/calendar.
evidence: Token discipline is now provable rather than grepped: after this round every file under apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar and apps/web/src/components/scheduling is delisted from packages/test-utils/tests/design-policies/design-token-debt.json, which means the scanner finds zero raw type utilities, zero hardcoded colours, zero non-overlay shadows and zero size-changing interactions in them. The route composes the app's one shell (AppShell via the (app) layout) and the shared SchedulingCanvas. It still does NOT compose `PageHeader`, which projects/initiatives/programs do — and that remains deliberate rather than fixed: PageHeader adds a titled band above the content, which would re-introduce the vertical chrome CAL-16 exists to bound and a second rendering of the date that CAL-18/CAL-19 forbid. Recorded as a conflict between two acceptance criteria rather than silently resolved either way.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). See docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: Calendar capabilities must be distributed across separate UI surfaces instead of packed into a single element.
sourceQuote: Please recognize that YOU DON'T NEED TO PUT EVERYTHING INTO A SINGLE UI ELEMENT.
acceptance: Grid, view settings, calendar sources/layers, and event details each live in their own surface; the persistent toolbar owns only navigation, range, New, and the two triggers. Screenshots show each surface opened independently, and calendar-toolbar.tsx no longer renders zoom, density, axis or comparison controls.
evidence: Four independent surfaces, each opened on its own and captured: the grid; the Display menu (apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/calendar-view-settings.tsx — View / Density / Zoom / Reset, apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/controls/display-1440-{light,dark}.png); the Calendars popover (calendar-layers-menu.tsx, apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/layers/calendars-1440-{light,dark}.png); and the item drawer (components/calendar/calendar-item-drawer.tsx, opened in e2e/calendar/calendar-panel-floor.spec.ts). The persistent toolbar renders only date navigation, the range label, Calendars, Display, the contextual Athena door and New — measured visible `main header` buttons: ['Today','Previous dates','Next dates','Calendars','Display settings','Open Athena for Calendar','New'] (apps/web/.data/design-review/cal-r3/controls/report.json). calendar-toolbar.tsx renders no zoom, density, axis or comparison control.
notes: Round 3 (2026-08-02). See docs/design/audits/2026-08-02-calendar-round-3.md.

requirement: The explicit Views page must be removed from the product.
sourceQuote: I don't like having explicit views pages. It just feels out of place.
acceptance: No "Views" entry appears in the sidebar at any width for any workspace type, and the /orgs/[orgId]/views route no longer renders a views page (it is removed and redirects to the corresponding entity list rather than 500ing).
evidence: Both halves of the acceptance fail, verified visually. Screenshot /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/shots-a/orgs-orgId-views-1440x900-light.png shows (a) a 'Views' entry in the sidebar, highlighted as the active route, and (b) the page fully rendering: heading 'Views', subtitle 'Saved filters over your tasks — open one, tweak it, or save the current filter as a new view.', a 'No saved views yet' empty state, and a 'New view' section with 'Add filter', 'Display' and 'Save as view' controls. The route file still exists at apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/views/page.tsx and is one of only five files that import FilterToolbar.
notes: Nothing has been removed and there is no redirect. Also captured at 390x844 and in dark (same directory).

requirement: Each individual entity view must carry robust in-place filter UI that covers what the Views page previously did.
sourceQuote: Instead, prefer more robust filter UI/UX in individual views.
acceptance: On the tasks, projects, and initiatives list surfaces, a filter toolbar allows adding, combining and removing filters across every field previously filterable from the Views page, plus grouping and sorting, with filter state reflected in the URL and restored on reload. Verified at 1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark.
evidence: Only one of the three named surfaces qualifies. PROJECTS: real toolbar — screenshot shots-a/orgs-orgId-projects-1440x900-light.png shows List/Dependencies/Timeline lenses plus '+ Add filter' and 'Display'. INITIATIVES: screenshot shots-a/orgs-orgId-initiatives-1440x900-light.png shows only a 'Filter initiatives…' text box, an 'All statuses' select and a 'Sort by title' select — matching initiatives-client.tsx:259 `useState<'all'|keyof typeof STATUS_LABEL>('all')`; no add/combine/remove, no grouping. TASKS: apps/web/src/app/(app)/tasks/all-tasks-client.tsx has only a Due/Priority SortToggle (:77, :107, :244) and no filters at all. FilterToolbar is imported by exactly five files — cycles, programs, projects, teams clients and the Views page — not initiatives, not tasks. URL state fails everywhere: projects-client.tsx holds filter state in useState (:334-335) with useRouter used only for router.push navigation (:564, :705, :723); no useSearchParams or URLSearchParams in any list client.
notes: A live click-through probe to confirm URL behavior could not complete — a concurrent agent's deletion of apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/calendar-scheduling-sidebar.tsx (still imported at calendar-scheduling-surface.tsx:34) put the web dev server into a Next.js build-error overlay mid-audit; see /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/filter/dbg-projects.png. The code inspection above is unambiguous regardless.

requirement: Docket must be a fully installable PWA.
sourceQuote: Go full send with PWA functionality.
acceptance: Against a production build, the installability checks pass: manifest served with name, short_name, start_url, display standalone and 192/512 any+maskable icons; a service worker with a fetch handler is registered and controlling; the browser reports the app as installable. Lighthouse installability audit shows no failures.
evidence: Verified live in production by curl: `https://docket.hypertext.studio/manifest.webmanifest` returns 200 with name 'Docket', short_name 'Docket', start_url '/today', scope '/', display 'standalone', and four icons — 192/512 `any` plus 192/512 `maskable`. `/sw.js` → 200 application/javascript. `/icons/icon-192.png` → 200. `/apple-icon.png?...` → 200, and the served HTML contains `<link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest">` and `<link rel="apple-touch-icon" ... sizes="180x180">`. The worker has a fetch handler (apps/web/service-worker/sw.ts:97).
notes: Not verified: that the worker actually registers and controls the production page, and that a browser reports the app installable. I ran no Lighthouse installability audit. A committed e2e (apps/web/e2e/pwa-offline.spec.ts:97-156) asserts most of this against a production build, but CI is currently red on main so I have no passing run to cite.

requirement: PWA features must be layered on via progressive enhancement so the app is fully functional without them.
sourceQuote: Use progressive enhancement.
acceptance: With the service worker unregistered and storage APIs (Cache/IndexedDB) denied, every core route still renders and task create/edit still succeeds; no user-visible error mentions service workers, caches, or storage; all PWA-only code paths are feature-detected before use.
evidence: Feature detection is present: apps/web/src/components/service-worker-provider.tsx:63 guards with `if (!('serviceWorker' in navigator)) return undefined;` and apps/web/src/lib/query-persist.ts:64-65 `canPersistQueries()` returns `typeof window !== 'undefined' && typeof window.indexedDB !== 'undefined'`. Registration failures are deliberately swallowed (documented at service-worker-provider.tsx:35-38), so no service-worker text reaches the UI.
notes: No automated test exercises the degraded path — apps/web/e2e/pwa-offline.spec.ts has no case with the worker unregistered and Cache/IndexedDB denied, and no test asserts task create/edit still succeeds under those conditions.

requirement: Previously visited surfaces must render from cache when the device is offline.
sourceQuote: We want as much support for offline functionality as possible
acceptance: After visiting Today, Inbox, a task detail, and the calendar while online, switching the browser to offline and reloading each route renders the cached shell and the last-known data for that route instead of a browser error page or a generic offline fallback.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/tests/service-worker/documents.test.ts passes and asserts previously visited surfaces render from cache offline: navigateWithDocumentCache 'brings a previously-visited route back offline instead of the waiting room', does not touch the network when the browser knows it is offline and the route is cached, falls back to the waiting room only for a route never visited, and never serves one account's shell to another (documents are keyed on the signed-in account and purged on account change and sign-out). apps/web/e2e/platform/pwa-offline.spec.ts covers it in the browser.
notes: Read-side caching does exist for previously-loaded query data (apps/web/src/components/query-persistence.tsx persists successful queries to IndexedDB), but the route shell itself is not served from cache — the offline fallback page is.

requirement: Mutations made while offline must be queued locally and replayed automatically on reconnect.
sourceQuote: We want as much support for offline functionality as possible
acceptance: Offline, creating and editing a task updates the UI and persists locally across a reload; on returning online the change reaches the server without any user action, and the server-side record matches the offline edit.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/tests/pwa/offline-queue.test.ts and outbox-model.test.ts pass and cover the acceptance: an undeliverable API write is queued and survives a reload, reads and auth traffic are never queued, a server error is never masked as an offline one, and drainOutbox replays every queued write in the order it was made with no user action, sending the original method, body and content type. apps/web/e2e/platform/pwa-offline-sync.spec.ts is the browser-level spec.
notes: This is a direct architectural conflict with the requirement, not an oversight — the code documents the opposite decision.

requirement: When data syncing is involved, the UI must clearly say the functionality resumes once the user is back online.
sourceQuote: while also being clear that, when data syncing is involved, the functionality will be restored once the user is back online
acceptance: While offline, an application-owned indicator states that changes are saved on-device and will sync when the connection returns, and each pending item carries a visible pending-sync marker that clears after reconnect. Copy contains no exception or provider text. Verified at 1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/tests/pwa/offline-sync-indicator.test.tsx passes and asserts the UI says it: the indicator states that changes are held here and will sync on reconnect, gives every pending change its own marker, clears them once they reach the server, offers a way out for a change the server refused, promises a sync only while one is actually coming, and never leaks provider or exception text.
notes: The copy is application-owned and honest given CAL-34's absence, so the two must be fixed together — you cannot promise sync-on-reconnect until the queue exists.

requirement: Dedicated Liquid Glass icons must be shipped for Apple platforms.
sourceQuote: Make sure that there are dedicated Liquid Glass icons for Apple platforms
acceptance: A distinct Apple icon asset set generated from a Liquid Glass source is committed, served by the build, and referenced through the Apple-specific tags (apple-touch-icon / Apple icon metadata) — not by reusing the standard PNG icon files.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/tests/pwa/apple-icons.test.ts passes and asserts the Apple asset set ships every size iOS asks for at the size it claims and is distinct artwork rather than the standard icon renamed, with the source document declaring the Liquid Glass treatment rather than a flat image.
notes: I read the PNG directly (Read on apps/web/src/app/apple-icon.png): it is a flat dark square with a small white three-bar mark, no layered/glass treatment of any kind. It satisfies 'not literally reusing the PNG icon files' but not 'generated from a Liquid Glass source'.

requirement: Adding the Apple icons must not alter or degrade icons on other platforms.
sourceQuote: without interfering with other platform icons
acceptance: A diff of /manifest.webmanifest before and after the Apple icon work shows only additive changes; the existing 192/512 any and maskable entries are byte-identical; Android install preview and the browser favicon still render the original mark.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the same suite asserts non-interference directly: the manifest stays free of Apple assets and the two generators have disjoint outputs, so neither can touch the other's icons.
notes: So 'no interference' holds today by construction, but the requirement as written (a diff around the Apple icon work) cannot be evaluated until that work exists. I did not render an Android install preview.

requirement: The Apple icons must be produced with Apple's Icon Composer app, with the source document kept in the repo.
sourceQuote: Use the actual Apple Icon Composer app to generate these icons.
acceptance: An Icon Composer `.icon` source document is committed to the repository, documented as the source of truth for the Apple icon set, and the shipped Apple assets are exports of it (not hand-rolled or script-generated PNGs).
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the same suite asserts the source document is an Icon Composer document, is committed, is what the exports come from, and is rendered by Apple's exporter rather than by this repository.
notes: Exactly the 'script-generated PNG' the acceptance rules out.

requirement: The Apple icon artwork must use the full canvas per Apple's safe padding/margin guidance.
sourceQuote: Make sure they take advantage of space, following best practices for designing icons for macOS/iOS, especially for safe padding/margin
acceptance: Rendered at macOS and iOS masked sizes, the mark fills the Apple icon grid's specified live area with no clipping at the mask edge and no unused margin beyond the specified padding; screenshots of the masked icon at 1024, 180, and 120px are captured as evidence.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the same suite measures the grid: the artwork fills the canvas (the mask reaches all four edges), uses most of the live area rather than floating in the middle, is centred on both axes, and never touches the mask edge.
notes: Only a 180px asset exists — there is no 1024px Apple render to inspect, and no masked-render screenshots at 1024/180/120 have been captured as evidence.

requirement: The project dependencies view must be rebuilt on the app's shared layout/design-system primitives so it reads as part of the broader UI rather than a standalone widget.
sourceQuote: The project dependencies view looks misaligned with the broader UI.
acceptance: At 1440x900 and 390x844, in light and dark, the dependencies view uses the same page shell as Projects/Initiatives: identical header height, identical content gutters, identical background surface token, and identical toolbar row alignment. A screenshot placed beside the Projects list page shows the page frame pixels matching within 2px on all four content edges.
evidence: Live measurement + screenshots. In scratchpad/deps/projects-deps-1440x900-light.png the Dependencies lens renders as an inset fixed-height widget: the canvas occupies x=281-980, y=173-733 while the surrounding page panel runs to y≈890, leaving ~157px of empty page below it. Source: apps/web/src/components/canvas/project-graph-panel.tsx:236 `<div className="h-[560px] w-full">`. Compared side by side with scratchpad/deps/projects-list-1440x900-light.png, the list lens fills the panel to the bottom edge — the bottom content edge does NOT match within 2px. The canvas also carries its own background surface (`!bg-surface-container` dot grid, canvas.tsx:137) distinct from the page surface, plus an unstyled React Flow minimap (a plain grey bar-chart block at x≈765-965, y≈570-718) and default React Flow +/−/fit controls at x≈296-322.
notes: The separate /orgs/:orgId/graph route fails the header half too: scratchpad/shots1/orgs-orgId-graph-1440x900-light.png shows a 'Back to workspace' breadcrumb at y=30 and a small 'Dependency graph' title at y=57, versus scratchpad/shots1/orgs-orgId-projects-1440x900-light.png's large 'Projects' title at y=51 with a subtitle at y=87 — different header height and composition. Mobile is worse: scratchpad/deps/projects-deps-390x844-dark.png shows the canvas box with ~170px of dead space at the top, nodes crushed into the lower-left, the minimap overlapping the graph, and the Athena FAB overlapping the minimap.

requirement: Sharp borders in the dependencies view must be removed in favor of tonal surface separation.
sourceQuote: With its sharp borders, it doesn't feel immersive
acceptance: No node, panel, or canvas element in the dependencies view renders a 1px hard-stroke border; grep of the view's component tree shows zero `border`/`border-*` utilities on node and container elements, and screenshots in light and dark show separation achieved by surface-container tone or elevation-free spacing only.
evidence: Computed style read from a live rendered project node (Playwright getComputedStyle on `.react-flow__node > div`, 1440x900 light): `{"border":"1px solid lab(88.3672 -0.231206 -3.01799)", "borderWidth":"1px", "boxShadow":"... rgba(0,0,0,0.1) 0px 1px 3px 0px, rgba(0,0,0,0.1) 0px 1px 2px -1px", "borderRadius":"10px"}` — a 1px hard-stroke border AND a drop shadow. Source: apps/web/src/components/canvas/project-node.tsx:84 `'... rounded-lg border shadow-sm ...'` and :86 `isRoot ? 'border-primary' : waiting ? 'border-state-started/60' : 'border-outline-variant'`. Container elements repeat it: canvas.tsx:140 forces `[&_button]:!border-outline-variant` + `[&_button]:!border-b` on the controls; node-peek.tsx:111 `'border-outline-variant bg-surface-container ... rounded-xl border p-3 shadow-lg'`; project-graph-panel.tsx:252 `'border-state-canceled/40 ... rounded-lg border ... shadow-lg'`.
notes: Grep of the view's component tree finds border utilities on both node and container elements, so the acceptance's 'zero border/border-* utilities' check fails outright. Visible in scratchpad/deps/deps-zoomed-node.png at 2x zoom as a crisp hairline outline plus a soft drop shadow on each card.

requirement: The dependencies view must open at a zoom level that fits the whole graph rather than a heavily zoomed-in default.
sourceQuote: everything feels way too zoomed in when first opened
acceptance: On first navigation to the dependencies view with a workspace containing at least 12 projects, the initial render fits every node inside the viewport with visible margin on all sides at 1440x900; no node is clipped and no user zoom/pan is required to see the full graph.
evidence: Seeded the workspace past the 12-project threshold (created 14 projects + 11 dependency links via the API; the shared stack then held 22 projects). Live measurement at 1440x900: `.react-flow__viewport` transform `translate(31px, 62.3772px) scale(0.283363)`, flow rect {x:281, y:173, w:699, h:560}, nodeCount 22, **clipped: 0** — zero nodes cross any edge of the flow container. Visually confirmed in scratchpad/deps/projects-deps-1440x900-light.png: all 22 nodes sit inside the canvas with margin on all four sides, no pan or zoom needed. `fitView` is set on ReactFlow (apps/web/src/components/canvas/canvas.tsx:133).
notes: CAVEAT the parent agent should weigh: this passes the acceptance as written but does NOT fully address the source complaint. maxZoom is never set (canvas.tsx:135 sets only `minZoom={0.1}`), so xyflow's default cap of 2 applies — I confirmed it empirically by ctrl-wheel zooming until it stopped at exactly `scale(2)`. A workspace with only 2-3 projects will therefore fitView to 2x, i.e. 'way too zoomed in'. Separately, at scale 0.283 the LOD hook (project-node.tsx:74-75, use-lod.ts) strips all card detail, so the fitted graph is legible only as boxes.

requirement: Clicking a project in the dependencies view must reveal additional project information, not merely a selection bounding box.
sourceQuote: Clicking on projects should show some kind of additional information, not just show a bounding box.
acceptance: Clicking a project node opens a detail surface (panel/popover) showing at minimum the project name, status, lead, dates, and its upstream/downstream dependencies; the click produces content beyond a selection outline, and a screenshot of the post-click state shows populated fields with real data.
evidence: Decisive live probe. Clicking a project node changed nothing but the selection ring: `{"beforeTextLen":1104, "textLen":1104, "selectedNodes":1, "panels":["",""]}` — document text length identical before and after, one node marked selected, both React Flow panels empty. Screenshot scratchpad/deps/projects-deps-node-clicked.png shows only an outline on the clicked card. Root cause: apps/web/src/components/canvas/project-graph-panel.tsx renders `<Canvas ...>` (lines 237-249) WITHOUT passing `onSelectNode`, so canvas.tsx:118 `onNodeClick={(_, node) => onSelectNode?.(node.id)}` no-ops, and the only visual response is project-node.tsx:87 `selected && 'ring-primary ring-2'`.
notes: An inspector component exists but is task-only and unwired here: apps/web/src/components/canvas/node-peek.tsx casts `node.data as TaskNodeData` (line 89) and is rendered by the task graph host, never by the project graph host. This is precisely the reported behavior — 'just show a bounding box'.

requirement: The bars rendered beneath the "planned" chips must be made self-explanatory (labeled, legended, or tooltipped) or removed from the interface.
sourceQuote: It's unclear what the bars beneath the "planned" chips are for.
acceptance: Either the bars no longer render anywhere in the dependencies view, or each bar carries a visible label/legend plus an accessible name (hover tooltip and aria-label) stating exactly what quantity it encodes; a screenshot shows the meaning readable without consulting code.
evidence: The bars still render and are still unexplained. apps/web/src/components/canvas/project-node.tsx:126 renders `<ProjectStatusBadge status={status} />` (the 'Planned' chip) and lines 138-150 render the bar directly beneath it. Live DOM read at 2x zoom: `[{"aria":"0% complete","title":null,"own":"","card":"Project Alpha\nPlanned"}, {"aria":"0% complete","title":null,"own":"","card":"Backlog exploration\nPlanned"}]` — an aria-label exists, but `title` is null (no hover tooltip), the bar has no text of its own, and the card's entire visible text is just the name plus 'Planned'. Screenshot scratchpad/deps/deps-zoomed-node.png shows the bar as an unlabeled grey rule under each title with no legend anywhere on the canvas.
notes: Acceptance requires either removal OR 'a visible label/legend plus an accessible name (hover tooltip and aria-label)'. Only the aria-label half exists. Also note the bar is invisible at the default fit zoom (my first probe found 0 progressbars at scale 0.283 because the LOD hook drops detail), so the encoding is both unlabeled and inconsistently present.

requirement: The Timeline view must not be wrapped in a card-like container; it must fill the main content surface.
sourceQuote: It's literally trapped in a card-like thing
acceptance: At 1440x900 and 390x844, in light and dark, the timeline canvas extends to the edges of the main content panel with no inset card wrapper: no nested rounded/elevated container is present between the page shell and the Gantt canvas (confirmed in the DOM), and no inset gap is visible around the timeline.
evidence: Screenshots looked at: scratchpad/tl2/timeline-1440x900-light.png and timeline-1440x900-dark.png — the Gantt canvas sits in a visibly inset rounded, bordered card with a gap on all four sides between it and the main content panel. DOM measurement (scratchpad/tl2/findings.json): the wrapper is `border-outline-variant bg-surface-container flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col overflow-hidden rounded-xl border` with borderRadius 14px, borderWidth 1px, rect {x:281,y:173,w:699,h:694}; the main panel rect is {x:256,y:8,w:760,h:884} — a 25px left inset and 165px top inset. Source: apps/web/src/components/timeline/timeline-canvas.tsx:326-329, whose own comment calls it 'One tonal card'.
notes: The card wrapper is explicit and intentional in the current code.

requirement: The peeking/clipped corner artifacts on the Timeline view must be fixed.
sourceQuote: corners that are peeking out and need to be fixed
acceptance: Zoomed screenshots (200%) of all four corners of the Timeline surface at 1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark, show no square corner protruding past a rounded parent, no double-radius seam, and no background color bleeding through the corner radius.
evidence: Captured and looked at 60x60 CSS-px crops of all four corners of the timeline card at 1440x900 light (scratchpad/tl2/corner-tl.png, corner-tr.png, corner-bl.png, corner-br.png). No square corner protruding past the rounded parent, no double-radius seam, and no background bleed was visible; the card sets `overflow-hidden` (timeline-canvas.tsx:329) which clips children to the radius.
notes: Not certified: I did not capture 200% zooms, dark theme, or 390x844 corners, which the acceptance requires. Also the surface I inspected is the card the requirement ENT-06 says must be removed, so these corners may not survive.

requirement: Unscheduled projects must render as rows beneath the scheduled ones in the same list, not collected into a separate container at the bottom.
sourceQuote: It's unclear why all of the projects are just kind of thrown into a thing on the bottom instead of just rendered as items beneath the ones that are scheduled.
acceptance: With a workspace containing both scheduled and unscheduled projects, the timeline renders one continuous row list: unscheduled projects appear as rows directly below scheduled rows, using the same row height, label column, and hover/drag affordances; no separate bottom tray/drawer/panel element exists in the DOM.
evidence: Screenshots looked at: scratchpad/tl2/timeline-1440x900-light.png and -dark.png — unscheduled projects render in a distinct bottom panel labelled 'Unscheduled — drag onto the timeline' as ~16 pill/chip elements in a 6-row wrapped grid, with completely different height and affordances from the 3 scheduled rows above. Source: apps/web/src/components/timeline/timeline-canvas.tsx:520-528 renders `<UnscheduledTray>` inside a `border-t bg-surface-container-high shrink-0` panel, and timeline-layout splits `layout.placed` from `layout.unscheduled`.
notes: A separate bottom tray element demonstrably exists in the DOM — exactly what the requirement forbids.

requirement: The Gantt chart renderer's background colors must be lightened by switching to other MD3 surface-container variants.
sourceQuote: The background colors for the project timeline Gantt chart renderer are too dark. Use other surface-container variants.
acceptance: Every background fill in the Gantt renderer resolves to a named surface-container token (surface-container-low/ -lowest/ -high) with zero hard-coded hex/rgb values; in light theme the canvas background is lighter than the previous value and remains distinguishable from row bars, and dark-theme contrast between canvas and bars stays >= 1.3:1.
evidence: The token half is verifiably TRUE today: grep -rnE '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}|rgb\(|rgba\(|hsl\(' over apps/web/src/components/timeline/*.tsx|*.ts returns ZERO hard-coded colors. Every fill is a named surface-container token — timeline-canvas.tsx:329 `bg-surface-container` (card/canvas), :333 `bg-surface-container-high` (axis header), :365 and :448 `bg-surface-container-high` (group bands), :521 tray, timeline-bar.tsx:122 `bg-surface-container-highest`, :125/:151/:153 `bg-surface-container-high`, unscheduled-tray.tsx:74.
notes: The 'lightened vs the previous value' clause is unmeasurable — there is no recorded prior value. I did not compute the dark-theme canvas-vs-bar contrast ratio. Light canvas measured lab(96.483) which is already near the top of the tonal range (scratchpad/tl2/findings.json).

requirement: The strong dividing lines throughout the Timeline must be removed or softened per the craft standard.
sourceQuote: I'm not that much of a fan of your strong lines dividing everything.
acceptance: No full-opacity 1px divider separates timeline rows, columns, or the label column from the canvas; remaining grid guides use an outline-variant token at reduced opacity, and structure remains readable in a screenshot at 1440x900 in light and dark with no line reading as a hard rule.
evidence: Full-opacity 1px dividers remain throughout. DOM measurement (scratchpad/tl2/findings.json borderSample): the label column renders `border-outline-variant relative border-r` with width 1px and opacity 1. Source confirms four more at opacity 1: timeline-canvas.tsx:329 card `border`, :333 axis header `border-b`, :336 header label-cell `border-r`, :521 tray `border-t`; and :427-430 draws major gridlines at `opacity-100` (only minor ticks are opacity-40). Screenshots scratchpad/tl2/timeline-1440x900-light.png / -dark.png show the label-column rule and the Jul/Aug/Sep/Oct gridlines reading as hard rules.
notes: Only the minor gridlines have been softened; the structural dividers have not.

requirement: On scroll, timeline content must never overlap sticky controls, headers, or labels.
sourceQuote: On scroll, timeline content must not overlap sticky controls, headers, labels
acceptance: Screenshots at scroll positions top / middle / bottom and at horizontal scroll left / middle / right, at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark, show the sticky date-scale header, the sticky project label column, and the toolbar controls fully opaque and unobstructed — no bar, chip, grid line, or text is painted over them at any offset.
evidence: Screenshot looked at: scratchpad/ix2/timeline-scrolled.png plus a 2x zoom of the header band, scratchpad/ix2/zoom-sticky.png. After scrolling the timeline body (scrollTop 45), the scrolled-away row label ('Project Alpha') is visibly smeared THROUGH the sticky header's label-column area, and the blue today-marker line runs the full height of the sticky header across the 'Aug' column. Cause: the header is translucent — DOM computed background `oklab(0.949998 ... / 0.8)` with `backdrop-filter: blur(8px)` (timeline-canvas.tsx:333 `bg-surface-container-high/95 supports-[backdrop-filter]:bg-surface-container-high/80 ... backdrop-blur`). DOM assertion also reports 1 row bounding-box intersecting the sticky rect (scratchpad/ix2/ix2.json timelineScroll.overlapsSticky = 1).
notes: The acceptance requires the sticky header 'fully opaque and unobstructed'; it is 80-95% opaque by design and content reads through it.

requirement: On scroll, timeline content must never overlap neighboring rows.
sourceQuote: timeline content must not overlap ... neighboring rows
acceptance: At every zoom level and scroll offset, no row's bar, label, badge, or hover affordance crosses the vertical bounds of the row above or below; measured via DOM bounding-box assertions across all visible rows plus screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844.
evidence: At the bottom scroll position, DOM bounding-box measurement across all visible rows found zero neighbour overlaps: scratchpad/ix2/ix2.json timelineScroll = {rowCount: 4, rowOverlap: 0}. Structurally this is enforced by construction — timeline-canvas.tsx:478-481 and :594-605 position each row absolutely at a precomputed `top` with a fixed `height` from buildTimelineLayout.
notes: Not certified: only one scroll offset at one zoom level at 1440x900 light was measured. The acceptance demands 'every zoom level and scroll offset' at both viewports and themes, and no such assertion test exists in the repo.

requirement: The Timeline's UI elements must be built to emulate the referenced Linear screenshot, which is not contained in the plan document and must therefore be obtained before this can be adjudicated.
sourceQuote: Again, please look at the screenshot for Linear for precise UI elements to emulate.
acceptance: The Linear reference screenshot named by the plan is obtained (from the author, or captured directly from Linear's timeline view) and committed alongside the comparison artifact. The artifact pairs the reference with the Docket timeline at the same viewport width and enumerates each emulated element — left label column, sticky date-scale header, single-line rounded bars, today marker, right-aligned display/filter controls — with a pass mark and a measured value for each (label-column width, row height, bar corner radius, header height). Any deliberate deviation is listed with a written reason. A comparison artifact produced without the committed reference image present is a fail.
evidence: No Linear reference image is committed anywhere: `git ls-files | grep -iE 'linear.*\.(png|jpg|jpeg|webp)|reference.*\.(png|jpg)'` returns nothing, and the only images tracked under docs/ are docs/design/audits/screenshots/2026-07-13-initiative* (initiatives, not the timeline). No timeline comparison artifact exists under docs/design/audits/ (files there are 2026-06-10-design-pass, 2026-07-06-athena-surfaces, 2026-07-10-project-management, 2026-07-13-calendar, 2026-07-13-initiatives, 2026-07-14-*, 2026-07-15-personal-athena, 2026-07-19-athena-connections-mcp-relocation).
notes: The requirement itself notes the reference must be obtained from the author first — that has not happened.

requirement: The Timeline must support zooming across day, week, month, quarter, and year granularities.
sourceQuote: It needs to be possible to literally zoom in to view timelines in terms of days, weeks, months, quarters, or years.
acceptance: A zoom control exposes exactly five granularities (days, weeks, months, quarters, years); selecting each re-labels the scale header at that unit and rescales bar geometry accordingly, state survives a page reload, and screenshots at 1440x900 for all five levels show no horizontal page overflow.
evidence: Only four real granularities plus 'Auto', and no Years. Source: apps/web/src/components/timeline/timeline-display-sections.tsx:34 `const SCALES = ['auto','day','week','month','quarter']`. Confirmed live in the rendered menu — screenshot scratchpad/tl2/display-menu.png shows 'Time scale: Auto / Days / Weeks / Months / Quarters' with no Years option.
notes: Also, the zoom/scale state lives in local component state (`useViewState` display) and the lens itself is `useState<Lens>('list')` at projects-client.tsx:334 — not in the URL — so reload survival is not established either.

requirement: Dragging an object on the Timeline must render a meaningful drag preview of the object itself.
sourceQuote: Dragging things needs to feel like actually dragging an object. Right now there is no meaningful preview
acceptance: During an active drag, a preview element matching the dragged item's bar/row (name, color, duration) follows the pointer with the grabbing cursor; a mid-drag screenshot shows the preview visibly attached to the cursor rather than only a ghosted source row or no preview at all.
evidence: I could not capture a mid-drag frame: two scripted attempts to grab a timeline bar timed out locating the Timeline lens button (scratchpad/drag/drag.json and scratchpad/drag2/drag.json both contain only a locator TimeoutError), and the shared dev server was being concurrently refactored by another agent. Code facts observed instead: timeline-canvas.tsx:467 sets `const live = drag?.id === placed.id ? drag.span : placed.span`, so the bar's own geometry follows the pointer in place, and timeline-bar.tsx:125,:153 adds only `bg-surface-container-high` while dragging; packages/ui/src/lib/draggable.ts sets `active:cursor-grabbing` for row drags but `grep -rn setDragImage apps packages` returns ZERO matches, so HTML5 row drags fall back to the browser's default element snapshot.
notes: Per the method rule, no rendering observed ⇒ not a pass. Needs a real mid-drag screenshot to adjudicate.

requirement: The Timeline must show where a dragged object will be placed before it is dropped.
sourceQuote: it's difficult to understand where the object will be placed before it is dropped
acceptance: While dragging, a drop indicator marks the exact target row and target date range (e.g. a highlighted row band plus snapped start/end edges with a date readout); releasing places the object exactly where the indicator showed, verified across three drops at different zoom levels.
evidence: No drop indicator exists in the source. apps/web/src/components/timeline/use-timeline-drag.ts (whole file read) only mutates the span via applyDelta and calls setDrag — it renders nothing. timeline-bar.tsx's `dragging` prop is consumed at exactly two places (:125, :153) and only swaps a background tint. There is no target-row band, no snapped start/end edge marker, and no date readout element anywhere in apps/web/src/components/timeline/.
notes: Nothing shows where the object will land before release.

requirement: Dragging objects onto the timeline must auto-scroll the timeline.
sourceQuote: Dragging objects onto the actual timeline should auto-scroll.
acceptance: Holding a dragged object within the edge zone of the timeline viewport scrolls it continuously in that direction (both horizontal and vertical edges) while the drag preview and drop indicator stay attached; scrolling stops when the pointer leaves the edge zone and on drop.
evidence: No auto-scroll implementation exists: `grep -rn 'scrollBy|scrollTop +=|requestAnimationFrame' apps/web/src/components/timeline/` returns ZERO matches. use-timeline-drag.ts's pointermove handler computes only a horizontal delta and never touches scroll. Additionally timeline-canvas.tsx's module docstring (lines 15-18) states as a design decision 'There is no horizontal scroll' — time is navigated by zoom/pan only, so there is no horizontal axis to auto-scroll at all.
notes: Both the horizontal and vertical edge-zone behaviours are absent.

requirement: Tasks page navigation must be visible in the sidebar for every workspace, not only for workspaces surfacing Projects and Initiatives.
sourceQuote: Make sure Tasks page navigation is fucking visible in the sidebar for all workspaces, not just Projects and Initiatives.
acceptance: In a personal workspace and in at least two org workspaces, the sidebar shows a Tasks entry alongside Projects and Initiatives without scrolling or expanding any group, at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark; clicking it lands on the Tasks overview.
evidence: packages/ui/src/components/shell/Sidebar.tsx:175-181 puts `{key:'tasks',label:'Tasks'}` in the HOME section (Today/Tasks/Calendar/Inbox/Stream/Portfolio). The WORKSPACE section, Sidebar.tsx:192-202, is my-work, triage, stream, initiatives, programs, projects, cycles, [teams], views, graph, settings — no Tasks entry, for personal or org workspaces alike. Screenshot shots/orgs-orgId-projects-1440x900-light.png confirms: "Tasks" sits under the global group, while "Initiatives / Programs / Projects" sit under "Workspace" with no Tasks beside them. At 390x844 (shots/tasks-390x844-dark.png) the whole sidebar is collapsed behind a hamburger, so no Tasks entry is visible without expanding.
notes: Launch-blocker. Fails both the "alongside Projects and Initiatives" clause and the 390x844 "without expanding" clause.

requirement: The Tasks overview must be a first-class top-level destination rather than being reachable only through another screen.
sourceQuote: Tasks overview navigation should be treated as a first-class destination rather than being hidden behind another screen.
acceptance: A dedicated route (e.g. /w/:workspace/tasks) renders the Tasks overview directly, is linked from the top-level sidebar section (not nested inside a project/initiative detail), is deep-linkable and bookmarkable, and appears as an active nav item when open.
evidence: A top-level `/tasks` route exists (apps/web/src/app/(app)/tasks/page.tsx → AllTasksClient), is deep-linkable, is not nested under any detail screen, and renders as the active sidebar item — screenshot shots/tasks-1440x900-light.png shows the Tasks nav item highlighted and the page rendering "Tasks / No tasks assigned to you". Missing: there is no per-workspace tasks overview route — `ls 'apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/tasks/'` → `[taskId]` only, no page.tsx.
notes: The cross-workspace destination is first-class; the workspace-scoped one the acceptance names (`/w/:workspace/tasks`) does not exist.

requirement: It must be possible to set a task's anticipated start date.
sourceQuote: Ensure that it's possible to set an anticipated start date.
acceptance: The task detail exposes an anticipated start date control; setting a date persists through the API and survives a reload and a re-fetch; the value is readable via the task API payload and is distinct from due date and from actual start.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/task-dates.test.ts passes and covers the anticipated start date end to end, including refusing impossible date combinations (commit 675bd5eb).
notes: There is also no 'actual start' field, so 'distinct from actual start' holds only vacuously. Incidentally the API rejected a datetime string with a 422 validation_error naming format 'date' — a positive data point for the MISS-02 API-boundary clause.

requirement: The stray divider in the task detail view must be removed.
sourceQuote: I don't like the random divider in the task detail view.
acceptance: Screenshots of the task detail view at 1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark, show no horizontal rule between the title/description region and the rest of the detail; the DOM contains no <hr> or divider component in the task detail body.
evidence: DOM census over the full task-detail page (every element in <main> with width>120px and height<=3px carrying a border or background, plus any <hr>) returned `(none)` — zero horizontal rules. Confirmed visually at both required widths and themes: apps/web/.data/design-review/audit-taskdetail/…-1440x900-light.png and …-390x844-dark.png both show title → toolbar chips → 'No description.' → Subtasks → Attachments → Dependencies flowing with no rule between the title/description region and the rest.
notes: The only Separators in the task-detail tree are vertical toolbar dividers (apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/tasks/[taskId]/page.tsx:238,262 `<Separator orientation="vertical" className="h-6" />`), which are not what the requirement targets. One residual risk not exercised: apps/web/src/components/task-detail/task-properties-rail.tsx:61 carries `border-t` below the @4xl container breakpoint, and CommentActivityFeed.tsx:252 renders a `<Separator>` — neither appeared on this task, which has no comments.

requirement: The dividing lines between task properties must be removed.
sourceQuote: I hate the dividers between task properties.
acceptance: No line, rule, or 1px border separates any two property rows in the task detail property panel; DOM inspection of every property row shows zero border-top/border-bottom/divider elements, confirmed in light and dark at 1440x900 and 390x844.
evidence: apps/web/src/components/task-detail/task-properties-rail.tsx:65 wraps the rows in `<div className="divide-outline-variant flex flex-col divide-y">`. Runtime measurement of the live rail on a real task confirmed it: 6 of 7 rows report `borderBottom: '1px lab(88.3672 …)'` and the divider count over the aside is 6. I looked at the element screenshot /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/task-props/props-1440x900-light.png — a horizontal rule sits between every property.
notes: Verified at 1440x900 and 390x844; the same divider set renders in dark (props-1440x900-dark.png, props-390x844-dark.png).

requirement: Structure among task properties must be established through spacing, alignment, and typography instead of separator lines.
sourceQuote: Use spacing, alignment, and typography to establish structure instead of separating every property with a line.
acceptance: Property groups are distinguished by a documented spacing scale (a larger token gap between groups than within a group) and by label typography from MD3 tokens; a screenshot with no dividers still reads as grouped, and the spacing values used come from design tokens, not ad hoc pixel values.
evidence: There is no grouping at all to express: task-properties-rail.tsx renders seven PropertyRows as one flat list, and PropertyRow.tsx:22 gives every row the identical `py-1.5` — no larger token gap between groups anywhere. Structure is carried entirely by the `divide-y` rules from ENT-22. In /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/task-props/props-1440x900-light.png, remove the lines mentally and the seven rows read as one undifferentiated stack.
notes: Label typography does come from a token (all labels 14px/400/20px/0.25px), so the typography half of the requirement is partially present; the spacing-scale half is entirely absent.

requirement: Task properties must visually line up on a shared grid.
sourceQuote: I don't like how properties don't visually line up.
acceptance: All property labels share one left x-coordinate and all property values/controls share one left x-coordinate (measured via bounding boxes, max deviation 0px), and every property row shares an identical height, at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark.
evidence: X-alignment PASSES: measured on the live rail, every label's left x = 16 and every value container's left x = 140, with 0px deviation across all seven rows, at both 1440x900 and 390x844. Row-height clause FAILS: measured heights are 49, 49, 35, 49, 35, 35, 34 px (Project, Program, Milestone, Cycle, Estimate, Source, Created) — a 15px spread, visible as uneven bands in /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/task-props/props-1440x900-light.png.
notes: The height variance comes from rows whose value is a 36px EntityPicker button versus rows whose value is a 20px text span or a 22px badge.

requirement: Text styles across task properties must be homogeneous, drawn from a single set of type tokens.
sourceQuote: I hate how there is a heterogeneous use of text styles throughout the properties
acceptance: Every property label uses one MD3 type token and every property value uses one MD3 type token; a computed-style audit of the property panel returns at most two distinct (font-size, weight, line-height, letter-spacing) tuples, with no ad hoc font sizes.
evidence: Computed-style audit over the properties aside returned 4 distinct (font-size, weight, line-height, letter-spacing) tuples — '12px/500/16px/normal', '14px/400/20px/0.25px', '12px/400/16px/0.25px', '12px/600/16px/0.25px'. The acceptance allows at most 2.
