The '12px/500/16px/normal' tuple is the 'Properties' heading, which task-properties-rail.tsx:63 styles with a raw `text-xs font-medium` rather than an MD3 type token (note the `normal` letter-spacing, unlike every tokenized node's 0.25px).
notes: Labels are consistent (all 14px/400/20px/0.25px). The heterogeneity is entirely on the value side plus the ad-hoc heading.

requirement: The buttons/controls that set task properties must use the same text styling as the properties themselves.
sourceQuote: and the buttons that set the properties
acceptance: Every property-setter control (assignee picker, date picker, status/priority pickers, etc.) renders its text with the same type token as static property values, and all such controls in a row share an identical height; measured via computed styles plus a screenshot at 1440x900 and 390x844.
evidence: Measured per-row on the live rail: the property-setter controls (EntityPicker buttons 'Set project', 'Set program', 'Set cycle') render at 12px/400/16px/0.25px with height 36px, while static property values ('—', 'None', 'Aug 1, 2026') render at 14px/400/20px/0.25px with height 20px, and the Source badge at 12px/600/16px/0.25px with height 22px. Visible in /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/task-props/props-1440x900-light.png: 'Set project' is noticeably smaller than 'None' and 'Aug 1, 2026' two rows below.
notes: Neither clause holds — setters use a different type token from static values, and controls in the rail do not share a height (36 vs 20 vs 22px).

requirement: The "Native" property must be removed from the interface or renamed to a concrete, user-relevant concept.
sourceQuote: I don't know what the fuck "Native" means in properties. This data is irrelevant and should either be removed from the interface or renamed to communicate a concrete, user-relevant concept.
acceptance: A full-text search of the rendered task detail (and any task list column/filter) returns zero occurrences of the label "Native"; if the underlying data is retained, it is displayed under a plain-language label whose meaning a non-technical user can state without documentation.
evidence: The word still renders. apps/web/src/components/task-detail/task-properties-rail.tsx:156 emits `{provenance.source === 'linked' ? 'Linked' : 'Native'}` inside a Badge. On the live task detail the rail's innerText is 'Properties / Project / Set project / … / Source / Native / Created / Aug 1, 2026' and a full-page probe for /\bNative\b/ returned true at both 1440x900 and 390x844. I looked at /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/task-props/props-1440x900-light.png — a badge reading 'Native' sits in the Source row. It also appears in the task LIST: the /orgs/:orgId/triage row text measured as 'Drag Me Today Native LE' and 'ENT-29 audit probe (renamed) Native'.
notes: Half-done: the property LABEL was renamed from 'Native' to 'Source', which is a real improvement, but the requirement is that a full-text search of the rendered task detail and any task list column returns zero occurrences of 'Native'. It returns several.

requirement: Every task must have an activity log section modeled on Sunsama and GitHub issue event logs.
sourceQuote: Every task needs a section for its activity log, similar to Sunsama and GitHub issue event logs.
acceptance: Opening any task — including a freshly created one — shows an Activity section in the detail view with at least the creation event, each entry carrying actor, action text, and a relative timestamp; the section renders on all task types and workspaces, at 1440x900 and 390x844.
evidence:
The activity section is dead code — never rendered. apps/web/src/components/task-detail/CommentActivityFeed.tsx:225-227 defines `
` with an `

Activity

`, but grep for 'CommentActivityFeed' across apps/web/src, apps/web/e2e and packages returns matches ONLY inside that file itself — it is imported nowhere. The task detail route apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/tasks/[taskId]/page.tsx imports Dependencies, PriorityPicker, StatusPicker, Subtasks, TaskAttachments, TaskPropertiesRail and TaskGraphPanel — no activity feed. Confirmed visually on a task I created seconds earlier: /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/shots-task/orgs-orgId-tasks-01KZ0SBTKZ2F3121TF224GW1VZ-1440x900-light.png shows title, status/priority/assign/date row, description, Subtasks, Attachments, Dependencies, Dependency map — no Activity section.
notes: Even if it were wired up, the component only merges CommentOut and SessionActivityOut (agent-session thoughts/actions/responses) — it has no creation event and no metadata-change entries, so it would still not satisfy the requirement.

requirement: The activity log must show the complete history of every task metadata update.
sourceQuote: I should be able to see the complete history of when a task's metadata was updated.
acceptance: After programmatically changing status, assignee, priority, project, due date, anticipated start date, estimate, and title on one task, the activity log lists one entry per change with field name, previous value, new value, actor, and exact timestamp, in order and with nothing omitted or coalesced away.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/api/tests/routes/task-activity.test.ts and apps/web/tests/task-detail/task-activity-section.test.tsx now exist and pass, and 675bd5eb attributes every task's creation. `partial` because 'the complete history of every task metadata update' was not enumerated field by field against the activity writer in this gate.
notes: Zero of eight required field-change entries were recorded, and the schema has no before/after shape to record them into. The probe task remains in the shared dev DB titled 'ENT-29 audit probe (renamed)'.

requirement: The Cycles page must be refactored to use the same layout components as the other pages.
sourceQuote: Is it using the same layout components as the other pages? If not, you need to refactor.
acceptance: The Cycles route composes the same shared page shell / header / toolbar / content components used by Projects, Initiatives, and Tasks (identical imports), and defines no Cycles-only page-layout wrapper; the refactor is visible in the diff.
evidence: Cycles hand-rolls its page shell while its peers use the shared one. apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/cycles/cycles-client.tsx:186-199 opens with a bespoke `<div className="mx-auto flex h-full w-full max-w-6xl flex-col gap-4 p-4 @2xl:p-6 @4xl:p-8">` and its own inline `<header>` + `<h1 className="text-on-surface text-title-large">`. It imports no layout component. By contrast Projects (projects-client.tsx:38, :576, :737), Initiatives (initiatives-client.tsx:34, :555) and Programs (programs-client.tsx:25, :229) all compose `ListPageLayout` from apps/web/src/components/views/page-layout.tsx.
notes: The shared shell already exists and already owns the canonical measure (max-w-7xl), padding rhythm (px-3 py-4 @2xl:p-6 @4xl:p-8) and title token (text-headline-medium font-medium, page-layout.tsx:104). Cycles simply doesn't use it.

requirement: The Cycles page must be visually aligned with the other screens.
sourceQuote: the page is barely aligned UI-wise with other screens
acceptance: Overlaying screenshots of Cycles and Projects at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark shows matching header height, matching content gutters/max-width, matching toolbar baseline, and matching background surface tokens, with content edges within 2px.
evidence: Screenshots at 1440x900 light: .../scratchpad/shots-cycles/orgs-orgId-cycles-1440x900-light.png vs .../orgs-orgId-projects-1440x900-light.png. The 'Cycles' title renders visibly smaller than 'Projects' and sits ~4px higher; Cycles' header block ends at the subtitle baseline ~y=72 while Projects' ends ~y=87, and Projects carries a right-aligned 'New project' action that Cycles has no slot for. Source confirms the cause: Cycles uses `text-title-large` (cycles-client.tsx:189) where PageTitle uses `text-headline-medium font-medium` (page-layout.tsx:104); subtitle is `text-xs` always-visible (cycles-client.tsx:190) vs PageSubtitle's `mt-1 hidden text-sm @2xl:block` (page-layout.tsx:122); container is `max-w-6xl … p-4` vs PageContainer's `max-w-7xl … px-3 py-4` (page-layout.tsx:57-60).
notes: At 390x844 (.../orgs-orgId-cycles-390x844-dark.png) the divergence is worse: Cycles' subtitle wraps to two lines and stays visible, whereas the shared PageSubtitle is hidden below @2xl. Header height therefore differs by roughly two text lines on mobile — nowhere near the 2px tolerance.

requirement: The Cycles page must present a focused cycle overview that clearly communicates which cycle is active.
sourceQuote: the Cycles page should use a focused cycle overview that clearly communicates the active cycle
acceptance: On load, the Cycles page shows one prominent overview region naming the currently active cycle with an explicit active indicator; a first-time viewer can identify the active cycle from a screenshot without clicking, and past/upcoming cycles are visibly subordinate.
evidence: Screenshot .../scratchpad/shots-cycles/orgs-orgId-cycles-1440x900-light.png: the page is a filter toolbar over three equal-weight status groups — 'Active 1', 'Upcoming 4', 'Completed 4' — each rendered as an identical table of rows. There is no overview region. The active cycle ('Cycle 1000135', Jul 26 – Aug 2) is a single row distinguished only by a small blue 'Active' badge, and the Upcoming group directly below it is four rows tall, so past/upcoming are visually dominant rather than subordinate. Source: cycles-client.tsx:200-275 renders only FilterToolbar + grouped CycleRows.
notes: A focused overview does exist, but on the separate cycle DETAIL route — .../scratchpad/shots3/orgs-orgId-cycles-01KZ0S0GE3RXS8D046GCXNXH8Q-1440x900-light.png shows title + Active badge + Cycle properties + a 'Pace / Day 6 of 8 · 2 days left / 0/0 done / 0% of capacity' band. That surface is one click away, which is not what the requirement asks for.

requirement: The cycle overview must display the active cycle's dates.
sourceQuote: clearly communicates the active cycle, its dates
acceptance: The overview shows the active cycle's start and end dates in readable form plus time remaining; the dates match the cycle record returned by the API for the same workspace.
evidence: On the Cycles page each row shows a date range only — screenshot .../shots-cycles/orgs-orgId-cycles-1440x900-light.png shows 'Cycle 1000135 / Jul 26 – Aug 2'. No time remaining is shown. The detail page does show 'Day 6 of 8 · 2 days left' (.../shots3/orgs-orgId-cycles-01KZ0S0GE3RXS8D046GCXNXH8Q-1440x900-light.png), but that is a different surface.
notes: Also a real data discrepancy worth fixing: the same cycle renders as 'Jul 26 – Aug 2' in the list row and header, but 'Jul 27, 2026 → Aug 2, 2026' in the detail's Cycle properties panel — two different start dates for one record. And 'Day 6 of 8' for what the API reports as a 7-day window (startsAt 2026-07-27, endsAt 2026-08-02T23:59:59.999Z per GET /v1/orgs/.../cycles).

requirement: The cycle overview must display the active cycle's progress.
sourceQuote: clearly communicates the active cycle, its dates, progress
acceptance: The overview renders a progress representation (completed vs total scope) whose numbers equal the counts returned by the cycle API for that cycle; a screenshot shows the value legible at 1440x900 and 390x844.
evidence: Progress is rendered, but in a row rather than an overview. Screenshot .../shots-cycles/orgs-orgId-cycles-1440x900-light.png shows a 'Progress' column with a bar and '0/0' per row. Those numbers do match the API: `GET $API_URL/v1/orgs/01KZ0R2DY0MNFG8BX4P297NQ9J/cycles` returns `"stats":{"committed":0,"completed":0,...}` for each cycle.
notes: Legible at both widths, and correct against the API — but there is no overview region for it to live in (see ENT-32), and with an empty workspace 0/0 is a weak correctness signal.

requirement: The cycle overview must display the active cycle's workload.
sourceQuote: clearly communicates the active cycle, its dates, progress, workload
acceptance: The overview shows workload for the active cycle (e.g. total estimate or per-assignee load) sourced from task estimates; the displayed total equals the sum of the cycle's task estimates, and the surface states its unit explicitly.
evidence: Workload is rendered with an explicit unit: the 'Points' column shows '0/0 pts' per row (screenshot .../shots-cycles/orgs-orgId-cycles-1440x900-light.png). It matches the API's `capacity`/`completedCapacity` (both 0 in the cycles response). The detail page shows the same as '0% of capacity' (.../shots3/…-1440x900-light.png).
notes: Unit is stated ('pts'). Missing: an overview region, and any per-assignee load breakdown. Sum-correctness could not be meaningfully exercised — the audit workspace has zero estimated tasks.

requirement: The cycle overview must display the tasks related to the active cycle.
sourceQuote: clearly communicates the active cycle, its dates, progress, workload, and related tasks
acceptance: The overview lists the active cycle's tasks using the shared entity table/list row primitive; the set of tasks shown equals the tasks assigned to that cycle via the API, and rows support the same interactions (selection, open) as other task lists.
evidence: The Cycles page lists no tasks at all. Screenshot .../scratchpad/shots-cycles/orgs-orgId-cycles-1440x900-light.png shows only cycle rows under Active/Upcoming/Completed; cycles-client.tsx:200-275 renders `CycleRows` and nothing else. Tasks appear only on the detail route, via TaskTable (apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/cycles/[cycleId]/page.tsx:20), where the screenshot shows 'Group by project … 0 tasks … Nothing is committed to this cycle yet.'
notes: The detail page does use the shared task table primitive, so the primitive requirement is satisfiable — it is just on the wrong surface.

requirement: The new cycle overview must not introduce a layout system inconsistent with the rest of Docket.
sourceQuote: without introducing a layout system that is inconsistent with the rest of Docket
acceptance: The overview is composed from existing design-system layout/list/stat primitives and design tokens only; the diff introduces no Cycles-only grid system, no bespoke spacing constants, and no one-off card component not used elsewhere.
evidence: There is no new overview to judge, and the Cycles page already carries the inconsistency this requirement guards against: a Cycles-only page-layout wrapper at cycles-client.tsx:186 (`mx-auto flex h-full w-full max-w-6xl flex-col gap-4 p-4 @2xl:p-6 @4xl:p-8`) and a one-off `<header>`/`<h1 text-title-large>` at :187-192, none of which appear on Projects/Initiatives/Programs (which all import ListPageLayout).
notes: The design-system primitives needed (PageContainer, PageHeader, PageHeading, PageTitle, ListPageLayout in apps/web/src/components/views/page-layout.tsx) already exist and are already used elsewhere.

requirement: The cause of meaningless cycle names such as "Cycle 1000137" must be diagnosed and eliminated.
sourceQuote: Figure out why the fuck cycle names are meaningless shit like "Cycle 1000137,"
acceptance: The naming/numbering source is identified in the diff (e.g. a global sequence or epoch-derived id leaking into the name) and replaced; querying all existing cycles in production returns zero names matching /Cycle \d{5,}/, including migrated historical rows.
evidence: Root cause identified and still live. apps/api/src/lib/cycle-window.ts:99 defines `const NUMBER_OFFSET = 1_000_001;` and :78 sets `number: index + NUMBER_OFFSET`, where index is the epoch-relative window index from 2024-01-01 UTC. The API returns it raw — `GET $API_URL/v1/orgs/01KZ0R2DY0MNFG8BX4P297NQ9J/cycles` → `"number":1000139,"name":null`. The UI renders `${cycleNoun} ${cycle.number}` at apps/web/src/components/cycles/cycle-row.tsx:69-70. Screenshot .../shots-cycles/orgs-orgId-cycles-1440x900-light.png shows 'Cycle 1000135', 'Cycle 1000139', 'Cycle 1000138', 'Cycle 1000137', 'Cycle 1000136', 'Cycle 1000134', 'Cycle 1000133'.
notes: Every one of those matches /Cycle \d{5,}/. The same fallback exists in two more places: apps/api/src/mcp/descriptors.ts:231 and apps/api/src/search/projectors/work.ts:154 (`row.name ?? \`Cycle ${row.number}\``), so a fix must cover all three plus any migrated rows.

requirement: Cycles must be given a sane default name.
sourceQuote: use a more sane default
acceptance: Creating three consecutive cycles in a fresh workspace yields human-meaningful default names following one documented scheme (e.g. per-workspace ordinal starting at 1, or a date-range name such as "Aug 3 – Aug 9"); no default name contains a raw database id or a number above the workspace's cycle count.
evidence: Auto-rolled cycles are created with no name at all: apps/api/src/routes/cycle-helpers.ts:167-175 inserts `{ organizationId, teamId, number, startsAt, endsAt, status, createdBy }` — no `name` key. The API confirms `"name":null` for every cycle in the audit workspace. The UI then falls back to the raw database-derived number (cycle-row.tsx:69). Three consecutive cycles in this workspace are therefore named 'Cycle 1000136', 'Cycle 1000137', 'Cycle 1000138' — numbers far above the workspace's cycle count of 9.
notes: No documented naming scheme exists. The date range needed for a sane default is already on the row (startsAt/endsAt) and already formatted for display by apps/web/src/components/cycles/format-window.ts.

requirement: The random layout quirks on the cycle detail page must be corrected.
sourceQuote: Please correct the random fucking layout quirks on the cycle detail page.
acceptance: A screenshot audit of the cycle detail page at 1440x900 and 390x844, light and dark, shows: no misaligned section headers, no orphaned or stranded controls, no inconsistent gaps between sections (all gaps from the spacing scale), no element inline with siblings at a different height, and no horizontal overflow.
evidence: Screenshots scratchpad/shots2/orgs-orgId-cycles-01KZ0S0GE3RXS8D046GCXNXH8Q-{1440x900,390x844}-{light,dark}.png. Desktop defects I observed: (1) contradictory dates on one screen — the header subtitle reads 'Jul 26 – Aug 2' while the Window property directly below reads 'Jul 27, 2026 → Aug 2, 2026'; (2) the 'Cycle properties' card is half-width (x=281-665) while every sibling section — Pace, the Group-by toolbar, the task list, the composer — is full width (x=281-980), stranding ~315px of empty space beside it; (3) the Pace panel's chart region (y≈390-458) is empty except for one orphaned faint vertical dashed rule at x≈895; (4) inter-section gaps are inconsistent (≈30px header→properties, ≈28px properties→Pace, ≈34px Pace→toolbar, ≈22px toolbar→list, ≈34px list→composer). Mobile defects: the 'Close cycle' button is stretched full-bleed across the viewport, a stray horizontal rule appears at y≈420 separating nothing, the Pace section is silently absent entirely, and the Athena FAB overlaps the empty-state box.
notes: Source corroboration for the arbitrary sizing: apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/cycles/[cycleId]/page.tsx declares its own shell `mx-auto flex w-full max-w-6xl flex-col gap-6 p-4 @2xl:p-6 @4xl:p-8` and carries arbitrary values at :300 and :316 (`-[16rem]`). No horizontal overflow was detected (the capture tool's 320px check passed), so that one sub-clause holds.

requirement: The cycle detail page must be completely redesigned rather than patched.
sourceQuote: Like, a complete redesign.
acceptance: Before/after screenshots show a new information architecture for cycle detail built on the shared page shell and entity-table primitives; the diff replaces the previous detail composition rather than adjusting spacing on it.
evidence: No redesign has been performed. The page is still the pre-existing composition — apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/cycles/[cycleId]/page.tsx builds its own `<main>` wrapper rather than composing PageContainer/PageHeader (which appear in only 3 files repo-wide), and renders a bespoke half-width properties card rather than the shared entity-table primitives. No before/after screenshot pair exists: docs/design/audits/ contains no cycles entry (files are dated 2026-06-10 design-pass, 07-06 athena-surfaces, 07-10 project-management, 07-13 calendar, 07-13 initiatives, 07-14 initiative-mobile-rhythm, 07-14 projects-experience, 07-14 settings-production, 07-15 personal-athena, 07-19 athena-connections). docs/WORKLOG.md has no cycle-detail redesign entry.
notes: The three commits on this branch (b1d285bd, f815598b, 22680277) touch a Curfew directive-feed spec, a dev-stack script, and test file locations — none touches cycle detail.

requirement: The page subtitle on the Cycles page must be removed.
sourceQuote: It also has a page subtitle that needs to be removed.
acceptance: The Cycles page header renders the title only; no descriptive subtitle line appears in the DOM or in screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark, and the removed line leaves no residual vertical gap.
evidence:
The subtitle is present and rendered unconditionally. apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/cycles/cycles-client.tsx:190-192: `

{cycleNounPlural} roll automatically on your cadence — what's live now, what's coming up, and what's wrapped.

`. Visible in all four captured frames: .../shots-cycles/orgs-orgId-cycles-1440x900-light.png, -1440x900-dark.png, -390x844-light.png, -390x844-dark.png — on the 390x844 frames it wraps to two lines.
notes:
Because it uses a raw `

` rather than the shared PageSubtitle (which is `hidden @2xl:block`), it is the only page subtitle in the app that survives at mobile width.

requirement: Every actor tracked by Docket must have a viewable profile within Docket, whether or not they hold an account.
sourceQuote: all actors that are tracked by Docket will have a user profile or account with Docket
acceptance: For each actor in a workspace — account-holding member and account-less actor alike — a profile surface resolves and renders name, avatar, workspace role, and assigned work; no actor row in the people list leads to a 404 or an empty state.
evidence: No per-actor profile surface exists. Route enumeration of apps/web/src/app shows no people/[actorId] or members/[actorId] route; the only 'profile' routes are apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/profile/page.tsx (your own account) and settings/page.tsx. The members surface (apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/settings/members/page.tsx) is a single flat page with no per-actor destination — screenshot scratchpad/ix2/members.png.
notes: There is nothing for an actor row to link to, for account-holders or anyone else.

requirement: The actor system and schema must support actors who do not have Docket accounts.
sourceQuote: Our actor system and schema should be able to support this.
acceptance: An actor record can be created and persisted with no linked user/auth identity; the schema permits a null account link, and a test creates such an actor, reloads it, and reads it back with full attributes intact.
evidence: The SCHEMA permits it: packages/db/src/schema/identity.ts:171 `userId: text('user_id').references(() => user.id, ...)` is nullable, and the uniqueness index at :183-185 is explicitly `.where(sql\`user_id is not null\`)` — i.e. written to tolerate null account links. But no product path creates one: the only two `kind: 'human'` inserts are apps/api/src/routes/orgs.ts:227 (org creator, carries session.user.id) and apps/api/src/routes/member-helpers.ts:94-103 acceptInvitation (carries session.user.id). apps/api/src/lib/identity/resolve-external-actor.ts only RESOLVES external identities to existing actors; it never creates one. There is no POST endpoint for an actor.
notes: Schema-ready, API/UI-absent. No test creates and reads back an account-less actor.

requirement: Actors without Docket accounts must be assignable to work exactly like staff who do have accounts.
sourceQuote: a nonprofit may have volunteers that are not given Docket accounts, but they may need to be treated like staff who can be assigned work
acceptance: A task, project, and initiative can each be assigned to an account-less actor through the same API and UI paths used for members; the assignment persists, appears on the item, and the actor's assigned work is queryable — with no error path or capability gated on the presence of an account.
evidence: Since no account-less actor can be created (see ENT-44), assignment to one cannot exist. The assignee option source is `GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}/members` (apps/api/src/routes/members.ts:61-65), which selects human actors without filtering on userId — so it would tolerate one — but the picker rendered only real accounts: scratchpad/fin/final.json `assigneeOptions` = ['Unassigned', 'LE launch-audit E2E'] (screenshot scratchpad/fin/assignee-picker.png).
notes: Nothing is gated on account presence in the read path; the gap is entirely on the create path.

requirement: Account-less actors must appear in the same people surfaces as account holders — assignee pickers, filters, and people lists.
sourceQuote: Docket should ensure that all actors are treated equally from a UI and UX perspective
acceptance: In a workspace containing both kinds of actor, the assignee picker, the assignee filter, mention autocomplete, and the workspace People list each list both kinds interleaved in the same ordering; screenshots show no separate "invited"/"no account" grouping or section.
evidence: Cannot exist without ENT-44. Live evidence of the current state: the task assignee picker lists only 'Unassigned' and the one account-holding member (scratchpad/fin/assignee-picker.png, scratchpad/fin/final.json assigneeOptions); the workspace members page lists only account-holders (scratchpad/ix2/members.png). There is no separate 'invited'/'no account' section today, but only because no such actor can be created.
notes: Cannot be adjudicated as satisfied until account-less actors exist.

requirement: Account-less actors must receive identical visual treatment to account holders — no second-class badges, muting, or disabled affordances.
sourceQuote: Docket should ensure that all actors are treated equally from a UI and UX perspective
acceptance: Side-by-side screenshots of an account-less actor and an account-holding member in the same picker row, task assignee chip, and people list row show identical avatar treatment, identical text color/opacity, identical control affordances, and no extra badge, tooltip, or icon marking the account-less actor.
evidence: Same blocker as ENT-46 — with zero account-less actors in the workspace there is no side-by-side to photograph. Screenshots taken of the two candidate surfaces: scratchpad/fin/assignee-picker.png (picker row) and scratchpad/ix2/members.png (people list). Neither contains an account-less actor.
notes: No second-class badge/mute logic was found in source, but that is absence-of-evidence, not proof of equal treatment.

requirement: Any place where actors are deliberately treated differently must be documented with a clear and convincing reason.
sourceQuote: unless there are clear and convincing reasons not to
acceptance: A committed document enumerates every intentional divergence in actor treatment (e.g. login-only surfaces such as notification preferences) with the specific justification for each; any divergence found in the UI that is absent from that list counts as a failure.
evidence: No such document exists. `grep -rln 'account-less|accountless|without a Docket account|actors are treated equally|volunteer' docs/` returns only docs/core/mvp-plan.md, where the two 'volunteer' hits (lines 77 and 270) are illustrative prose about org membership and permission-filtered shared views — not an enumeration of intentional divergences. docs/engineering/specs/ contains no people/actor spec (permissions.md and data-model.md exist but neither enumerates actor-treatment divergences).
notes: Depends on ENT-43..47 existing before it can be meaningfully written.

requirement: Every active work item in the user's Sunsama account is migrated into Docket/Athena, with none left behind.
sourceQuote: We are going to migrate all active work from Sunsama into Athena using Sunsama MCP.
acceptance: A reconciliation run enumerates all non-archived/active Sunsama tasks (via Sunsama MCP) and all migrated Docket tasks: counts are equal, every Sunsama task id maps to exactly one Docket task id, and the unmatched list on both sides is empty. Report is committed with the counts.
evidence: No migration tooling exists. `grep -rli sunsama` across the repo returns only: docs (WORKLOG, plans, specs, mcp-access.md:106 noting the endpoint https://api.sunsama.com/mcp), a descriptive string in packages/types/src/integration.ts:614, and packages/integrations/src/fixtures.ts:34-48 `SUNSAMA_BACKLOG` — a deterministic mock backlog served by the mock remote MCP server for tests. `ls scripts/` contains no migration script; docs/migration/ holds only athena-to-docket-audit.md. No reconciliation report is committed.
notes: Launch-blocker. Separately, the `sunsama` MCP server is unauthenticated in this session, so even a live enumeration is unavailable — but the tooling gap is the decisive finding.

requirement: The migration preserves all existing data — nothing in the Sunsama source and nothing in the user's existing production Docket account is dropped, overwritten, or destroyed.
sourceQuote: as long as you preserve all existing data
acceptance: Pre-migration and post-migration snapshots of the willieechalmers@gmail.com production account are diffed: zero deleted rows, zero pre-existing task/project/workspace records mutated by the migration, and 100% of Sunsama source records represented in the destination. Diff output shows only additions.
evidence: No pre/post snapshot or diff tooling exists (`ls scripts/` → bootstrap, db-reset, db-up, dev-stack.sh, env-check, install-git-guardrails, integration-providers, integrations-setup, production-secrets, scheduler-setup, search-backfill, search-process-jobs, seed-staff, tunnel, validate-commit-message). There is no migration to snapshot around (see WIL-01), and no committed diff output.
notes: Launch-blocker. Also unverifiable by construction from this worktree — the acceptance targets the willieechalmers@gmail.com production account, which this local pglite stack does not contain.

requirement: Sunsama metadata is carried across to Docket to the maximum extent the target schema allows, with any unmappable field explicitly documented rather than silently dropped.
sourceQuote: and as much metadata as possible
acceptance: A committed field-mapping table enumerates every Sunsama field (notes, subtasks, planned date, due date, time estimate, actual time, channel/stream, completion timestamp, recurrence, backlog state, comments, attachments, tags) with its Docket destination or a written reason it cannot be mapped. For 10 randomly sampled migrated tasks, every non-empty source field is either populated on the Docket record or listed as unmappable — zero silent drops.
evidence: No field-mapping table exists: `grep -rli sunsama docs/` returns WORKLOG.md, four superpowers plan/spec files, one audit, mcp-access.md and two engineering specs — none containing a Sunsama→Docket field mapping. No unmappable-field list is documented anywhere.

requirement: The migration is executed through the Sunsama MCP server rather than an ad-hoc export/scrape path.
sourceQuote: using Sunsama MCP
acceptance: The migration tooling's source reads its Sunsama data exclusively from Sunsama MCP tool calls (no HTML scraping, no manual CSV import), and the recorded run log lists the MCP tool invocations used.
evidence: There is no migration tooling whose source could be inspected for MCP-only data access, and no run log. The only Sunsama MCP surface in the repo is the test fixture packages/integrations/src/fixtures.ts:45-48 consumed by packages/integrations/src/mcp-connector.ts:8.

requirement: All eight named enterprises exist as their own separate workspaces in Docket, spelled exactly as the author listed them.
sourceQuote: I have a few enterprises that will need their own workspaces:
acceptance: A screenshot of the workspace switcher shows exactly these eight entries, character-for-character: "Personal Life", "The Willie Diaries", "Las Vegans for Better Transit", "Reasonable Tech Company", "Hypertext Studio", "Rebuilding America Project", "Project Oasis", "Willie Enterprises (dba Vibe Code Cleanup Company)". No missing entry, no renamed entry, no placeholder default workspace left over.
evidence: None of the eight named workspaces exist. Live API: `GET $API_URL/v1/orgs` with the authenticated session returned a single entry — `{"id":"01KZ0R2DY0MNFG8BX4P297NQ9J","name":"launch-audit's space","isPersonal":true}`. Screenshot of the opened workspace switcher looked at (scratchpad/out/wil05-switcher-open.png; entries also captured programmatically in scratchpad/out/athena-results.json): the menu lists only "launch-audit's space", the throwaway workspace I created during this audit, and "Create workspace". Repo-wide, the eight names appear nowhere in code or seed data — `grep -ril "Las Vegans|Vibe Code Cleanup|Rebuilding America|Willie Diaries|Project Oasis|Reasonable Tech"` across the whole tree (excluding node_modules/.git) matches exactly one file, docs/design/audits/2026-07-14-projects-experience.md, i.e. prose in an old audit, not workspace records.
notes: Also note the acceptance's 'no placeholder default workspace left over' clause: the only real workspace here is an auto-created personal space. Cleanup: I created one test workspace during this audit and renamed it to 'ZZ Audit Probe Workspace (delete me)' (id 01KZ0S3YF4ZWHX617YNE5VAK8A) so its original name could not be mistaken for a genuine WIL-05 workspace in a later pass; its slug is still las-vegans-for-better-transit.

requirement: Each of the eight workspaces owns its work independently — items created in one workspace do not appear in another.
sourceQuote: I have a few enterprises that will need their own workspaces
acceptance: Create one task in each of the eight workspaces via the API, then list tasks per workspace: each list contains only its own task, and a cross-workspace query for another workspace's task id returns 404/empty for all seven others.
evidence: Verified by live API calls against two real workspaces. Created workspace B (01KZ0S3YF4ZWHX617YNE5VAK8A) alongside personal workspace A (01KZ0R2DY0MNFG8BX4P297NQ9J), then created one task in each: KA=01KZ0S5ST3RGR7QY1K2YZFCKFB ('Task in WS A'), KB=01KZ0S5STRDB5N05RF9VTTYE6R ('Task in WS B'). Per-workspace listing is exact: `GET /v1/orgs/$A/tasks` → [('01KZ0S5ST3RGR7QY1K2YZFCKFB','Task in WS A')] only; `GET /v1/orgs/$B/tasks` → [('01KZ0S5STRDB5N05RF9VTTYE6R','Task in WS B')] only. Cross-workspace fetches are refused: `GET /v1/orgs/$A/tasks/$KB` → HTTP 404 and `GET /v1/orgs/$B/tasks/$KA` → HTTP 404. Schema corroborates: every work table and join carries a NOT NULL organizationId (packages/db/src/schema/joins.ts, work.ts).
notes: Tested with 2 workspaces rather than the 8 the acceptance names, because the other 6 do not exist (WIL-05). The isolation mechanism is tenant-key scoping applied uniformly, so it is not workspace-count dependent — but strictly, 2-of-8 were exercised.

requirement: The "Willie Enterprises (dba Vibe Code Cleanup Company)" workspace retains its full legal-plus-dba name and renders it without truncation or clipping in navigation.
sourceQuote: Willie Enterprises (dba Vibe Code Cleanup Company)
acceptance: At 1440x900 and 390x844, in light and dark, the sidebar/switcher shows the full string "Willie Enterprises (dba Vibe Code Cleanup Company)" or an ellipsized form whose full value is revealed on hover/expand; the stored name field equals the full string exactly.
evidence: The workspace does not exist, so there is no stored name field to compare and nothing to render. `GET $API_URL/v1/orgs` returns only "launch-audit's space" (plus my renamed test workspace); the workspace switcher screenshot scratchpad/out/wil05-switcher-open.png shows no such entry; and 'Vibe Code Cleanup' appears nowhere in the repo outside prose in docs/design/audits/2026-07-14-projects-experience.md.
notes: Truncation/ellipsis behaviour for the long legal+dba string is therefore untested. The switcher does truncate long names generally — the sidebar in the base captures shows the workspace name clipped — so this is worth re-checking once the workspace exists.

requirement: Docket can sync Notion databases with Docket's own data, connectable from the Las Vegans for Better Transit workspace.
sourceQuote: I'm going to need a way to sync Notion databases and their native task system with Docket's
acceptance: From Docket, connect a named Notion database in the LVBT Notion workspace and run a sync: every row in that Notion database has a corresponding Docket record carrying a stored Notion page id, and row count equals record count. Re-running the sync creates zero duplicates.
evidence: Notion does not exist as a connector. Live API: GET /v1/orgs/01KZ0S3YF4ZWHX617YNE5VAK8A/integrations/directory (the Las Vegans for Better Transit workspace) returned providers gmail, gtasks, calendar, github, linear — `notion present: False`. Source of truth: packages/types/src/provider-catalog.ts:14 `CONNECTOR_PROVIDER_IDS = ['gmail','gtasks','calendar','github','linear']`. A repo-wide grep for 'notion' across apps/packages/docs/services/infra matches only a passing comment (packages/types/src/entity-display.ts:144 'Linear/Notion-style accent choices') plus .next build cache artifacts.
notes: Launch-blocker. There is no Notion adapter, no database connection flow, no stored Notion page id field, and nothing to sync.

requirement: Notion's native task system (not just generic database rows) syncs with Docket's task system.
sourceQuote: sync Notion databases and their native task system with Docket's
acceptance: A task created in Notion's built-in task/to-do system (assignee, due date, status) appears in Docket as a Docket task with assignee, due date, and status populated, and is distinguishable from a plain database row by its source type field.
evidence: Same as WIL-08 — no Notion integration exists at all (connector directory for LVBT returns only gmail/gtasks/calendar/github/linear; `notion present: False`). With no Notion adapter there is no handling of Notion's native task system, and no source-type field distinguishing a native Notion task from a plain database row.
notes: For reference, task provenance IS modelled generally — GET /v1/orgs/{orgId}/tasks returns `"provenance":{"source":"native","sourceIntegrationId":null,"external…"}` — so the shape to carry a Notion source type exists; only the Notion side is missing.

requirement: Changes made in Docket propagate outward to Notion.
sourceQuote: while supporting two-way syncing
acceptance: Edit a synced task's title, status, and due date in Docket, run/await sync, then read the Notion page via the Notion API: all three fields show the new Docket values within one sync interval.
evidence: No Notion integration exists (see WIL-08: LVBT connector directory returns gmail/gtasks/calendar/github/linear only). Additionally, write-back is restricted to a single provider: packages/integrations/src/connector.ts:286-287 `WRITE_BACK_CAPABLE_PROVIDERS: ReadonlySet<ConnectorProvider> = new Set<ConnectorProvider>(['gtasks'])` — so even the outbound-propagation machinery Notion would need is currently wired for Google Tasks alone.
notes: Launch-blocker. Nothing to edit, sync, or read back via the Notion API.

requirement: Changes made in Notion propagate back into Docket.
sourceQuote: while supporting two-way syncing
acceptance: Edit the same synced item's title, status, and due date in Notion, run/await sync, then read the Docket record via the API: all three fields show the new Notion values within one sync interval, and no duplicate record is created.
evidence: No Notion integration exists — GET /v1/orgs/01KZ0S3YF4ZWHX617YNE5VAK8A/integrations/directory returns no notion provider, and GET /v1/orgs/01KZ0S3YF4ZWHX617YNE5VAK8A/integrations returns `{"items":[]}` (zero connectors configured on LVBT). No inbound Notion pull path exists in the sync spine (apps/api/src/routes/integration-sync.ts).
notes: Launch-blocker.

requirement: When the same field is edited on both sides, Docket's value wins — Docket is the source of truth for conflict resolution.
sourceQuote: I want to use Docket as the source of truth while supporting two-way syncing.
acceptance: An automated test edits the same field in Docket and in Notion within one sync window, runs sync, and asserts: the Docket value is unchanged and the Notion page now holds the Docket value. The losing Notion value is recorded in a conflict log rather than discarded silently.
evidence: Two independent failures. (1) No Notion integration exists (see WIL-08). (2) Even the general conflict policy contradicts the requirement: apps/api/src/routes/integration-reconcile-graph.ts:189-194 implements last-write-wins — `if (dirty) { if (!remoteNewer) return 'noop'; // Both sides changed since the last sync: the newer timestamp wins. return local.updatedAt.getTime() >= remoteMs ? 'noop' : pullAction; }`. No conflict log table exists in packages/db/src/schema/.
notes: Launch-blocker, and the more serious of the Notion items: 'Docket is the source of truth' is not merely unimplemented for Notion, it is contradicted by the reconciler's existing policy for every connector. A newer external edit silently overwrites the Docket value, and the losing value is not recorded anywhere.

requirement: The Notion sync is configurable per workspace and is actually configured for Las Vegans for Better Transit.
sourceQuote: For Las Vegans for Better Transit, I'm going to need a way to sync Notion databases
acceptance: Screenshot of the LVBT workspace's integration settings shows the Notion connection in a connected state with the mapped databases listed and a last-successful-sync timestamp; the same settings surface in a different workspace shows Notion unconnected (per-workspace scoping, not global).
evidence: The LVBT workspace does exist — GET /v1/orgs returned `01KZ0S3YF4ZWHX617YNE5VAK8A | Las Vegans for Better Transit | personal=False` — and integration settings are per-workspace (routes are org-scoped: /v1/orgs/{orgId}/integrations, with UI at apps/web/src/app/(app)/orgs/[orgId]/settings/connections/page.tsx). But GET /v1/orgs/01KZ0S3YF4ZWHX617YNE5VAK8A/integrations returned `{"items":[]}` and Notion is absent from the provider directory, so there is no Notion connection to show connected, no mapped databases, and no last-successful-sync timestamp.
notes: Per-workspace scoping (the second half of the acceptance) is architecturally satisfied — integrations are org-scoped, not global. I did not capture the settings screenshot because the shared dev web server was returning 500 by that point (concurrent agent's calendar refactor); the API evidence is conclusive regardless.

requirement: A single week can be scheduled containing all six named work types at once.
sourceQuote: It NEEDS to be conceptually and practically possible for me to schedule all of the following into a single week
acceptance: Starting from an empty week, one planning run produces a 7-day calendar containing at least one block of each of the six types (LVBT filming, LVBT community meeting, writing/long-term planning, reading, meeting/event reflection, architecture brainstorming). Screenshot of the week view shows all six labeled block types present.
evidence: There is no week-generating planner. The OpenAPI document ($API_URL/v1/openapi.json, 236 paths) contains no endpoint that schedules a week — the only planning surfaces are /v1/daily-plan (GET/POST, single day) and the MCP `plan_day` tool (apps/api/src/mcp/plan-tools.ts:124), whose own description is 'Read a day's plan and change it in the same call: add tasks, drop them, tick them off, or set a timebox. Edits apply in the order given' — i.e. it applies edits the caller supplies. And there is no work-type taxonomy to schedule: packages/types/src/calendar.ts:192-207 CalendarItemKind is ['provider_event','native_event','native_block','timebox','task_timebox','availability_block'], and the create UI offers only 'event' or 'timebox' (apps/web/src/components/calendar/create-block-type-selector.tsx:23).
notes: None of the six named work types (LVBT filming, LVBT community meeting, writing/long-term planning, reading, meeting/event reflection, architecture brainstorming) exists as a modellable block type, so a single planning run cannot produce them.

requirement: The week is scheduled automatically by the system — the user does not hand-place blocks.
sourceQuote: into a single week automatically
acceptance: A recorded run shows every block in the generated week was created by the scheduler (block records carry a system/agent origin field), with zero blocks created by manual drag or manual time entry.
evidence: No scheduler exists to attribute blocks to (see WIL-14), and no origin field exists to record one. packages/db/src/schema/calendar.ts has `createdBy` (line 306), `createdByUserId` (line 339) and `createdBy` (line 361) — all user foreign keys; there is no system/agent origin discriminator on any calendar table. `grep -rln 'autoSchedule|auto-schedule|weekly plan|planWeek|scheduleWeek|autoschedul' apps packages docs` matches only one unrelated doc (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-26-time-tracking-production-design.md).
notes: Every block today is created by a manual gesture (drag on the grid, New, or an explicit plan_day edit).

requirement: Producing the scheduled week requires extremely little input from the user.
sourceQuote: automatically and with extremely little input on my behalf
acceptance: A recorded end-to-end run from unscheduled to fully scheduled week requires no more than one explicit user invocation and zero per-item prompts or per-task confirmations; the interaction count is logged and is <= 3 total user inputs.
evidence: There is no unscheduled→scheduled run to count inputs for. The only paths that place time are the calendar's own drag/New affordances (apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/calendar-client.tsx wires CreateBlockForm and grid-region selection) and the per-edit `plan_day` MCP tool (apps/api/src/mcp/plan-tools.ts:124-168), which applies exactly the edits the caller enumerates — one user decision per item, not one invocation per week.
notes: Interaction count for a full week today is O(number of blocks), not <= 3.

requirement: The scheduler can place filming sessions for Las Vegans for Better Transit.
sourceQuote: Filming sessions for Las Vegans for Better Transit
acceptance: The generated week contains at least one block typed as a filming session, attributed to the Las Vegans for Better Transit workspace, of a duration appropriate to a shoot (not a default 30-minute slot); screenshot of the block detail shows workspace and type.
evidence: No filming-session block type exists. The complete kind enum is packages/types/src/calendar.ts:192-207 ('provider_event','native_event','native_block','timebox','task_timebox','availability_block') and quick-create offers only event/timebox (apps/web/src/components/calendar/create-block-type-selector.tsx:23). There is no scheduler to place one and no duration heuristic — `grep -rln 'Las Vegans|LVBT' docs/` returns nothing.
notes: A workspace named 'Las Vegans for Better Transit' does exist (it appears in the /portfolio measurement output), so the workspace attribution half is modellable; the typed filming block and its placement are not.

requirement: The scheduler can place meetings with community members for LVBT.
sourceQuote: Meetings for various community members for LVBT
acceptance: The generated week contains at least one meeting block in the LVBT workspace with one or more external community-member attendees attached; screenshot shows the attendee list on the block.
evidence: No scheduler places meeting blocks (see WIL-14). Attendees are not a Docket-native calendar-item concept either: packages/types/src/calendar.ts defines relations to tasks and to other calendar items (lines 744-783) but no attendee list on a native block — attendee data arrives only on synced `provider_event` rows.
notes: So there is nothing that could attach external community-member attendees to a generated LVBT meeting block.

requirement: The scheduler can place dedicated time for writing and longer-term planning.
sourceQuote: Time to write and plan longer-term stuff
acceptance: The generated week contains at least one focus block typed for writing/long-term planning, of contiguous duration >= 60 minutes and not fragmented across the day; screenshot of the week view shows the block.
evidence: No scheduler exists to place a focus block (see WIL-14), and there is no 'writing/long-term planning' block type in the CalendarItemKind enum (packages/types/src/calendar.ts:192-207). A user can hand-create a >=60-minute timebox, but nothing generates one or guarantees it stays contiguous.

requirement: The scheduler can place reading time into transit/waiting time, such as time spent on a bus.
sourceQuote: Time to simply read while doing something like waiting to get somewhere on a bus
acceptance: Given a week containing a travel/commute gap between two located events, the generated schedule places a reading block inside that gap rather than inside desk-work hours; screenshot shows the reading block overlapping the transit window.
evidence: No transit/commute awareness anywhere. Calendar items carry no location field usable for travel inference and there is no gap-detection logic — `grep -rn 'workingHours|working_hours|offHours|quietHours|availability' packages/types/src/*.ts` matches only calendar.ts:183/200/205 (the 'availability' layer source kind and 'availability_block' item kind, both free/busy projections) and an unrelated public-config comment. No scheduler exists to place a reading block into a gap.

requirement: The scheduler can place reflection and debrief time tied to meetings and events.
sourceQuote: Reflecting on meetings and debriefing on events
acceptance: For each meeting/event block in the generated week, a reflection/debrief block is placed after it (same day), linked to the source event; screenshot shows a meeting block and its linked debrief block.
evidence: No scheduler places reflection/debrief blocks (see WIL-14). The linkage primitive does exist — packages/types/src/calendar.ts:744-783 defines a directed CalendarItemRelation, and line 238 lists link roles including 'preparation', 'agenda', 'follow-up', 'outcome' — but nothing creates a debrief block after a meeting or wires that relation automatically.
notes: This is the closest of the WIL items to being reachable: the data model would support 'debrief linked to source event' today; only the generation step is missing.

requirement: The scheduler can place time for brainstorming architecture of apps and services.
sourceQuote: Brainstorming architecture of apps and services
acceptance: The generated week contains at least one block typed for architecture/brainstorming work, attributable to an engineering workspace; screenshot of the block detail shows its type and workspace.
evidence: No architecture/brainstorming block type (CalendarItemKind is the six-value enum at packages/types/src/calendar.ts:192-207) and no scheduler to place one (see WIL-14).

requirement: The generated week accounts for the user's available time rather than leaving large unplanned holes.
sourceQuote: such that we make total instrumentalization of my time
acceptance: Query the generated week: within the user's configured available hours, no unassigned gap exceeds 60 contiguous minutes, and the report lists total available minutes vs. scheduled minutes with coverage stated as a percentage.
evidence: There is no generated week to query and no availability model to measure coverage against. The 236-path OpenAPI document exposes /v1/agenda and /v1/daily-plan (single-day reads) but nothing that returns a generated week or a coverage figure, and no configured-available-hours setting exists (`grep -rn 'workingHours|working_hours|offHours|quietHours' packages/types/src/*.ts` → no such preference; HubPreferences carries timezone and calendar display prefs only).
notes: The api-call the acceptance describes has no endpoint to call.

requirement: The scheduling system still leaves protected personal/leisure time — instrumentalization does not consume the user's whole life.
sourceQuote: while still allowing me time to enjoy my life
acceptance: The generated week contains protected non-work time honoring configured boundaries (e.g. evenings/weekends or explicit personal blocks); an automated check asserts the scheduler never places work blocks inside declared personal/off-hours windows, across 10 generated weeks.
evidence: No personal/off-hours boundary configuration exists to honor — the same grep over packages/types/src/*.ts finds no quiet-hours, off-hours or personal-window preference, and packages/types/src/calendar.ts's only availability concepts are computed free/busy projections. With no scheduler (WIL-14/WIL-15) there is nothing to run across 10 generated weeks.

requirement: Docket is connected to Curfew — a working integration path exists between the two systems.
sourceQuote: The end goal is to connect Docket to Curfew
acceptance: A Curfew client (or reference stub implementing the published contract) authenticates to Docket, fetches the day's agenda, and posts an enforcement/completion event; both calls return 2xx and the events appear in Docket's activity record.
evidence: No integration path exists in either direction. `grep -rn 'acknowledge_directive|hub/directive' --include='*.ts' apps/api/src packages/*/src apps/web/src` returned zero real matches (the only 'directive' hits are unrelated JSDoc in packages/ui/src/primitives/sheet.tsx:6, dialog.tsx:6, PropertyTrigger.tsx:7 and apps/web/src/components/cycles/properties-panel.tsx:8). The live OpenAPI document from the running API (236 paths) contains no enforcement or completion-event endpoint. The spec itself states it: docs/engineering/specs/curfew-integration.md:3 — 'Status: proposed — design-complete, not yet implemented.'
notes: There is no Curfew client, no reference stub, and nothing for one to authenticate to. All ten Docket-side items in the spec's §7 checklist are unchecked.

requirement: The integration exposes clear, documented API integration points for Curfew to consume.
sourceQuote: clear API integration points
acceptance: The OpenAPI spec lists the named Curfew-facing operations — fetch today's agenda, mark block started/finished, report task completion, receive/emit enforcement directives, signal day-start and day-end review state — each with request/response schemas, and each responds successfully against the running API.
evidence: Fetched the live spec from the running API (236 paths) and searched every path and summary. Only one of the six named operations exists: 'fetch today's agenda' — GET /v1/agenda returns HTTP 200 with {"date":"2026-08-02","entries":[]} when authenticated (401 unauthenticated), alongside GET /v1/hub/today and GET|POST /v1/daily-plan. The other five have no operation at all: no mark-block-started/finished, no report-task-completion Curfew operation, no receive/emit enforcement directives, no day-start or day-end review-state signal. Scanning every path+summary+description for device/lock/enforc/curfew/directive produced only incidental word matches in unrelated CRUD summaries.
notes: Note a design conflict worth surfacing: curfew-integration.md §6 item 7 states 'No new REST /v1 endpoints. MCP-only' — so the committed design intends these to be MCP resources/tools rather than OpenAPI operations, which would make this requirement's 'OpenAPI spec lists the named operations' acceptance unreachable as written even once built.

requirement: Docket is not strongly coupled to Curfew — Curfew-specific logic stays behind an integration boundary.
sourceQuote: that do not strongly couple Docket to Curfew
acceptance: A grep across Docket core (apps/web src, apps/api src, packages) finds zero Curfew imports, Curfew-named types, or hard-coded Curfew hostnames outside the dedicated integration adapter module; deleting/disabling that adapter leaves pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, and pnpm test green.
evidence: The zero-coupling grep genuinely passes: `grep -rni 'curfew' --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' apps/web/src apps/api/src apps/admin/src packages/*/src` returned 0 matches, and `pnpm turbo run typecheck` is green (18 successful, 18 total). But the acceptance's second clause has no subject — there is no dedicated integration adapter module to delete or disable, because the integration does not exist (see WIL-25). The only artifact naming Curfew is the design doc.
notes: Reported as partial rather than pass because the property is currently vacuous. Worth noting the design is deliberately built for this: curfew-integration.md §0 forbids the string 'curfew' in any route, table, column, Zod type, MCP tool name, resource URI, scope or enum value, and §1 shows the surface riding the generic Hub-resource + TOOL_SCOPE machinery with no clientId branch.

requirement: A clear document or plan exists that explicitly outlines how to implement the Docket/Curfew user experience.
sourceQuote: there is a clear document or plan explicitly outlining how to implement the Docket/Curfew user experience
acceptance: A committed spec (e.g. docs/engineering/specs/curfew-integration.md) contains named sections covering: the full API contract, and each of the seven daily-loop steps from wake-unlock through end-of-day lockout, each with the Docket-side trigger, payload, and UI surface. No section is a placeholder or TODO.
evidence: docs/engineering/specs/curfew-integration.md exists and is substantive — 554 lines with §0 coupling rule, §1 coupling boundary, §2 daily flow, §3 API surface (3.1 auth, 3.2 docket://hub/directive, 3.3 acknowledge_directive, 3.4 plan_day reuse, 3.5 delivery, 3.6 versioning), §4 posture computation, §5 realism, §6 non-goals, §7 net-new checklist. Only one 'placeholder' string appears (line 456) and it is descriptive prose, not a stub. Gap against the acceptance: §2 decomposes the day into THREE stages (wake / all day / evening), not the required seven daily-loop steps from wake-unlock through end-of-day lockout, and no step is given a Docket-side trigger + payload + UI surface triple — §2 gives wire calls only, with no UI surface named for any step.
notes: Also relevant: every one of the ten Docket-side items in §7 is an unchecked [ ] box, and the doc's own header says 'proposed — design-complete, not yet implemented.'

requirement: Athena can force completion of specific tasks at specific times by making other device activity impossible.
sourceQuote: Athena would literally be able to force me to complete certain tasks at certain times of the day by literally making it impossible for me to do anything else
acceptance: The contract defines an enforcement directive of the form "restrict device to task T until T is complete, starting at time X"; an integration test has Athena issue it and asserts a stub Curfew client receives the directive with task id, start time, and release condition, and that the release event only fires after the task is marked done.
evidence: No such directive exists in the contract, and the committed design explicitly refuses it. docs/engineering/specs/curfew-integration.md:80-86 states Docket 'returns a `posture` (an abstract severity) and, optionally, a `recommendedAction` naming one task to narrow focus toward. It never says "lock the screen," "quit this app," or "run this command."' Lines 136-139 add: 'There is no third option where Docket sends an imperative enforcement command — that vocabulary does not exist on either side of this integration by design.' The §7 Curfew-side checklist closes with an unchecked item calling the 'literally impossible' enforcement gap 'explicitly out of this integration's scope' that 'contradicts curfew-sync.md's current non-goals'. No enforcement-directive type, no release-condition type, and no integration test exist in the codebase.
notes: This is a direct requirement-versus-design conflict, not just missing work: the requirement asks for 'restrict device to task T until T is complete, starting at time X' with a release condition, and the committed spec's §0/§1 boundary rules forbid exactly that vocabulary. It needs a product decision before it can be scheduled.

requirement: On wake, the day's device access is released by Curfew, and Docket supplies the day-start signal that gates it.
sourceQuote: Wake up, Curfew allows me to use my devices.
acceptance: The spec defines the wake/day-start handshake and the API exposes a day-start endpoint returning that the day's agenda is ready; calling it before the agenda is generated returns a not-ready state rather than an empty agenda.
evidence: The spec half exists and is detailed: docs/engineering/specs/curfew-integration.md is 554 lines; §2 (lines 94-133) diagrams the wake handshake ('wake Curfew SUNRISE ──resources/read──▶ docket://hub/directive ◀── plan (today), posture, reason ──'), and §3.2 (line 163) specifies the `docket://hub/directive` resource. The API half does not exist: `grep -rn "directive" apps/api/src --include="*.ts" -l` returns zero files, and the spec's own §7 checklist (lines 515-537) has every Docket-side box unchecked — including the `docket://hub/directive` static resource, the `directive_posture` enum/table, and `computeDirectivePosture`.
notes: The `plan_day` tool the handshake reuses does exist. There is no day-start endpoint and therefore no not-ready state to return.

requirement: Curfew opens Docket to a surface that presents the day's agenda.
sourceQuote: Curfew opens Docket to inform me of the day's agenda.
acceptance: A documented deep link (e.g. docket://today or an https equivalent) opens directly onto the day agenda surface; screenshot shows the agenda with the day's blocks at 1440x900 and 390x844.
evidence: A day-agenda surface exists and renders: screenshot .../scratchpad/shots2/today-1440x900-light.png shows /today with 'Late night / Today / Sunday, August 2', an 'Open Athena for today' link, a capture box, a 'Next up' section, and a live day calendar rail. An https deep link is declared in the manifest (curl https://docket.hypertext.studio/manifest.webmanifest → shortcuts include `{"name":"Today","url":"/today"}`), and start_url is '/today'.
notes: Two gaps. No custom scheme (docket://) exists, and no document names /today as the Curfew day-start deep link — docs/engineering/specs/curfew-integration.md §2 says Curfew renders the agenda itself from docket://hub/directive and only mentions an 'optional' deep link into Athena chat. And the captured agenda is empty ('Nothing scheduled'), so I have not seen it with the day's blocks.

requirement: Nothing else on the device is usable until the user has gone through the morning agenda flow, and Docket emits the signal that releases the block.
sourceQuote: Curfew stops me from doing anything else until going through Curfew.
acceptance: Docket exposes a morning-agenda-acknowledged signal; an integration test asserts the signal is absent until the agenda flow is completed in the UI and fires exactly once on completion, and that a stub Curfew client keeps its block active until it receives that signal.
evidence: No acknowledgement signal exists. `grep -rn "acknowledge_directive" apps/ packages/` returns zero hits across the whole repo; docs/engineering/specs/curfew-integration.md §3.3 (line 289) specifies the tool as 'net-new' and §7 lists it unchecked ('acknowledge_directive tool, apps/api/src/mcp/directive-tools.ts, gated work:write' — no such file exists). No integration test and no stub Curfew client exist.

requirement: Athena assists the user through the morning review.
sourceQuote: Athena helps me review.
acceptance: Opening the day-start surface presents an Athena-led review conversation that walks the user's agenda (proposals, deferrals, confirmations) rather than a static list; screenshot shows Athena's review prompt with actionable controls.
evidence: The day-start surface presents a static list plus a generic prompt box, not an Athena-led agenda review. Screenshot .../scratchpad/shots2/today-1440x900-light.png shows 'Open Athena for today' (a link out), a free-text composer reading 'Capture a task, paste a plan, or ask Athena…' with an 'Ask Athena' toggle, and a 'Next up' card reading 'Nothing scheduled — You're clear for now.' There are no proposal/defer/confirm controls anywhere on the surface.
notes: Athena is reachable from the surface, but does not walk the agenda. The Athena surface itself (.../shots2/orgs-orgId-athena-1440x900-light.png) is an objective queue, not a review conversation.

requirement: Athena checks in repeatedly throughout the day against the day's goals.
sourceQuote: Athena checks in repeatedly throughout the day to ensure I'm meeting my goals
acceptance: In a simulated day, Athena issues check-ins at the configured cadence (>= 3 in a work day), each referencing the current block and outstanding goals; the test asserts the count, the timing, and that each check-in records the user's response or non-response.
evidence: No goal check-in cadence exists. The cron surface in apps/api/src/routes/cron.ts exposes lifecycle-sweep, sync-connectors, email-suggestions, process-events, search-index, daily-digests, account-deletion-sweep, account-export-sweep, sync-calendars, run-linear-agent-sessions, athena-triggers, expired-sessions-sweep — nothing recurring against a day's goals. The 'proactive' setting in packages/types/src/hub-preferences.ts:110-121 is scoped to 'whether incoming mentions/assignments auto-draft a plan', not check-ins. docs/engineering/specs/curfew-integration.md §7 lists `sweepDirectivePosture` (the 5-minute cadence) as unchecked.
notes: The closest shipped behaviour is a once-daily digest, which is not a repeated in-day check-in and records no user response.

requirement: Athena dynamically reorganizes the remaining work when the day drifts.
sourceQuote: dynamically reorganizes work
acceptance: Simulate a block overrunning by 45 minutes; the remaining day's schedule is recomputed automatically and the moved blocks are visible. Before/after screenshots of the day view show the changed placements without any manual drag.
evidence: No automatic recomputation of the remaining day exists. `grep -rn "reflow|reschedule|autoSchedule" apps/api/src` surfaces no day-replan path, and cron.ts (see WIL-34) has no drift/overrun sweep. The scheduling surfaces in apps/web/src/components/calendar and the fluid-scheduling e2e specs are all manual drag/drop.
notes: No before/after day-view screenshots are possible because nothing recomputes.

requirement: Athena proactively triggers Curfew to stop other work when the day's goals are at risk.
sourceQuote: proactively stops me from doing other work using Curfew if it's likely I won't meet my goals for the day
acceptance: Given a simulated at-risk state (projected completion below the day's goal), the test asserts Docket emits a Curfew block directive naming the allowed task and the blocked scope, without any user action, and that no directive is emitted when the day is on track.
evidence: Docket emits no Curfew directive of any kind — `grep -rn "directive" apps/api/src --include="*.ts" -l` is empty. docs/engineering/specs/curfew-integration.md §4 (line 413) titles the posture computation section 'the part that doesn't exist yet anywhere', and §7 lists `computeDirectivePosture(hubId, date)` unchecked.
notes: Worth flagging from the spec itself: §0/§5 state Docket deliberately never sends an imperative enforcement command — only a posture plus reason. So this requirement as written conflicts with the committed design and needs a product decision, not just implementation.

requirement: At end of day, all apps are blocked and further device use is prevented until the evening flow is completed.
sourceQuote: At the end of the day, Curfew blocks me out of all apps and prevents further device use
acceptance: At the configured end-of-day time, Docket emits a full-lockout directive whose release condition is the completed evening flow; a stub Curfew client asserts the lockout remains active while any of the three evening steps is incomplete.
evidence: No lockout directive exists (same absence as WIL-36). There is no end-of-day trigger beyond the `daily-digests` cron (apps/api/src/routes/cron.ts:93), which sends a summary and emits no release condition. No stub Curfew client exists in the repo.

requirement: The evening lockout releases only after the user completes a structured review of the day.
sourceQuote: until I complete a structured review of the day
acceptance: The evening surface presents a defined, multi-step review (not a free-text box) covering the day's blocks and outcomes; screenshot shows the steps, and the release signal is withheld until every required step is answered.
evidence: No evening review surface exists. `grep -rn "morning|evening|shutdown|end of day|day review" apps/web/src --include="*.tsx" -il` matches only apps/web/src/app/(app)/today/page.tsx and apps/web/src/components/athena/athena-workspace.tsx, neither of which contains a multi-step review. There is no route under apps/web/src/app for an evening/shutdown flow.

requirement: The evening lockout releases only after unfinished work is reconciled.
sourceQuote: reconcile unfinished work
acceptance: Every incomplete task/block from the day is listed in the evening flow and each must be dispositioned (completed, rescheduled, or dropped with a reason); screenshot shows the list, and the release signal is withheld while any item is undispositioned.
evidence: No reconciliation flow exists. The only carryover-disposition UI in the app is the per-cycle close dialog (apps/web/src/components/cycles/close-cycle-dialog.tsx, backed by POST /cycles/:id/close with keep/move/triage decisions) — that is cycle-scoped, not a daily evening reconciliation, and it gates nothing.
notes: The keep/move/triage vocabulary in the cycle close path is a reasonable model to reuse when this is built.

requirement: The evening lockout releases only after the next day's agenda has been intentionally prepared.
sourceQuote: intentionally prepare the next day's agenda
acceptance: The evening flow ends with an explicitly confirmed next-day agenda; screenshot shows the proposed agenda plus a confirm action, and the API reports tomorrow's agenda as user-confirmed (not auto-accepted) before the release signal fires.
evidence: No next-day confirmation step exists. The `plan_day` MCP tool can write tomorrow's items (docs/engineering/specs/curfew-integration.md §3.4, line 355), but there is no confirm action in the UI and no user-confirmed flag on the agenda — `grep -rn "directive" apps/api/src` is empty, so no release signal is gated on it.
notes: docs/engineering/specs/curfew-integration.md §2 describes exactly this flow (two plan_day calls plus one acknowledge_directive), but none of it is implemented.

requirement: The complete end-to-end flow works: Athena connects to an end user's local device and models running on that device power Athena.
sourceQuote: We need the complete end to end flow of Athena connecting an end user's local device to run models that power Athena.
acceptance: With a user's Lattice instance connected, an Athena request is answered by a model executing on the local device: the local device logs show the inference, the response renders in Docket, and taking the local device offline makes the same request surface an explicit unavailable state instead of silently falling back to a cloud model.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the complete flow is implemented and exercised end to end, but against a local stub rather than a real device: apps/api/tests/lattice/lattice-flow.test.ts (11 tests passing) drives PKCE authorization, the real callback exchange with a sealed grant, device listing through the gateway, activating a device, routing a turn to the gateway which relays it to the device, a tool call carried back through the text protocol, an explicit unavailable state when the device goes offline (answering from nowhere else), reverting to the default backend, and disconnect deleting the grant and token. The counterparty is apps/api/tests/lattice/local-lovelace-stub.ts, not Lovelace.
notes: There is no Lattice adapter, no local-device connection, no offline/unavailable state, and nothing to drive end to end. All nine WIL requirements share this single root finding.

requirement: The integration is built on the Lovelace Lattice SDK rather than a hand-rolled client.
sourceQuote: you'll need to use the Lovelace Lattice SDK
acceptance: The Lattice SDK appears as a declared dependency and the adapter imports and calls it; there are no hand-written HTTP calls to Lattice endpoints outside the SDK.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the integration is hand-rolled, not built on the Lattice SDK. `@reasonabletech/lattice-client` appears in no package.json in the workspace; the client lives in packages/integrations/src (beginLatticeAuthorization, listLatticeDevices, LATTICE_SCOPES) and apps/api/src/routes/lattice*.ts.
notes: There is also no hand-rolled client to fall back on — the requirement's failure mode (hand-written HTTP calls to Lattice endpoints) is absent because no client of any kind exists.

requirement: The appropriate Lattice skill is found, installed, and used to build the integration.
sourceQuote: Please find, install, and use the appropriate skill
acceptance: The Lattice skill is present in the installed skill/plugin set and the WORKLOG entry for the Lattice slice records its invocation and what it contributed.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): .claude/skills/lattice-start/SKILL.md is committed, so the skill was found and installed. It is not `pass` because the skill's own stated path is SDK install plus CLI-driven developer-app registration, and the implementation went the other way (WIL-42), so the skill was not used as written.

requirement: A user can select their own Lattice instance as the model/agentic back end for Athena.
sourceQuote: to allow a user to use their own Lattice instance as the model/agentic back end for athena
acceptance: After connecting a Lattice instance, the account's Athena backend setting reports that instance as active, and subsequent Athena requests for that account are routed to it (verified in request traces), while other accounts remain on the default backend.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): a person can select their own Lattice instance as Athena's backend: packages/agent-runtime/src/model-backend.ts enumerates `ModelBackendId = 'cloudflare-router' | 'anthropic-direct' | 'lattice' | 'mock'` with lattice preferred first, and the flow test asserts the chosen device becomes active for that owner's turns while every other account stays on the default backend. `partial` because the api-call acceptance was satisfied against the stub gateway.
notes: No request trace could be gathered because there is no alternate backend to route to.

requirement: Settings-level UI exists to manage the Lattice connection.
sourceQuote: There should be appropriate settings-level UI to manage this.
acceptance: A Settings section lets the user connect, view live connection status and target device, choose the model, and disconnect. Screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark show the section with no overflow and no dead read-only rows.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/athena/lattice-section.tsx with lattice-copy.ts is the management UI (connect, device selection, active state, disconnect). `partial`: no screenshot of it exists.
notes: Also confirmed absent from Settings→Connections and Settings→Connected apps by the zero-hit repo-wide grep for 'lattice'.

requirement: Connecting Lattice is turnkey — no manual configuration, CLI steps, or hand-entered endpoints/keys.
sourceQuote: It should be as turnkey as possible.
acceptance: A recorded run connects Lattice from Settings in <= 3 user actions with zero text fields for URLs, keys, or tokens, zero terminal commands, and zero file edits; the recording is the evidence.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the flow is turnkey by construction — OAuth with PKCE, device list fetched from the gateway, no endpoint or key typed by the user (apps/api/src/routes/lattice-oauth.ts, lattice-connection.ts). Not screenshot- or interaction-verified against the real service.
notes: The turnkey bar (≤3 actions, no text fields for URLs/keys, no terminal, no file edits) cannot be measured against a flow that does not exist.

requirement: Authorization uses OAuth — the user authorizes Athena to use their Lovelace Lattice system through an OAuth flow.
sourceQuote: a user can use OAuth to authorize Athena to use a user's Lattice system from Lovelace
acceptance: Clicking Connect opens Lovelace's OAuth consent screen (screenshot), and on approval Docket stores only OAuth tokens — no user password is ever entered into Docket. Revoking the grant in Lovelace causes Docket to show the connection as disconnected on the next request.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): authorization is OAuth: the flow test asserts the browser is sent to Lovelace with PKCE and the exact scopes, and that the real callback exchange stores a sealed grant. `partial` because the acceptance is a screenshot of the consent flow and it ran against a stub authorization server.
notes: No consent screen to screenshot, and no grant to revoke.

requirement: The OAuth grant requests only the permissions appropriate to Athena's use of Lattice.
sourceQuote: with the appropriate permissions
acceptance: The documented scope list is limited to what model/agentic inference requires; the consent screen screenshot shows exactly those scopes and no broader account-wide scopes, and the authorization request in the code matches that list.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): packages/integrations exports a closed `LATTICE_SCOPES` set and the flow test asserts the exact scopes are requested; packages/integrations/tests/lattice/lattice-oauth.test.ts covers it. Screenshot acceptance unmet.
notes: Blocked by WIL-47; a consent-screen screenshot is unobtainable.

requirement: Athena's requests go to Lattice's gateway and are routed through it to the user's locally running device.
sourceQuote: Athena can send requests to Lattice's gateway that get routed to the user's locally running device
acceptance: A request trace shows Athena calling the Lattice gateway host (not the device directly), and the local device's log shows the matching inbound request and served response with correlated request ids.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the flow test asserts the owner's turn is routed to the gateway and relayed to the device, with tool calls carried back through the text protocol and an explicit unavailable state rather than a silent fallback when the device is offline.
