The gateway is the local stub, so the api-call acceptance against the real Lattice gateway is unmet.
notes: Blocked by WIL-41/42.

requirement: Athena is demonstrated working end to end on Cloudflare's model router using the project's own API keys.
sourceQuote: after Athena is shown to work using Cloudflare's model router and by using our own api keys
acceptance: With Lattice disabled, a recorded end-to-end Athena run (chat, tool call, and a scheduled agent action) succeeds against Cloudflare's model router using the project's own API keys; the run output and request traces are committed as evidence.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the Cloudflare model-router tier exists as a first-class backend in packages/agent-runtime/src/model-backend.ts ('the product ships on Cloudflare's model router with Docket's own keys') and apps/api/tests/lattice/verify-athena-backend.ts is the verifier harness. `partial` because no run against Cloudflare with the project's own keys was executed in this gate — locally the container resolves the mock runtime (no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, APP_MODE=local).
notes: Chat + tool call + scheduled agent action against the real router with the project's own keys has never been demonstrated or captured.

requirement: The Lattice work is sequenced strictly after the Cloudflare model-router path is proven — it is not shipped or enabled before that.
sourceQuote: This should only be done after Athena is shown to work using Cloudflare's model router and by using our own api keys.
acceptance: The WORKLOG shows the Cloudflare verification entry dated before the first Lattice implementation commit, and the Lattice settings surface is gated (not user-reachable) until the Cloudflare path is recorded as verified.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the sequencing the requirement mandates was not honored: the Lattice tier shipped complete and is listed first in `MODEL_BACKEND_IDS` (packages/agent-runtime/src/model-backend.ts), while the Cloudflare model-router path it was supposed to follow has not been proven end to end (WIL-50).
notes: Ordering is currently unviolatable because Lattice does not exist, but the acceptance's evidence (a dated verification entry + a gate on the Lattice settings surface) cannot be produced today. Blocked behind WIL-50.

requirement: Interaction and design-system decisions must be portable to native apps — the plan's stated reason for aggressively consulting MD3 — rather than adopting web-only patterns that cannot carry over.
sourceQuote: because we eventually do want to create native apps for everything on the web
acceptance: A committed document maps every interaction pattern and design-system primitive shipped on web (context menu, list selection, drag-and-drop, chips, menus, inputs, navigation, elicitation cards, voice mode, timer control) to its named Material 3 / Apple HIG native counterpart. Any pattern with no native counterpart is listed as an explicit exception with a written reason and a migration note. The count of shipped patterns that are neither mapped nor listed as an exception is zero.
evidence: `grep -rli 'Apple HIG|SwiftUI|Jetpack Compose|native counterpart' docs/` → zero hits. `ls docs/design/` → audits/, craft-rubric.md, ghost-grammar.md; neither doc maps web patterns to native Material 3 / HIG counterparts, and neither lists exceptions with migration notes.
notes: The stated rationale for consulting MD3 (portability to native) has no committed artifact behind it.

requirement: Every kind of data Docket stores — not only dates — must be protected by strong constraints at the schema and API boundary.
sourceQuote: Any data stored by Docket should have strong constraints.
acceptance: A schema-audit test enumerates every Drizzle table and fails, naming table+column, when: a column stores an enumerated domain as free text instead of a pg enum or CHECK; a required relationship is not a NOT NULL foreign key with an explicit ON DELETE rule; a uniqueness invariant stated in the product (workspace slug, published-domain host, action id, actor email, cycle name per workspace) has no unique index; or a numeric/duration column permits negative or out-of-range values. Separately, every write endpoint's Zod schema rejects out-of-domain values with a 4xx Problem rather than coercing. The audit passes with zero entries at the launch commit and zero allowlist exemptions.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): packages/types/tests/dto/task-data-integrity.test.ts now exists and passes, and apps/api/tests/routes/task-dates.test.ts covers the date boundary, so the constraint story is no longer date-only. `partial` because the requirement is 'every kind of data Docket stores' and no repo-wide policy test proves constraint coverage across the schema — the @docket/types coverage run reports 61.53% branch coverage, which is where unvalidated shapes would hide.
notes: Marked fail rather than not-built because substantial constraint coverage and a working Zod boundary genuinely exist; what is absent is the enumerating audit test and a handful of named invariants. My constraint gaps were found by targeted inspection, not an exhaustive per-column sweep, so the true gap list may be longer.

requirement: A working subscription system must exist on the web — purchasable plans, a plans page at the exact URL the phone announcement dictates, and an entitlement that actually gates Athena phone access — otherwise the gating announcement points at nothing.
sourceQuote: telling the user that they'll need to sign up for an appropriate subscription plan on the web, giving specific instructions for the link to go to
acceptance: On the production domain, the exact URL spoken by the ACH-19 announcement loads a plans page listing at least one purchasable plan with its price and what it includes. A test account with no plan completes sign-up and payment end to end on the web; immediately afterward the account's entitlement reads as active from the API, and a call from that account's verified number reaches the live agent instead of the ACH-16/ACH-17 announcement. Cancelling the plan returns the account to the gated path on the next call.
evidence: Working: GET /pricing → HTTP 200, rendering two plans with prices and inclusions — 'Free $0 forever … One personal workspace, Unlimited projects and tasks, Connect your own tools, MCP access for AI clients' and 'Pro $8 per month … Everything in Free, Multiple workspaces, Priority support'. POST /v1/orgs/{orgId}/billing/checkout → HTTP 200 `{"url":"https://billing.mock.docket.local/checkout/cs_000001"}` (mock gateway in dev; RealStripeGateway exists at packages/billing/src/stripe.ts). A real entitlement gate exists: apps/api/src/billing/entitlement.ts, enforced at apps/api/src/agent/loop.ts:419 `await assertAgentSessionsEntitled(contextOrganizationId)` with 402 at apps/api/src/error.ts:132. Missing: NO telephony exists — grep for twilio|vonage|telnyx|webrtc|sip across every package.json returns nothing, and no ACH-19 announcement copy exists (grep for the plans URL / 'subscription plan on the web' across apps, packages, docs returns nothing). /plans → HTTP 404.
notes: Launch-blocker as scoped. The web half is largely real — purchasable plans, checkout, and an entitlement that genuinely gates Athena agent sessions. The half that makes this requirement load-bearing is absent: there is no phone system, so there is no ACH-19 announcement to dictate a URL, no verified-number call routing, no live agent to reach, and no phone-specific entitlement. I also verified only against local dev, not the production domain.

requirement: A workspace's verified custom domain must actually serve that workspace's published briefs over HTTPS — verification and uniqueness are covered, but nothing requires the domain to serve.
sourceQuote: We'll need to support custom domains by workspace
acceptance: For a domain that has passed DNS verification: `curl -I https://<domain>/<brief-path>` from an unauthenticated client outside the app returns 200 with a valid TLS certificate whose SAN covers that host, and the body is that workspace's brief. Before verification the identical request returns 4xx with no brief content. After the domain is removed from the workspace it stops serving Docket content. A brief belonging to a different workspace is not reachable on this host.
evidence: No custom domain can be configured, so there is no verified host to curl. `grep -ril "customDomain|custom_domain|dnsVerif|domainVerif" apps packages --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` returns zero hits; the live OpenAPI document (236 paths from $API_URL/v1/openapi.json) contains zero paths matching /domain|publish|brief|slug/i; there is no domain table among the ~110 pgTable declarations in packages/db/src/schema/*.ts; and there is no public route group in apps/web/src/app to serve a brief. The prerequisite artifact — a published brief — also does not exist (CORE-26).
notes: The api-call acceptance (curl -I https://<domain>/<brief-path>) could not be attempted because no domain, no TLS provisioning path, and no brief route exist. Reported not-built on positive evidence of absence, not as an untested item.

requirement: Third-party developers must be able to register an application, complete the OAuth flow, and call the Docket API under exactly the scopes shown on the consent screen — the consent page otherwise informs users about access that does not exist.
sourceQuote: third-party developers will rely on it to properly inform the user how they're using their resources
acceptance: Against the production API: a third-party client is registered with a redirect URI, runs the authorization-code flow with PKCE through /oauth/authorize, exchanges the code for an access token, and successfully calls at least one endpoint for every scope granted. A call to an endpoint outside the granted scopes returns 403 with a stable Problem code; an expired or revoked token returns 401; revoking the grant from the user's settings makes the next call fail. Every scope string the server can issue is exercised by this test and has an enforcement point in code.
evidence: The core flow WORKS against the running API: `pnpm exec playwright test e2e/mcp-connect.spec.ts` → '1 passed (3.5s)'. Reading apps/web/e2e/mcp-connect.spec.ts, that run covers unauthenticated 401 with a discovery-pointing challenge advertising all five scopes (lines 34-48), dynamic client registration (line 55), browser consent through /oauth/authorize + PKCE code exchange (lines 58-61, 91-100), a Bearer MCP read (lines 63-71), a 403 `insufficient_scope` step-up on a write with `work:write` named in the challenge (lines 79-85), re-consent, a refresh token when offline_access is granted (lines 101-104), and the write verified back through the typed /v1 API (lines 106-114). All four capability scopes have enforcement points: apps/api/src/mcp/scope.ts:64-88 TOOL_SCOPE maps tools to work:read/work:write/agents:run/connectors:link, gated by requireScope() at :105.
notes: Three acceptance clauses are NOT exercised: (1) 'every scope string the server can issue is exercised' — the test only exercises work:read, work:write and offline_access; agents:run and connectors:link are merely asserted to appear in the challenge string; (2) 'an expired or revoked token returns 401'; (3) 'revoking the grant from the user's settings makes the next call fail' — a revoke endpoint exists (DELETE /v1/me/connected-apps/{clientId}) but no test drives it. Also, the first run of this spec failed on a 30s waitForResponse timeout during sign-up (cold Turbopack compile) before passing on retry — worth knowing for CI flake budgets.

requirement: Athena must have a universal inbox event stream that aggregates every inbound channel and event class — the plan names it as the destination for email, but nothing requires the stream itself to be universal.
sourceQuote: Emails that are received by Athena appear in Athena's universal inbox event stream
acceptance: One inbox surface renders, in a single chronologically interleaved list, at minimum: a received email, a raised elicitation, a spawned-agent milestone, a phone-call turn, and a connector sync event — each entry labeled with its channel and linking to its origin object. No event class shown there is reachable only from a channel-specific surface, and no channel writes to a parallel stream. Screenshots at 1440x900 and 390x844 in light and dark.
evidence: The stream is not universal — the event taxonomy has no email, elicitation or phone-call class. packages/notifications/src/web/types.ts:4-16 and packages/types' NotificationType enumerate exactly: mention, assignment, approval_request, status_change, comment, invitation, agent_session, connector_sync_failed, connector_needs_reauth, automation, service_announcement. Demonstrated live: with 4 Athena sessions awaiting the user (GET $API_URL/v1/me/athena/sessions → '"counts":{"needsYou":4,...}' and the UI pill reading 'Athena 3 needs you'), GET $API_URL/v1/me/notifications returned {"items":[]} and /count returned {"unread":0,"pendingApprovals":0} — and the Inbox rendered 'Inbox zero — No approvals, mentions, or assignments need your response right now' (screenshot /Users/.../audit-2026-08-02/surfaces/inbox-1440x900-light.png, which I looked at). Email writes to a parallel surface: apps/api/src/routes/email-suggestions.ts:1-9 documents that email-derived items 'sit in a triage lane', not the inbox.
notes: Of the five required event classes: connector sync (connector_sync_failed) and spawned-agent milestone (agent_session) are representable; received email goes to Triage instead; raised elicitations live only on the Athena rail; and no phone-call channel exists at all (no inbound voice route anywhere in apps/api/src/routes). The Inbox surface itself is well built — tabs All / Unread / Needs action / Announcements / Mentions & assignments / Activity — it just is not the universal destination.

requirement: The work must be broken into sequenced product slices and each slice recorded in docs/WORKLOG.md per the repo's branch/commit conventions, with linear history preserved.
sourceQuote: it needs to be broken into sequenced work slices, each independently planned and shipped per this repo's branch/commit conventions (one coherent product slice per branch, in `docs/WORKLOG.md`)
acceptance: docs/WORKLOG.md contains one completed entry per shipped slice naming the branch, the requirement IDs it closes, the files changed, and the validation output. Every requirement ID in the launch manifest appears in exactly one WORKLOG entry — no ID unclaimed, none claimed twice — and `git rev-list --merges --count origin/main..HEAD` prints 0.
evidence: Final gate 2026-08-02 (branch claude/docket-production-launch-ebe2d9): the linear-history half passes, re-verified: `git rev-list --merges --count main..HEAD` → 0 across all 45 commits on the branch. The record half is now structural rather than absent — docs/engineering/launch/slices/*.md is the canonical per-worker record per docs/engineering/launch/README.md — but only 4 slice files exist, so the great majority of requirement ids are claimed by no slice and no WORKLOG entry.
notes: docs/WORKLOG.md is substantial (4970 lines, 151 headed entries) and follows the repo convention well for prior work — the gap is specifically that this launch's slices have not been started or recorded.

requirement: Migrated Sunsama work must land in the correct one of the eight named workspaces rather than in a single catch-all destination — the migration and the workspace list are specified separately with no routing between them.
sourceQuote: We are going to migrate all active work from Sunsama into Athena using Sunsama MCP.
acceptance: A committed mapping table assigns every Sunsama stream/channel/project to exactly one of the eight named workspaces. After migration, a per-workspace count report shows every migrated task in the workspace its mapping specifies; the number of tasks landing in a default/unassigned/inbox workspace equals the number the mapping explicitly routes there, and that number is declared in the mapping before the run rather than discovered after. Zero migrated tasks have a null workspace.
evidence: `grep -rli 'eight named workspaces|eight workspaces' --include=*.md` across the repo → zero hits. No stream/channel→workspace mapping table exists in docs/, and there is no migration run to produce a per-workspace count report (see WIL-01).
notes: Neither half of the routing contract — the pre-declared mapping nor the post-run count report — exists.
